rules.title: About This Work
rules.body:
# A Higher Sanskrit Grammar

**Author:** @[moreśvara rāmacandra kāle]
**Original Publication:** 1894

---

This digital edition presents the complete text of _A Higher Sanskrit Grammar_ by M.R. Kale, a comprehensive treatise on Sanskrit grammar that has served generations of students and scholars since its first publication in 1894.

It is the best available grammar of the Sanskrit language in English written by a native grammarian. As such we hope to start with this work as a foundation for a more comprehensive modern grammar for the Sanskrit language that aspires to supercede the extant references (i.e. Macdonell, Whitney, etc.).

Those works are undoubtedly important to the modern English-speaking student of sanskrit, but they suffer from the 19th century condecension of their authors' era. One can recognize the monumental work of Whitney and Macdonell, but we hope to be able to remedy this by writing a modern grammar without the same flaws-- perhaps with flaws all our own. Please contribute to the project if you find such an error.

_The original work is in the public domain._

rules.title: Sanskrit Language and Devanāgarī Alphabet
rules.body:
Sanskrit, or the refined language, is the language of @deva[देव] (@[deva]) or gods,[^1] and the alphabet in which it is written is called @deva[देवनागरी] (@[devanāgarī]), or that employed in the cities of gods.

The correct name for the Sanskrit alphabet is @deva[दैवनागरी] (@[daiva-nāgarī]) sometimes abbreviated into @deva[नागरी] (@[nāgarī]). Perhaps in the word @deva[देवनागरी] we have a history of the times when the Aryans entered and settled in Northern India. The Aryans who were much fairer in colour than the aborigines of India are the @deva[देव] (@[deva]) referred to in the name @deva[देवनागरी] (from @deva[दिव्] (@[div]) "to shine", those of a brilliant complexion); and @deva[नागरी] (@[nāgarī]) means the Aryan settlements within the precincts of which the sacred language was spoken.

The Sanskrit language is generally written in different parts of the country, in that alphabet which is used for the vernacular (e.g., Bengali, Marathi, etc.). That character, however, in which the earliest monuments are written (such as the inscriptions containing the edicts of Aśoka) and which is employed throughout Upper India is generally considered to be the real @deva[देवनागरी].

---

[^1]: @deva[संस्कृतं नाम देवी वाग्व्याख्याता महर्षिभिः] | @[saṃskṛtaṃ nāma devī vāg vyākhyātā maharṣibhiḥ] — Dandin

rules.title: Devanāgarī Alphabet Structure and Pāṇinian Classification
rules.body:
The Devanāgarī alphabet consists of forty-two letters or @deva[वर्ण] (@[varṇa]), nine vowels or @deva[स्वर] (@[svara]), and thirty-three consonants or @deva[व्यञ्जन] (@[vyañjana]).[^1]

These express nearly every gradation of sound, and every letter stands for a particular and invariable sound.

**Note:** This explains why there are no names, as in Greek, for the different letters of the alphabet.

---

[^1]: Thus given by Pāṇini:—
  1. Vowels
    @deva:
    अइउण् ।
    ऋऌक् ।
    एओङ् ।
    ऐऔच् ।
    :@

  2. Consonants
    @deva:
    हयवरट् ।
    लण् ।
    ञमङणनम् ।
    झभञ् ।
    घढधष् ।
    जबगडदश् ।
    खफछठथचटतव् ।
    कपय् ।
    शषसर् ।
    हल् ।
    :@

  The alphabet, it will be seen, is divided into 14 sections by Pāṇini, which are called @deva[शिवसूत्राणि] (@[śivasūtrāṇi]), or the sūtras revealed by @[śiva]. Each section ends with an indicatory letter called @deva[इत्] (@[it]) which is not to be counted among the letters of the alphabet. These "Its" serve an important purpose in Sanskrit grammar, as they enable the grammarians to express several letters, or groups of letters, in a very convenient and condensed form. For any letter, with the following @deva[इत्] added to it, is not only expressive of itself but of all letters that intervene between it and this @deva[इत्]; e.g. @deva[अण्] means @deva[अ], @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[इक्] means @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ], @deva[ऌ], &c. Similarly @deva[अच्] means technically the whole alphabet, @deva[अम्] any vowel, and @deva[हल्] any consonant; @deva[यण्] a semivowel, @deva[हश्] a soft consonant, @deva[खर्] a hard consonant, @deva[जश्] a soft unaspirate, @deva[झष्] a soft aspirate &c. Each of these significant terms is technically called a @deva[प्रत्याहार] (@[pratyāhāra]).

  Since short vowels include the long and the protracted vowels (See @ref[3]. a.) another @deva[इत्] '@deva[ट्]' is generally employed to mark a particular vowel: e.g. @deva[अ] means @deva[अ], @deva[आ] and @deva[आ३], but @deva[अट्] means @deva[अ] (of six kinds) only; so @deva[कृट्] means @deva[कृ] and nothing else.

rules.title: Vowel Classification: Simple, Diphthongs, and Modifications
rules.body:
The nine primary vowels consist of five simple vowels viz. @deva[अ], @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ] and @deva[ऌ], and four diphthongs viz. @deva[ए], @deva[ऐ], @deva[ओ] and @deva[औ].

A vowel may be @deva[ह्रस्व] (@[hrasva]) or short, @deva[दीर्घ] (@[dīrgha]) or long, or @deva[प्लुत] (@[pluta]) or protracted (also called prolated by some) according to the time required to pronounce it.[^1] The vowels are thus divided:

(1) Short vowels—@deva[अ] @[a], @deva[इ] @[i], @deva[उ] @[u], @deva[ऋ] @[ṛ], @deva[ऌ] @[ḷ];

(2) Long vowels—@deva[आ] @[ā], @deva[ई] @[ī], @deva[ऊ] @[ū], @deva[ॠ] @[ṝ], @deva[ए] @[e], @deva[ऐ] @[ai], @deva[ओ] @[o], @deva[औ] @[au]; and

(3) Protracted vowels @deva[आ३] @[ā3], @deva[ई३] @[ī3], @deva[ऊ३] @[ū3], @deva[ॠ३] @[ṝ3], @deva[ऌ३] @[ḷ3], @deva[ए३] @[e3], @deva[ऐ३] @[ai3], @deva[ओ३] @[o3], and @deva[औ३] @[au3].

**N.B.** As the @deva[प्लुत] or protracted vowels are not commonly to be met with in classical Sanskrit, the vowels are usually given as thirteen, represented by the thirteen signs given above under (1) and (2).

Each of these vowels may be again of two kinds, @deva[अनुनासिक] (@[anunāsika]) or nasalised, and @deva[अननुनासिक] (@[ananunāsika]) or without a nasal sound.[^2]

Vowels are also further discriminated into @deva[उदात्त] (@[udātta]) or acute, @deva[अनुदात्त] (@[anudātta]) or grave, and @deva[स्वरित] (@[svarita]) or circumflex. @deva[उदात्त] is that which proceeds from the upper part of the vocal organs, @deva[अनुदात्त] that which proceeds from their lower part, while @deva[स्वरित] arises out of a mixture of these two.[^3] But these are ignored in classical Sanskrit. They are marked only in Vedic works: the Udātta is left unmarked; the Anudātta is marked with a horizontal line underneath; and Svarita has a perpendicular stroke above it. e.g. @deva[क्रं३बोऽभाः]; &c. Ṛg. V. 61. 2 @deva[रथानां न हे३रः।] &c. Ṛg. X. 78. 4. @deva[ज्ञातब्रह्म यो रे हुः] &c. Ṛg. X. 145. 4.

Thus there are eighteen different modifications of each of the vowels @deva[अ], @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ], and twelve of @deva[ऌ], @deva[ए], @deva[ऐ], @deva[ओ] and @deva[औ]; for there is no long @deva[ḷ] and the last four have not their corresponding short vowels.

---

[^1]: @deva[कुक्कुटोऽष्टविघोषणः] — Pāṇ. I. 2. 27. The crowing of the cock in the morning represents in its three stages these three kinds of vowels. The time required to pronounce a short vowel is called a @deva[मात्रा] (@[mātrā]). A long vowel has two mātrās and a Pluta vowel three.

[^2]: @deva[युक्तानुनासिकश्चनोः] — Pāṇ. I. 1. 8.

[^3]: @deva[उच्चैरुदात्तः। नीचैरनुदात्तः। समाहारः स्वरितः।] — Pāṇ. I. 2. 29, 31.

rules.title: Consonant Classification: Sparśa, Antastha, and Ūṣman
rules.body:
The consonants are divided into @deva[स्पर्श] (@[sparśa]) or mutes (those involving a complete closure or contact and not an approximate one of the organs of pronunciation), @deva[अन्तस्थ] (@[antastha]) (or intermediate, i.e. the Semivowels,) and @deva[ऊष्मन्] (@[ūṣman]) or sibilants.

These are represented by thirty-three syllabic signs arranged as below:—

**(a) Mutes:**

(1) @deva[कवर्ग] or the group @deva[क]—@deva[क] @[k], @deva[ख] @[kh], @deva[ग] @[g], @deva[घ] @[gh], @deva[ङ] @[ṅ].

(2) @deva[चवर्ग] or the group @deva[च]—@deva[च] @[c], @deva[छ] @[ch], @deva[ज] @[j], @deva[झ] @[jh], @deva[ञ] @[ñ].

(3) @deva[टवर्ग] or the group @deva[ट]—@deva[ट] @[ṭ], @deva[ठ] @[ṭh], @deva[ड] @[ḍ], @deva[ढ] @[ḍh], @deva[ण] @[ṇ].

(4) @deva[तवर्ग] or the group @deva[त]—@deva[त] @[t], @deva[थ] @[th], @deva[द] @[d], @deva[ध] @[dh], @deva[न] @[n].

(5) @deva[पवर्ग] or the group @deva[प]—@deva[प] @[p], @deva[फ] @[ph], @deva[ब] @[b], @deva[भ] @[bh], @deva[म] @[m].

These are also called the five classes designated as @deva[कवर्ग] (@[kavarga]), @deva[चवर्ग] (@[cavarga]), @deva[टवर्ग] (@[ṭavarga]), @deva[तवर्ग] (@[tavarga]), and @deva[पवर्ग] (@[pavarga]) respectively.

**(b) Semivowels**

@deva[य] @[y], @deva[र] @[r], @deva[ल] @[l], @deva[व] @[v].

**(c) Sibilants**

@deva[श] @[ś], @deva[ष] @[ṣ], @deva[स] @[s].

**(d) Sonant Aspirate**

@deva[ह] @[h].

Besides these we have two more characters occurring in the Veda, viz. @deva[ळ] and @deva[ऴ] (often substituted for @deva[ल] and @deva[ळ]; as @deva[कॆळ] for @deva[कॆलॆ], @deva[सीळूरॆ] for @deva[सीलूरॆ] &c.). In Marāthi @deva[ळ] is generally substituted for the final @deva[ल] of Sanskrit words.

---

[^1]: @deva[उच्चैरुदात्तः। नीचैरनुदात्तः। समाहारः स्वरितः।] — Pāṇ. I. 2. 29, 31.

rules.title: Hard and Soft Consonants
rules.body: The first two letters of the five classes and the sibilants are called surds or hard consonants. The rest are called sonants or soft consonants.

rules.title: Nasal Sounds and Visarga
Aspiration of Consonants: Alpa-prāṇa and Mahā-prāṇa
rules.body: Some consonants are pronounced with a slight aspiration and are designated as @deva[अल्पप्राण] (@[Alpa-prāṇa]), while others which are pronounced with a stronger aspiration are called @deva[महाप्राण] (@[Mahā-prāṇa]). The first and third letters of each class, the nasals and the semi-vowels belong to the first class; the rest belong to the second class. For the sake of convenience the first and third letters of each class are sometimes called "unaspirates."

rules.title: Classification by Organs of Pronunciation
Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Letters: Savarṇa and Asavarṇa
rules.body:
Those letters are called @deva[सवर्ण] (@[savarṇa]) or homogeneous whose place of pronunciation in the mouth and the effort required to pronounce them is the same or equal.[^1] Letters which are not @deva[सवर्ण] or similar are called @deva[असवर्ण] (@[asavarṇa]) or heterogeneous.

---

[^1]: @deva[तुल्यास्यप्रयत्नं सवर्णम्] — Pāṇ. I. 1. 9.

rules.title: Vowels and Consonants Defined
rules.body:
A @deva[स्वर] (@[svara]) or vowel is that which can be pronounced without the help of any other letter; a @deva[व्यञ्जन] (@[vyañjana]) or consonant is that which is pronounced with the help of a vowel. The consonants, therefore, are written with a slanting nether stroke to denote their imperfect character.

Hence the consonants are given, in the system of Pāṇini, with an @deva[अ] added to them for the sake of pronunciation.

As already remarked, there are no separate names for the letters of the Sanskrit alphabet, except the two mentioned before, viz. @deva[अनुस्वार] and @deva[विसर्ग], and @deva[रेफ] (@[Refa]) which is the name sometimes given to @deva[र]. The word @deva[कार] (@[kāra]) is therefore used as an affix to denote a particular letter; e.g. @deva[अकार] the letter '@deva[अ]', @deva[ककार] the letter '@deva[क]', &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[तुल्यास्यप्रयत्नं सवर्णम्] — Pāṇ. I. 1. 9.

rules.title: Definition of Akṣara (Syllable)
rules.body: A vowel by itself or a consonant, simple or conjunct, with a vowel added to it, is called an @deva[अक्षर] (@[Akṣara]) or a syllable.

rules.title: Vowel Signs and Conjunct Consonants
Punctuation and Orthographic Marks
rules.body:
As sandhi is of primary importance in Sanskrit, @deva[विराम] (@[virāma]) or pause can be indicated only at the end of a sentence. The signs of punctuation, therefore, are only two, । and ॥. The former is used to mark the close of a sentence or the first half of a śloka or poetical stanza; the latter is employed to denote the close of a śloka.

The sign called @deva[अवग्रह] (@[Avagraha]) (and which represents half @deva[अ] @deva[अर्धकार] @[Ardhakāra]) is generally employed to mark the elision of short @deva[अ] after @deva[ए] or @deva[ओ]; e.g. @deva[तेऽपि] (@deva[ते] + @deva[अपि]), @deva[कालोऽस्ति] (@deva[कालो] + @deva[अस्ति]). The double mark @deva[ऽऽ] is sometimes used to indicate the elision of @deva[आ] after initial long @deva[आ]; @deva[तथा] + @deva[आस्ते] = @deva[तथाऽऽस्ते].

The mark @deva[०] is sometimes used to show that something is omitted, and which is to be understood from the context; e.g. @deva[अ०] may stand for @deva[अर्जुन], @deva[०प्रार्थी] for @deva[कवियशःप्रार्थी],[^1] &c.

---

[^1]: The scan of this word is heavily blurred; the reading @deva[कवियशःप्रार्थी] is the most plausible one consistent with the visible akṣaras.

rules.title: Prosodial Length of Short Vowels
rules.body: Short vowels when followed by a conjunct consonant are said to be prosodially long.

rules.title: Guṇa and Vṛddhi: Vowel Grades
rules.body:
The vowels @deva[अ], @deva[ए], @deva[ओ] and the syllables @deva[अर्] and @deva[अल्] are called @deva[गुण] (@[Guṇa]); the vowels @deva[आ], @deva[ऐ], @deva[औ] and the syllables @deva[आर्] and @deva[आल्] are called @deva[वृद्धि] (@[Vṛddhi]).[^1] The Guṇa and Vṛddhi vowels and syllables that are substituted for the simple vowels will appear from the following table:

| Simple V. | @deva[अ] | @deva[इ] & @deva[ई] | @deva[उ] & @deva[ऊ] | @deva[ऋ] & @deva[ॠ] | @deva[ऌ] |
|-----------|----------|---------------------|---------------------|---------------------|----------|
| **Guṇa**  | @deva[अ] | @deva[ए]            | @deva[ओ]            | @deva[अर्]          | @deva[अल्] |
| **Vṛddhi**| @deva[आ] | @deva[ऐ]            | @deva[औ]            | @deva[आर्]          | @deva[आल्] |

---

[^1]: @deva[वृद्धिरादैच्। अदेङ् गुणः। उरण् रपरः] — Pāṇ. I. 1. 1, 2; I. 1. 51.

rules.title: Nasalization of Semivowels
rules.body: The three semivowels @deva[य्], @deva[र्] and @deva[ल्] are sometimes nasalised and then they are written with the @deva[अनुनासिक] sign over them, as @deva[य̐], @deva[र̐], @deva[ल̐].

rules.title: Numerical Figures in Sanskrit
rules.body:
The numerical figures in Sanskrit are:
    @deva[१, २, ३, ४, ५, ६, ७, ८, ९, ०]
    1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 0.

These are combined to express larger figures precisely in the same way as in English; @deva[१२५] 125, @deva[५४०] 540, &c.

rules.title: Definition of Sandhi and Saṃhitā
rules.body:
By Sandhi (from @deva[सम्] together, and @deva[धा] to join) is meant the coalescence of two letters coming in immediate contact with each other.[^1]

@deva[संहिता] (@[saṃhitā])[^2] or sandhi is necessary in the case of the internal structure of a @deva[पद] (@[pada]), prepositions and roots joined together and a compound word (@deva[समास] @[samāsa]), while in that of a sentence i.e. in the case of the finals and initials of the different words in a sentence, it depends on the will of the writer.

**I. SVARASANDHI, OR THE COMBINATION OF FINAL AND INITIAL VOWELS.**

---

[^1]: @deva[परः सन्निकर्षः संहिता] — Pāṇ. I. 4. 109. Saṃhitā is the extreme contiguity of letters.

[^2]: @deva[संहितैकपदे नित्या नित्या धातूपसर्गयोः। नित्या समासे वाक्ये तु सा विवक्षामपेक्षते॥] — Sid. Kau. This couplet gives the rule for the observation of Sandhi.

rules.title: Combination of Similar Vowels (Savarṇa Dīrgha)

derivations.gloss: the ṛkāra pronounced by the sacrificer (since there is no long

rules.body:
If a simple vowel, short or long, be followed by a similar vowel, short or long, the substitute for them both is the similar long vowel[^1] e.g. @deva[देव] + @deva[अरि:] = @deva[देवारि:]; @deva[यज्ञ] + @deva[आसीत्] = @deva[यज्ञासीत्]; @deva[पद्म] + @deva[अभवत्] = @deva[पद्माभवत्]; @deva[विद्या] + @deva[आतुर:] = @deva[विद्यातुर:] eager to gain knowledge; @deva[इति] + @deva[ईश] = @deva[इतीश]; @deva[अपि] + @deva[ईश्वरे] = @deva[अपीश्वरे]; @deva[श्री] + @deva[ईश:] = @deva[श्रीश:]; @deva[भानु] + @deva[उदय] = @deva[भानूदय:]; @deva[साधु] + @deva[ऊरु:] = @deva[साधूरु:]; @deva[चमू] + @deva[ऊर्जि:] = @deva[चमूर्जि:] the strength of the army; @deva[कवि] + @deva[ऋजु:] = @deva[कवीर्जु:], @deva[कृ] + @deva[ऋकार:] = @deva[कॄकार:]; @deva[होतृ] + @deva[ॠकार:] = @deva[होतॄकार:] the ṛkāra pronounced by the sacrificer (since there is no long @deva[ऌ] long @deva[ऋ] is substituted for both).

If @deva[ऋ] or @deva[ऌ] be followed by a short @deva[ऋ] or @deva[ऌ], short @deva[ऋ] or @deva[ऌ] is optionally substituted for both;[^2] @deva[होतृ] + @deva[ऋकार:] = @deva[होतृऋकार:], and also @deva[होतर्कार:] (vide @ref[23]. sec. b); so three forms altogether @deva[होतृऋकार:], @deva[होतृकार:] and @deva[होतर्कार:]; @deva[होतृ] + @deva[ऌकार:] = @deva[होतृऌकार:] and also @deva[होतृळ्कार:].

---

[^1]: @deva[अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 101.

[^2]: @deva[स्वं सवर्णे ऋ वा। ऌतो सवर्णे ऌ वा] — Vārttikas on the above.

rules.title: Guṇa Combination: अ/आ + इ/उ/ऋ/ऌ

derivations.gloss: chief guess (or this may be the acc

rules.body:
When @deva[अ] or @deva[आ] is followed by @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ], @deva[ऌ], short or long, the @deva[गुण] letter corresponding to the latter takes the place of both[^1] e.g. @deva[उप] + @deva[इन्द्र] = @deva[उपेन्द्र:] Vishnu; @deva[परम] + @deva[ईश्वर:] = @deva[परमेश्वर:] the great lord; @deva[रमा] + @deva[इच्छा] = @deva[रमेच्छा] the wish of Ramā; @deva[यथा] + @deva[इच्छित] = @deva[यथेच्छितम्] according to wish or desire; @deva[हित] + @deva[उपदेश:] = @deva[हितोपदेश:] a friendly instruction; @deva[तव] + @deva[ऊरु] = @deva[तवोरु:] Kṛṣṇa's thigh; @deva[गङ्गा] + @deva[उदक] = @deva[गङ्गोदक], @deva[मङ्ग] + @deva[ऊरु] = @deva[मङ्गोरु]; @deva[कृष्ण] + @deva[ऋद्धि:] = @deva[कृष्णर्द्धि:] Kṛṣṇa's prosperity; @deva[महा] + @deva[ऋषि:] = @deva[महर्षि:] a great sage; @deva[तव] + @deva[ऌकार:] = @deva[तवल्कार:] The ḷkāra pronounced by you.

**(a)** If @deva[ऋ] or @deva[ऌ] be followed by homogeneous consonants, except the nasals, the semivowels, and @deva[र], the first of them is optionally dropped;[^2] @deva[कुम्भ] + @deva[ऋद्धि:] = @deva[कुम्भर्द्धि:] by the general rule; then @deva[कुम्भर्] + @deva[उ] + @deva[द्] + @deva[धि] = @deva[कुम्भोद्धि:] by this rule, the @deva[ऋ] being dropped; and also a third form @deva[कुम्भॠद्धि:] (vide @ref[22], sec. d., below).

**(b)** A consonant of the first five classes except @deva[र] coming after a semivowel is optionally doubled; so @deva[तवल्कार:] also becomes @deva[तवल्ल्कार:], @deva[तवल्ल्लकार:] and @deva[तवल्ल्ल्लकार:], 4 forms altogether.

**Exceptions:** Vṛddhi substitute takes place in the following cases:[^3]

**(a)** When a word ending in @deva[अ] is followed by @deva[ऊह], and @deva[अ] by @deva[ऊढ], @deva[ऊढा] and @deva[ऊहि]; e.g. @deva[प्रध] + @deva[ऊह:] = @deva[प्रधौह:], chief guess (or this may be the acc. pl. of @deva[प्रधवाह] a young bull trained to the yoke); @deva[प्र] + @deva[ऊह:] = @deva[प्रौह:] principal reasoning. Similarly @deva[प्रौढ:] full grown; @deva[प्रौढि:]; but @deva[प्रोहवान्] (as @deva[ऊहवान्] is not mentioned in the Sūtra).

**(b)** @deva[अक्ष] + @deva[ऊहिनी] = @deva[अक्षौहिणी] a complete army.[^4] (The change of @deva[उ] to @deva[ऊ] will be explained further on).

**(c)** When @deva[स्व] is followed by @deva[ईर] and @deva[ईरित्] both derived from @deva[ईर्] to go; e.g. @deva[स्व] + @deva[ईर:] = @deva[स्वैर:], one acting wilfully, self-willed; @deva[स्व] + @deva[ईरिणी] = @deva[स्वैरिणी]; so @deva[स्वैरी], @deva[स्वैरी] (@deva[स्वेन ईरितं कीलसदृशं इति]).

**(d)** When @deva[अ] is followed by @deva[कृत:] and there is an inst. Tat.; as @deva[सुख] + @deva[कृत] = @deva[सुखैकृत:] blessed with happiness (@deva[सुखेन कृत:]), but @deva[परमत्कृत:] very adorable (@deva[परमश्रद्धया कृत:]).

**(e)** When the word @deva[ऋण] comes after @deva[प्र], @deva[वत्सतर], @deva[ऋण], @deva[दशन] and @deva[नदी]; @deva[प्र] + @deva[ऋण] = @deva[प्राऋण:] principal debts, so @deva[वत्सतराऋणे] debt for a calf; @deva[ऋणाऋणे] (a debt contracted to liquidate a previous debt); @deva[दशाऋणे:] (Name of a country; lit. the country with ten fortresses); also @deva[दशाऋणी नदी] (lit. the river into which ten other rivers flow).

**(f)** When[^5] a preposition ending in @deva[अ] is followed by a root having an initial @deva[ऋ]; as @deva[उप] + @deva[ऋच्छति] = @deva[उपार्च्छति]; @deva[प्रार्च्छति]; but if the root be a denominative, the Vṛddhi is optional; @deva[प्र] + @deva[ऋषभीयति] = @deva[प्रर्षभीयति] or @deva[प्रार्षभीयति] acts like a bull: but @deva[उप] + @deva[ऊकरीयति] = @deva[उपोकरीयति], as the @deva[ऊ] is long; also @deva[प्र] + @deva[ऌकारीयति] = @deva[प्रा] + @deva[ऌकारीयति] very much wishes for @deva[ऌकार] lkāra; for @deva[ऌ] is grammatically considered to be similar to @deva[ऋ].

---

[^1]: @deva[आद्गुणः] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 87.

[^2]: @deva[झरो झरि सवर्णे] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 65.

[^3]: @deva[पूर्वत्रासिद्धम्] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 89. The first part of the sūtra (viz. @deva[एचोऽयवायावः]) forms a counter-exception to @ref[21]. a (which see). @deva[प्राङ् ब्रुवःऋतश्चोपधेभ्यः]; @deva[अङ्गाऋणैत्याध्यर्थस्थानम्]; @deva[ऋत आद्रौहिणोः]; @deva[ऋङे च तुनीयार्षिपरपवक्तव्यम्]; @deva[प्रवत्तारसब्रवाससनयोदशनादीनीया नव्यचनायाम्], Vārttikas on the above Sūtra.

[^4]: Properly an army consisting of 21870 chariots, as many elephants, 65610 horse and 109350 foot. @deva[अक्षौहिण्या: प्रतिष्ठानात् रथानां द्विरदस्तथा:। संख्या गणितमत्वन्त: सहस्राण्येकविंशति:।। द्वासप्तच्छूरणि चैवाहौ तथा धुर्य्य समाहिते। गजानां तु परीमाणमेतदेव विनिर्दिशेत्।। हयं शत सहस्रं तु सहस्राणि नवैव तु। नतुणामपि पञ्चाशच्छतानि षणि जानया:।। पञ्चषाष्टि: सहस्राणि तथाश्वानां शतानि च। दशोत्तराणि षट् प्राहुर्यमाविदहि संख्यया।।] Mahā-Bhār. Ad. P. II. 23-26.

[^5]: @deva[एचोऽयवायावः] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 78.

rules.title: Vṛddhi Combination: अ/आ + ए/ऐ/ओ/औ

derivations.gloss: one who moves from one mansion to another, a woman of bad character
name of the celebrated author of the Mahābhāṣya (a vast commentary on the sūtras of Pāṇini)
an antelope with a spotted skin or a kind of bird

rules.body:
When @deva[अ] or @deva[आ] is followed by @deva[ए] or @deva[ऐ] and @deva[ओ] or @deva[औ], @deva[ऐ] and @deva[औ] are respectively substituted for both;[^1] @deva[छुन्न] + @deva[एकान्त] = @deva[छुन्नैकान्त्य]; @deva[देव] + @deva[ऐश्वर्य] = @deva[दैवैश्वर्य] the majesty of god; @deva[सा] + @deva[एव] = @deva[सैव] she alone; @deva[भव] + @deva[औषधम्] = @deva[भवौषधम्] medicine against birth and re-birth. @deva[विद्या] + @deva[औत्सुक्यं] = @deva[विद्यौत्सुक्यं] longing for knowledge.

**Exceptions:**

**(a)** If a preposition ending in @deva[अ] be followed by a root beginning with @deva[ए] or @deva[औ], @deva[ए] or @deva[औ] is substituted;[^2] @deva[प्र] + @deva[एजते] = @deva[प्रेजते] quakes very much; @deva[उप] + @deva[ओषति] = @deva[उपोषति] burns something near; but if the root be a denominative, vṛddhi is optional; @deva[उप] + @deva[एककीयति] = @deva[उपेककीयति] or @deva[उपैककीयति]; @deva[प्र] + @deva[औषीयति] = @deva[प्रोषीयति] or @deva[प्रौषीयति].

**Counter-exception:** If a form of the root @deva[√इ] to go, or @deva[एध] to grow, with an initial @deva[ए], comes after @deva[अ], and @deva[इष] or @deva[इष्य] derived from @deva[इष्] of the 4th, 6th or 9th conj., after @deva[प्र], vṛddhi takes place; @deva[उप] + @deva[एति] = @deva[उपैति]; @deva[उप] + @deva[एधते] = @deva[उपैधते]; (but @deva[उप] + @deva[इतः] = @deva[उपेतः]; @deva[अवेहि] know; from @deva[अव] + @deva[एहि] which is equal to @deva[अव] + @deva[आ] + @deva[इहि], and not @deva[अवैहि]; @deva[मा भवान् प्र] + @deva[इदिधत्] = @deva[प्रेदिधत्]); @deva[प्र] + @deva[एषः] = @deva[प्रैषः] sending or directing; @deva[प्र] + @deva[एष्यः] = @deva[प्रैष्यः] a servant. But @deva[प्रेषः], @deva[प्रेष्यः] (from @deva[ईष्]).

**(b)** When @deva[अ] is followed by @deva[एव] in an indefinite sense, @deva[ए] is substituted for both:[^3] @deva[क] + @deva[एव] = @deva[केव] @deva[भोक्ष्यसे] where will you dine to-day? (The place being not definitely known); but @deva[तवैव] (why, I shall dine at your house).

**(c)** @deva[अ] followed by @deva[ओम्] and @deva[आ] (prep.) is dropped[^4] e.g. @deva[शिवाय] + @deva[ओं नमः] = @deva[शिवायों नमः]; @deva[शिव] + @deva[एहि] (@deva[आ] + @deva[इहि]) = @deva[शिवेहि].

**(d)** The vṛddhi is optional when the ending @deva[अ] of a word is followed by @deva[ओतु] a cat, or @deva[ओष्ठ] the lower lip, in a compound:[^5] @deva[स्थूल] + @deva[ओतुः] = @deva[स्थूलोतुः] or @deva[स्थूलौतुः]; @deva[बिम्बोष्ठः], @deva[बिम्बौष्ठः].

**(e)** The final vowel or the final consonant with the preceding vowel is dropped in the case of the following words when followed by certain words in a compound:[^6][^7] @deva[शाक] the country of the Śakas + @deva[अन्धु] a well = @deva[शाकन्धुः]; @deva[कर्क] name of a country + @deva[अम्बु] = @deva[कर्कन्धुः]; @deva[कुल] + @deva[अटा] = @deva[कुलटा] one who moves from one mansion to another, a woman of bad character; @deva[सीमन्] + @deva[अन्तः] = @deva[सीमन्तः] (the white line left by the parting of the hair on each side of the head); but @deva[सीम्नान्तः] when the meaning of the word is 'The last line or limit of a boundary.' @deva[मनस्] + @deva[ईश] = @deva[मनीश] wish; so @deva[लाङ्गलीश] the pole of a plough; @deva[हलीश:]; @deva[पतत्] + @deva[अञ्जलिः] = @deva[पतञ्जलिः] name of the celebrated author of the Mahābhāṣya (a vast commentary on the sūtras of Pāṇini); lit. 'fit to be adored with joined hands; or according to tradition 'who fell down from the hands of a certain sage as he was offering water to the sun at the time of Sandhyā adoration.' @deva[शार] + @deva[अङ्कः] = @deva[शारङ्कः] an antelope with a spotted skin or a kind of bird; but @deva[शाराङ्कः] one with a beautiful skin. This is an Ākṛtigaṇa i.e. words of similar formation and requiring grammatical explanation but not actually found in the gaṇa may be classed under it; e.g. @deva[मृत] + @deva[अण्डः] = @deva[मार्तण्डः] (derived from @deva[मृताण्ड]) lit. born of a dead egg, the sun.

---

[^1]: @deva[वृद्धिरेचि] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 88.

[^2]: @deva[उपधमाङ्नेति पाठो] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 91. @deva[वा इत्यादिषेप्य] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 92.

[^3]: @deva[एवे चानियोगे] — Vārtik.

[^4]: @deva[ओमाङोश्च] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 95.

[^5]: @deva[ओतोष्ठयोः समासे वा]

[^6]: @deva[शकन्ध्वादिषु परस्पदं वाच्यम्] — Vārt.

[^7]: And also in the case of an onomatopœic word in @deva[अत्] followed by @deva[इति] e.g. @deva[पटत्] + @deva[इति] = @deva[पटिति]; but not in the case of a monosyllabic word @deva[भद्] + @deva[इति] = @deva[भदिति]; and when the word is repeated, only the @deva[त्] is optionally dropped, as @deva[पटत्पटत्] + @deva[इति] = @deva[पटत्पटिति] or @deva[पटत्पटदिति].

rules.title: Semi-vowel Substitution: इ/उ/ऋ/ऌ → य्/व्/र्/ल्
rules.body:
When @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ] and @deva[ऌ], short or long, are followed by a dissimilar vowel, @deva[य्], @deva[व्], @deva[र्] and @deva[ल्] are respectively substituted for them[^1]; e.g. @deva[इति] + @deva[आह] = @deva[इत्याह]; @deva[बुधी] + @deva[उपास्यः] = @deva[बुध्युपास्यः] adored by the wise; @deva[मधु] + @deva[अरिः] = @deva[मध्वरिः] the enemy of @deva[मधु] i.e. Viṣṇu, @deva[पितृ] + @deva[अंशः] = @deva[पित्रंशः] a portion of the creator; @deva[ऌ] + @deva[आकृतिः] = @deva[लाकृतिः] a figure like that of @deva[ऌ] &c.

**Obs.** Several of the above words may have more than one form when combined; e.g. @deva[बुधी] + @deva[उपास्यः] = @deva[बुध्यु] + @deva[उपास्यः] by the general rule:—

**N.B.** The following rules and the two (a), (b) given under @ref[20], though they properly form the subject of the next section, are given here to avoid confusion. Ordinary students may pass over these except sec. (b) of the present rule.

**(a)** A consonant except @deva[ङ्], preceded by a vowel, is optionally doubled, if no vowel follows[^2]; @deva[बुध्यु] + @deva[उपास्यः] = @deva[बुद्ध्युपास्यः] by the general rule; then @deva[बुद्ध्यु] + @deva[उ] + @deva[पास्यः] = @deva[बुद्ध्युपास्यः] by this rule, the @deva[उ] being dropped; and also a third form @deva[बुद्धूपास्यः] (vide § 22, sec. d., below).

**(b)** When a consonant, except a nasal or a semivowel, is followed by a soft unaspirate or aspirate (3rd or 4th letter of a class) it is changed to the soft unaspirate (3rd letter) of its class[^3]; @deva[बुद्ध्यु] + @deva[उपास्यः] = @deva[बुद्ध्युपास्यः].

**(c)** Semivowels, when preceded by a letter of the first five classes except @deva[म्] are optionally doubled[^4]; thus @deva[बुद्ध्यु] + @deva[उपास्यः] = @deva[बुद्ध्यु] + @deva[उपास्यः] and @deva[बुद्ध्य्यु] + @deva[उपास्यः]; @deva[बुद्ध्युपास्यः] = @deva[बुद्ध्युपास्यः] and @deva[बुद्ध्य्युपास्यः]. Thus there are four forms ultimately, viz. @deva[बुध्युपास्यः], @deva[बुद्ध्युपास्यः], @deva[बुद्धूपास्यः] and @deva[बुद्ध्य्युपास्यः].

Similarly @deva[मधु] + @deva[अरिः] = @deva[मध्वरिः], @deva[मद्ध्वरिः], @deva[मद्धुवरिः], and @deva[मद्धुव्वरिः]. @deva[पित्] + @deva[अङ्कः] = @deva[पितङ्कः] and @deva[पित्तङ्कः]. In @deva[ल्] + @deva[आकृतिः] of course there is no possibility of any other form.

**(d)** A consonant except @deva[ङ्], coming after @deva[र्] or @deva[ल्] preceded by a vowel is optionally doubled[^5]; e.g. @deva[हरि] + @deva[अनुभवः] = @deva[हर्य्] + @deva[अनुभवः] = @deva[हर्यनुभवः] by the general rule; and optionally @deva[हर्य्य्] + @deva[अनुभवः] = @deva[हर्य्यनुभवः] (Hari's experience) by this rule; so @deva[न हि] + @deva[अस्ति] = @deva[न ह्यस्ति] and @deva[न ह्य्यस्ति].

---

[^1]: @deva[इको यणचि] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 77.

[^2]: @deva[अनचि च] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 47.

[^3]: @deva[झलां जश् झशि] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 53.

[^4]: @deva[यणो द्वे चे वाच्ये] — Vārt.

[^5]: @deva[अन्यो रहाम्यां द्वे] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 46.

rules.title: Optional Non-combination of Final इ/उ/ऋ/ऌ
rules.body:
**(a)** @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ] or @deva[ऌ], short or long, at the end of a word followed by a dissimilar vowel except in a compound, are optionally not combined, and when so they are shortened if long[^1] e.g. @deva[चक्रि] + @deva[अत्र] = @deva[चक्रित्र], Viṣṇu here, and @deva[चक्रि अत्र]; but @deva[वापी] + @deva[अम्बुः] = @deva[वाप्यम्बुः] a horse in a well. @deva[गौरी] + @deva[औ] (a term.) = @deva[गौर्यौ].

**(b)** @deva[अ], @deva[इ], @deva[उ] and @deva[ऋ], short or long, at the end of a word followed by a short @deva[ऋ] are also optionally not combined, and when not combined are shortened if long[^2]; e.g. @deva[ब्रह्म] + @deva[ऋषिः] = @deva[ब्रह्मर्षिः] A Brāhmaṇa saint, and @deva[ब्रह्म ऋषिः]; @deva[सप्तर्षीणाम्] of the seven sages, and @deva[सप्त ऋषिणाम्] (a comp. expression).

---

[^1]: @deva[इकोऽसवर्णे शाकल्यस्य ह्रस्वश्च]

[^2]: @deva[ऋत्यकः] — Pāṇ. VIII. 1. 127.

rules.title: Diphthong Transformation: ए/ओ/ऐ/औ → अय्/अव्/आय्/आव्

derivations.gloss: produced from a cow as milk, ghee &c

rules.body:
@deva[ए], @deva[ओ], @deva[ऐ] and @deva[औ], when followed by a vowel, are changed to @deva[अय्], @deva[अव्], @deva[आय्], and @deva[आव्] respectively[^1]; e.g. @deva[हरे] + @deva[ए] = @deva[हरय] for Hari; @deva[विष्णो] + @deva[ए] = @deva[विष्णव] for Viṣṇu; @deva[नै] + @deva[अकः] = @deva[नायकः] A leader; @deva[पौ] + @deva[अकः] = @deva[पावकः] the purifier i.e. fire.

**(a)** @deva[य] or @deva[व] at the end of a word and preceded by @deva[अ] or @deva[आ] is optionally dropped when followed by a vowel or a soft consonant[^2]; e.g. @deva[हरे] + @deva[एहि] = @deva[हरयेहि] or @deva[हर एहि]; @deva[विष्णो] + @deva[इह] = @deva[विष्णविह] or @deva[विष्णु इह]; @deva[श्रिये] + @deva[उत्कः] = @deva[श्रियायुत्कः] or @deva[श्रिया उत्कः] intent on getting money; @deva[गुरो] + @deva[उत्कः] = @deva[गुरावुत्कः] or @deva[गुरा उत्कः] longing to see the preceptor.

**Note:** Two vowels brought together by the disappearance of an intervening consonant or visarga do not coalesce.

**(b)** @deva[ओ] and @deva[औ], when followed by a termination beginning with @deva[य], become @deva[अव्] and @deva[आव्] respectively[^3]; e.g. @deva[गो] + @deva[य] = @deva[गव्यम्] produced from a cow as milk, ghee &c. @deva[नौ] + @deva[य] = @deva[नाव्यम्] accessible by a boat, navigable.

**N.B.** This rule holds good, in the case of roots, only when the @deva[ओ] or @deva[औ] is brought in by virtue of a termination;[^4] e.g. @deva[छो] + @deva[य] = @deva[छो] + @deva[य] = @deva[छव्यम्] fit to be lopped off. @deva[अवछिपत्] + @deva[य] = @deva[अवछिपौ] + @deva[य] = @deva[अवछिपाव्यम्] which ought necessarily to be cut off.

**(c)** The @deva[ओ] of the word @deva[गो] is also changed to @deva[अव्] when followed by the word @deva[यूति] (in the Veda and) in ordinary language when it means a particular measure of length[^5]; e.g. @deva[गव्यूतिः] four miles.

**(d)** The @deva[य] of the roots @deva[क्षि] and @deva[शी] is changed to @deva[अय्] when followed by the @deva[य] of the potential participle indicating capability[^6] e.g. @deva[क्षि] + @deva[य] = @deva[क्षै] + @deva[य] = @deva[क्षय्य] what can be reduced; so @deva[शय्य] what can be conquered; but @deva[क्षेयं], @deva[शेयं], @deva[योग्यं], @deva[हेयं] (what is fit to be removed but may not be so) @deva[वाच्यं], @deva[जेयं] (what ought to be curbed but which it may not be always possible to curb as) @deva[मनः].

---

[^1]: @deva[एचोऽयवायावः] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 78.

[^2]: @deva[लोपः शाकल्यस्य] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 19.

[^3]: @deva[वान्तो यि प्रत्यये] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 79.

[^4]: @deva[धातोरचिन्नित्यम्] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 80.

[^5]: @deva[गोयूतेच्च]

[^6]: @deva[क्षय्यादयः]

rules.title: Merger of अ into ए/ओ (Avagraha)
rules.body:
When @deva[ए] or @deva[ओ] at the end of a word is followed by @deva[अ] the latter merges into the former[^1] and the sign @deva[ऽ] is sometimes written in its place; e.g. @deva[हरे] + @deva[अव] = @deva[हरेऽव] protect, Oh Hari; @deva[विष्णो] + @deva[अव] = @deva[विष्णोऽव].

**(a)** If the word @deva[गो], ending in @deva[ओ], be followed by @deva[अ], the @deva[अ] is optionally retained, and if by a vowel, @deva[अव] is optionally substituted for @deva[ओ];[^2] @deva[गो] + @deva[अग्र] = @deva[गोग्र], @deva[गोऽग्र] and @deva[गवाग्र] a multitude of cows or chief among cows; but if it be followed by @deva[इन्द्र] and @deva[अक्ष] it necessarily changes its @deva[ओ] to @deva[अव]; @deva[गो] + @deva[इन्द्रः] = @deva[गवेन्द्रः] an excellent bull; @deva[गवाक्षः] a lattice-window, similarly.

---

[^1]: @deva[पूर्वरूपम्]

[^2]: @deva[गोः प्रथमायाः क्वचित्] Vārt.

rules.title: Pragṛhya: Exceptions to Sandhi
rules.body:
No sandhi is possible in the case of[^1]—

**I.** What are called the @deva[प्रगृह्य] (@[Pragṛhya]) exceptions; viz.—

**(a)** When a dual form (whether of a noun, pronoun or verb) ends in @deva[ई], @deva[ऊ], or @deva[ए];[^2] e.g. @deva[हरी एतौ]; @deva[विष्णू इमौ]; @deva[गुरवे अयं]; @deva[पश्यैते इमौ].

**(b)** When @deva[ई] or @deva[ऊ] follows the @deva[इ] of the pronoun @deva[अदस्][^3] e.g., @deva[अमी ईशाः] these lords; @deva[अमू आसाते] the two sit down.

**Obs.** The @deva[इ] of the Vedic forms @deva[अस्मे] and @deva[युष्मे] also does not blend with a following vowel (@deva[सेध] Pāṇ. I. 1. 13.); e.g. @deva[अस्मे इन्द्राबृहस्पती] &c. Ṛg. IV. 49. 4. Similarly a Vedic word having the sense of the loc. (but not ending in the termination of the loc.) remains unaffected by a following vowel; @deva[सोमो गौरी अविष्टितः] &c. Ṛg. X. 12. 3. where @deva[गौरी] stands for @deva[गौर्याम्] the loc. term, being dropped by @deva[पुङ्ग वुञ्च] Pāṇ. VII. 1. 30.

**(c)** Particles consisting of a single vowel, except @deva[आ] meaning 'a little, or a limit' exclusive or inclusive or used as a preposition, when followed by a vowel,[^4] e.g. @deva[इ इन्द्र] Oh Indra. @deva[उ उद्येध], @deva[आ पूर्वं न मन्यसे] ah, you think so; but @deva[आ] + @deva[उष्णम्] = @deva[औष्णम्] (a little warm) &c.

**(d)** When an indeclinable ends in @deva[ओ]; e.g. @deva[अहो ईशाः]; the final @deva[ओ] of a noun in the vocative case optionally combines when followed by @deva[इति]; e.g. @deva[विष्णो इति] = @deva[विष्णविति], and @deva[विष्णो इति]; also @deva[विष्ण इति] (see @ref[24] a.).

**N.B.** All these vowels which do not blend with others, and sometimes the words in which they occur are technically called @deva[प्रगृह्य].

**II.** Protracted and pluta vowels; e.g. @deva[पश्य छागा३ अत्र गोष्ठगताः] Come, Kṛṣṇa; here is the cow grazing.

A vowel becomes pluta under the following circumstances:[^5]

**(1)** The last vowel of a sentence uttered in reply to a salutation from a male person other than a Śūdra when the name or the family is actually mentioned, e.g. @deva[धो आयुष्मानेधि देवदत्त] live long, O Devadatta, which is said in reply to "@deva[अभिवादये देवदत्तोऽहम्]" I, Devadatta, bow to you; but the last @deva[अ] in "@deva[धो आयुष्मती भव भार्ये]" or in @deva[आयुष्मानेधि] is not pluta; for in the 1st we have the name of a female and in the 2nd no name at all.

But if the sentence end in the word @deva[भोः] or in the name of a Kṣatriya or Vaiśya the last vowel becomes optionally pluta e.g. @deva[आयुष्मान् एधि भोः] or @deva[भो३]; @deva[आयुष्मानेधि अर्धवर्धन] or @deva[र्ध३]; @deva[आयुष्मानेधि अर्धवर्षिष्ठ] or @deva[ष्ठ३].

**(2)** The final vowel of a sentence addressed from a distance to a person, and that of the particles @deva[है] and @deva[हे] used in such a sentence; e.g. @deva[आगच्छ देवदत्त३]; @deva[हे रामा३]; @deva[है३] @deva[हे३].

---

[^1]: @deva[छन्दसि प्रगृह्या अपि नित्यम्] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 125.

[^2]: @deva[ईदूदेद्द्विवचनं प्रगृह्यम्]

[^3]: @deva[अदसो मात्] — Pāṇ. I. 1. 11, 12.

[^4]: @deva[निर्धारणे एकाजनाह्वे। ओत्। संबुद्धौ शाकल्यस्येतावनार्षे] — Pāṇ. I. 1. 14-16.

[^5]: @deva[वाक्यस्य टेः प्लुत-उदात्तः। प्रत्यभिवादे अशूद्रे] — Pāṇ. VIII. 2. 82-83. @deva[द्वित्वं च। भोजनचर्यिका चेति वाच्यम्] — Vārtikas on the latter sūtra. @deva[दूराह्वये च। हैहेप्रयोगे हैहयोः] — Pāṇ. VIII. 2. 84-85.

rules.title: Optional Transformation of उ to व
rules.body:
The particle @deva[उ], preceded by a letter of the first five classes except @deva[अ] and followed by any vowel, is optionally changed to @deva[व][^1]; @deva[किंव उक्ते] @deva[किंतु उक्ते] and @deva[किंव उक्ते] (by @ref[26] c.).

**II. HALSANDHI, OR THE COALESCENCE OF FINAL CONSONANTS WITH VOWELS AND CONSONANTS.**

---

[^1]: @deva[भ उजो वा वा] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 33.

rules.title: Palatal and Lingual Assimilation
rules.body:
When @deva[स्] or a consonant of the dental class comes in contact with:—

**(a)** @deva[श] or a consonant of the palatal class, the corresponding letter of the latter class is substituted for the former, and @deva[श] for @deva[स्];[^1] @deva[हरिस्] + @deva[शेते] = @deva[हरिश्शेते] Hari sleeps; @deva[रामः] + @deva[चिनोति] = @deva[रामश्चिनोति] Rāma collects: @deva[सत्] + @deva[चित्] = @deva[सच्चित्] Reality and knowledge; @deva[शान्तिं] + @deva[जय] = @deva[शान्तिञ्जय] Be you victorious, Oh Kṛṣṇa.

**Exception:** (1) Dentals coming after @deva[श्] are not changed into the corresponding palatals: e.g. @deva[विश्र्यः] that which spreads lustre; @deva[श्राः].

**(b)** @deva[ट] or a consonant of the lingual class, @deva[ष] is substituted for @deva[स्] and the corresponding letter of the latter class for the former; @deva[रामस्] + @deva[षष्ठः] = @deva[रामष्षष्ठः] Rāma who is sixth. @deva[रामस्] + @deva[टीकते] = @deva[रामष्टीकते] Rāma goes; @deva[षट्] + @deva[टीका] = @deva[षट्टीका] A commentary on that; @deva[कृष्णस्] + @deva[टीकसे] = @deva[कृष्णष्टीकसे] Oh Kṛṣṇa, thou goest; @deva[पेष्] + @deva[ता] = @deva[पेष्टा] one who pounds.

**Exception:** (1) If a letter of the lingual class coming at the end of a word be followed by @deva[स्] or a letter of the dental class, the @deva[स्] as well as the dentals except the @deva[त्] of @deva[तात्], @deva[नवति] and @deva[मति] remain unaffected; @deva[षट्] + @deva[सन्तः] = @deva[षट्सन्तः] six good men; (see also @ref[39].); @deva[षट्] + @deva[ते] = @deva[षट्ते] these six; but @deva[षष्टुते] (since the @deva[ष] of @deva[षष्टु] is not at the end of a word) he praises. So @deva[षण्णवतिः] Ninety-six, @deva[षण्णगराः] six towns; but @deva[सर्पिस्] + @deva[तत्त्व] = @deva[सर्पिष्टत्त्व] abundance of ghee; as the exception excludes @deva[स्].

---

[^1]: @deva[स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः। च टि। ष्टुना ष्टुः] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 40. 44, 41.

rules.title: No Lingual Substitution Before क
rules.body: If a letter of the @deva[ट] group be followed by @deva[क्] it does not substitute its corresponding lingual; @deva[षट्] + @deva[कः] = @deva[षट्कः] sixth good man.

rules.title: Nasal Substitution for Final Consonants
rules.body:
If a consonant, except @deva[र्] or @deva[ह्], coming at the end of a word, be followed by a nasal, the nasal of its class is optionally substituted for it[^1]; @deva[एतत्] + @deva[मुरारिः] = @deva[एतन्मुरारिः] and @deva[एतत्मुरारिः] (see @ref[22] sec. b.) this Murāri; @deva[षट्] + @deva[मासाः] = @deva[षण्मासाः] and @deva[षट्मासाः] six months.

**N.B.** If the nasal belong to a termination the change is necessary; @deva[तन्मात्रम्] that alone; @deva[चिन्मात्रं] mere knowledge. @deva[वाक्] + @deva[मय] = @deva[वाङ्मय]. The word @deva[कङ्कूवक] (see Ragh. IV. 22.) is irregularly formed.

---

[^1]: @deva[अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः]

rules.title: Dental to Nasalized ल Before ल
rules.body:
A letter of the dental class, followed by @deva[ल्] is changed to @deva[ल्], the nasalised @deva[ल्] taking the place of @deva[न्][^1]; @deva[तत्] + @deva[लयः] = @deva[तल्लयः] the destruction of that; @deva[विद्वान्] + @deva[लिखति] = @deva[विद्वाँल्लिखति] a learned man writes.

---

[^1]: @deva[तोर्लि] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 60.

rules.title: Retroflexion of स in स्था/स्तम्भ after उद्
rules.body:
The @deva[स्] of @deva[स्था] and @deva[स्तम्भ] is changed into @deva[ष्] when after the preposition @deva[उद्];[^1] @deva[उद्] + @deva[स्थानम्] = @deva[उद्] + @deva[ष्थानम्] = @deva[उद्ष्थानम्] and @deva[उद्स्थानम्] (see @ref[20]. a), and then @deva[उद्ढ्ठानम्], @deva[उच्छ्ठानम्] rising up; similarly @deva[उद्] + @deva[स्तम्भम्] and @deva[उद्स्तम्भम्] upholding.

---

[^1]: @deva[उद्ः स्थास्तम्भोः पूर्वस्य] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 61.

rules.title: Optional Aspiration Before स
Final Consonant Devoicing and Softening
rules.body:
Any consonant, except a nasal or a semi-vowel, is changed to the first of its class, when followed by a hard consonant, and to the first or third when followed by nothing;[^1] @deva[वाक्], @deva[वाग्].

---

[^1]: @deva[खरि च। झलाञ् जशोऽन्ते] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 63, 65.

rules.title: Optional Change of श to छ
म to Anusvāra Conversion
rules.body:
@deva[म्] at the end of a word is changed into an Anusvāra when followed by a consonant;[^1] e.g. @deva[हरिम्] + @deva[वन्दे] = @deva[हरिं वन्दे] I salute Hari. But @deva[गम्] + @deva[य्] + @deva[ते] = @deva[गम्यते] as @deva[म्] is not at the end of a word. The word @deva[सञ्जिह्वः] is an exception (see Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 23).

**(a)** @deva[म्] and @deva[न्], not at the end of a pada, are turned into an Anusvāra when followed by a consonant except a nasal or a semivowel or @deva[ह्]; @deva[आक्रम्] + @deva[स्यते] = @deva[आक्रंस्यते] he will overcome; @deva[यशस्] + @deva[सि] = @deva[यशांसि] (nom. pl. of @deva[यशस्] fame); but @deva[मन्यते] he thinks, as @deva[म्] is followed here by @deva[य] which is a semi-vowel; @deva[ग्रामम्] + @deva[गच्छति] = @deva[ग्रामं गच्छति] as @deva[म्] is at the end of a pada (grammatical form).

**(b)** This change is optional in the case of @deva[म्] when @deva[ह] followed by @deva[य] comes after it; e.g. @deva[किम्] + @deva[ह्रयति] = @deva[किंह्रयति] and @deva[किम्ह्रयति] what does he shake?; but if this @deva[ह] be followed by @deva[न], and if by @deva[य], @deva[ञ], @deva[न्], the nasalised @deva[य्], @deva[ञ्], @deva[न्], are optionally substituted for @deva[म्] e.g. @deva[किम्] + @deva[ह्नुते] = @deva[किंह्नुते] or @deva[किञ्ह्नुते] what does he conceal? @deva[किम्] + @deva[ह्यः] = @deva[किंह्यः] and @deva[किञ्ह्यः] what! yesterday! so @deva[किंह्रयति], @deva[किञ्ह्रयति]; @deva[किंह्रादयति] and @deva[किञ्ह्रादयति]; but @deva[अहम्] + @deva[आगतः] = @deva[अहमागतः] I have come.

---

[^1]: @deva[मोऽनुस्वारः। नश्चापदान्तस्य झलि] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 23, 24 and Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 27, I. 3. 10. (see sec. b).

rules.title: Anusvāra to Class Nasal Conversion
rules.body:
An Anusvāra followed by any consonant except @deva[म्], @deva[य], @deva[र्] or @deva[ह्] is changed to the nasal of the class to which the following letter belongs, necessarily when in the middle, and optionally when at the end of a word[^1]; e.g. @deva[अङ्क्] + @deva[इतः] = @deva[अं] + @deva[क्] + @deva[इतः] (by the preceding rule and then) @deva[अङ्कितः] marked (by this); so @deva[अर्च्] + @deva[इतः] = @deva[अर्चितः] honoured; @deva[छण्डितः] obstructed; @deva[शान्तः] calmed; @deva[युक्तितः] woven; @deva[त्वम्] + @deva[करोषि] = @deva[त्वं करोषि] or @deva[त्वङ्करोषि] thou doest; similarly @deva[संयन्ता] or @deva[सय्यन्ता] a restrainer; @deva[संवत्सरः] or @deva[सव्वत्सरः] a year; @deva[यं लोकम्] or @deva[यल्लोकम्] to which people.

---

[^1]: @deva[अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः। वा पदान्तस्य] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 58.

rules.title: Optional क्/ट् Epenthesis and Aspiration
rules.body:
If @deva[ह्] and @deva[ण्] be followed by a sibilant, @deva[क्] and @deva[ट्] respectively are suffixed to them optionally; and hard unaspirates are optionally changed into hard aspirates when followed by a sibilant @deva[ष्];[^1] @deva[षष्] + @deva[ठः] = @deva[षष्ठः], @deva[षाड्ढः], @deva[षाड्ढुकः] the sixth man gone before; @deva[सुगण्] + @deva[ठः] = @deva[सुगण्ठः], @deva[सुगण्ढः], @deva[सुगण्ढुकः] the sixth good counter.

---

[^1]: @deva[अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः। वा पदान्तस्य] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 48-52.

rules.title: Optional ट Insertion and Consonant Doubling
rules.body:
If @deva[ट्] or @deva[स्] at the end of a word be followed by @deva[त्], @deva[ट्] (changed to @deva[ड्]) is optionally inserted between them;[^1] e.g. @deva[षष्] + @deva[सन्तः] = @deva[षट्सन्तः] or @deva[षट्] + @deva[ट्] + @deva[सन्तः] = @deva[षट्ट्सन्तः] six good men; so @deva[सत्] + @deva[सः] = @deva[सत्सः] or @deva[सत्त्सः] that good man.

**(a)** @deva[ट्], @deva[स्] and @deva[त्] at the end of a word and preceded by a short vowel double themselves when followed by a vowel[^2]; e.g. @deva[प्रत्यक्] + @deva[आत्मा] = @deva[प्रत्यग्गात्मा] the individual soul; so @deva[सुपरिष्ट्ट्] the best reckoner; @deva[सदच्युतः] good Achyuta.

---

[^1]: @deva[षट् सि]

[^2]: @deva[हशि च]

rules.title: Complex Sandhi with त and श
rules.body:
**Obs.** If the ending @deva[त्] of a word be followed by @deva[श], @deva[त्] is optionally inserted between them[^1] e.g. @deva[सत्] + @deva[शम्भुः] = @deva[सच्छम्भुः] and @deva[सत्त्शम्भुः] Śambhu existing for all times; and @deva[सच्छम्भुः] = @deva[सच्छम्भुः] and @deva[सत्त्छम्भुः] (by @ref[35]); then by @ref[28] (a) @deva[त्] being changed to @deva[ञ्] (and @deva[त्] to @deva[च्]) @deva[सञ्छम्भुः], @deva[सञ्च्छम्भुः] and @deva[सञ्त्छम्भुः] and finally by dropping @deva[त्] optionally (by @ref[20] a.) @deva[सञ्छम्भुः], @deva[सञ्च्छम्भुः] and @deva[सञ्छम्भुः].

---

[^1]: @deva[तोः शि]

rules.title: Retroflexion: ण to न after ऋ/ॠ/ऌ
rules.body:
If the final consonant of a word be @deva[ण] its preceding vowel @deva[ऋ], @deva[ॠ], @deva[ऌ] and following consonant be @deva[न], the latter @deva[न] is changed into @deva[ण] (being affected by the influence of its preceding letters)[^1]; e.g. @deva[सुतृण्] + @deva[नेता] = @deva[सुतृण्णेता] good judge of straw; @deva[सुतॄण्] + @deva[नयः] = @deva[सुतॄण्णयः] leading well over straw.

---

[^1]: @deva[पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः ण इति वक्तव्यम्] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 2.

rules.title: Retroflexion of स to ष (Ṣatva)
rules.body:
If @deva[स्] be the last letter of a word, and its vowel or consonant next to it, or consonant of the preceding syllable be a cerebral letter or @deva[ऋ], @deva[ॠ], @deva[ऌ], this @deva[स्] is changed to the cerebral @deva[ष्];[^1] e.g. @deva[अग्निष्] + @deva[टः] = @deva[अग्निष्ठः] the fire burnt; @deva[हविः] + @deva[भिः] = @deva[हविर्भिः] by oblations (changed to @deva[ष्] by this rule before being changed to @deva[र्] by @ref[32]); @deva[धनुः] + @deva[टङ्कारः] = @deva[धनुष्टङ्कारः] the twang of a bow; @deva[नृ] + @deva[सु] = @deva[नृष्षु] (loc. pl.) in men.

---

[^1]: @deva[षत्वं तुना सिद्ध्यति] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 59.

rules.title: Special Sandhi of सस्/पुंस्/कांस्
Insertion of च before छ
rules.body:
When the final consonant of a word is followed by the initial letter @deva[छ्], @deva[च्] is inserted;[^1] e.g. @deva[तत्] + @deva[छात्रः] = @deva[तच्छात्रः] that scholar.

---

[^1]: @deva[श्छोऽट्] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 63.

rules.title: Conversion of स/ष/र to Visarga
rules.body: Before an unvoiced guttural or labial consonant @deva[स्], @deva[ष्], and @deva[र्] at the end of a word are changed to Visarga (@deva[ः]); @deva[हरिः] + @deva[पचति] = @deva[हरिः पचति] Hari cooks; @deva[हविः] + @deva[क्रियते] = @deva[हविः क्रियते] an oblation is made.

rules.title: Complex Visarga Sandhi Rules
rules.body:
When @deva[अः] at the end of a word is followed by soft letter, it is changed to @deva[ओ];[^1] e.g. @deva[रामः] + @deva[गच्छति] = @deva[रामो गच्छति] Rāma goes.

**(a)** When @deva[अः] is followed by a soft guttural or labial it is optionally changed to @deva[ओ];[^2] e.g. @deva[देवः] + @deva[गच्छति] = @deva[देवो गच्छति] and @deva[देव गच्छति] the deity goes; @deva[रामः] + @deva[बलवान्] = @deva[रामो बलवान्] and @deva[राम बलवान्] Rāma is strong.

**(b)** Before a sibilant (i. e. @deva[श्], @deva[ष्], @deva[स्]), @deva[अः] at the end of a word is changed into the Visarga or the sibilant which follows it;[^3] @deva[रामः] + @deva[शेते] = @deva[रामः शेते] and @deva[रामश्शेते] Rāma sleeps; @deva[हरिः] + @deva[षष्ठः] = @deva[हरिः षष्ठः] and @deva[हरिष्षष्ठः] Hari the sixth; @deva[रामः] + @deva[सेवते] = @deva[रामः सेवते] and @deva[रामस्सेवते] Rāma worships. Formerly there was only this option of changing the Visarga into the sibilant which followed, or of letting it remain unchanged. But later grammarians have added a third change, viz., of changing the Visarga optionally into the very breath-sound itself; and this has now been generally current in most parts of India; e.g. @deva[रामः शेते], @deva[रामश्शेते] and @deva[राम शेते] Rāma sleeps; so @deva[हरिः षष्ठः], @deva[हरिष्षष्ठः] and @deva[हरि षष्ठः], @deva[रामः सेवते], @deva[रामस्सेवते] and @deva[राम सेवते].

**(c)** When @deva[इ] or @deva[उ], except @deva[अ], precedes Visarga, it is changed to @deva[ष्] before @deva[क्] or @deva[प्];[^4] e.g. @deva[हरिः] + @deva[करोति] = @deva[हरिष्करोति] Hari makes; @deva[साधुः] + @deva[पचति] = @deva[साधुष्पचति] a good man cooks; but @deva[रामः] + @deva[करोति] = @deva[रामः करोति] Rāma makes, as @deva[अ] precedes the Visarga.

**(d)** When the preceding vowel is @deva[अ], it is optionally changed to @deva[स्] in place of Visarga;[^5] @deva[रामः] + @deva[करोति] = @deva[रामः करोति] and @deva[रामस्करोति]; but when the preceding vowel is @deva[आ], no such change takes place; @deva[रामाः] + @deva[पतन्ति] = @deva[रामाः पतन्ति] Rāmas fall.

**(e)** When the Visarga at the end of a word is preceded by @deva[अ] or @deva[आ], and followed by any other vowel except @deva[अ], it is changed to @deva[र्] by the best authors; other writers substitute, however, it by @deva[य्], @deva[व्] or @deva[ल्] or leave the Visarga altogether, though irregularly;[^6] e.g. @deva[देवाः] + @deva[उत्तिष्ठन्ति] = @deva[देवा उत्तिष्ठन्ति] or @deva[देवा रुत्तिष्ठन्ति] the gods rise; @deva[रामः] + @deva[इच्छति] = @deva[रामा इच्छति] or @deva[राम इच्छति] or @deva[रामय्इच्छति] or @deva[रामरिच्छति] or @deva[रामलिच्छति] or @deva[रामविच्छति]; but @deva[रामा रिच्छति] is the best. (See Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 15 and Siddh. Kaum. on Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 19).

**(f)** When such a Visarga is followed by @deva[अ], it may be entirely dropped;[^7] e.g. @deva[रामः] + @deva[अस्ति] = @deva[रामोऽस्ति] (by applying preceding sub-rule c) or @deva[रामाऽस्ति] or @deva[राम अस्ति] by this (f), Rāma is.

**(g)** Before @deva[र्], the Visarga is dropped;[^8] @deva[रामः] + @deva[रजते] = @deva[रामो राजते] or @deva[राम राजते] Rāma shines.

---

[^1]: @deva[अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते। हशि च] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 34-36.

[^2]: @deva[वाऽवसाने] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 37.

[^3]: @deva[शरः शर्] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 41.

[^4]: @deva[विसर्जनीयस्य सः। वा शरि] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 34, 36.

[^5]: @deva[रः खयोर्वा] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 15.

[^6]: @deva[हशि च। रोरि। वा शरि] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 47, 15, 36.

[^7]: @deva[ससजुषो रुः। विसर्जनीयस्य सः] — Pāṇ. VIII. 2. 66 and Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 15.

[^8]: @deva[रो रि] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 50.

rules.title: Visarga to ओ Conversion
rules.body:
Final @deva[अः] may be changed to @deva[ओ] before @deva[उ];[^1] @deva[पुनः] + @deva[उक्तम्] = @deva[पुनरुक्तम्] and @deva[पुनोऽक्तम्] said again (by change of @deva[रः] into @deva[ओ]); @deva[मनः] + @deva[उत्तमम्] = @deva[मनरुत्तमम्] and @deva[मनोऽत्तमम्] the best mind.

---

[^1]: @deva[रो रि॥ ८.३.१४॥] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 50.

rules.title: Visarga Dropping after आ
rules.body:
Visarga after @deva[आ] may be dropped before a soft consonant;[^1] e.g. @deva[पुराः] + @deva[भव] = @deva[पुराः भव] and @deva[पुरा भव] go in advance; @deva[धनुराः] + @deva[धरः] = @deva[धनुराः धरः] and @deva[धनुरा धरः] bow-bearer.

---

[^1]: @deva[अतोऽनुप्रयोगे॥ ८.४.५६॥] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 56.

rules.title: Visarga to र् Conversion with Exceptions
rules.body:
@deva[अः] at the end of a word is changed to @deva[र्] before @deva[र्];[^1] e.g. @deva[पुनः] + @deva[रमते] = @deva[पुनर्रमते] he again rejoices.

**Exception.** This change of Visarga into @deva[र्] is not admissible in the following cases, as they are prohibited in the Vedas, viz.:—

**(a)** When there are two or more words besides the one to which the succeeding @deva[र्] is attached; e.g. @deva[पूर्णः पूर्णं राज्यशतम्] not @deva[पूर्णः पूर्णर्राज्यशतम्]. The rule applies when there are only one or two words, as @deva[पूर्णं राज्यशतम्] or @deva[पूर्णर्राज्यशतम्].

**(b)** When the word is already a compound; @deva[राजपुत्रः] + @deva[रमते] = @deva[राजपुत्रः रमते], not @deva[राजपुत्रर्रमते] the prince rejoices.

**(c)** When the compound is a Bahuvrīhi or Dvandva or consists of an indeclinable and a verb; as @deva[पीतोदकः] + @deva[रमते] = @deva[पीतोदकः रमते], not @deva[पीतोदकर्रमते] one who has drunk water rejoices. So @deva[रामकृष्णौ रमेते] not @deva[रामकृष्णौ र्रमेते] Rāma and Kṛṣṇa rejoice; @deva[अनु राजते] not @deva[अनुर्राजते] he shines after.

**(d)** In Tatpuruṣa compound, it is optional; @deva[राजपुत्रः] + @deva[रमते] = @deva[राजपुत्रः रमते] or @deva[राजपुत्रर्रमते] the prince rejoices.

---

[^1]: @deva[रो रि] Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 15.

rules.title: Dropping स् in Demonstrative Pronouns
rules.body:
The @deva[स्] of the Nominative Singular masculine of the pronouns @deva[एषः], @deva[सः], and the like is dropped if the preceding word ends in any vowel except @deva[अ] or @deva[आ];[^1] e.g. @deva[हरिः] + @deva[एषः] = @deva[हरि एषः] this is Hari; @deva[विष्णुः] + @deva[सः] = @deva[विष्णु सः] that is Viṣṇu; @deva[अनयोः] + @deva[एषः] = @deva[अनयो एषः] this is of the two; but @deva[हरिर्एषः], @deva[विष्णुर्एषः] are equally correct; but @deva[कृष्णः] + @deva[एषः] = @deva[कृष्णोऽयम्] or @deva[कृष्ण एषः] or @deva[कृष्णरेषः] this is Kṛṣṇa. Here @deva[स्] is dropped on the authority of this aphorism, and if it be not dropped, then it is either changed into @deva[र्] or else it may remain, and @deva[अः] be dropped (Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 19, VIII. 3. 15, VI. 1. 133).

**Note.** Thus ends the chapter on Sandhi, a thorough knowledge of which is necessary before one can begin the study of the language.

---

[^1]: @deva[एषः सोऽयमिति च निर्दिश्यमानस्य] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 19.

rules.title: Introduction to Declension
rules.body: In the present chapter Declension or the inflection of nouns, substantive and adjective, is considered.

rules.title: Definition of Prātipadika (Crude Form)
rules.body: The crude form of a noun (any declinable word) not yet inflected is technically called a Prātipadika (@deva[प्रातिपदिक]).

rules.title: Three Genders of Nouns
rules.body: A noun has three genders: masculine gender (mas.), a feminine gender (fem.), and the neuter (neu.). The question about the determination of the gender of nouns will be considered in a separate chapter.

rules.title: Three Numbers: Singular, Dual, Plural
rules.body:
There are three numbers:—Singular (sing.), dual (du.) and plural (pl.). The singular number denotes one, the dual two and the plural three or more.[^1]

---

[^1]: @deva[एकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने । बहुषु बहुवचनम्] — Pāṇ. I. 4. 22. 21.

rules.title: Eight Cases in Sanskrit
rules.body:
There are eight cases in each number:—Nominative (Nom. or N.), Vocative (Voc. or V.), Accusative (Acc. or A.) Instrumental (Ins. or I.), Dative (Dat. or D.), Ablative (Abl. or Ab.), Genitive (Gen. or G.), and Locative (Loc or L.). These express nearly all relations between words in a sentence.

**N. B.** These genders, numbers and cases will, for the sake of convenience, be denoted by their abbreviations enclosed into brackets after each.

rules.title: Sup: Technical Term for Case Terminations
rules.body:
Sup (@deva[सुप्]) is the technical term for a case termination in Sanskrit. Declension consists in adding the case termination to the crude form or base.[^1]

---

[^1]: The general terminations as given by Pāṇini are—@deva[सुजोसमौ-च्छष्टाभ्यामिभिस्ङेभ्याम्भ्यस्ङसिभ्याम्भ्यस्ङसोसाम्ङ्योस्सुप्] — Pāṇ. IV. 1. 2. i. e. Nom. @deva[सु औ जस्]; Acc. @deva[अम् औट् शस्]; Ins. @deva[टा भ्याम् भिस्]; Dat. @deva[ङे भ्याम् भ्यस्]; Ab @deva[इसि भ्याम् भ्यस्]; Gen. @deva[ङस् ओस् आम्]; Loc. @deva[ङि ओस् सुप्]. Some of these terminations, as in common with Pāṇini's system of nomenclature, have certain Its (servile letters) added or prefixed to them; e.g. @deva[ट] in @deva[सु], @deva[टु] in @deva[जस्] &c. It will be easily seen that the term @deva[सुप्] is obtained by taking the first letter and the last It in the sūtra.

rules.body:
The following are the normal case-terminations:—

rules.title: Vocative Case Explained
rules.body: The Vocative is considered to be a different aspect of the nom. and is identical with it in the dual and plural, It is, therefore, supposed to have no separate terminations of its own. In the sing. it sometimes coincides with the original stem, sometimes with the nom., at others, it differs from both.

rules.title: Two Classes of Declension
rules.body:
Declension is for the sake of convenience divided into two classes:—

I. BASES ENDING IN VOWELS.

II. BASES ENDING IN CONSONANTS.

rules.title: Declension of Adjectives and Vowel Bases
rules.body:
The declension of adjectives does not, in general, differ from that of substantives. It will not, therefore, be given here separately; the points of difference only will be noted.

## SECTION I.

## 1. BASES ENDING IN VOWELS.

**Note:**—The variations and modifications, which the general terminations given above undergo when applied to several of the vowel bases are so numerous, that it has been thought advisable not to notice them here, as being tedious, but simply to give the forms and leave the students to find them out for themselves. Every word declined here should be considered a model and words alike in form should be declined similarly to it.

## Nouns ending in @deva[अ] Mas. and Neu.

rules.title: Declension of अ-Stems: राम and ज्ञान Paradigms
rules.body:
| | @deva[राम] m. Rāma | | | @deva[ज्ञान] n. knowledge | | |

| V. | @deva[राम] | ,, | ,, | V. @deva[ज्ञान] | ,, | ,, |

| L. | @deva[रामे] | @deva[रामयोः] | @deva[रामेषु] | | | |

---

[^1]: The @deva[न] of @deva[इन] is changed to @deva[ण] by @ref[41]. Ins. sing. of @deva[जन] is @deva[जनेन].

rules.title: General Rule for अ-Stems with Special Note on अह्
rules.body:
Decline all nouns ending in @deva[अ] mas. and neu. similarly.

**(a)** The Loc. sing. of words ending in @deva[अह्] (substituted for @deva[अहन्] a day, at the end of a Tat. comp.) is optionally formed like that of nouns ending in @deva[न्]; e. g. @deva[स्वह्] has @deva[स्वहे], @deva[स्वहि] or @deva[स्वहनि]. So @deva[त्यहे], @deva[त्यहि] or @deva[त्यहनि] &c. See p. 73.

rules.title: Declension of आ-Stems Masculine: गोपा Paradigm
rules.body:
@deva[गोपा] mas. a cow-herd.

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|

| A. | @deva[गोपाम्] | ,, | @deva[गोपः] |

rules.title: आ-Stem Compounds from Roots vs. Non-Root Compounds
rules.body:
Decline similarly @deva[विश्वपा] the protector of the world, @deva[शङ्खध्मा] a conch-shell-blower, @deva[सोमपा] one who quaffs the soma-juice, @deva[धूमपा] one who inhales smoke, @deva[बलदा] strength-giver or Indra, and other comp. nouns derived from roots ending in @deva[आ].

rules.body:
**Obs.** **(a)** @deva[औडुलोमि] a descendant of Uduloman (@deva[उदुलोमः अपत्यं पुमान्]) is declined like @deva[हरि] in the sing. and dual and like @deva[ब्राह्म] in the plural, the original word @deva[उदुलोम] being substituted;[^1]

N. @deva[औडुलोमिः औडुलोमी], @deva[उदुलोमाः] &c.

**(b)** Words of similar derivation (see Pāṇ.- II. 4. 62. 63. 65. 66 and IV. 1. 105) also substitute their originals in the plural, e.g. @deva[गार्ग्यस्य अपत्यं गार्ग्यः] N. @deva[गार्ग्यः गार्ग्यौ गार्गाः] &c.

---

rules.title: Root Nouns in ई and ऊ: Multiple Paradigms
rules.body:
Root nouns in @deva[ई] or @deva[ऊ] M. F. N.

Rule of Sandhi:—**(a)** The ending @deva[इ] or @deva[उ], short or long, of nouns derived from roots with the affix @deva[क्विप्] (0) and of @deva[ङी], is changed to @deva[इय्] or @deva[उव्] before the vowel terminations[^1]; the fem. nouns of this description are optionally declined like @deva[नदी] in the Da. Ab. Gen. and Loc. singulars and the Gen. plu.

**(b)** But if the ending @deva[इ] or @deva[उ] of a many-voweled noun having a root at the end be not preceded by a radical conjunct consonant or the root noun has a preposition termed @deva[गति] (e. g. as added to the root) or a word governed by the root preceding it, it is changed to @deva[य्] or @deva[व्], except in the case of @deva[स्त्री] and nouns ending in @deva[क्षी].[^2]

rules.body:
Words derived from roots with the affix @deva[तृ] (@deva[तवृ] and @deva[तृन्] [?.f.f. 1. 133. and 2. 135]), such as @deva[कर्तृ] a maker, &c. and the words @deva[स्वसृ] f, @deva[नप्तृ], @deva[नेष्टृ], @deva[क्षत्तृ], @deva[होतृ], @deva[पोतृ], and @deva[प्रशास्तृ] as also @deva[उद्गातृ] change their @deva[तृ] to @deva[आर्] in the Nom. sing. and to @deva[आर्] in the first five inflections. The @deva[तृ] is lengthened in the Acc. and Gen. pl. and changed to @deva[उर्] before the Ab. and Gen. sing; the Voc. sing. ends in @deva[अर्].

[^1]: @deva[अनुदात्तस्य चदुपधस्यान्यतरस्याम्] — Pāṇ. VI. 4. 11. @deva[उद्गातृशास्त्रस्य भवेत्येव सपूर्वस्य 'उद्गातारः' इति भाष्यप्रयोगात्] — Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Kinship Terms in तृ: पितृ and मातृ
rules.body:
Nouns expressive of relationship like @deva[पितृ] m. a father, @deva[मातृ] f. a mother, @deva[देवृ] m. a husband's brother, &c. with the exception of @deva[नप्तृ] a grandson, @deva[भर्तृ] a husband and @deva[स्वसृ] a sister, as also the words @deva[स्तोतृ] one who praises (Un. II, 92), @deva[नृ] a man (Un.II. 98) and @deva[सप्तेतृ] a charioteer, do not change their @deva[ऋ] to @deva[आर्] in the N. dual and plural and Acc. sing. and dual; e. g.

| | @deva[पितृ] | | | | @deva[मातृ] | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| N. | @deva[पिता] | @deva[पितरौ] | @deva[पितरः] | N. | @deva[माता] | @deva[मातरौ] | @deva[मातरः] |
| V. | @deva[पितः](@deva[र्]) | ,, | ,, | V. | @deva[मातः](@deva[र्]) | ,, | ,, |
| A. | @deva[पितरम्] | ,, | @deva[पितॄन्] | A. | @deva[मातरम्] | ,, | @deva[मातॄः] |

The rest like @deva[धातृ]. The rest like @deva[स्वसृ].

Decline similarly @deva[भ्रातृ]. Decline similarly @deva[यातृ] a hus-
@deva[जामातृ], @deva[देवृ], @deva[स्तोतृ], @deva[सप्तेतृ] and... band's brother's wife, @deva[दुहितृ] a
@deva[नृ]. The Gen. plu. of @deva[नृ] is daughter, and @deva[ननान्दृ] or @deva[ननन्दृ]
@deva[नृणाम्] or @deva[नूणाम्][^1] a husband's sister.

---

[^1]: @deva[नृ न] — Pān. VI. 4. 9. @deva[नृ इत्येतस्य नृणाम् वा नॄणाम् स्यात्] — Sid. Kau.

rules.title: क्रोष्टृ (Jackal): Optional Declension
rules.body:
The word @deva[क्रोष्टृ] a jackal, is declined like a word ending in @deva[ऋ] necessary in the first five inflections and optionally before the vowel terminations beginning with the Inst. sing. except that of the Gen. plu.[^1] e. g.

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| N. | @deva[क्रोष्टा] | @deva[क्रोष्टारौ] | @deva[क्रोष्टारः] |
| V. | @deva[क्रोष्टः] | ,, | ,, |
| A. | @deva[क्रोष्टारम्] | ,, | @deva[क्रोष्टॄन्] |
| I. | @deva[क्रोष्ट्रा-त्रुणा] | @deva[क्रोष्टृभ्याम्] | @deva[क्रोष्टृभिः] |
| D. | @deva[क्रोष्टे-त्रे] | ,, | @deva[क्रोष्टृभ्यः] |
| Ab. | @deva[क्रोष्टुः-क्रोष्टोः] | ,, | ,, |
| G. | ,, | @deva[क्रोष्टोः-त्रोः] | @deva[क्रोष्टृणाम्] |
| L. | @deva[क्रोष्टरि-त्रौ] | ,, | @deva[क्रोष्टृषु] |

**(a)** @deva[क्रोष्टृ] becomes @deva[क्रोष्ट्रृ] in the fem. also (by @deva[स्त्रियाम् च] Pāṇ. VIII. 1. 96.) which with the fem. term. @deva[ई] becomes @deva[क्रोष्ट्री] and is declined like @deva[नदी].

**Obs.**—The word @deva[प्रियक्रोष्टृ] neu. is declined like @deva[मधु] and optionally like @deva[क्रोष्टृ] mas. before the vowel terminations from the I. sing.; e. g. D. sing. @deva[प्रियक्रोष्टुणे-त्रे-त्रुणे].

---

[^1]: @deva[तृन्नकोः विभाषा तृतीयादिष्वजि] — Pāṇ. VII, I. 95, 97. @deva[क्रोष्टृ च नन्दे] — Un. II 97 '@deva[न नन्दुते ननान्दा । इह ज्ञातिनिवृत्ते इत्येके । 'नन् त्रा तु स्वस्रा पत्युरनन्दा नन्दिनी च सा]' @deva[इति शब्दार्णवः] — Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Imitative कृ and खृ Stems
rules.body:
There are no words ending in @deva[कृ] or @deva[खृ]; therefore, the imitative sounds of the roots @deva[कृ] and @deva[खृ] and @deva[शक्कृ] and @deva[डक्खृ] are taken to show what the forms of such words will be, if there be need to use such words.

@deva[कृ] m.

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| N. V. | @deva[किरः], @deva[कृः] | @deva[किरौ], @deva[कौ] | @deva[किरः], @deva[कृः] |
| A. | @deva[किरम्], @deva[कृम्] | ,, | @deva[किरः], @deva[कृन्] |
| I. | @deva[किरा], @deva[कृा] | @deva[कीर्भ्याम्], @deva[कृभ्याम्] | @deva[कीर्भिः], @deva[कृभिः] |
| D. | @deva[किरे], @deva[कृे] | ,, | @deva[कीर्भ्यः], @deva[कृभ्यः] |
| Ab. | @deva[किरः], @deva[कृः] | ,, | ,, |
| G. | ,, | @deva[किरोः], @deva[कोः] | @deva[किराम्], @deva[कृाम्] |
| L. | @deva[किरि], @deva[कृि] | ,, | @deva[कीर्षु], @deva[कृषु] |

Decline @deva[खृ] similarly.

@deva[शक्कृ] m.

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| N. | @deva[शक्कृ] | @deva[शक्कृवौ] | @deva[शक्कृवः] |
| V. | @deva[शक्कृः] | ,, | ,, |
| A. | @deva[शक्कृवम्] | ,, | @deva[शक्कृवन्] |
| I. | @deva[शक्कृवा] | @deva[शक्कृभ्याम्] | @deva[शक्कृभिः] |
| D. | @deva[शक्कृवे] | ,, | @deva[शक्कृभ्यः] |
| Ab. | @deva[शक्कृवात्] | ,, | ,, |
| G. | ,, | @deva[शक्कृवोः] | @deva[शक्कृवाणाम्] |
| L. | @deva[शक्कृवि] | ,, | @deva[शक्कृषु] |

rules.title: Diphthong Stems ए and ऐ: से and रै
rules.body:
Here simply the terminations should be added and Sandhi rules observed.

@deva[से] (@deva[सेह् इना कामेन वर्त्तेऽस्सौ])

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| N. | @deva[सेः] | @deva[सयौ] | @deva[सयः] |
| V. | @deva[से][^1] | ,, | ,, |
| A. | @deva[सयम्] | ,, | ,, |
| I. | @deva[सया] | @deva[सेभ्याम्] | @deva[सेभिः] |
| D. | @deva[सये] | ,, | @deva[सेभ्यः] |
| Ab. | @deva[सेः] | ,, | ,, |
| G. | ,, | @deva[सयोः] | @deva[सयाम्] |
| L. | @deva[सयि] | ,, | @deva[सेषु] |

Decline similarly @deva[स्थते] (@deva[स्थतः तत्]) one who has thought of Kāma.

@deva[रै] m. f. wealth.

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| N. V. | @deva[राः] | @deva[रायौ] | @deva[रायः] |
| A. | @deva[रायम्] | ,, | ,, |
| I. | @deva[राया] | @deva[राभ्याम्] | @deva[राभिः] |
| D. | @deva[राये] | ,, | @deva[राभ्यः] |
| Ab. | @deva[रायः] | ,, | ,, |
| G. | ,, | @deva[रायोः] | @deva[रायाम्] |
| L. | @deva[रायि] | ,, | @deva[रासु] |

The neu. @deva[प्रवरे] (@deva[प्रकृष्टा वै यस्य]) changed to @deva[प्ररि] (by @deva[पररिरयप्रसङ्देश] Pāṇ. I. 1. 48. and I. 2. 47.) should be declined like @deva[वारि] except before the consonantal terminations, when it should be declined like @deva[रै] m. f.

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| N. A. | @deva[प्ररि] | @deva[प्ररिणी] | @deva[प्ररीणि] |
| I. | @deva[प्ररिणा] | @deva[प्रराभ्याम्] | @deva[प्रराभिः] &c. |

---

[^1]: The Kau. does not specially mention this form. Just as it stops after giving the Nom. forms in the case of words like @deva[रै], @deva[गौ], @deva[स्त्रियौ] &c., so does it do in the case of @deva[से] also, implying thereby that the Voc. forms of @deva[से] are also like the Nom. ones. But the Sutra @deva[एङ् ह्रस्वात्सम्बुद्धेः] Pāṇ. VI. 1. 69 (@deva[एङन्तात् ह्रस्वान्तात् अङ्गात् हल् उच्यते सम्बुद्धेः चेत्]) (Kau.) seems to apply in the present case and by dropping the final @deva[म्] we get the form @deva[से].

rules.title: Diphthong Stems ओ and औ: गौ and रक्षौ
rules.body:
Vṛddhi (@deva[औ]) is substituted for the @deva[ओ] of words ending in @deva[ओ] in the first five inflections except the Acc. sing.; @deva[आ] is substituted for @deva[ओ] in the Acc. sing. and plural.[^1] Nouns ending in @deva[औ] are regularly declined.

Decline similarly @deva[स्थतो] (@deva[स्थतः उः शङ्करः येन]) and @deva[खो] f. the sky. The neu. @deva[प्रयो] (@deva[प्रष्ठत यो: यस्मिन् तत्]) changed to @deva[प्रयु] should be declined like @deva[मधु].

rules.title: Introduction to Consonant-Ending Bases
rules.body:
## SECTION II.

## BASES ENDING IN CONSONANTS.

Bases ending in any of the first four letters of a class, and in @deva[ण्], @deva[र्], @deva[श्], @deva[ष्], @deva[स्], @deva[ह्] and @deva[ह्]. The declension of these bases consists, for the most part, in adding the general case terminations and observing the rules of sandhi.

rules.title: Bases Ending in र्, न्, and स्
rules.body: Bases ending @deva[र्], @deva[न्], and @deva[स्].

rules.title: न्-Ending Bases: कमल् Paradigm
rules.body:
**(a)** After final @deva[न्] the @deva[सु] of the loc. is changed to @deva[षु].

**(b)** @deva[र्] (optionally changeable to @deva[र्]) may be optionally inserted between @deva[न्] and @deva[सु].

@deva[कमल्] m. f. neu. naming the goddess of wealth or a lotus (@deva[कमले कमलौ वा आवसताम्:—वा—पौ—वा])—

Mas. and Fem.

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| N. V. | @deva[कमल्][^1] | @deva[कमलौ] | @deva[कमलः] |
| A. | @deva[कमलम्] | ,, | ,, |
| I. | @deva[कमला] | @deva[कमलभ्याम्] | @deva[कमलभिः] |
| D. | @deva[कमले] | ,, | @deva[कमलेभ्यः] |
| Ab. | @deva[कमलः] | ,, | ,, |
| G. | ,, | @deva[कमलोः] | @deva[कमलाम्] |
| L. | @deva[कमलि] | ,, | @deva[कमलषु] |

Decline similarly @deva[सुगण्], @deva[सुगणन्], m. f. one who counts well, @deva[द्वार्] f. a door and other words ending in @deva[र्] or @deva[न्]. The loc. plu. of @deva[सुगण्] is @deva[सुगण्षु-पटसु,-पट्षु]. The Nom. sing. of @deva[द्वार्] is @deva[द्वाः].

Neu.

|---|---|---|---|
| N. A. | @deva[कमल्] | @deva[कमली] | @deva[कमलि] |

The rest like the mas.

rules.title: Bases Ending in क्, ख्, ग्, ट्, ठ्, ड्, ङ्, छ्, त्, थ्, द्, ध्, प्, फ्, ब्, भ्
rules.body: Bases ending in @deva[क्], @deva[ख्], @deva[ग्], @deva[ट्], @deva[ठ्], @deva[ड्], @deva[ङ्], @deva[छ्], @deva[त्], @deva[थ्], @deva[द्], @deva[ध्], and @deva[प्], @deva[फ्], @deva[ब्], @deva[भ्].

rules.title: General Rules for Consonant-Ending Bases
rules.body:
**(a)** As a general rule the @deva[स्] of the nom. singular is dropped. If there be a conjunct consonant at the end of a word the first consonant only is retained.

**(b)** The final letter is changed to the first or third of its class when followed by nothing, to the third when followed by a soft consonant and first when followed by a hard consonant and remains unchanged before a vowel termination.

**(c)** @deva[न्] is prefixed to the @deva[इ] of the N. & Acc. plural in the case of neuter nouns ending in a consonant except a nasal or a semi-vowel; but not in the case of a noun derived from the frequentative base.

rules.title: Bases Ending in च्, छ्, ज्, झ्, ट्, ड्, ढ्
rules.body: Bases ending in @deva[च्], @deva[छ्], @deva[ज्], or @deva[झ्] and @deva[ट्], @deva[ड्], @deva[ढ्].

rules.title: Palatal and Retroflex Consonant Changes
rules.body:
**(a)** @deva[च्] or @deva[ज्] is changed to @deva[क्] when followed by a hard consonant or by nothing, and to @deva[ग्] when followed by a soft consonant.[^1]

**(b)** The ending @deva[ष्] or @deva[छ्] of root-nouns and the final of @deva[त्रष्], @deva[भष्], @deva[वृष्], @deva[षष्], @deva[पज्], @deva[राज्], and @deva[झाष्] are changed to @deva[ट्] when followed by any consonant except a nasal or a semi-vowel or by nothing[^2]; the @deva[ट्] is changed to @deva[ड्] or @deva[ड्] when at the end of a word, and to @deva[ड] when followed by a soft consonant. The @deva[ष्] of @deva[परिव्राज्] is similarly changed to @deva[ड्] or @deva[ड्].

**(c)** But the @deva[ज्] of the root-nouns @deva[दिज्], @deva[दज्], @deva[स्थुज्] and @deva[सज्] is changed to @deva[क्] as also the @deva[ट्] of @deva[धृष्टुट्] 'a bold or impudent man' and the @deva[ष्] of such words as @deva[विष्टुष्] &c. The @deva[ज्] of @deva[नज्] is optionally changed to @deva[ट्] or @deva[क्], as also the @deva[ष्] of @deva[तष्] and @deva[गौरष्]. The @deva[ज्] of @deva[कृत्विज्] is changed to @deva[क्].

**(d)** @deva[न] may optionally be inserted between @deva[च्] and the loc. pl. term. @deva[इ].

**(e)** Before vowel terminations final @deva[इ] may optionally be changed to @deva[य्].

---

[^1]: @deva[जोः कः] — Pāṇ. VIII. 2. 30.

[^2]: @deva[त्रषभसवृषषष्पजराजझाषगोत्राणाम्] — Pāṇ. VIII, 2. 36.

rules.title: Special Rules for च् Changes
rules.body:
**(a)** @deva[च्] is changed to @deva[क्] when at the end of a pada or when followed by a consonant except a nasal or a semi-vowel.

**(b)** In the case of roots beginning with @deva[च्] it is changed to @deva[य्] under the same circumstances;

**(c)** when forming part of the roots @deva[चृ], @deva[धृ], @deva[दृज्] and @deva[सिच्], it is optionally changed to @deva[य्] i. e. to @deva[क्] or @deva[य्];

**(d)** and in the case of the root @deva[वह्] it is changed to @deva[य्] under the above-mentioned circumstances.[^1]

**(e)** The @deva[च्] of @deva[उष्णिच्ह्] f. a kind of metre is changed to @deva[क्] when followed by a hard consonant or by nothing, and to @deva[ग्] before a soft consonant (Pāṇ. III. 2, 59).

---

[^1]: @deva[च्] is changed to @deva[क्] when at the end of a pada or when followed by a consonant except a nasal or a semi-vowel.

rules.title: Monosyllabic Roots with Initial व्, य्, or च्
rules.body:
When a mono-syllabic root (or root-noun) begins with @deva[व्], @deva[य्] or @deva[च्] and ends with @deva[च्], @deva[छ्], @deva[थ्], @deva[भ्] or @deva[ह्], the @deva[च्], @deva[य्] or @deva[च्] is respectively changed to @deva[अ], @deva[व्] or @deva[य्] before @deva[च्] or @deva[च्ह्] or when followed by nothing or when the final soft aspirate is changed to an unaspirate letter[^1].

---

[^1]: @deva[एकाचो वशो भध् धसन्तस्य स्तोः] — Pāṇ. VIII. 2. 37.

rules.title: Directional Nouns from अञ्च् 'to go'
rules.body:
Nouns derived form the root @deva[अञ्च्] 'to go' by means of such affixes as @deva[क्रिन्], @deva[क्रिप्] &c. such as @deva[प्राञ्च्] (@deva[प्रा-अञ्च्]) eastern, @deva[प्रत्यञ्च्] (@deva[प्रति-अञ्च्]) western, @deva[सम्यङ्] (@deva[सह्-अञ्च्]) a companion, @deva[तिर्यञ्च्] (@deva[तिरस्-अञ्च्]) going away, @deva[सम्यञ्च्] (@deva[सम्-अञ्च्]) going with or well, @deva[विष्वञ्च्] (@deva[विश्वञ्च्-अञ्च्]) following, @deva[देवव्रञ्च्] (@deva[देव-अञ्च्])adoring a deity, @deva[सर्वञ्च्] (@deva[सर्व-अञ्च्]) going everywhere, @deva[उदञ्च्] northen,, @deva[अन्वञ्च्] following, @deva[उद्भ्रञ्च्], @deva[भ्रद्भ्यञ्च्], @deva[अद्भ्यञ्च्] going to that( all these derived from @deva[भ्रद्स्+अञ्च्]), @deva[गोष्ठञ्च्] &c.

**(a)** In the Nom sing. @deva[अञ्च्] becomes @deva[अङ्]. The nasal of @deva[अञ्च्] is dropped before all terminations beginning with the Acc. plu. and the preceding semi-vowel is changed to its corresponding long vowel before the vowel terminations after which @deva[अ] is dropped. When @deva[अञ्च्] is not preceded by a semi-vowel, its @deva[अ] is changed to @deva[ई] if not preceded by a long vowel; otherwise it remains unchanged. @deva[तिर्यञ्च्] becomes @deva[तिरश्च्] under similar circumstances. In other respects these words are declined like words ending in @deva[च्].

rules.body:

rules.body:

Voc. and Acc. of neuter nouns. Voc. and Acc. dual of the latter.

In the Voc. sing. the @deva[त्] of neu. nouns is optionally retained.

@deva[अहन्] n. meaning 'a day' changes its final @deva[न्] (which becomes visarga finally to visarga) when followed by consonantal terminations or by nothing; in other cases it is declined like @deva[नामन्].

rules.title: अर्वन् (Horse): Special Declension
rules.body:
@deva[अर्वन्] m. a horse, except when preceded by the negative particle @deva[अन्] (forming a neg. Tat.) is declined like a word ending in @deva[न्] in all cases except the Nom. and Voc. singulars; e. g. N. @deva[अर्वा] @deva[अर्वन्तौ] @deva[अर्वन्तः]; V. @deva[अर्वन्] @deva[अर्वन्तौ], @deva[अर्वन्तः]; A. @deva[अर्वन्तम्], @deva[अर्वन्तौ], @deva[अर्वतः] &c. But @deva[अनर्वन्] (@deva[न विद्यतेऽर्वास्य]) is regularly declined like @deva[युवन्]; @deva[अनर्वा] @deva[अनर्वाणौ] &c.

@deva[स्वर्वन्] neu. is declined as @deva[स्वर्वत्] @deva[स्वर्वती] @deva[स्वर्वन्ति] Nom. Voc. Acc.; the rest like @deva[अर्वन्] mas.

rules.title: Perfect Participles Ending in वत् or ईवत्
rules.body:
Bases ending in @deva[वत्] or @deva[ईवत्]—

These are the perfect participles derived from roots with the affix @deva[वत्] to which the intermediate @deva[इ] is prefixed in some cases. They have a @deva[न्] prefixed to their final @deva[त्] in the first five inflections, the penultimate @deva[अ] being lengthened before it. In the Nom. sing. m. the @deva[त्] is dropped and the Voc. sing. ends in @deva[वन्]. @deva[इ] is substituted for @deva[अ], before which the preceding short @deva[इ], if any, is dropped, before the vowel terminations beginning with those of the Acc. plu. and before the @deva[ई] of the Nom. Voc. and Acc. dual of the neuter nouns. The final @deva[त्] of a root is changed to @deva[द्] before @deva[वत्] reappears before this @deva[इ]; final @deva[त्] is changed to @deva[द्] before the consonantal terminations and in the Nom. Voc. and Acc. sing of the neuter.
