| @deva[ह्रस्व] 'short' | @deva[ह्रसीयस्] | @deva[ह्रसिष्ठ] |

---

[^1]: @deva[अन्तिकबाह्योर्नेडसाधौ ।] Pāṇ. V. 3. 36.

[^2]: @deva[युवाल्पयोः कनन्यतरस्याम् ।] Pāṇ. 3. 54.

[^3]: @deva[क्षियाक्षिपरिक्षिपेष्वहल्युडब्दुलश्रुदृप्रथीघच्छन्दारकाणाकाणां प्रथमस्य तितक्षुरिचबृप्राघिच्छन्दः ।] Pāṇ. VI. 4. 157. @deva[क्ष], @deva[स्थ], @deva[स्क], @deva[बृ] &c. are substituted for @deva[क्षिप्], @deva[स्थिर], @deva[स्क्रिप्], &c. respectively.

[^4]: @deva[स्थूलदृढुयोडाभीमभूयःश्लाघ्याणां शणादियुत् पूर्वस्य च गुणः ।] Pāṇ. VI 4. 156. The words @deva[स्थूल] &c. drop their final portion beginning with @deva[यण्] (@deva[य], @deva[र], @deva[ल्] or @deva[व्]) and the preceding vowel takes guṇa.

[^5]: @deva[प्रशस्यस्य श्रः । ज्य च । उच्चस्य च] Pāṇ. V. 3. 60-62. @deva[बह्वल्पोपौ च बहोः । क्षुद्रस्य क्षोद्र च ।] Pāṇ. VI. 4. 158-159.

[^6]: See note X p. 112.

rules.title: Intensification with तर and तम
rules.body:
Sometimes the terminations @deva[तर] and @deva[तम] are added to the comp. and super. in @deva[ईयस्] and @deva[इष्ठ] to intensify the meaning; as @deva[पापीयस्तर], @deva[पापीयस्तम]; @deva[श्रेष्ठतर], @deva[श्रेष्ठतम].

---

# Chapter VII.

# COMPOUNDS.

rules.title: Vṛitti: The Five Types of Complex Formations
rules.body: Vṛitti (@deva[वृत्ति]) is the general term for any complex formation in Sanskrit requiring explanation or resolution. These Vṛittis are five in number; viz. @deva[कृद्वृत्ति] or the formation of words from roots by primary affixes; @deva[तद्धितवृत्ति] or the formation of derivative bases from nouns by secondary affixes; @deva[धातुवृत्ति] or the formation of derivative verbs from primitive roots; @deva[समासवृत्ति] or the formation of a compound word by the composition of several words; and @deva[एकशेषवृत्ति] or the composition of words in which one of several nouns generally alike in form is retained. The first three will be treated in their proper places. We will treat of the last two in this Chapter.

rules.title: Samāsas: Compound Words
rules.body:
In Sanskrit simple words, whether substantives, adjectives, verbs or indeclinables, have the power of entering into combination with one another and forming what are called 'Samāsas', compound words or, in short, compounds.

**(a)** A compound thus formed may further be compounded with another simple or compound word, and this again may become the member of a new compound.

rules.title: General Rules for Compound Formation
rules.body: In a compound, as a general rule, words are simply joined together, without any relation between the component parts being actually expressed; the whole compound word has the power to express the various relations that exist between the several parts. The last word only takes the case termination required by its grammatical position in a sentence, the remaining words (those ending in a consonant) generally assuming their crude forms before the consonantal case terminations; e. g. @deva[विद्युत्] + @deva[जनः] = @deva[विद्युज्जनः] (see below), @deva[राजन्] + @deva[पुरुषः] = @deva[राजपुरुषः], &c.

rules.title: Sandhi Rules in Compounds
rules.body: Final vowels or consonants (modified as mentioned above) of preceding members of compounds combine with the initial letters of the succeeding members according to the usual rules of Sandhi.

rules.title: Aluk Compounds: Retention of Case Endings
rules.body: In a few cases, the intermediate members retain their case endings in which case the compounds are called 'Aluk' (@deva[अलुक्]); e. g. @deva[देवानांप्रियः] a fool, @deva[युधिष्ठिरः] name of the eldest Pāṇḍava &c.

rules.title: Vigrahavākya: Expounding Compounds
rules.body:
The expounding of a Samāsa (i. e. giving its Vigrahavākya) consists in the expression of the various relations existing between the objects or ideas denoted by the various members of a Samāsa by means of the proper cases or subordinate sentences.

**(a)** When the Vigrahavākya cannot be given, or cannot be given by using the words actually compounded, the compound is called nityasamāsa (@deva[अविग्रहो नित्यसमासः अरुपपदविग्रहो वा ।] Sid. Kau.).

---

[^1]: From @deva[अस्] with @deva[सम्] to throw together.

rules.title: Four Principal Classes of Compounds
rules.body:
Compounds are divided into four principal classes:—(1) Dwandwa or Copulative, (2) Tatpurusha or Determinative, (3) Bahurīhi or Attributive, and (4) Avyayībhāva or Adverbial.

**N. B.** These names themselves mean nothing i. e. they do not denote any of the characteristics of the different compounds. They are simply proper names distinguishing the various classes from one another (to which they vaguely refer if they do so at all).

## DWANDWA OR THE COPULATIVE COMPOUNDS.

rules.title: Dwandwa Compound: Definition and Three Species
rules.body:
A Dwandwa compound consists of two or more nouns which, if not compounded, would be connected by the copulative particle @deva[च] (and),[^1] as @deva[राजदेवौ] which is equal to @deva[राजश्च देवश्च]; @deva[पाणिपादौ] which is the same as @deva[पाणी च पादौ च]. There are three species of the Dwandwa; viz. @deva[इतरेतरद्वन्द्व], @deva[समाहारद्वन्द्व] and @deva[एकशेष].[^2]

---

[^1]: @deva[चार्थे द्वन्द्वः ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 22.

[^2]: The Ekasesha is not strictly speaking a subdivision of Dwandwa. It is a separate Vṛitti by itself (Vide @ref[179]). Sanskrit grammarians do not regard it as a Dwandwa, though it may be so regarded for the sake of convenience. 'It is not a Dwandwa,' remarks Bhattoji Dikshita, 'as it does not contain more than one subanta (@deva[अनेकसुबन्ताभावादद्वन्द्वः]).' It should be further remembered that since it is not a samāsa, its final vowel does not become udātta, as in the case of a Dwandwa compound.

rules.title: Itaretara Dwandwa: Separate Members
rules.body:
When the several members of a Dwandwa compound are viewed separately, it is called Itaretara Dwandwa, e. g. @deva[धवखदिरौ छिन्धि], 'cut down the Dhava and the Khadira trees' In this species each member is of equal importance i. e. has its own independent meaning. It takes the dual or the plural according as the objects denoted by it are two or more in number; the gender of the final noun is the gender of the whole;[^1] as @deva[कुक्कुटश्च मयूरी च कुक्कुटमयूर्यौ इमे] (fem. dual of @deva[इमद्]); but @deva[मयूरी च कुक्कुटश्च मयूरीकुक्कुटौ इमौ]; @deva[रामश्च लक्षमणश्च भरतश्च शत्रुघ्नश्च रामलक्षमणभरतशत्रुघ्नाः] &c.

**Exception**—@deva[अश्वश्च वडवा च अश्ववडवौ] (mas. dual) a horse and a mare; @deva[अहश्च रात्रिश्च अहोरात्रः] (mas. sing. day and night).

---

[^1]: @deva[परवल्लिङ्गं द्वन्द्वतत्पुरुषौ ।] Pāṇ. II. 4. 26.

rules.title: Samāhāra Dwandwa: Aggregate Meaning
rules.body: Samāhāra Dwandwa is that species of Dwandwa which implies an aggregate of the things enumerated in which constitute a complex idea. It is always singular and neuter Thus @deva[आहारनिद्राभयम्] does not merely mean 'food, sleep and fear' but all that characterises animal life. In this species the meaning of the different members is subordinate to the collective sense of the whole compound.

rules.title: Obligatory Samāhāra Dwandwa Cases
rules.body:
A Dwandwa compound of words denoting limbs of the body of an animal, players on musical instruments, parts of an army, inanimate objects (things or @deva[द्रव्य]s and not qualities) names of rivers differing in gender, as also of countries (and not villages), and insects, and animals between which there is naturalantipathy, is always of this nature;[^1] @deva[पाणौ च पादौ च पाणिपादम्] hands and feet; @deva[रथिनाश्च अश्वारोहाश्च रथिनाश्वारोहम्] chariot-warriors and horse-men @deva[माद्र्दङ्गिकाश्च पाणविकाश्च माद्र्दङ्गिकपाणविकम्] players on mridanga and panava (kinds of tabors); @deva[धानाश्च] fried barley or rice @deva[इक्षुदण्डश्च] a kind of sweetmeat @deva[धानेक्षुदण्डम्]; but @deva[रूपं च रसश्च रूपरसौ] form and flavour, as these denote qualities; @deva[गङ्गा च शोणश्च गङ्गाशोणम्] the rivers Ganges and Sona; but @deva[गङ्गायमुने] as these do not differ in gender; @deva[कुरवश्च श्रैवश्च कुरुश्रैवम्] names of countries; but @deva[ग्रामशाखाटकियौ] (two villages of that name), @deva[मद्राश्च केकयाश्च मद्रकेकयौ] (two names of the same gender), @deva[यूका] a louse @deva[च लिक्षा] a nit @deva[च यूकालिक्षम्]; @deva[अहिश्च नकुलश्च अहिनकुलम्] a snake and an ichneumon, &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[अङ्गप्राणितुर्येसेनाङ्गानाम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 4. 2; @deva[जातीरुपाणाम्] Pāṇ. II. 4. 6.; @deva[विशिष्टलिङ्गो नदीदेशोऽग्रामः ।] Pāṇ. II. 4. 7., @deva[शत्रुनिततः] Pāṇ. II. 4. 8. @deva[वैरं च द्विषतोः शाश्वतिकम्] Pāṇ. II. 4. 9.

rules.title: Optional Samāhāra Dwandwa Cases
rules.body: Names of trees, deer, grass, corn, condiments, beasts, birds, the pairs of words—@deva[भभ] and @deva[वह्व], @deva[पूर्व] and @deva[अपर], @deva[उत्तर] and @deva[अधर]—and words of opposite import not qualifying things (@deva[द्रव्य]s), are optionally compounded into a Samāhāra-Dwandwa; instances in order—@deva[इक्षुश्च न्यग्रोधश्च इक्षन्यग्रोधम्-वौ]; similarly @deva[रुरुप्रभम्-वौ] (kinds of deer), @deva[कुशकाशम्-वौ] kinds of grass, @deva[व्रीहियवम्-वौ] kinds of corn, @deva[दधिघृतम्-ते], @deva[गोमहिषम्-षौ]; @deva[शुककारम्-टौ]; @deva[अधरवरम्-रौ], @deva[पूर्वापरम्-रे], @deva[भयोत्तरम्-रे]; but @deva[शीतोष्णे जले।]

rules.title: Samāhāra Dwandwa for Fruits, Army Parts, etc.
rules.body:
The names of fruits, parts of an army, herbs, deer, birds, insects, corn and grass form a Samāhāra-Dwandwa, only when they are taken in the plural;[^1], as @deva[बदराणि च आमलकानि च बदरामलकम्], but @deva[बदरं च आमलकं च बदरामलके]; @deva[रथिनाश्च अश्वारोहाश्च रथिनाश्वारोहम्], &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[फलसेनाङ्गानस्पतिव्याघ्रमृगान्वयानां बहुत्वविवक्षे तद् एकवदिति वाच्यम्] Vārtika.

rules.title: Irregular Dwandwa Compounds
rules.body:
The following compounds are always what they are laid down to be ( though they do not conform to the proper rules ); viz.

**(a)** Samāhāra Dwandwas:—@deva[गावश्च अजावश्च गवाजम्]; @deva[पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च पुत्रपौत्रम्]; @deva[वृकपोत्रम्]; so @deva[स्त्रीकुमारम्], @deva[वडवगर्दभम्] camels and asses, @deva[वडवशशम्] camels and rabbits, @deva[मोक्षपथम्], @deva[दर्भशरम्] holy grass and reeds, @deva[दर्भकुलम्] grass and soft grass or shrubs, @deva[द्राक्षीदाक्षम्] &c.

**(b)** Itaretara Dwandwas:- @deva[दधिपयसी] curds and milk, @deva[कुशकाशिकी] holy sticks and grass, @deva[सर्पिर्मधुनी], @deva[मधुसर्पिषी] honey and ghee, @deva[शुक्रकृष्णे], @deva[अध्ययनतपसी], @deva[आतपसाने], @deva[उतलूतले], @deva[ऋक्सामे] (@deva[ऋक्+सामन्]) Rik and the Sāman verses, @deva[वाङ्मनसे] (@deva[वाक्+मनस्]) speech and mind (the @deva[न्] of @deva[सामन्] dropped and @deva[अ] added to @deva[मनस्] irregularly by Pān. V. 4. 77)

---

[^1]: @deva[द्रव्याणाम् इक्षुवृक्षामृगतृणध्वजसेनाङ्गाजन्यविसहपुरीषोत्तरापराणाम्] । @deva[विभाषा विध्यथानविकराणाम्] Pāṇ. II. 4. 12, 13.

rules.title: ऋ → आ in Dwandwa with Relationships
rules.body:
When words ending in @deva[ऋ] and implying relationship by blood or literary avocation are compounded together, the last but one word changes its @deva[ऋ] to @deva[आ]. The same happens when the word @deva[पुत्र] follows a word ending in @deva[ऋ] under the same circumstances;[^1] @deva[होता च पोता च होतापोतारौ] two priests so called, @deva[होता च पोता च नेष्टा च उद्गाता च होतृपोतृनेष्टृद्गातारः], (but if two words be taken at a time the @deva[ऋ] may, at every step, be changed into @deva[आ]; as @deva[होता च पोता च होतापोतारौ तौ च उद्गाता च होतापोतोद्गातारः] &c.); @deva[पिता च पुत्रश्च पितापुत्रौ], @deva[माता च पिता च मातापितरौ], also @deva[मातरपितरौ] (Pān. VI. 3. 32.), and @deva[पितरौ] (vide @ref[197] a).

---

[^1]: @deva[आनङ् ऋतो द्वन्द्वे] Pān. VI. 3. 25. @deva[द्व्योरेकोऽनेकं द्वन्द्वे उपमिते च होतापोतोद्गातारः] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Vowel Changes in Deity Names
rules.body:
**(a)** When the names of deities well known to be in constant association with each other are compounded, @deva[आ] is substituted for the final vowel of the preceding word, except in the case of the word @deva[वायु];[^1] e.g. @deva[मित्रावरुणौ], @deva[सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ], @deva[अग्निमरुतौ], &c. but @deva[अग्निवायू] or @deva[वाय्वग्नी].

**(b)** The word @deva[अग्नि] followed by the word @deva[सोम] or @deva[वरुण] lengthens its @deva[इ]; as @deva[अग्नीषोमौ], @deva[अग्नीवरुणौ].

---

[^1]: @deva[देवताद्वन्द्वे च] Pān. VI. 3. 26. @deva[वायुवाक्समयोगे प्रतिषेधः] Vārt. @deva[ऋत्विग्भ्यः सोमवक्त्रयोः] Pān. VI. 3. 27.

rules.title: Adding अ to Samāhāra Dwandwa Endings
rules.body: When a Samāhāra-Dwandwa ends in a consonant of the palatal class or @deva[इ], @deva[ई], or @deva[ए], @deva[अ] is added to it: @deva[वाक् च त्वक् च वाक्त्वचम्] speech and skin, @deva[त्वक्स्रजम्] a bark and a garland, @deva[छत्रोपानहम्], @deva[नाहि-क्षवम्], @deva[छत्रोपानहम्] an umbrella and shoes, &c, But @deva[भावधशास्त्रौ] ( as it is not a Sam. Dwa. ).

rules.title: Irregular Dwandwa Compounds
rules.body:
The following compounds are instances of irregular Dwandwas:—

**(a)** @deva[द्यौश्च पृथिवी च द्यावापृथिव्यौ] or @deva[दिवस्पृथिव्यौ][^1] heaven and earth; so @deva[द्यावाभूमी], @deva[द्यावाक्षमे]; @deva[उषस् + सूर्य = उषासूर्यौ][^2] the goddess of dawn and the sun.

**(b)** @deva[जाया + पति = दम्पती].[^3] @deva[दम्पती] and @deva[जायापती] husband and wife.

**(c)** @deva[क्षौ च पुरौ च क्षौपुरौ], @deva[पेङ्गश्च अनङ्गश्च पेङ्गानङ्गौ]. @deva[अक्षिणी च श्रोत्रे च अक्षिश्रोत्रम्], @deva[दाराश्च गावश्च दारगवम्], @deva[ऊरू च अधीवत्तौ च ऊर्वधीवम्] ( thighs and knees. ), @deva[पादौ च अधीवत्तौ च पादाधीवम्]; @deva[नक्तं च दिवा च नक्तदिवम्], @deva[रात्रौ च दिवश्च रात्रिदिवम्], @deva[अहनि च दिवा च अहर्दिवम्], all meaning 'day and night'.

---

[^1]: @deva[द्वन्द्वच्छन्दस्यनसमाहारे] Pāṇ. V. 4 106. @deva[दिवो द्यावा । दिवसश्च पृथिव्याश्च] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 29, 30.

[^2]: A final @deva[अ] is added in the case of these compounds according to a Sūtra of Pāṇ. ( @deva[अचर्च] V. 4. 77. ) quoted further on under @ref[284].

[^3]: @deva[दम्पती] is considered by some to be a word of regular formation. @deva[दम्] in the Vedic literature means 'a house' and @deva[पति] 'a master'. Hence the full word @deva[दम्पती] would mean 'the mistress of the house.'

rules.title: Ekaśeṣa-Dwandwa: Retention of One Word
rules.body:
When several words of the same form ( or dissimilar in form but of the same import[^1] ) are compounded together, only one of them is retained with the necessary number-

e. g. @deva[रामश्च रामश्च रामौ], @deva[रामश्च रामश्च रामश्च रामाः] This is called @deva[एकशेषद्वन्द्वः]. In the case of the mas. and fem. genders the one of the mas. gender is retained.[^2] as @deva[हरी च हरयश्च हरीः]; similarly @deva[शाखौघी], @deva[खुरौ], @deva[अजौ], &c.

**(a)** This principle is further extended to some words dissimilar in form, as in the following examples:—@deva[भ्राता च स्वसा च भ्रातरौ]; @deva[पुत्रश्च दुहिता च पुत्रौ]; @deva[माता च पिता च पितरौ] (see also @ref[193]), @deva[श्वशुरश्च श्वश्रूश्च श्वशुरौ][^3] (also @deva[श्वश्रूश्वशुरौ]); @deva[सः च सा च तौ], @deva[सः च देवदत्तश्च तौ], @deva[सः च यश्च तौ] or @deva[तौ][^4]. In the case of words of the mas. fem and neu. gender that of the neu. gender is retained; as @deva[तत्र देवदत्तश्च ते]; @deva[तत्र देवदत्तश्च यज्ञदत्ता च तानि]

---

[^1]: @deva[विरूपाणामपि समानार्थानाम्] Vārt. @deva[वन्दुमुण्डश्च कुटिमुण्डश्च वन्दुकुण्डौ] or @deva[कुटिकुण्डौ]

[^2]: @deva[एकीभाच् शिष्यते] Pāṇ. 1. 2. 67.

[^3]: @deva[मातुःस्वसुश्च स्वसृदुहितृभ्याम् । पिता मात्रा । श्वशुरश्च श्वश्र्वा । पुत्रादीनि संज्ञापूर्वकम्] Pāṇ. 2. 68, 70; 1. 2. 71. 72.

[^4]: @deva[द्वयोरेकशेषोऽपि इष्यते इति भाष्यम्] Sid. Kau. on Pāṇ. 1. 2. 72.

rules.title: Order of Members in Dwandwa Compounds
rules.body:
The following rules should be observed in arranging the various members of a Dwandwa Compound:—

**(a)**[^1] A word ending in @deva[ऋ] or @deva[उ] should be placed first, and when there are more than one of such words one of these should be placed first, the rest being arranged according to the will of the speaker or writer; @deva[हरिहरौ], @deva[हरिहरश्वराः]; @deva[हरियहराः], &c.

**(b)**[^2] Words beginning with a vowel and ending in @deva[अ] ought to precede others; as @deva[अश्वरथयोः] or @deva[इन्द्राग्न्योः]. This rule should have preference even over the above rule in case both would be simultaneously applicable; @deva[इन्द्राग्नी].

**(c)**[^3] A word that has fewer syllables should be placed first and in case there are more words than one having an equal number of syllables, the one that has more short syllables should be placed first; e. g. @deva[चिरक्षमावो], @deva[ग्रीष्मवसन्तौ], @deva[कुशाकरवः], &c.; the names of seasons and stars, under this latter circumstance, should be arranged according to their astronomical order; as @deva[इन्द्रविशाखरवसन्ताः], @deva[शततभरोहिणी], &c. Also a word of more important significance should precede others; as @deva[तापसपर्वतौ].

**(d)**[^4] Names of the four castes of men should be arranged according to their order, beginning from the highest and so should be the names of brothers beginning from the eldest; e. g. @deva[ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियवैश्यशूद्राः]; @deva[युधिष्ठिरार्जुनौ].

---

[^1]: @deva[ऋद्धोरुच्] Pāṇ. II. 2. 32. @deva[अनेकमसातावेकत्र नियमोऽनियमः शेषे] Vārt.

[^2]: @deva[अजाद्यदन्तम्] Pāṇ. II. 2. 33.

[^3]: @deva[अल्पाक्षरम्] Pāṇ. II. 2. 34. @deva[छन्दसि पूर्वम् । एकतद्ग्रहणं क्रमानवधारणार्थमुपन्यस्तम् । अभ्यर्हितं च] Vārt.

[^4]: Names of the four castes of men should be arranged according to their order, beginning from the highest and so should be the names of brothers beginning from the eldest.

rules.title: राजदन्तादि and धर्मादि: Reverse Order Exceptions
rules.body:
In the case of words of the @deva[राजदन्तादि] class that which ought to be placed first is placed last; while in the case of words of the @deva[धर्मादि] group (a sub-division of @deva[राजदन्तादि]) the rule is observed optionally; @deva[शूद्रार्यम्] a Śudra and an Arya, @deva[धर्मोऽर्थ] or @deva[धर्मार्थौ] or @deva[अर्थधर्मौ]; so @deva[अर्थशब्दौ] or @deva[शब्दार्थौ], @deva[अर्थकामौ] or @deva[कामार्थौ], &c.

---

## II. TATPURUSHA OR THE DETERMINATIVE COMPOUNDS.

rules.title: Definition of Tatpurusha Compound
rules.body: When a compound consists of two members and the first determines the sense of the other, that is called Tatpurusha.

rules.title: Six Varieties of Tatpurusha
rules.body:
According to the grammatical nature of the first or attributive member the Tatpurusha is divided into six varieties:-(1) Tatpurusha proper or the Inflectional, (2) Nañ or the Negative Tatpurusha, (3) Karmadhāraya or the Appositional including 'Dwigu', (4-5) Prādi and Gati or the Prepositional compounds, and (6) Upapada. These are either nouns, adjectives or adverbs.

---

## 1 Tatpurusha.

rules.title: Shortening of Feminine Vowels in Compounds
rules.body:
The final vowel of a feminine noun ending in any of the affixes @deva[आ], @deva[ई] or @deva[ऊ] and forming the second member of a compound used adjectively is shortened; the @deva[औ] of @deva[गौ] is changed to @deva[उ] under the same circumstances[^1]; e. g. @deva[प्राक्+जीविका=प्राग्जीविकः] (Tat.), @deva[आदिमाः] (Tat.); @deva[पञ्चगुः] something bought for five cows; @deva[बहुयो नाड्यो यस्मिन् बहुनाडिः] many-veined @deva[देहः] (Bah.); @deva[चित्रा गावो यस्य चित्रगुः] having variegated cows, &c - but @deva[कल्याणपञ्चमीकः] as the @deva[ई] is not final.

**(a)** If the final @deva[ई] or @deva[ऊ] be not a fem. termination, it remains unchanged; @deva[शम्भुर्धीः सा शम्भुधीः];, @deva[बहुतन्त्री वीणा मनी].

---

[^1]: @deva[गोश्चीयोरुपसर्जनस्य] Pāṇ. I. 2. 48. @deva[राजदन्तादिषु परम्] Pāṇ. II. 2. 31. @deva[धर्मादिष्वनियमः] Vārt.

rules.title: First Variety: Inflectional Tatpurusha
rules.body: The first variety consists of such Tatpurusha compounds as have the attributive member in any one of the oblique cases when dissolved. There are six sub-varieties of this corresponding to the six oblique cases

rules.title: Accusative Tatpurusha
rules.body:
**(a)** A noun in the Accusative case is compounded with @deva[श्रित], @deva[अतीत], @deva[पतित], @deva[गत], @deva[अत्यस्त], @deva[प्राप्त], @deva[आपन्न], @deva[गमी], @deva[बुभुक्षु], and others[^1]; as @deva[कृष्णं श्रितः कृष्णश्रितः] one who has resorted to Kṛishṇa ( as his refuge); @deva[दुःखमतीतः दुःखातीतः] one who has overcome pain; @deva[सुखं आपन्नः सुखापन्नः] one who has obtained happiness, @deva[ग्रामं गमी ग्रामगमी] going to a village, a passenger; @deva[अन्नं बुभुक्षुः अन्नबुभुक्षुः] &c.

**N. B.** @deva[प्राप्त] and @deva[आपन्न] may also be placed first; as @deva[प्राप्तो जीविको प्राग्जीविकः] or @deva[जीविकाप्राप्तः] one who has obtained livelihood; similarly @deva[आपन्नजीविकः] or @deva[जीविकापन्नः]; @deva[प्राप्तजीविका स्त्री], &c.

**(b)** A word expressive of the duration of an action or state is compounded with another expressive of the action or state, in the Accusative case, e. g. @deva[क्षणमात्रं सुखं क्षणमात्रसुखम्] 'happiness lasting for a moment'; @deva[संवत्सरं वासः संवत्सरवासः] 'residence for a year' &c.

**(c)** The word @deva[खट्वा] forms an Accusative Tatpurusha with a p. p. participle when censure is implied or contempt is to be shown[^2]; as @deva[खट्वाम् आरूढः खट्वारूढः] 'a silly fool'. cf. Bhatti. V. 10

**(d)** Sometimes a preposition or a word denoting a period of time may take the place of the Accusative[^3]; as @deva[साधिकृतं] 'half done,' @deva[मासप्रभवः] (@deva[प्रतिपश्चरः]) 'what marks the commencement of a month as the new moon.'

---

[^1]: @deva[द्वितीया श्रितातीतपतितगतात्यस्तप्राप्तापन्नैः] Pāṇ. II, 1, 24. @deva[गम्यादीनामुपसंख्यानम्] Vārtika.

[^2]: @deva[खट्वाशब्दे] Pāṇ. II. 1. 26. @deva[अन्यतरस्यायोगे च] Pāṇ. II. 1. 29.

[^3]: @deva[साधिः । कालः] Pāṇ. II. 1. 27, 28.

rules.title: Instrumental Tatpurusha
rules.body:
A noun in the Instrumental may be compounded—

**(a)**[^1] with another expressive of an effect produced by what is denoted by the noun in the Instrumental case, and with @deva[अर्थं], as @deva[शस्त्रेण भिन्नः शस्त्रभिन्नः] severed by means of a knife; @deva[धान्येन अर्थः धान्यार्थः] wealth obtained by means of grain.

**(b)**[^2] with verbal derivatives when the Instrumental has the sense of the agent or the instrument or means of the action; as @deva[हरिणा त्रातः हरित्रातः] saved by Hari; @deva[नखैर्भिन्नः नखभिन्नः] torn with the nails &c.

**(c)** with the words[^3] @deva[पूर्व], @deva[सदृश], @deva[सम], @deva[तुल्य] and words having the sense of @deva[कृत], @deva[कल्प], @deva[निपुण], @deva[मिश्र], @deva[शीतपूर्व] and @deva[अवर]; as @deva[मात्रेण पूर्वः मातृपूर्वः]; @deva[मात्रा सदृशः मातृसदृशः] like his mother; @deva[पितृसमः] equal to his father; @deva[सरेण ऊनं मासूनम्]; so @deva[मासव्यकल] ( less by one māsha, a particular weight ); @deva[वाचा कलहः वाक्कलहः] a quarrel ( in words ); @deva[आचारनिपुणः]; @deva[युद्धभिक्षः], @deva[आचारक्षीणः] 'thin by the discharge of religious duties' @deva[मासेन अवरः मासावरः] 'younger by a month.'

**(d)**[^4] With another noun signifying an article of food or something eatable, the noun in the Instrumental case denoting some kind of condiment used to season it or another article of food mixed with it; as @deva[दध्ना ओदनः दध्योदनः] rice mixed with curds; @deva[गुडेन भक्तः गुडभक्तः] fried rice mixed with treacle.

**(e)** Sometimes @deva[स्वयं] may take the place of the Instrumental as @deva[स्वयंकृतः] done by one's self.

---

[^1]: @deva[तृतीया तत्कृतार्थेन गुणवचनेन] Pāṇ. II. 1. 30.

[^2]: @deva[कर्तृकरणे कृता बहुलम्] Pāṇ. II. 1. 32.

[^3]: @deva[पूर्वसदृशसमानोत्तरपदकलनिपुणमिश्रश्लक्ष्णश्लिष्टपूर्वादयश्च] Pāṇ. II. 1. 31.

[^4]: With another noun signifying an article of food or something eatable, the noun in the Instrumental case denoting some kind of condiment used to season it or another article of food mixed with it.

rules.title: Aluk of Instrumental: Retaining Case Endings
rules.body:
Instances of the Aluk of the Instrumental[^1] ( i. e. in which the noun in the Inst. does not drop its case term. )—@deva[अञ्जसा कृतं अञ्जसाकृतम्] 'done honestly'; @deva[ओजसाकृतम्] 'done with might'; @deva[पूर्वाग्रजः] 'one having an elder brother'; @deva[जन्माधः] 'blind from birth'. @deva[मनसाप्रियः], @deva[मनसाप्रिया], when proper names, otherwise @deva[मनोप्रियः], @deva[मनोप्रिया], &c. @deva[आत्मन्] followed by an ordinal number retains its case ending; as @deva[आत्मना पञ्चमः आत्मनापञ्चमः]

---

[^1]: @deva[ओजःसहस्रामत्तूर्तिसाऽत्मभिः] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 3. @deva[अञ्जस उपसंख्यानम्] Vārt.

rules.title: Dative Tatpurusha
rules.body:
A noun in the Dative is compounded[^1]—

**(a)** with another expressive of the material of which the thing expressed by the noun in the Dative case is made; as @deva[यूपाय दारु यूपदारु], 'wood for a sacrificial post.'

**(b)** and with the words @deva[अर्थ], @deva[बलि], @deva[हित], @deva[सुख] and @deva[रक्षित]. The compound with @deva[अर्थ] is a nityasamāsa and takes the gender and number of the noun it qualifies; @deva[द्विजाय अर्थं द्विजार्थः सूपः] broth for a Brāhmana; @deva[द्विजाय बलिं द्विजायै यवागूः] ( water-gruel ) @deva[द्विजाय बलिं द्विजायै पयः]; @deva[भूतेभ्यो बलिः भूतबलिः] an offering to the bhūtas( certain created beings ); @deva[गवे हितं गोहितम्] good for a cow; @deva[गवे सुखं गोसुखम्]; @deva[गवे रक्षितं गोरक्षितम्].

---

[^1]: @deva[बहुर्षी तृतीयायबलिहितसुखरक्षितैः] Pāṇ. II. 1. 36. @deva[अन्नेन व्यञ्जनम् । भक्षेण मिश्रीकरणम्] Pāṇ. II. 1. 34. 35.

rules.title: Aluk of Dative: Retaining Case Endings
rules.body: Instances of the Aluk of the Dat. @deva[पुत्रायैतत्यम्], @deva[पुत्रायभाग्या]; @deva[आत्मनेपदम्], @deva[आत्मनेभाग्या].

rules.title: Ablative Tatpurusha
rules.body:
A noun in the Ablative case is compounded—

**(a)** with words expressive of fear or rather with the words @deva[भय], @deva[भीत], @deva[भीति] and @deva[भी]:; as @deva[चोराद् भयं चोरभयम्] fear from a thief; @deva[वृकाद् भीतः वृकभीतः] afraid of a wolf, &c.

**(b)** in a few cases with the words @deva[अपेत], @deva[अपोढ], @deva[मुक्त], @deva[पतित], and @deva[अप्रवाह], as @deva[सुखादपेतः सुखापेतः] deprived of happiness; @deva[कल्पनाया अपोढः कल्पनापोढः] 'transcending thought' or 'a fool;' @deva[चक्रमुक्तः], @deva[स्वर्गपतितः] 'fallen from heaven, as a sinner'; @deva[तरङ्गाप्रवासः] 'afraid of waves'.

**(c)** in the case of the words @deva[स्तोक] a little, @deva[अन्तिक] near, @deva[दूर] after, and words having the sense of these; and @deva[कृच्छ्र] a difficulty, there is an Aluk of the Ablative; as @deva[स्तोकाद् मुक्तः स्तोकान्मुक्तः]; @deva[अल्पान्मुक्तः]; @deva[अन्तिकादागतः]; @deva[अभ्याशादागतः]; @deva[दूरादागतः]; @deva[विप्रकृष्टादागतः]; @deva[कृच्छ्रादागतः]

rules.title: Genitive Tatpurusha: General Rule
rules.body: A noun in the Genitive may, as a general rule, be compounded with any other noun; @deva[राज्ञः पुरुषः राजपुरुषः] the king's man ( an officer or a servant ).

rules.title: Restrictions on Genitive Compounds
rules.body:
**(a)** It is not compounded with verbal derivatives[^1] ending in @deva[तृ] and @deva[अक्] and denoting the agent of the action; @deva[कर्तृसखा] and not @deva[कर्तृसखा]; @deva[घटस्य कर्ता], @deva[ओदनस्य पाचकः] &c.; but @deva[हृदयं भक्षयति स्तूकभक्षिका] as the @deva[अक्] here does not denote the agent.

**Exception**[^2]:—But a compound is allowed in the case of the words @deva[याजक] one who employs as sacrificing priests, @deva[पूजक], @deva[परिचारक], @deva[परिवेषक] a waiter at meals, @deva[स्नापक] a servant who bathes his master or brings bathing water for him, @deva[अध्यापक], @deva[उत्साहक] one who destroys, @deva[होतृ], @deva[भर्तृ], when it does not mean 'a holder,' and others not very important; @deva[ब्राह्मणयाजकः], @deva[देवपूजकः], @deva[राजपरिचारकः]: &c.; @deva[अधिहोता], @deva[क्षुमर्तृ], &c. but @deva[वज्रस्य भर्तृ] 'the thunderbolt-bearer'.

**(b)**[^3] A specific Genitive (i.e. from which a singling out is made) is not compounded with any other words; as @deva[द्विजानो द्विजः श्रेष्ठः]

**(c)**[^4] A noun in the Genitive is not compounded with ordinal numbers, words denoting qualities, words implying satisfaction present participles, past participles meaning 'honoured or approved of' or showing the place of the act, verbal indeclinables and verbal nouns ending in @deva[तव्य]; e.g. @deva[द्विजेषु पञ्चमः], @deva[ब्राह्मणस्य शुक्लः] (@deva[हस्तः]); @deva[काकस्य कार्ष्येयः]; @deva[फलानां तृप्तितः] 'satisfied with fruits'. (an Inst. Tat. is, of course, allowed in these cases); @deva[द्विजस्य कुर्वन् कुर्वाणो वा किंचित्], @deva[सतां मतः] esteemed by the good; @deva[राज्ञां पूजितः]; @deva[इदमेषां आसीदिति] (place of sitting) @deva[गतो दृष्टं वा]; @deva[ब्राह्मणस्य छन्दा], @deva[नृस्य कर्तव्यम्] &c.

**N. B.** Compounds like @deva[राजपूजितः], @deva[राजमतः], &c. ought to be considered as Instrumental Tatpurushas.

**Exceptions.**

**(1)** If the word denoting a quality ends in @deva[तर] it does combine with a noun in the Genitive, and the @deva[तर] is dropped; @deva[सर्वेषां श्वेततरः सर्वश्वेतः] whiter than all others; similarly @deva[सर्वेषां महत्तरः सर्वमहान्] &c.

**(2)**[^5]The words @deva[द्वितीय], @deva[तृतीय], @deva[चतुर्थ] and @deva[तुर्य] are compounded with nouns signifying the whole of which they are parts, and are optionally placed first; @deva[द्वितीयं भिक्षायाः द्वितीयभिक्षा], @deva[भिक्षाद्वितीयम्] half of the quantity of alms; but @deva[द्वितीयं भिक्षायाः] ( begging alms a second time ) @deva[भिक्षाकरणम्].

**Note.**—Compounds like @deva[द्वितीयभिक्षा], @deva[पूर्वकायः] ( see further on ) &c. are not strictly Gen. Tat. as the case of the first word determines the name, but mere Tat.; some call these Nom. Tat. ( @deva[प्रथमतत्पुरुष] ).

**(a)**[^6] A noun in the Genitive, used as an object in a sentence, when the agent and object of the action denoted by the nouns formed by kṛit affixes are both used, is not compounded; as @deva[आश्चर्यो गवां दोह्नगोपेन] 'the milking of cows by one, not a cowherd, is a wonder.'

---

[^1]: @deva[षष्ठी क्तैः कृति] Pāṇ. II. 2. 15. @deva[पञ्चमी भयेन] Pāṇ. II. 1. 37. @deva[भयभीतिभीभ्यभिरिति वाच्यम्] Vartika. @deva[अपेतापोढमुक्तपतिताप्रवाहैश्चेत्यपः] Pāṇ. II. 1. 38. @deva[स्तोकान्तिकदूरार्थैः कृच्छ्राणि क्तेन] Pāṇ. II. 1. 39

[^2]: @deva[याजकादिभिश्च] Pāṇ. II. 2. 9

[^3]: @deva[न विधेयेन] Pāṇ. II. 2. 10.

[^4]: @deva[पूरणगुणसन्निधितृप्तव्यतव्यमानाधिकरणैश्च । केन च पूजायाम् अधिकरणशब्दिना च] Pāṇ. II. 2. 11-13. The prohibition with respect to a word expressive of a quality (@deva[गुण]) is not obligatory, remarks Dikshita; as Pāṇ. himself uses such compounds as @deva[संज्ञाप्रमाणत्व] &c. Hence compounds like @deva[अर्थगौरवम्], @deva[बुद्धिमान्त्वम्], &c. are justified (@deva[अतिरोधे गुणेन निषेधः तदविषये संज्ञाप्रमाणत्वादित्वादिनिर्देशात् । तेनार्थगौरवं बुद्धिमान्त्वमित्यादि सिद्धम्]).

[^5]: @deva[द्वितीयतृतीयचतुर्थतुर्यानामन्यतरस्याम्] Pāṇ.II. 2. 3.

[^6]: @deva[कर्मणि च] Pāṇ. II. 2. 14.

rules.title: Genitive Compounds with पूर्व, अपर, अधर, उत्तर, अर्ध
rules.body:
@deva[पूर्व], @deva[अपर], @deva[अधर] @deva[उत्तर] and @deva[अर्ध] n. are compounded with nouns in the Genitive expressive of the whole and are placed first;[^1] e. g. @deva[पूर्वं कायस्य पूर्वकायः] the forepart of the body; @deva[अपरकायः] @deva[अधरकायः] &c. @deva[अर्धं पिप्पल्याः अर्धपिप्पली]; but @deva[ग्रामार्धः] as ( @deva[अर्ध] is mas. here ).

**N B.** In order that the above rule should hold the noun expressive of the whole must denote a single object; hence @deva[पूर्वः] the first @deva[छात्राणाम्]. among pupils, @deva[अर्धं पिप्पलीनाम्] half of a number of pippalis &c. and not @deva[पूर्वछात्राः] &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[पूर्वापराधरोत्तरामेकदेशिनैकाधिकरणे । अर्धं नपुंसकम्] Pāṇ. II. 2. 1, 2.

rules.title: Parts Compounded with Time Periods
rules.body: A word expressive of a part is compounded with another signifying a period of time and is placed first; @deva[मध्यं अह्नः]; @deva[मध्याह्नः] mid-day; @deva[सायाह्नः]; @deva[मध्यरात्रं] &c.

rules.title: Time Elapsed Since Occurrence
rules.body:
A word expressive of a period of time that has passed since a certain occurrence is compounded with another expressive of the occurrence;[^1] as @deva[मासो जातस्य यस्य स मासजातः] 'one since whose birth a month has elapsed'; so @deva[द्व्यहजातः]; @deva[संवत्सरजातः] &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[कालाः परिमाणिना] Pāṇ. II. 2. 5.

rules.title: Aluk of Genitive: Retaining Case Endings
rules.body:
Instances of the Aluk of the Gen. The noun in the Genitive may retain its case ending—[^1]

**(a)** when reproach is to be implied, as @deva[चोरस्यकुलम्], but @deva[ब्राह्मणकुलम्]. Also when @deva[देवानां] is followed by @deva[प्रिय] and the whole means a fool; otherwise @deva[देवप्रियः].

**(b)** when the words @deva[वाच्], @deva[दिश्] and @deva[पक्षत्] are followed by @deva[पति], @deva[दण्ड] and @deva[हर] respectively; as @deva[वाचस्पतिः] 'skilful speech,' @deva[दिशोदण्डः]: 'a particular appearance of stars in the shape of a staff in the sky;' @deva[पक्षतोहरः] 'one who robs another in his very presence while he is looking on,' hence 'a goldsmith, a rogue.'

**(c)** in the following cases:—@deva[विशेषसः]: 'a king of Kāśhī,' @deva[दिवस्पतिः] 'Indra,' @deva[वाचस्पतिः] lord of speech, Brihaspati; @deva[शुनःशेपः], @deva[शुनःपुच्छः] and @deva[शुनोलाङ्गूलः]: 'sons of Ajigarta.'

**(d)** and optionally when followed by @deva[पुत्र] and censure is implied;[^2] @deva[दास्याः पुत्रः] or @deva[दासीपुत्रः] a bastard, a knave; but @deva[ब्राह्मणीपुत्रः].

**(e)** When a word ending in @deva[तृ] is compounded with another and there is the relation by blood or some kind of learning, the aluk is necessary; and optional when it is followed by @deva[स्वसृ] and @deva[पति]. The initial @deva[स] of @deva[स्वसृ] is optionally changed to @deva[ष] when preceded by @deva[मातृ] or @deva[पितृ] and when there is aluk, and necessarily when there is no aluk in a compound; e. g. @deva[होतुःपुत्रः], @deva[होतृपुत्रोपवासी], a pupil of the hotri; @deva[मातुःस्वसा], or @deva[मातुःषसा] and @deva[मातृष्वसा]; so @deva[पितुःस्वसा], &c. (but @deva[मातः स्वसा], @deva[पितः स्वसा] when uncompounded); @deva[स्वसृपतिः] or @deva[स्वसुः-पतिः]; but @deva[होतृपूजनम्].

---

[^1]: @deva[पञ्चमीया आक्रोशे] Pāṇ VI. 3. 21. @deva[देवनुष्यान्निष्ठायाम् इति च सूत्रम्] Vārtikam-@deva[वाच्प्रद्युद्यो पतिदण्डहरेषु । शेपपुच्छलाङ्गूलेषु शुनः । दिवश्च द्रष्टै] Vartikas.

[^2]: @deva[पुत्रे न्यत्रस्याम्] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 22.

rules.title: Locative Tatpurusha
rules.body:
A noun in the Locative is compounded—

**(a)**[^1] with @deva[शौण्ड], @deva[धूर्त], @deva[कितव] a rogue, @deva[प्रवीण], @deva[संवीत] adorned, invested with, @deva[अन्तर], @deva[आधीन], @deva[पट], @deva[पण्डित], @deva[कुशल], @deva[चतुर], @deva[निपुण], @deva[सिद्ध], @deva[शुष्क], @deva[पक्व], and @deva[बन्ध]; as @deva[अक्षेषु शौण्डः अक्षशौण्डः] skilled in dice; @deva[ईश्वरे आधीन ईश्वराधीनः] dependent on God (when compounded the affix @deva[स] i. e. @deva[ईन] is compulsory; so the compounded form is always with @deva[अधीन]); @deva[आतपशुष्कः] dried in the sun; @deva[स्थालीपक्वः] cooked in a pot; @deva[वक्रबन्धः] a kind of poetic composition; &c.

**(b)**[^2] with words meaning a 'crow' when contempt is implied; @deva[तीर्थे काकं इव तीर्थकाकः] said in contempt of one who is very greedy; so @deva[तीर्थकाकः]; similarly @deva[नगरकाकः]:—@deva[वायसः] &c. &c. There are a few Loc. Tat. compounds given in the list @deva[धावेसमिताद्] having a similar sense; e. g. @deva[कूपे मण्डूक इव कूपमण्डूकः] a well-abiding frog i. e. one who knows nothing of the world outside the pale of his own village; so @deva[कूप-उदपान-मण्डूकः]; @deva[उदुम्बरष्टाभिः-मत्स्याकः] lit. an insect in the fruit of the Udumbara tree; metaphorically it means the same as @deva[कूपमण्डूकः]; @deva[कूपकेश्यगः] &c. In some cases there is an aluk of the Loc., as @deva[गेहेशूरः] 'a boasting coward', @deva[गेहेख्यातः] 'a braggadocio', @deva[गेहेनद्री] 'a househero', 'a carpet knight', @deva[ग्रासेकुशलः] 'clever in eating only' i. e. 'a good-for-nothing fellow'; @deva[पायसेपटुः]; @deva[गोष्ठेयुधः]; @deva[गोष्ठेविजयी]; @deva[गेहेमृगः], &c.

**Note:**—Words of this class do not enter into further combination with other words.

**(c)**[^3] with another, when they both imply a name (@deva[संज्ञा]); there is an aluk of the Loc. term. when the noun ends in a consonant or @deva[अ]; as @deva[अरण्येतिलकः] lit. 'wild sesamum yielding no oil, hence anything not answering to one's expectations:' similarly @deva[वनेकुरुन्टका]; @deva[स्थलिसारः] 'a bamboo' (also @deva[स्थकुसारः]; vide Si. IV. 61.). These compounds are nitya (obligatory) as remarked by Bhaṭṭoji (@deva[वाच्येन संज्ञायावगमादित्यतमनित्यम्]).

**(d)** with potential p. participles in @deva[य] implying an obligation; @deva[मार्गेदेयं] (@deva[कपर्द]); @deva[पुरोहितेयं] (@deva[साम]); the aluk by @ref[217] (b) below.

**(e)**[^4] with p. p. participles when it expresses a part of the day or night; @deva[तत्र] may take the place of the Loc.; as @deva[पूर्वाह्णे कृत्ते पूर्वाह्णकृतम्]; @deva[अपराह्नकृतम्] @deva[तत्रकृतम्] &c; but @deva[अह्नि दृष्टं]; and with the p. p. participles when reproach is implied, with an aluk of the Loc; as '@deva[अवसन्नेनकुलरिपुते तवैतत्]' 'this thy action is similar to that of a mungoose on the hot ground.' @deva[अवसन्नेनकुलरिपुते] is used to express the inconstancy of a person.

---

[^1]: @deva[सप्तमी शौण्डैः । सिद्धशुष्कपक्वबन्धेभ्यः] Pāṇ. II. 1. 40, 41. @deva[कृतो विद्यायोतिसृस्वसृभ्यः । विभाषा स्वसृपत्योः] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 23, 24; @deva[मातृपितृभ्यामन्यतरस्याम् । मातृपितृभ्यां स्वस्ता] Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 84, 85.

[^2]: @deva[काकेण क्षेपे । धावेसमिताद्यश्च] Pāṇ. II. 1. 42, 43. @deva[चकारोऽत्रपदार्थार्थः । तेनैषां समासान्तरे षट्कत्वा प्रवेशो न] Sid. Kāu.

[^3]: @deva[संज्ञायाम् । हलभमात्संज्ञायाः संज्ञायाम् । गतिकुपुरस्त्योः स्थितः] Pāṇ. I. 44. VI. 3 9. VIII. 3. 9. 5.

[^4]: @deva[केनचिद्राजावययवः । तत्र । द्वेधे] Pāṇ. II. 2. 45-47.

rules.title: Additional Aluk Cases of Locative
rules.body:
Additional instances of the aluk of the Loc.

**(a)** Aluk is necessary in the case of the words—(1) @deva[गो] and @deva[तुर] followed by @deva[दिव्]; as @deva[गविदिव्]:, 'stationary in the sky', @deva[तुरदिव्]: firm in battle; (2) @deva[हृद्] and @deva[दिव्] followed by @deva[स्पृश्]; @deva[हृदिस्पृश्], @deva[दिविस्पृश्] (@deva[हृदयं दिवं च स्पृशतीति]); (3) @deva[अन्त] and @deva[मध्य] followed by @deva[गुरु]: @deva[मध्ये-गुरुः], @deva[अन्तेगुरुः] and (4) words expressive of parts of the body except @deva[कृषीव] and @deva[सक्थन्] and not followed by @deva[काम]; @deva[कण्ठेकाम]:, @deva[उरसिलोमा] (having the hair on the breast: Bah.), but @deva[मूर्धसक्थनि-शिरसि], @deva[मूर्धे कामो अस्य मुखकामः]·

**(b)**[^1] When a noun in the Loc. is compounded with a verbal derivative and the whole is a name, aluk takes place in most cases; e. g. @deva[स्तम्बेरमः] (@deva[स्तम्बे] a kind of grass @deva[रमते अत्र]) an elephant; @deva[कर्णेजपः] one who whispers into the ear, a spy; @deva[स्वर्चरः] a heavenly being; @deva[पङ्केरुह] a lotus; @deva[कुक्षिशय्य], @deva[जलेशयः] a fish; but @deva[कुशवसः], @deva[सतदिवस्] or @deva[सरोवस] &c.

**(c)** There is optional aluk of the Loc. of a word expressive of time when compounded with @deva[काल] and words ending in the affixed @deva[तर], @deva[तम] and @deva[तन]; @deva[पूर्वाह्णे-हे-काले]; @deva[पूर्वाह्णे-हे-तरः] &c. @deva[पूर्वाह्णे-हे तनः]·

**(d)**[^2] When the compound is not a name, aluk is necessary when @deva[ज] comes after @deva[प्राहृद्], @deva[शरद्], @deva[काल] and @deva[दिव्]; and optional when it comes after @deva[वर्ष], @deva[हर], @deva[शर] and @deva[धर]; as @deva[प्राहृदि-शरदि-काले-दिवि-जः]; @deva[वर्षेजः] or @deva[वर्षजः] produced in the rainy season, &c.

**Exceptions**[^3]:—No aluk takes place in the case of verbal derivatives ending in @deva[इन्] and the words @deva[सिद्ध], @deva[चन्द्र], and @deva[स्थ] in the ordinary language; as @deva[स्थलशायिन्] 'an ascetic,' @deva[साद्वद्यवसिद्धः]; @deva[चक्रचन्द्रः]; @deva[समस्थः]; but @deva[छुप्णोऽध्यासिनः] &c.

**(e)**[^4] When a noun in the Loc case ending in @deva[अ] or a consonant and not denoting time is compounded with @deva[शरण्य], @deva[शाय] and @deva[वासिन्] and with @deva[बन्ध] aluk is optional; @deva[वनेशरण्य]:, @deva[ग्रामेशवासः], @deva[ग्रामेवासी], @deva[कूलेसम्बन्धः], but @deva[स्थविवासः], @deva[मनिबन्धः] &c.

---

## 2. Nañ or the Negative Tatpurusha.

---

[^1]: @deva[तत्पुरुषे छन्दसि बहुलम्] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 14.

[^2]: @deva[प्राहृच्छरत्कालदिवं जे । विभाषा वर्षशरधरात्] Pāṇ VI. 3. 15. 16.

[^3]: @deva[नेन्सिद्धचन्द्राभ्याम् च । स्थे च भाषायाम्] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 19. 20.

[^4]: @deva[बन्धे च विभाषा । शरणवासवासिन्यकालात्] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 13. 18.

rules.title: Nañ or Negative Tatpurusha: Definition
rules.body:
**(a)** The negative particle @deva[न] changes to @deva[अ] before a consonant and @deva[अन्] before a vowel, may be compounded with any noun to form the Negative-Tatpurusha;[^1] as @deva[न ब्राह्मणः अब्राह्मणः], one not a Brāhmaṇa, @deva[न सत्यः असत्य], @deva[असत्], non-existent, or not good, &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[नञ्] Pāṇ. II.2.6. @deva[न लोपो नञ: । तत्पुरुषान्तबहुव्रीहौ] Pāṇ.VI. 3,73.74

rules.title: Exceptions to न → अ/अन् Change
rules.body:
The @deva[न] is not changed to @deva[अ] or @deva[अन्] in the following cases[^1]:—@deva[नभाः] 'that which does not shine,' 'a cloud;' @deva[नपात्](pres. p.) 'one who does not protect;' @deva[नवेद्यः] 'one who does not know,' @deva[नासत्यौ] [ @deva[न सत्यौ असत्यौ न असत्यौ नासत्यौ][^2] ] the two Aświns, the physicians of the gods. @deva[नहुषिः] [ @deva[न हृष्यतीति]: ] name of a demon slain by Indra; @deva[नकुलः] [ @deva[न कुलस्य], for the mongoose is supposed to belong to no particular species of animals ]; @deva[नख] [ @deva[न खनस्य] that which leaves no cavity, or does not go to heaven being burnt down with the dead body ]; @deva[नपुंसकम्] [ @deva[न स्त्री पुमान्] ]; @deva[नक्षत्रम्] [ @deva[न क्षरतीति] ] that which does not move from its proper place, hence a star; @deva[नक्रः] [ @deva[न क्रामतीति] that which does not go far off from water ]; @deva[नाकः] [ @deva[न कं अकं न अकं आदिपत्] ]; @deva[नञ्] when it does not qualify an animal retains its @deva[न] optionally as @deva[नजः] or @deva[अजः] 'a mountain or a tree,' but @deva[अजः गृष्टः] 'a Sudra that cannot move.'

**N. B.** It should be noted that some of these are Bahuvrihi compounds.

---

## 3. KARMADHĀ'RAYA OR THE APPOSITIONAL COMPOUNDS.

---

[^1]: @deva[नभादनपात्रवेदनासत्यनहुषिनकुलनखनपुंसकनक्षत्रनक्रनाकेषु] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 75. @deva[नञोऽस्त्राणिस्यन्यतरस्याम्] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 77.

[^2]: @deva[अत्र बहुव्रीहिनाभिप्रेतं] ( is not the point ) @deva[तेन 'नासत्यावाश्विनौ देवौ' इति सिद्धम्] Tatvabodhinī.

rules.title: Definition of Karmadhāraya
rules.body:
Panini defines a 'Karmadhāraya' as @deva[समानाधिकरण तत्पुरुषः] or Tatpurusha both the members of which are in the same case relation i. e. have the same case when dissolved.

**N. B.** The difference between the Tatpurusha proper and Karmadhāraya is this:-In the case of the former the attributive member has one of the oblique cases when dissolved, while in the case of the latter it is in apposition to the other member. It may thus be a noun or an adjective qualifying the other member.

rules.title: Karmadhāraya with Standards of Comparison
rules.body:
**(a)**[^1] A word expressive of the standard of comparison (@deva[उपमान]) may be compounded in a Karmadhāraya with another denoting the common quality or ground of comparison; as @deva[घन इव श्यामः घनश्यामः] dark like a cloud. Such compounds are called @deva[उपमानपूर्वपदकर्मधारय].

**(b)**[^2] Similarly a noun denoting the person or thing compared (@deva[उपमेय]) may be compounded with words indicative of excellence, such as @deva[व्याघ्र],[^3] @deva[सिंह], @deva[चन्द्र], @deva[कमल], &c. no mention the common attribute ( of similarity ) being made; as @deva[पुरुषो व्याघ्र इव पुरुषव्याघ्रः] a man like a tiger ( i. e. as bold as a tiger ); @deva[मुखं चन्द्र इव मुखचन्द्रः] a moon-like face i. e. as delightful as the moon; @deva[मुखं कमलमिव मुखकमलम्] &c.; these are called @deva[उपमानोत्तरपदकर्मधारय].

**Note. 1.**—The difference between the two is this:—In the former the common quality of comparison is actually expressed; while in the latter it is left to be understood; in fact if it be expressed there can be no compound; as @deva[पुरुषः व्याघ्र इव शूरः]

**Note. 2.**—The above Karmadhārayas may be dissolved as @deva[मुखमेव चन्द्रः मुखचन्द्रः], @deva[मुखमेव कमलं मुखकमलम्], &c. Dissolved in either way there will be no difference in the formation of the compounds; but there will be difference both in the meaning and in the metaphor. In one case prominence will be given to @deva[चन्द्र] or the moon and the figure will be 'upamā ( a simile ),' while in the other to @deva[मुख] or the face in which case the figure will be 'Rūpaka[^4].' Compounds like @deva[पाद एवपद्मं पादपद्मम्], @deva[विद्या एव धनं विद्याधनं], &c. are termed @deva[अवधारणापूर्वपदकर्मधारयs].

---

[^1]: @deva[तत्पुरुषः समानाधिकरणः कर्मधारयः] Pāṇ. I. 2. 42. @deva[उपमानानि सामान्यवचनैः] Pāṇ. II. 1. 55.

[^2]: @deva[उपमितं व्याघ्रादिभिः सामान्यप्रयोगे] Pāṇ. II. 1. 56.

[^3]: All these words are included under what is called the group of @deva[व्याघ्र]. The more important of these words are @deva[व्याघ्र], @deva[सिंह], @deva[केसर], @deva[केशव], @deva[चन्द्रमस्], @deva[इन्दु], @deva[गृष्ट], @deva[वराह], @deva[हस्तिन्], @deva[रुरु], @deva[मृगर्], @deva[पण्डरीक], &c.; @deva[चन्द्र], @deva[पद्म], @deva[कमल], @deva[किञ्जल्क], &c.; cf. @deva[दृष्टनायपदे व्याघ्रपुंगवाश्वेन्द्रकुञ्जराः । सिंहशार्दूलनागाश्च पूति सप्रथयेषनराः] ॥ Amara III. 1. 59.

[^4]: So when the common attribute is applicable in its expressed ( @deva[वाच्य] ) sense to the @deva[उपमेय] as in @deva[मुखपद्मं सहासं] dissolve the comp. as @deva[मुखं पद्ममिव] and when to the @deva[उपमान] as in @deva[मुखपद्मं विकसितं] dissolve as @deva[मुखमेव पद्मम्].

rules.title: Adjective-Noun Compounds (विशेषणपूर्वपदकर्मधारय)
rules.body:
An adjective may be compounded with the noun it qualifies in most cases[^1] as @deva[नीलं च उत्पलं च नीलोत्पलं], a blue lotus &c.; @deva[कृष्णश्चासौ सर्पश्च कृष्णसर्पः] where the comp. is necessary; but @deva[कामदत्तो रामः] Such compounds are called @deva[विशेषणपूर्वपदकर्मधारयs].

As a general rule in such compounds the qualifying word is placed first; but there are several exceptions which are given below.

**(a)**[^2] The qualified word is placed first and is always of the mas. gender if it denotes a class or species, when compounded with certain adjectives; e. g. @deva[युथजवती]: 'a young female elephant', @deva[अग्नितोक]: 'a small fire', @deva[उदविकतिपय्] 'butter-milk mixed with a little water', @deva[गोप्रथै]: 'a cow that has brought forth a calf for the first time', @deva[गोवेद्य]: 'a milch-cow (@deva[नवप्रसूतिका])'; @deva[गोवध्या] 'a barren cow', @deva[गोवेहत] ( @deva[गर्भपातिनी गौ:] ), @deva[गोवत्सकपणी] 'a cow whose calf is one year old,' @deva[कटप्रौषिध्य]: 'an agnihotrin Brāhmaṇa of the Kaṭha branch of the Yajurveda,' @deva[कटाध्यापक]: 'a teacher of the Kaṭha branch,' @deva[गो-मतल्लिका-मध्यल्लिका-प्रकाऽइ][^3] (also mas. according to some) @deva[-उद्द]: (@deva[गवोद्द] )@deva[-मह्यन] 'an excellent cow'. The last mentioned five words, all of which denote excellence, retain their own gender invariably; as @deva[ब्राह्मणमतल्लिका] 'an eminent Brāhmaṇa' &c.; but @deva[कुमारी मतल्लिका], as no class is meant here.

**(b)**[^4] The words @deva[कहार], @deva[खञ्ज], @deva[सोढ] lame, @deva[काण], @deva[कुण्ठ] blunt, dull, @deva[खल्वति] bald-headed, @deva[गौर], @deva[वृद्ध], @deva[भिक्षुक] @deva[पिङ्ग], @deva[पिङ्गल], @deva[तड], @deva[जरठ] hard, stiff, @deva[वधिर], @deva[कुब्ज] and @deva[बधिर], may optionally precede the words in apposition to them; as @deva[जैमिनिकहार]: or @deva[कहारजैमिनि]: 'Jaimini who is turned tawny on account of his having practised penance in the sun,' &c.

**(c)**[^5] Words expressive of the persons or things condemned or reproached are placed first; as @deva[वैयाकरणवक्षुर्वि]: 'a bad grammarian,' 'one who has forgotten his grammar and therefore can make no use of his knowledge,' ( @deva[वृष: सत् प्रज्ञं विस्मारिविद् सै क्षुवयति अध्यासव्यैयंति एकह्व्ये] Tatv. ); so @deva[मीमांसकदुर्ष्क]: 'a mīmāṃsaka who is a sceptic' or 'an unbeliever'; except in the case of the words @deva[पाप], @deva[अपक] and @deva[किम्]; as @deva[पापनापित]: 'a bad barber,' @deva[अपककुलाल]: 'a mean, silly potter,' @deva[कुसित: राजा किराज]:, @deva[किबसा] ( @deva[कुसित: सखा] ), &c.

**(d)**[^6] Words in apposition to @deva[इन्द्राक्ष], @deva[नाय] and @deva[कुजर] are also placed first; e. g. @deva[इषपद्नारक]: 'an eminent king,' @deva[नायसकुजर], @deva[इषवनाथ]:, &c.

**(e)**[^7] @deva[कदर] and @deva[कतम] are compounded only when they ask a question with reference to a class ( @deva[जाति] family), and are placed first; e.g. @deva[कदर-कतम-कठ]: 'which Brāhmaṇa of the Kaṭha branch?' @deva[कदर-कतम-कलाप]: 'which Brāhmaṇa of the Kalāpa branch?' But @deva[कतर: सुत]: 'which son'!

**(f)**[^8] The word @deva[कुमार] ( and also @deva[कुमारी] changed to @deva[कुमार] ) is placed first when compounded with one of the words @deva[भ्रमणा], @deva[प्रव्रजिता], @deva[कुलटा], @deva[गर्भिणी], @deva[तापसी], @deva[दासी], @deva[अध्यापक], @deva[पण्डित], @deva[पड्], @deva[इध्], @deva[दुबल], @deva[चपल] and @deva[निपुण]; as @deva[कुमारभ्रमणा] 'a female mendicant,' @deva[कुमारप्रव्रजिता] 'a young female ascetic'; @deva[कुमारइध्:द्री] 'a delicate boy or girl, @deva[कुमारगर्भिणी], @deva[कुमारअध्यापक]:, &c.

**(g)**[^9] The words @deva[एक], @deva[सर्व], @deva[जरद्], @deva[पराण], @deva[नव] and @deva[कैवल]: and the words @deva[एकं], @deva[अपर], @deva[चरम], @deva[जघन्य] 'hindmost,' @deva[समान], @deva[महत्], @deva[मध्यम] and @deva[वीर] are always placed first in a Karmadhāraya compound. @deva[अपर] when followed by @deva[कर्म] is changed to @deva[अश्म]: as @deva[एकनाथः] 'sole master or lord,' @deva[वृद्धकालः]:, @deva[जरद्वैयापिकः]:, 'an old logician,' @deva[पुराणकौ-सांख्यः]:, 'old mimamsā philosophers,' @deva[नवपाचकाः]:, @deva[पूर्वबैयाकरणाः]:, 'the old grammarians,' @deva[अपराङ्गयापकः]: @deva[अपरक्षातों] @deva[अयंक्ष पक्षाक्षै]: 'the hinder part or side of the body;' @deva[चरमराजः]: the last king, @deva[समानतधिकरणम्] 'being in the same category or predicament'; @deva[वीरैकः]: 'a sole warrior i. e. an eminent warrior', &c. The form @deva[एकवीर] ( found used by great writers ) also may be defended.[^10]

**(h)**[^11] The words @deva[सत्], @deva[महत्], @deva[परम्], @deva[उत्तम] and @deva[उच्छृष्ट] are compounded with another noun when they are used as terms of praise or excellence; @deva[सद्वैद्यः]: 'an excellent physician' @deva[महाविद्याकरणः]:. &c., but @deva[उच्छ्रृती गौः]: where @deva[उच्छृष्ट] means 'uplifted, or 'drawn out of '

---

[^1]: @deva[विशेषणं विशेष्येण बहुलम्] Pāṇ. II. 1. 57.

[^2]: @deva[पोटायुवतिस्तोककतिपयमुष्टिवेषवसायैहृष्कृपणीप्रवक्रभ्रातृव्याष्याप-कृत्स्नजाति: । दुरक्षेषपरपजातीयवेशोपिषु] Pāṇ. II. 1. 65. VI. 3. 42.

[^3]: @deva[प्रकर्षाद्वचनेश्व] Pāṇ. II. 1. 66. ( @deva[मतल्लिकादयो निपातलिङ्गा न तु विशेषनिष्ठा:] Sid. Kau ). @deva[मतल्लिकामध्यल्लिकाप्रकाण्डहृष्टतष्टौ । प्रकर्षवाचकान्यमूनि] Amara.

[^4]: @deva[कहार: कर्मधारये] Pāṇ. II. 2. 38.

[^5]: @deva[कुत्सितानि कुत्सनै: । पापाणके कुत्सिते:] Pāṇ. II. 1. 53 54. @deva[कि क्षेपे] Pāṇ. II 1. 64.

[^6]: @deva[इन्द्राक्षनागकुञ्जरै: पूर्वमसानम्] Pāṇ. II. 1. 62.

[^7]: @deva[कदरकतमौ जातिपरिप्रश्ने] Pāṇ. II. 1. 63.

[^8]: @deva[कुमार: भ्रमणादिभि:] Pāṇ. II. 1. 70.

[^9]: @deva[पूर्वकालैकसर्वजरत्पुराणनवकेवला: समासाधिकरणेन] Pāṇ. II. 1 49. @deva[पूर्वोपप्रथमंन्तराभ्यामन्यतमान्तमध्यमध्येमवीतराप्र] Pāṇ. II. 1. 58. @deva[अपर-व्यापे क्रमावो व क्तव्य:] Vārt.

[^10]: @deva[कथमेक वीर इति । पूर्वकालेकेति वाधिनरा परत्वादनेन समास वीरैके इति हि स्यात् । बहुल ग्रहणाद्भविष्यति] How do you justify the form @deva[एकवीर] ? For the Sūtra @deva[पूर्वीपर] &c. being a subsequent one ought to have preference over the preceding Sūtra @deva[पूर्वकालेक] &c. and we should have @deva[वीरैकः]: We reply.—The form may be justified by supposing that the rule operates in most cases only @deva[बहुलग्रहणात्] and not in a few ).

[^11]: @deva[सन्महत्परमोत्तमोत्कृष्टाः पूज्यमानैः] Pāṇ. II. 1. 61

rules.title: Quarters and Numerals in Karmadhāraya
rules.body:
Names of quarters and numerals form a Karm. compound with any subanta ( a declinable word ) but only when the whole compound is an appellation;[^1] e. g. @deva[सप्तर्षिः]: 'Name of a constellation of stars,' 'Ursa Major;' @deva[पञ्चजनाः]:[^2] &c., @deva[पूर्वेयुकामशर्मी] 'Name of a town in the east;' @deva[उत्तरा वृक्षाः] 'Northern trees; @deva[पञ्च ब्राह्मणाः] &c. The compound is forbidden in other cases.

**(α)**[^3] "But words denoting a cardinal point or numerals may be compounded with any other noun when a Taddhita termination is to be affixed to the compound so formed ( or it conveys in addition to its sense as a Karm. a derivative meaning such as is usually denoted by a Tad. aff. ) or when the compound itself becomes the first member of another compound or when the compound forms a proper name; @deva[पूर्वा शाला पूर्वशालाः]; @deva[पूर्वस्यां शालायां भवः पौर्वशालः]: ' being in the eastern hall ' from @deva[पूर्वशाला+अ] ( i. e. Tad. aff. @deva[अ] added by @deva[दिक्पूर्वपदाड्ढकञौ अः] Pāṇ. IV. 2. 107 ); so @deva[षड्+मातृ=षण्मातृ] ' six mothers'+Tad. @deva[अ]=@deva[षाण्मातुरः]: the son of six mothers; @deva[पूर्वा शाला यिद्य यस्य स पूर्वशालाविद्यः] where @deva[पूर्वशाला] is a @deva[पूर्वपद] and not used independently; @deva[उत्तरधुवः]; @deva[दक्षिणधुवः]: &c. which are names.

---

[^1]: @deva[दिक्संख्ये संज्ञायाम्] Pāṇ. II. 1. 51.

[^2]: These are gods, men, Gandharvas, serpents, and Pitṛis, according to some; and Brāmaṇas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Śūdras and Nishādhas or barbarians, according to others. ( Vide Shankarāchārya on Brah. Sū. I. 4. 11.-13. )

[^3]: @deva[तद्धितार्थोत्तरपदसमाहारे च] Pāṇ. II. 1. 51.

rules.title: कु Particle in Karmadhāraya
rules.body:
The particle @deva[कु] forms a Karm. compound with any other word, @deva[कुपुरुषः] ( @deva[कुत्सितः पुरुषः] ) a bad man; @deva[कुयवः] &c.

**(α)**[^1] @deva[कु] is changed to ( 1 ) @deva[कद्] when followed by a noun with an initial vowel in a Tat. by @deva[त्रि] and the nouns @deva[रथ] and @deva[वद] and by @deva[ऋण] ' denoting a species;' @deva[कुत्सितोऽश्वः कदश्वः]: ' bad horse;' so @deva[कदन्नं] 'coarse food;' but @deva[कुद्रः] ' having bad camels' (a Bah. comp.) @deva[राजा]; @deva[कुत्सिताः त्रयः कद्त्रयः]: ' three inferior things;' @deva[कद्रथः] ' a bad chariot,' @deva[कद्व्रः]: 'speaking ill, a bad speaker,' @deva[कनृणम्] ' a kind of fragrant grass.'

(2) To @deva[का] when followed by @deva[पश्चिम्] and @deva[अक्ष] and when meaning 'a little,' and optionally when prefixed to @deva[पुरुष]; @deva[कापश्यम्], @deva[काक्षः] ' a sidelong look or a frown of displeasure;' see Bh.V. 54 (@deva[अक्षसादेश्च तत्पुरुषः अधिक्शब्देन बहुत्रीहिर्या́] Sid- Kau. ). @deva[इंषज्जलं काजलं] 'a little water,' @deva[इषत्पुरुषः काषुरुषः], but @deva[कुत्सित:पुरुष: कुपुरुष:] or @deva[कपुरुष]:.

(3) And to @deva[का] or @deva[कब] when followed by @deva[उष्णः]; @deva[कोष्णं], @deva[कबोष्णं] and @deva[कडुष्णं] by ( 1 ), all meaning 'luke-warm'.

---

[^1]: @deva[कोः कत्पुरुषस्त्रि] ( '@deva[त्रौ च]' Vārt: ) @deva[रथवदयोश्च । दुर्णे च जातौ + कापश्चसयोः । ईषदर्थे । विभाषा पुरुषे । कर्वं चोक्तम्] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 101-107.

rules.title: Two Adjectives and Other Special Karmadhāraya Cases
rules.body:
Two adjectives may also be compounded into what is called the @deva[विशेषणोभयपदकर्मधारयः] as @deva[शुक्लकृष्णः], @deva[कृष्णसारंगः].

**(a).**[^1] Two participles expressive of two consecutive actions of the same individual may be compounded together, the one expressive of the previous action being placed first; @deva[आदौ स्नातः पश्चादनुलिप्तः स्नातानुलिप्तः] 'first bathed and then anointed'; similarly @deva[पीतोद्गीर्णश] 'first drunk and afterwards vomited out' @deva[पीतप्रतिबद्धः], @deva[पहीतप्रतिष्ठक:] ( Rag. II. 1. IV. 43 ), &c.

**(b).** In the case of the two sets of words given above ( @ref[222].g. ) forming compounds with one another those beginning with @deva[पूर्व] are placed first. In the case of @deva[एक] compounded with @deva[वीर] it may precede or follow it; as @deva[वीरैक:] or @deva[एकवीर:]; the former, however, is preferable. In the case of the first set of words viz. @deva[एक]......@deva[केवल] the one succeeding precedes the one preceding when compounded together; as @deva[पुराणनवत्], @deva[केवलपु-राणम्], &c.

**(c)**[^2] A past participle is compounded with another with the negative particle prefixed to it; '@deva[कृताकृतम्],' what is done and not done i. e. 'partially done'.

**(d).**[^3] The word @deva[युवन्] ( m. f. ) enters into a Karm. comp. with the words @deva[खलति], @deva[पलित], @deva[वलित] having wrinkles, and @deva[जरती], and is placed first; i. e. @deva[युवा+खलतिः युवखलतिः] 'a young bald-headed man', @deva[जटी] 'a young bald-headed woman'; @deva[युवजरती] 'a young woman looking old'; @deva[युवपलितः] 'a young man whose hair is grey', &c.

---

[^1]: See Pān. II. 1.49. ( @deva[पूर्वकाल-पूर्वस्य सम्भवन्पक्त्वा:पूर्वकालेऽपर-कालेन समस्यते] Tatv. quoted above )

[^2]: @deva[केन नष्टशब्दोऽनानम्] Pān. II. 1. 60.

[^3]: @deva[युवाखलतिपलितवलितजरतीभिः] Pān. II. 67.

rules.title: ईषत् 'Little' in Compounds
rules.body:
The word @deva[ईषत्] 'little' is compounded with any other word except a verbal derivative, and even with a verbal derivative when it expresses a quality;[^1] as @deva[ईषद्विपुलः] 'a little brown', @deva[ईषत्कपिः] 'reddish.' &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[ईषदर्था] Pāṇ. II. 2. 7. @deva[ईषद्भववचनेनेति वाच्यम्] Vārt

rules.title: Compounds with तलय, अभीय, य, धन्य
rules.body:
Words ending in the terminations @deva[तलय], @deva[अभीय], @deva[य] and @deva[धन्य] and words having a similar meaning, may be compounded with any subanta not importing a particular kind;[^1] e. g. @deva[भोज्यो-पाय्] 'any hot eatable', @deva[तुल्यश्वेतः] 'of a similar white colour,' @deva[सदृशसुभ्रतः], &c.; but @deva[भोज्यः भोजनः] as the latter word refers to a kind of food here.

---

[^1]: @deva[धन्यतल्याख्या अजाताया] Pāṇ. II. 1. 68.

rules.title: Irregular Compounds: मयूरव्यंसकादि Class
rules.body:
The following are the more important of the compounds given by Pāṇ. as irregular under the class @deva[मयूरव्यंसकादि][^1]— @deva[मयूरव्यंसो यंवक्रम मयूरव्यंसकः] 'a cunning peacock', so @deva[जावव्यंसकः] @deva[उच्चश्च अवाचु श्च उच्चावचम्], so @deva[उच्चनीचम्] 'high and low', 'great and small', @deva[तिष्ठतं च प्रचितं च तिष्ठप्रचम्], @deva[नारित् किंचित् यस्य अस्तिचनः]; @deva[नास्ति कृतो भयं यस्य स अकृतोभयः]; @deva[अन्यो राजा राजान्तरम्], @deva[अन्यो मागः मागान्तरम्], @deva[भिन्नश्च भिन्नमानं] (these are nitya-samāsas). @deva[अशीत पिबत इत्येवं सततं यत्राभिधीयते सा अशीतापिबता] that in which are constantly uttered the words 'eat and drink', so @deva[पचतप्र-जगता], @deva[सादुसमोदता]; @deva[अहं अहं इति यस्यां क्रियायामभिधीयते सा अहमहमिका], that in which are uttered the words 'I alone; I alone;' hence hard competition, &c. @deva[अहं पूर्वं अहं पुर्वेति यस्यां क्रियायामभिधीयते सा अहंपुर्विका]; so @deva[अहोडुत्तरिका] 'great self-conceit or pride' (Bhatti. V. 27); 'vaunting', (Bv.I. 84) &c. Also @deva[छान्दिश्लोक] put to flight,' @deva[पृथुच्छा] 'accident,' &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[मयूरव्यंसकादयश्च] Pāṇ. II. 1. 72.

rules.title: Madhyamapadālopi: Dropping Middle Member
rules.body:
In some Karmadharaya compounds the last member of the first word which is itself a compound word is dropped; e. g. @deva[शाकप्रियः पार्थिवः: शाकपार्थिवः]: 'a king who likes vegetables', @deva[दैत्यराजको ब्राह्मणः: दैत्यब्राह्मणः]: &c. These compounds, though they should be properly called "@deva[उत्तमपदालोपि]" are popularly designated "@deva[मध्यमपदालोपि]". Any compound requiring a similar explanation is classed under this group (@deva[शाकपार्थिवादि]) which is an @deva[आकृतिगण].

---

## DWIGU OR NUMERAL APPOSITIONAL COMPOUNDS.

rules.title: Definition of Dwigu
rules.body: When the first member of a Karmadharaya compound is a numeral it is called 'Dwigu'.

rules.title: Formation Conditions for Dwigu
rules.body:
A Dwigu compound is possible[^1] (a) under the circumstances mentioned in @ref[223] (a) i. e.-

(1) when a Taddhita affix is to be added to the compound so formed, @deva[षण्णां मातृणामपत्यं कार्त्तिकेयः]: 'the son of six mothers, Kārtikeya' (vide Ku. IX); @deva[पञ्चकपालः]: &c; or (2) when the compound itself becomes the first member of another compound, as @deva[पञ्चगावः पणं यस्य असौ पञ्चगवधनः]:, @deva[पञ्च: गतिषु:] &c

(b) And when the compound denotes an aggregate; in this case it is singular;[^2] as @deva[त्रयाणां भुवनानां समाहारः: त्रिभुवनम्] the three worlds (taken collectively); as @deva[पञ्चगवधम्], @deva[पञ्चगवधम्], &c.

---

## PREPOSITIONAL COMPOUNDS.
## 4. Pradi.

---

[^1]: @deva[शाकपार्थिवाद्यानां सिद्धये उत्तरपदलोप्यप्यपसंख्यानम्] Vārt on Pāṇ. II. 1. 60. @deva[संख्यापूर्वो द्विगुः] Pāṇ. II. 1. 52.

[^2]: @deva[द्विगुरेकवचनम्] Pāṇ. II. 4. I

rules.title: Prādi: Prepositional Compounds
rules.body:
Those Tatpurusha compounds whose first member is a preposition are termed Prâdi by Sanskrit grammarians;[^1] some of these prepositions combine with a following noun in the Nom., with a noun in the Acc. &c., e. g. @deva[प्रगतः आचार्यः प्राचार्यः] 'an eminent teacher', @deva[संगतः अध्वाने समध्वः] 'taken to a path-way' (vide Bhatti. III. 45). @deva[प्रढ्ढो वातः प्रवातः] 'strong or excessive wind,' &c.; @deva[अतिक्रान्तो मालां अतिमालः] 'excelling a garland' (in fragrance or beauty), @deva[अतिक्रान्तो रथं राथ्यैर्वा अतिरथः] 'a chariot-warrior who has no rival or equal'; so @deva[अतिमात्र] 'exceeding measure,' @deva[अतिसर्व] &c. @deva[अवष्टब्धः कोकिलया अवकोकिलः] 'attracted by the cuckoo;' @deva[परिश्लान्तः अध्ययनात् पर्येध्ययनः] 'tired of studying,' @deva[निष्क्रान्तः कौशाम्ब्याः निष्कौशाम्बिः] 'gone out of Kauśâmbî;' so @deva[निर्लुब्ध] &c. A compound with prepositions which govern cases (@deva[कर्मप्रवचनीय]) is forbidden, @deva[दृशं प्रति].

---

## 5 Gati.

---

[^1]: @deva[कुगतिप्रादयः] Pāṇ. II. 2. 18. @deva[प्रादयो गतार्थयै प्रथमया । अध्यादयः कान्तार्थयै द्वितीयया । अवादयः छ्द्दार्थयै तृतीयया । पर्यादयो गत्यार्थयै चतुर्थ्या । निरादयः क्रान्तार्थयै पञ्चम्या । कर्मप्रवचनीयानां प्रतिषेधः] Vârtikas.

rules.title: Gati: Compounds with Indeclinables
rules.body:
Compounds of the following words with verbal indeclinables are called Gati.

**(a)**[^1] The particles @deva[उरी], @deva[उरती], @deva[बोल्ड], @deva[वष्ट], @deva[स्वाहा], @deva[स्वधा], @deva[प्राद्], @deva[आविष्] and @deva[अस्] and the word @deva[कारिका] meaning an action; as @deva[उरीकृत्य], @deva[उरतीकृत्य] 'having accepted; @deva[वषट्कृत्य] 'having uttered the word Vashat;' @deva[प्रादूर्भूय], @deva[कारिकाकृत्य] 'having done the act.'

**(b)**[^2] Onomatopoetic words not followed by @deva[इति], as @deva[खाट्कृत्य]; but @deva[खाटिति कृत्वा] (@deva[निरुक्तिवत्]).

**(c)**[^3] The words @deva[सत्] and @deva[असत्] showing respect and disrespect respectively, the prepositions @deva[अलं] in the sense of 'adorning,' @deva[पुर:], @deva[अग्र:] @deva[अंत:], @deva[कुणु], @deva[मन:], @deva[अस्तं], @deva[अच्छ], and @deva[तिर:]; as @deva[अलंकृत्य] 'having adorned', but @deva[अलं कृत्वा] doing enough (@deva[पर्याप्तिसिद्धयै:] Sid. Kau.); @deva[पुरस्कृत्य] 'placing in the front'; @deva[अग्र:कृत्य] (@deva[अग्रीकृत्य]) @deva[अन्तर्कृत्य] (@deva[मध्ये कृत्वा] Sid. Kau.); @deva[कुणुकृत्य], as @deva[कुणुकृत्य पय: पिबति] 'he drinks milk to his heart's content', @deva[अच्छोद्य] 'having gone up to and spoken' (@deva[अभिमुखं गत्वा उक्त्वा च इत्यर्थे:] Sid. Kau.); @deva[तिरोध्य], @deva[मनोहत्य] (till disgust is produced); @deva[अस्तंगत्य], @deva[अच्छुगत्य] 'going towards.'

**(d)**[^4] The words @deva[हस्ते], @deva[पाणौ] and @deva[प्राच्यै]; as @deva[हस्तेकृत्य], @deva[पाणौकृत्य], 'having married'; @deva[प्राच्यैकृत्य] 'having forced to yield.'

**(e)**[^5] The particles @deva[उपाजे], @deva[अन्वाजे], @deva[साक्षात्], @deva[मिथ्या], @deva[अधा], @deva[प्रादु:], @deva[आवि:] and @deva[नमस्], the words @deva[प्रदक्षि], @deva[उरसि], (except when there is the sense of juxtaposition or extreme contact), @deva[मध्ये], and the word @deva[पदे] form compounds with verbal indeclinables optionally; @deva[उपाजेकृत्य], @deva[उपाजे कृत्वा], @deva[अन्वाजेकृत्य] @deva[अन्वाजे कृत्वा] 'giving strength to the weak' [@deva[दुर्बलस्य बलमाधाय इत्यर्थै:] Sid. Kau.]; @deva[साक्षात्कृत्य-त्वा], @deva[लघणीकृत्य-त्वा], @deva[उरसिकृत्य-त्वा] (having accepted) @deva[मनसिकृत्य कृत्वा]; but @deva[उरसि कृत्वा पाणिं क्षेते]; @deva[मध्येकृत्य-त्वा], @deva[पदेकृत्य], @deva[पदे कृत्वा], &c.

**(f)** These compounds are also formed with nouns derived from roots for their second members; e. g. @deva[अस्तमय:] 'setting of the sun,' @deva[पुरस्कार:] 'reception, showing respect,' @deva[तिरस्कार:], @deva[सत्कार:], @deva[अलंकृति:], &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[उपयुक्तिनिविदावप्यन्य] Pāṇ. I. 4. 61. @deva[कारिकाशब्दस्योपसंख्यानम्] Vârtikas.

[^2]: @deva[अनुकरणं चानितिपरम्] Pāṇ. I. 4. 62.

[^3]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 63-71.

[^4]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 77-78.

[^5]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 73-76. (@deva[अनत्यधाने उरसिमनसी]).

rules.title: द्विग Formations as Prepositional Compounds
rules.body:
The @deva[द्विग] formations (see Chap. XI.) are also classed as prepositional Tatpurusha compounds; as @deva[शुक्लीकृत्य] having turned white what was not so before.

---

## 6. UPAPADA COMPOUNDS.

rules.title: Upapada Compounds: Definition
rules.body:
When the second member of a Tat. Comp. is a root-noun derived from a root which takes a particular Krit affix by virtue of the presence of the first member, it is called an Upapada Tat.; as @deva[कुम्भं करोतीति कुम्भकारः] 'a potter,' so @deva[साम गायतीति सामगः] 'one who chants a verse of the Sàman Veda,' @deva[मांसं कामयती मांसकामा] 'desirous of meat'; similarly @deva[अश्वक्रीति] (@deva[अश्वेन क्रीता]) 'bought for a horse,' @deva[कच्छपी] 'a female tortoise,' &c. The noun prefixed to the last member, such as @deva[कुम्भ], is called an upapada.

**N. B.** The latter member of such compounds must neither be the conjugated form of a root nor a separate verbal derivative i. e. formed independently of the last member; e. g. @deva[पयोधर] is not an Upapada Tat., as the word @deva[धर] can be independently formed; it is a Gen. Tat. @deva[धरतीति धरः पयसां धरः पयोधरः] 'a cloud' or 'the female breast.'

rules.title: Upapada with Namul and Indeclinables
rules.body: Sometimes the second member of an Upapada Tat. my be a Namulanta or the verbal indeclinable in @deva[अप्]; as @deva[स्वादुकृत्य भुङ्क्ते] 'he eats having sweetened the food;' @deva[अग्रेभोजं] 'having dined first;' sometimes this compound is optional. @deva[मूलकोपदंशं] or @deva[मूलकेन उपदंशं भुङ्क्ते] 'he eats the condiment with a raddish,' &c.

rules.title: Upapadas with त्वा/य Indeclinables
rules.body:
Some upapadas such as @deva[उच्चै], @deva[नीचै], @deva[तिर्यक्], @deva[छसत्], &c. also optionally form compounds with the verbal indeclinable in @deva[त्वा] (changeable to @deva[य]); as @deva[उच्चैःकृत्य] (or @deva[उच्चैः कृत्वा]), @deva[तिर्यक्कृत्य], @deva[छसतीक्षय], @deva[नानाकृत्य], @deva[एकधाकृत्य], &c. For further particulars vide the Chapter on verbal derivatives.

---

## GENERAL RULES APPLICABLE TO THE TATPURUSHA COMPOUNDS.

---

[^1]: @deva[तत्रोपपदं संज्ञीत्यम्] Pāṇ. III. 1. 92. @deva[उपस्यपदे कर्मणीत्यादौ वाक्येन क्रियते कुम्भादि तदाख्यकं पदमुपदसंज्ञं स्यात्] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: अङ्गुलि → अङ्गुल in Compounds
rules.body:
The word @deva[अङ्गुलि] at the end of a Tatpurusha compound changes its final to @deva[अ] when preceded by a numeral or an indeclinable,[^1] as @deva[द्वे अङ्गुली प्रमाणमस्य द्विङ्गुलं दारु] 'a piece of wood measuring two fingers,' @deva[निर्गतमङ्गुलिभ्यो निरङ्गुलम्] &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[तत्पुरुषपदाङ्गुले: संख्याव्ययादे:] Pāṇ. V. 4. 86.

rules.title: Vowel Dropping and अ Addition in Compounds
rules.body:
The following words, when at the end of a Tatpurusha, drop the final vowel, together with the following consonant if there be any, and add @deva[अ] under the circumstances mentioned:—

**(a)**[^1] @deva[रात्रि] when preceded by a numeral, an indeclinable, a word expressive of a part of the whole, such as @deva[पूर्व], @deva[अपर], &c., or by the words @deva[सर्व], @deva[संख्यात] and @deva[पुण्य]; as @deva[द्वयो: रात्र्यो: समाहार: द्विरात्र] an aggregate of two nights (Dwi.); @deva[अतिक्रान्तो रात्रिरति-रात्र:] that has passed a night, the dead of night; @deva[पूर्वं रात्रे: पूर्वरात्र:] the first part of the night, @deva[सर्वा रात्रि: सर्वरात्र:], @deva[संख्याता रात्रि: संख्यातरात्र:], @deva[पुण्यरात्र:] an auspicious night.

The same happens when @deva[रात्रि] is preceded by @deva[अहर्] in a Dwandwa; as @deva[अहश्च रात्रिश्च अहोरात्र:].

**(b)**[^2] @deva[राजन्], @deva[अहर्] and @deva[सति]; as @deva[परम: राजा परमराज:] a great king, @deva[मह्राणं राजा महाराज:]; @deva[उत्तमं अह: उत्तमाह:] an excellent day, @deva[एकं च तदह: एकाह्]; @deva[द्वयोरह्नो: समाहार: द्वह:], so =@deva[एह:], @deva[सप्ताह:], &c. @deva[पुण्यं अह: पुण्याह्] a holy day, @deva[सदिताह्] (vide @ref[245], b.), @deva[कृष्णस्य सत्ता कृष्णसत्व:] &c.

**(c) Exceptions**[^3]—@deva[अहर्] when preceded by an indeclinable, or a word denoting a part of the whole, or by @deva[सर्वे] or by a numeral with a Taddhita affix added to the whole compound, becomes @deva[अह्न्]; as @deva[अतिकान्तमह्:] exceeding a day (in duration) @deva[अह्नह्:], @deva[पूर्वाह्न:] forenoon, @deva[सर्वाह्न:] the whole day, @deva[संख्यताह्न्:], @deva[द्वयोरह्नो: भव: द्व्यह्न:] (@deva[-ह्ना] fem.), @deva[त्र्यह्नीय:] &c.; with @deva[संख्यात्] the change is optional; as @deva[संख्यताह्न्:], or @deva[ह्न:].

**N. B.** The[^4]@deva[न्] of the substitute is changed to @deva[ण्] when preceded by @deva[र्] belonging to the first member ending in @deva[अ]; as @deva[सर्वाह्ण:]; but @deva[परगतं अह: पराह्न:] (as @deva[परा] ends in @deva[आ]).

**(d)**[^5] @deva[तक्षन्] when preceded by @deva[ग्राम] or @deva[कौट], and @deva[श्वन्] by @deva[अति] or an inanimate object with which it is compounded; e. g. @deva[ग्रामस्य तक्षा ग्रामतक्ष:] 'a village carpenter i. e. one not very skilful,' @deva[कुत्स्यो भव: कौट:] (@deva[स्वतन्त्र:] ) @deva[स चासौ तक्षा च कौटतक्ष:] 'an independent carpenter'; @deva[अतिश्व:] [@deva[दराह्:]] 'fleeter than a dog'; @deva[अतिश्वी] (worse than a dog's life) @deva[सेवा]; @deva[आकष्टे: श्वा इव आकर्षश्व:] 'a dog like i. e. bad or unlucky throw of dice,' but @deva[वानरश्वा] 'a monkey like a dog'.

**(e)**[^6] @deva[सक्थिन्] when preceded by @deva[उत्तर], @deva[मृग] or @deva[पूर्व] or by a word denoting an inanimate object with which it is compounded; @deva[उत्तरसक्थम्] 'the upper part of the thigh', @deva[मृगसक्थम्] 'the thigh of a deer,' @deva[पूर्वसक्थम्], @deva[फलकामिव सक्थिन् फलकसक्थम्] 'a thigh like a board'.

**(f)** A numeral when compounded in a Tat. @deva[त्रिंशति त्रिंशत्: त्रिंशति वर्षाणि] (@deva[चैत्रस्य]) more than thirty; @deva[त्रिंशत्: त्रिंशतांगुलिभ्य: त्रिंशत्: खड्ग:] a sword more than thirty fingers in length.

---

[^1]: @deva[अह: सर्वैकदेशसंख्यातपुण्याच्च रात्रे:] Pāṇ. V. 4. 87.

[^2]: @deva[राजाह: सखिभ्यष्टच्] Pāṇ. V. 4. 91.

[^3]: @deva[अह्नोऽह्न एतेभ्य:] Pāṇ. V. 4. 88.

[^4]: @deva[शद्धो'न्तात्] Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 7.

[^5]: @deva[ग्रामकौटाभ्यां च तक्षन् । अते: श्वन्: । उपमानात्सक्थादिषु] Pāṇ. V. 4. 96-97.

[^6]: @deva[उत्तरमृगपूर्वाच्च सक्थ्न:] Pāṇ. V. 4. 98.

rules.title: Addition of अ to Final Member
rules.body:
The following words have an @deva[अ] added to them when at the end of a Tatpurusha compound:—

**(a)** @deva[गो] except when a Tad. aff. is added and then dropped;[^1] e. g. @deva[परमगवः] an excellent bull, @deva[पञ्चगवम्]-( a collection of five cows ) @deva[धनः], but @deva[द्विगुः] exchanged or bartered for two cows.

**(b)**[^2] @deva[उरच्] meaning 'chief or eminent'. @deva[अश्वानां उर एव अश्वोरसम्] 'the chief of horses i. e. an excellent horse.'

**(c)**[^3] The words @deva[अनच्] @deva[अह्नच्], @deva[अपच्] and @deva[सच्] when they denote a class or form names; @deva[उपानसम्] ( @deva[उपवर्त्यते अन:] ) 'a cart-load,' @deva[महानसः] 'a kitchen'; @deva[अह्नतामः] 'a kind of stone like the moon-stone' [ in this case the final @deva[अन्] is dropped ]; @deva[कालायसम्] 'black iron', @deva[मण्डूककरसम्] 'a lake full of frogs'; @deva[जलरसम्] 'a lake of that name.'

**(d)**[^4] @deva[नौ] at the end of a Dwigu, except when the Tad. affix is dropped ), as @deva[द्राख्मौ नौः पञ्चगासमगाः द्विनावख्यः] ( when the aff. i-not dropped ), @deva[द्विनावः] 'a collection of two boats', so @deva[त्रिनावम्] &c; but @deva[पञ्चभिः नौभिः क्रीतः पञ्चनौः], also when it is preceded by @deva[अर्थ]; as @deva[नावः अर्थेन अर्थनावम्] the neuter is irregular ( @deva[लौकात्] Sid. Kan. ).

**(e)**[^5] @deva[शारी] ( a measure of corn ) under similar circumstances takes the @deva[अ] optionally, the final @deva[ई] being dropped before it: @deva[द्विशारय-रि:] @deva[अर्धशारय-रि].

**(f)**[^6] @deva[अञ्जलि], preceded by @deva[द्वि] or @deva[त्रि] in a Dwigu, optionally takes @deva[अ], except when the Tad. aff. is dropped, before which the final @deva[इ] is dropped; @deva[द्व्यञ्जल्-द्वि] 'two handfuls'; but @deva[द्राख्याञ्जल-लिभ्यां क्रीतः पञ्चजलिः]

---

[^1]: @deva[गोतडितलुकि] Pāṇ. V. 4. 92.

[^2]: @deva[उरच्] meaning 'chief or eminent'.

[^3]: The words @deva[अनच्] @deva[अह्नच्], @deva[अपच्] and @deva[सच्] when they denote a class or form names.

[^4]: @deva[नौ] at the end of a Dwigu, except when the Tad. affix is dropped.

[^5]: @deva[शारी] ( a measure of corn ) under similar circumstances.

[^6]: @deva[अञ्जलि], preceded by @deva[द्वि] or @deva[त्रि] in a Dwigu.

rules.title: Dropping न् from ब्राह्मण
rules.body:
The @deva[न्] of @deva[ब्राह्मण] is optionally dropped when preceded by @deva[कु] and @deva[महत्];[^1] @deva[कुब्राह्मण:] a bad Brāhmaṇa, @deva[महाब्राह्मण:]. The @deva[र्] is dropped necessarily when the compound implies the country in which the Brāhmaṇa dwells; e. g. @deva[सुराष्ट्रवश] a Brāhmaṇa dwelling in Surāshtra.

---

[^1]: @deva[नञ्चणो जनपदशब्दायाम् । कुमहद्राजन्यतख्याम्] Pāṇ. V. 4. 104. 105. @deva[अष्टाध्यायपाठतः] Pāṇ. V. 4. 93. @deva[अनोऽस्मायः सत्सां जातिसंज्ञयोः] Pāṇ. V. 4. 94. @deva[नावो द्विगोः । अपाच्] Pāṇ. V. 4. 99. 100. @deva[शार्याः प्राचाम्] Pāṇ. V. 4. 101. @deva[द्वित्रिपूर्वाञ्जलेः] Pāṇ. V. 4. 102.

rules.title: महत् → महा in Compounds
rules.body:
The word @deva[महत्] is changed to @deva[महा] when it forms the first member of a Karmadharaya or a Bahuvrihi compound, or when the termination @deva[जातीय] follows,[^1] as @deva[महादेव:] the great god, @deva[महाबाहु:] a great arm (Tat.) or one having a great arm (Bah.), @deva[महाजातीय:]; but @deva[महत्: सेवा महत्सेवा] (Gen. Tat.).

**Exception:**—When it is followed by @deva[यश], @deva[कर] and @deva[विशिष्ट] the change takes place necessarily; @deva[महतो महत्या वा कर: महाकर्]; similarly @deva[महायशस्], @deva[महाविशिष्ट:].

---

[^1]: @deva[आत्महत्: समानाधिकरणजातीययो:] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 46. and the Vārtikas on it.

rules.title: अष्टन् → अष्टा before कपाल and गो
Exceptions for Negative Tatpurusha
rules.body:
All the rules given above for the change of the finals of the Tat. compounds do not hold good in the case of the Neg. Tat.;[^1] e. g. @deva[न राजा अराजा] one not a king; @deva[न सखा: असखा], &c.

**(a)** But in the case of the word @deva[पथिन्] the final @deva[इन्] is optionally dropped and @deva[अ] added; @deva[अपथं] or @deva[अपथ्या:] 'absence of a road'. @deva[पथिन्] when so modified in a Tat. is neu.;[^2] (but @deva[अपथ्य: देश:]).

---

## GENDERS OF TATPURUSHA COMPOUNDS.

---

[^1]: @deva[नञ्सत्तत्पुरुषात् । पथो विभाषा] Pāṇ. V. 4. 71, 72.

[^2]: @deva[अपथं नपुंसकम्] Pāṇ. II. 4. 3.

rules.title: Gender Rules for Tatpurusha Compounds
rules.body:
As a general rule a Tatpurusha compound follows the gender of the final noun.[^1]

**Exceptions:**[^2]

**(a)** Compounds with @deva[प्राप्त] and @deva[आपन्न] for their first member and the Prādi compounds follow the gender of the words they qualify; @deva[प्राप्तजीविकः नरः], @deva[प्राप्तजीविका स्त्री], @deva[निष्कोषात्मकः पुरुषः] &c.

**(b)** A Tatpurusha ending in @deva[राज], @deva[अह्न] and @deva[अह] is masculine, except when @deva[राज] is preceded by a numeral and @deva[अह] by @deva[पुण्य] and @deva[द्विन]; e. g. @deva[पूर्वराजः], @deva[मध्याह्नः], @deva[सप्ताहः], @deva[नवराजम्], @deva[गणराजम्], @deva[पुण्याहम्], @deva[द्विनाहम्]; also that ending in @deva[पथ] ( substituted for @deva[पथिन्], vide @ref[280] ) preceded by a numeral or an indeclinable; as @deva[त्रयाणां पन्थाः त्रिपथम्], @deva[विरूपः पन्थाः विपथम्], a bad or a wrong way; but @deva[सुपन्था], @deva[अतिपन्थाः] as they do not end in @deva[पथ]; ( see @ref[285] )

**(c)**[^3] A collective Dwigu is neu.; but that ending in @deva[अ] is generally feminine, and that ending in @deva[आ] is optionally so in which case it takes the termination @deva[ई]; @deva[पञ्चगर्व] a collection of five cows; @deva[त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः त्रिलोकी]; but @deva[पञ्चपर्णम्], @deva[त्रिभुवनम्], @deva[चतुर्युगम्] &c.; @deva[पञ्चानां सहानां समाहारः पञ्चसहस्री], @deva[पञ्चसहस्र्म्]. The @deva[न] of final @deva[अन्] is dropped and the Dwigu is optionally feminine @deva[पञ्चतन्त्री-त्रम्], ( fr. @deva[पञ्च + तन्त्रम्] a carpenter ).

**(d)**[^4] A Tatpurusha ending in @deva[उपज्ञा] and @deva[उपक्रम] is of the neuter gender, when the idea of @deva[प्राथम्य] 'being the first' of what is known or commenced ( introduced ) is meant to be expressed; @deva[पाणिनीयोपज्ञा पाणिनीयपूर्वं प्रयुक्तः] the work ( grammar ) first taught or composed by Pāṇini. @deva[नन्दोपक्रमं द्रोणः] the drona ( a measure of corn ) first brought into use in the reign of King Nanda.

**(e)**[^5] A Tatpurusha ending in @deva[छाया] is neuter when the objects casting the shade are many @deva[वृक्षूणां वृक्षच्छायम्].

**(f)**[^6] A Tatpurusha having for its first member a synonym of @deva[राजन्] ( and not @deva[राजन्] itself ) or the words @deva[रक्षस्], @deva[पितामह] &c. and @deva[सभा] for its latter member is neuter; as @deva[इन्द्रसभम्], @deva[ऐश्वरसभम्], a king's council; but @deva[राजसभाः] @deva[रक्षःसभम्], @deva[पितामहसभम्]; also that ending in @deva[सभा] when it means 'a multitude'; as @deva[स्त्रीसभम्] 'an assembly of women'; but @deva[धर्मसभा] in the sense of @deva[धर्मशाला].

**(g)**[^7] A Tatpurusha ending in @deva[सेना], @deva[सुरा], @deva[छाया], @deva[शाला] and @deva[निशा] is optionally neuter; @deva[ब्राह्मणसेना-नम्], @deva[मधुसुरा-रम्] malt liquor beer, @deva[कुड्यच्छाया-यम्], the shadow of a wall; @deva[गोशाला-लम्], @deva[श्वनि-शा प्रम्] ( the 14th day of the dark half of a month, so called because certain dogs observe a fast on this night, according to the Sābarabhāṣya ).

**N. B.** These rules hold good in the case of Tat. alone; so @deva[इन्द्रसेनो राजा] ( Bah. ); @deva[असेना] ( Neg. Tat. ), @deva[परमसेना] ( Karm. ).

---

## III. BAHUVRĪHI OR THE ATTRIBUTIVE COMPOUNDS.

---

rules.title: Definition and Nature of Bahuvrīhi
rules.body:
A Bahuvrīhi compound consists of two or more nouns in apposition to each other the attributive member being placed first and denotes or refers to something else than what is expressed by its members.[^1] It generally attributes that which is expressed by its second member, determined or modified by what is denoted by its first member, to something denoted by neither of the two; e. g, @deva[महाबाहुः] 'one whose arm is great;' @deva[पीताम्बरः] 'one whose garment is yellow.' When dissolved it must have the pronoun @deva[यत्] in any one of the oblique cases; as @deva[महान् बाहुः यस्य स महाबाहुः] [ @deva[नटः] ]; @deva[पीतं अम्बरं यस्य स पीताम्बरः] [ @deva[हरिः] ]. A Bahuvrīhi compound partakes of the nature of an adjective and assumes the gender of the substantive it qualifies.

**Note**—In English such compounds are by no means rare; cf. high-souled, good-natured, narrow-minded &c.

**N. B.** The difference between a Karm. and Bah. comp. is this:—In the former, one of the members alone is in apposition to the substantive it qualifies, while in the latter the whole compound is an adjective. In the former the sense is complete in the comp. itself, in the latter it is not so; e. g. @deva[यनकघ्रामः नटः], here one of the members viz. @deva[घ्रामः] is in apposition to @deva[नटः] and therefore the comp. is a Karm. @deva[गंभीरनादः] as a Karm. simply means @deva[गंभीरश्चासौ नादः] 'a deep sound,' and the sense is complete; as a Bah. it is equivalent to @deva[गंभीरः नादः यस्य] 'some one whose sound is deep'; here the sense is not complete unless it is known whose sound is meant.

---

[^1]: @deva[अनेकमन्यपदार्थे] Pāṇ. II. 2. 24. @deva[समर्थश्चायमतद्धितार्थेषु पूर्वप्रयोगे । इत्यर्थः] Th.

rules.title: समानाधिकरण and व्यधिकरण Bahuvrīhi
rules.body:
