rules.body: The feminine of words expressive of relationship is irregular; @deva[श्वशुर-श्वश्रू], @deva[पितृ-मातृ], &c.

rules.title: Feminine of पति
rules.body:
The feminine of @deva[पति] is @deva[पत्नी] meaning 'the sharer with her husband in the fruit of the sacrifices performed by him;[^1] but if it end a compound it may optionally remain unchanged[^2] except when preceded by @deva[समान], @deva[एक], @deva[चोर], @deva[पिण्ड], @deva[त्व धात्र], @deva[मह], and @deva[पुत्र] &c. before which this change is necessary; @deva[गृहपति] or @deva[गृहपत्नी], the mistress of the house; or @deva[इन्द्रपति] or @deva[इन्द्रपत्नी]; @deva[उषलपति] or @deva[उषलपत्नी] &c. but @deva[समानः पतिर्यस्याः सा सपत्नी] a co-wife, @deva[एकपत्नी], @deva[चोरपत्नी].

**N. B.**— If there be no compound this change does not take place; as, @deva[ग्रामस्य पतिः] 'the mistress of a village', and not @deva[पत्नी], similarly @deva[गवां पतिः] &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[पत्युर्नो यज्ञसंयोगे] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 33. @deva[पतिशब्दस्य नकारादेशः स्यात् यज्ञेन संबन्धे] । @deva[चिस्त्रियं पत्नी] । @deva[तत्कर्तैकपुत्रस्य फलभोक्त्रीत्यर्थः] । Sid. Kau.

[^2]: @deva[विभाषा गर्भवेष्य] । @deva[नित्यं सपत्न्यादिषु] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 34. 35.

rules.title: Feminine with न् Insertion
rules.body: The words @deva[अन्तर्वत्] and @deva[पतिवत्] form their feminine in @deva[ई] but have a @deva[न्] prefixed to the @deva[ई], @deva[अन्तर्वत्नी] 'a woman big with a child'. @deva[पतिवत्नी] 'a woman whose husband is living'. But if the word @deva[पति] means 'a lord or master of' @deva[ई] only is added; as @deva[पतिमती पृथ्वी] (the earth having a king).

rules.title: इ-Ending Adjectives Unchanged
rules.body: Adjectives ending in @deva[इ] short or long, have no other form for the feminine; as @deva[शुचिः शुचीः] &c.

rules.title: Optional ई for उ-Ending Adjectives
rules.body: Adjectives ending in @deva[उ] not preceded by a conjunct consonant, except @deva[स्वक्], take @deva[ई] optionally; e.g. @deva[मृदुः-मृदुः-दी]. @deva[पटुः-वी]. @deva[बहुः-वी]:; but @deva[स्वकः] 'a girl who chooses her husband' (@deva[पतिवरा कन्या] Sid. Kau.); @deva[पाण्डुः] and not @deva[पाण्डुई] as the @deva[उ] is preceded by a conjunct consonant; @deva[आयुः] as it is a noun.

rules.title: Lengthening to ऊ for उ-Ending Words
rules.body:
A prātipadika ending in @deva[उ] not preceded by @deva[य] and denoting mankind forms its feminine in @deva[ऊ]:;[^1] e.g. @deva[कुरुः] 'a woman of the Kuru country'; but @deva[अध्वर्युः] 'the wife of an Adhvaryu'; also when it does not denote animal-kind; as @deva[अक्षाहुः]. @deva[कुक्कुटुः]; except in the case of @deva[रज्जु] and @deva[हनु];[^2] @deva[रज्जूः]; @deva[हनूः].

**(a)** **Obs.** A prātipadika ending in @deva[बाहु] and used as a proper name, and the word @deva[पञ्चगु] also form their feminine in @deva[ऊ];[^3] as @deva[भद्रबाहुः] 'a woman of that name'; but @deva[वृत्तबाहुः] 'a woman having well-rounded arms'; @deva[पञ्चगूः] !

**(b)** @deva[कङ्] and @deva[कमण्डलुः] if used as proper names take @deva[ई]; @deva[कङ्गी]: 'a woman of that name,' @deva[कमण्डल्वी]:; but @deva[कमण्डलुः कुः] in other cases.

---

[^1]: @deva[ऊङुत:] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 66. @deva[उकारान्तादयोपधात्पन्मनुष्यजातिवाचिनः] । @deva[स्त्रियामुदमः] । Sid. Kau.

[^2]: @deva[अपाणिजातेश्वारज्ज्वादीनामुपसंख्यानम्] । Pāṇ. Vārtika.

[^3]: @deva[बाह्वन्तात्संज्ञायाम्] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 67. @deva[पञ्चगोश्च] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 68. @deva[संज्ञायाम्] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 72.

rules.title: Feminine of ऊरु Compounds
rules.body:
If a compound has for its last member @deva[ऊरु] and for its first, words signifying a standard of comparison, or one of the words @deva[सहित], @deva[शक्], @deva[क्षमण], @deva[वाम], @deva[महित] and @deva[सह], it forms its feminine in @deva[ऊः];[^1] @deva[रम्भोरुः रम्भे इव ऊरु यस्याः] plantain-thighed; @deva[करभोरुः] having thighs ( beautifully tapering ) like the fore-arm or the trunk of an elephant; @deva[दृढितोरुः] having well-turned thighs; @deva[शक्तो खुरौ वातृविव संनियच्छत्यादूरु यस्याः सा शक्तोरुः]; [ @deva[हितेन सह सहितो ऊरु यस्याः सा] ] @deva[सहितोरुः]; [ @deva[सहते इति सहो ऊरु यस्याः सा] ] @deva[सहोरुः] 'a woman whose thighs are capable of enduring great fatigue or pain'; or 'one having excellent thighs.'

---

[^1]: @deva[ऊरुत्तरपदादूपूर्वे] । @deva[संहितशक्क्षमणवाममहितसहाद्येश] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 69, 76 @deva[सहितसहाभ्यां चेति वक्तव्यम्] । Vārtika.

rules.title: ऐ Before ई for Specific Words
rules.body:
The fem. of @deva[उशकपि], Vishṇu or Shiva, @deva[आर्धि], @deva[कुसित] or @deva[कुसिद] 'a usurer' is formed in @deva[ई] before which the final vowel of these is changed to @deva[ऐ];[^1] @deva[उशकऐपयी], @deva[भगायी], @deva[कुसितायी] or @deva[कुसिदायी].

---

[^1]: @deva[उशकपिविष्णुकुसितकुसिदानामुदात्तः] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 37.

rules.title: Optional Feminine of मनु
rules.body:
The feminine of @deva[मनु] is optionally formed by adding @deva[ई] before which the final @deva[उ] is changed to @deva[ओ] or @deva[ऐ];[^1] @deva[मनावी]. @deva[मनायी] or @deva[मनुः] ।

---

[^1]: @deva[मनोर्वा] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 38. @deva[मनुशब्दस्यौकारादेश: स्यादउत्येकारप्र] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Feminine of क/द-Ending Words and युवन्
rules.body:
A prātipodika ending in short @deva[क] or @deva[द] forms its feminine by the addition of @deva[ई];[^1] @deva[कर्क-कर्की], @deva[दण्डयु-दण्डयुनी], @deva[स्वनी], @deva[मञ्जनी], @deva[परिदेवयु-परिदेवनी]; &c.

**N. B.** Words like @deva[स्वसु], @deva[ननान्दु], @deva[विधु], @deva[हरितु], @deva[स्वश्रु] &c. being themselves feminine do not take this termination.

**(a)** @deva[युवन्] forms its feminine by the addition of @deva[ति] before which the final @deva[न्] is dropped; @deva[युवतिः]

---

[^1]: @deva[क्रयेभ्यो ङीप्] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 5.

rules.title: वन् → वर् Before ई
rules.body:
If prātipadika end in @deva[वन्] it changes its @deva[न्] to @deva[र्] before @deva[ई];[^1] @deva[शक्वन्-शक्वरी] the strong one; @deva[पीवन्-पीवरी], @deva[शर्वन्-शर्वरी] the night, @deva[सुत्वानमतिक्रान्ता अतिशर्वरी], @deva[अतिपीवरी], &c.

**Exception.**— But if a base end in @deva[वन्] applied to roots ending in a soft consonant; or if a compound has such a base for its latter member, the fem. is formed by adding @deva[आ] only, before which the preceding @deva[अन्] is dropped,[^2] e. g. @deva[अवाबन्+आ=अवाबा] a Brāhmaṇa woman (@deva[ब्राह्मणी]) or a female thief; @deva[राजगुप्ता].

---

[^1]: @deva[वनोरच्] । Pāṇ. VI. 1. 77, 7.

[^2]: @deva[अनो ब्रह्मणोः] । @deva[अव इत्पातोप्यतोऽन्यतरस्याम्] Pāṇ. IV 1. 12. 28.

rules.title: Feminine of Bahuvrīhi Ending in अन्
rules.body:
A Bahuvrīhi ending in @deva[अन्] forms its fem. in @deva[आ] optionally; as @deva[श्र+पर्वन्=श्रपर्वन्-नी], @deva[बहु+भजन्=न्जा], &c. but if the word ending in @deva[अन्] be such as drops its @deva[अ] before the @deva[आ] of the Inst. sing. it takes @deva[ई] also optionally; e.g. @deva[बहु+राजन्=बहुराजन्-राजा-राज्ञी] &c.

**(a)** If a Bah. ends in @deva[वन्], the @deva[न्] is optionally changed to @deva[र्];[^1] as @deva[बहुपूर्ववन्-बहुपूर्वा] or @deva[बहुपीवरी] a town in which there are many fishermen.

---

[^1]: @deva[बहुपीवरो वा] । Vārt. on Pāṇ. IV. 1. 7

rules.title: Feminine of ऊधस् and Age-Related Compounds
rules.body:
If a Bah. end in @deva[ऊधस्] it takes the suffix @deva[ई] in the fem. before which @deva[न्] is substituted for the final @deva[अस्];[^1] @deva[पीन ऊधः यस्याः सा पीनोधनी] having a large udder; @deva[कुण्डोधनी] (see Rag. I. 84.); also when it is preceded by a numeral or an indeclinable; @deva[अद् बृहती], @deva[अत्यती] having an udder exceedingly large; but @deva[ऊघः अतिकान्ता अत्यघा].

**(a)** Similarly a Bah. ending in @deva[द्वायन्], and @deva[हायन्] denoting age, and having a numeral for its first member takes @deva[ई] in the fem.; @deva[द्विहायनी], @deva[त्रिहायनी] 'a girl two years old;', @deva[त्रिहायणी], &c; but @deva[द्विहायना शाला] a building built two years since.

**N. B.**—the @deva[य] of @deva[हायन्] is changed to @deva[ण] after @deva[द्वि] and @deva[बहुर्] only when it takes @deva[ई]; @deva[बहुहैयणी बाला]; but @deva[द्विहायना], @deva[बहुहैयना शाला].

---

[^1]: @deva[ऊधसोऽनङ्] । Pāṇ. V. 4. 131. @deva[बहुरीहेरूधसो ङीप्] । @deva[संख्यापूर्वस्याद्येर्ङीप्] । @deva[दासभार्यनान्ताच्] Pāṇ. IV. 1 25-27. @deva[वक्तव्यमव्ययस्यैव शाप्यधुनैव ङीत्वञ् चेष्यते] । Vārtika.

rules.title: Feminine of Limb-Denoting Compounds
rules.body:
When a compound has for its second member a word denoting a limb of the body of an animal and having no conjunct consonant preceding its final vowel, the fem. is formed by the addition of @deva[आ] or @deva[ई];[^1] @deva[अतिकेशा-शी]; 'a women having abundant hair;' @deva[सुकेशा-शी]; @deva[चन्द्रमुखा-खी]; but @deva[सुगुल्फा] having beautiful ankles; @deva[हस्तनी] or @deva[हस्तना] (@deva[आ वा प्रतिषेधा वा];) @deva[हट्टका शाला] 'an edifice with a beautiful front'.

**(a)** If the word denoting the limb, however, be one of the words @deva[कोष], @deva[नास्] @deva[जङ्घ], @deva[उस्रा], @deva[शिखा], @deva[वाल], @deva[शाफ], @deva[शुक], @deva[भुज], @deva[कर] &c. or have more than two syllables, the fem. is formed in @deva[आ] alone;[^2] @deva[काश्यपात्कोषा] (@deva[अद्रिमाचूर्णः कोषा] Sid. Kau.), @deva[पृथुजघना], having large hips; @deva[बहुलनयना], &c.

**(b)** Also when the first member is one of @deva[स], @deva[सह], or @deva[विष्वमात्], the fem. is formed in @deva[आ] necessarily;[^3] @deva[सकेशा], @deva[अकेशा], @deva[विष्वमात्नासिका], @deva[सहनासिका] &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[स्वाङ्गाद्योपधयवायावपातात्] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 54.

[^2]: @deva[न कोषाद्यभिधेयायाः] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 56.

[^3]: @deva[सहस्य विष्वमातोश्च] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 57.

rules.title: Specific Body-Part Compounds
rules.body:
Of Bah. compounds having for their last member one of the words @deva[नासिका], @deva[उदर], @deva[ओष्ठ], @deva[जङ्घ], @deva[दन्त], @deva[कर्ण], @deva[रूप], @deva[अङ्गुल], @deva[गात्र], @deva[कण्ठ] and @deva[पुच्छ] the fem. is fomed either in @deva[आ] or @deva[ई];[^1] @deva[तुङ्गनासिका का]; @deva[कनोष्ठी-ष्ठी] 'a woman having a slender waist;' @deva[बिम्बौष्ठी-ष्ठा] 'with a lip as red as the bimba fruit,' @deva[दीर्घे जङ्घे यस्या: सा दीर्घे- जङ्घ-ही] 'one having long legs,' hence 'a she-camel;' @deva[स्वङ्गा सी] ( @deva[शोभने अङ्गे यस्याः सा] ) fair-bodied; @deva[शुपुच्छा-च्छी]: &c.

**(a)** but if @deva[पुच्छ] be preceded by @deva[कवर], @deva[मणि] and @deva[विष], or if @deva[पुच्छ] and @deva[पक्ष] be used in a Bah. involving comparison, the fem. is formed in @deva[ई] only; @deva[कवरपुच्छी], 'one having a variegated plumage' i. e. 'pea-hen'; @deva[उलूकपक्षी शाला] 'a hall having its sides like the wings of an owl'; @deva[उलूकपुच्छी सेना] 'an army with its rear arrayed in the shape of the tail of an owl'

---

[^1]: @deva[नाङिकर्मणिनिष्ठानुकंपूर्वाच्च] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 55. @deva[अत्र प्रावकटेभ्यो यत्क्तम्] । @deva[पुच्छाद्य] । @deva[क्तरादिभिर्निषेधरेषो निष्ठम्] । @deva[उपमाना संज्ञाम् पुच्छाद्य] Vārtikas.

rules.title: Feminine of नख/मुख Names
rules.body:
A Bah. ending in @deva[नख] and @deva[मुख] and used as proper names forms fem. in @deva[आ];[^1] @deva[सुवर्णनखा], @deva[गौरमुखा]; but @deva[ताम्रमुखी] a girl having a ruddy face.

---

[^1]: @deva[नखमुखात्संज्ञायाम्] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 58.

rules.title: Feminine of Cardinal + Limb Compounds
rules.body:
Names of the limbs of the body, preceded by words denoting a cardinal point in a compound, form their fem. in @deva[ई][^1] @deva[उदक्मुखी], &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[दिक्पूर्वपदान्ङीप्] । Pāṇ. IV. 1. 60.

rules.title: Feminine of पाद् Compounds
rules.body:
A Bah. ending in @deva[पाद्] (substituted for @deva[पाद] ) optionally forms its fem. in @deva[ई] before which it is changed to @deva[पद्];[^1] @deva[व्याघ्रस्य इव पादौ यस्याः सा व्याघ्रपाद्-पदी], @deva[सिंहपाद्-पदी] and in @deva[आ] when @deva[पाद्] means 'a foot of a Vedic verse'; @deva[द्विपदा छन्द्], @deva[एकपदा] &c.

**(a)** But if @deva[पाद्] be preceded by one of the words @deva[कुम्भ], @deva[शाल], @deva[तूण], @deva[हंस], @deva[काक], @deva[शकुन्], @deva[सूकर]. &c. the fem. is necessarily formed in @deva[ई]. @deva[पाद्] changing into @deva[पद्] as before; @deva[कुम्भपदी] 'a woman whose feet are as big as a pitcher.'

**(b)** In other cases the fem. of pratipadikas ending in @deva[पाद्] is formed by adding @deva[आ]; @deva[हरिपादा], @deva[अजपादा], &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[पादोऽन्यतरस्याम्] । @deva[वाङिच] । Pāṇ. IV.1. 8, 9.

rules.title: Feminine of Dwigu Compounds
rules.body: A Dwigu ending in @deva[अ] forms its fem. in @deva[ई]; as @deva[त्रिलोकी]; but if the ending word be one of those included in the Ajadi group ( see foot-note on p. 108 ) its fem. is formed in @deva[आ]; @deva[सेना]., @deva[त्रिसेना] ( consisting of three battalions ) @deva[सेना], &c.

rules.title: Dwigu with Measurement Words
rules.body:
**(a)** A Dwigu ending in @deva[काण्ड] ( a particular measure ) and qualifying a word denoting 'a field' has its fem. formed by the addition of @deva[आ], but when a Taddhita affix has been first added to it and then dropped; as @deva[द्वे काण्डे प्रमाणौ यस्यः अस्य द्विकाण्ड + मात्रा = द्विकाण्डा क्षेत्रभक्तिः] 'a piece of land 30 hands in extent'; but @deva[द्विकाण्डी रज्जुः] 'a rope, 30 hands in length'; also when the ending word is one that does not denote a measure, except the words @deva[विस्त] 'a tola', @deva[आविध] 'the load of a cart,' and @deva[केवल्य] ( a weight equal to 3½ tolas ); @deva[पञ्चश्रीः अस्यः क्रीता पञ्चश्रा], @deva[द्वौ विस्तौ पञ्चविष्टवैति द्विविस्ता स्थाली]; so @deva[द्व्याविधा], @deva[द्विकेवल्या].

**(b)** When the word @deva[पुरुष] expressive of measurement ends a Dwigu and the Taddhita affix is added and dropped as before, its fem. is formed both in @deva[आ] and @deva[ई]; @deva[द्वौ पुरुषौ प्रमाणौ अस्याः द्विपुरुषा-षी खनिका] 'a ditch two purushas ( 13 feet ) in depth'

rules.title: Feminine of Participles and Adjectives
rules.body: Participles ( those of the Pres. and Fut. ) of Parasm. roots take @deva[ई] in the fem., @deva[न] being inserted before @deva[त्] as in the Nom. or Acc. dual of the Neu. ( see @ref[116] ) and so do adjectives ending in a consonant; @deva[पचन्ती]; @deva[याद्र्ती], @deva[खादती], @deva[ददती], @deva[धीयन्ती], @deva[महती], &c.

rules.title: Introduction to Kṛit and Taddhita Affixes
rules.body:
# Chapter IX. Secondary Nominal Bases Derived by the Addition of the Taddhita or Secondary Affixes

The terminations used to form derivative bases, in Sanskrit are distinguished into two classes; (1) Kṛit (@deva[कृत्]) or Primary Affixes and (2) Taddhita (@deva[तद्धित]) or Secondary affixes. Kṛit are those affixes that are added to verbs, and the Nominal Bases formed by their means are called PRIMARY NOMINAL BASES; while TADDHITA affixes are those that are added to substantives, primary or derived from roots, and the bases formed with them are called SECONDARY NOMINAL BASES (vide @ref[179]).

rules.title: Scope of Chapter on Taddhita Affixes
rules.body: In this chapter we will treat of the more general secondary nominal bases formed by means of the Taddhita affixes, reserving for a future chapter the formation of the primary nominal bases derived by means of the Kṛit affixes from roots.

rules.title: General Rules for Taddhita Affixes
rules.body:
The Taddhita affixes are added in various senses. They occasion various changes in the words to which they are added. The following general observations should be paid attention to.

**(a)** As a general rule the first vowel of a word takes its Vṛiddhi substitute before the terminations @deva[अ], @deva[य], @deva[एक], @deva[इन्], @deva[एय], @deva[ख], &c.; as @deva[अश्वपति + अ = आश्वपति + अ].

**(b)** Before terminations beginning with a vowel or @deva[य] (1) the final @deva[अ], @deva[आ], @deva[इ], and @deva[ई] are rejected; (2) @deva[उ] and @deva[ऊ] take their Guṇa substitute; (3) @deva[ओ] and @deva[औ] obey the ordinary rules of sandhi; @deva[आश्वपति + अ = आश्वपत] 'belonging to Aśvapati,' &c. n. n.; @deva[मनु + अ = मानवः] 'a descendant of Manu'; @deva[गो + य = गव्य] 'belonging to a cow', so @deva[नाव्य] fr. @deva[नौ] &c.

**(c)** In the case of derivatives form compound words sometimes the initial vowel of the second word takes its Vṛiddhi substitute, and sometimes the Vṛiddhi is double; @deva[पुरेवार्षिकः] 'belonging to the last year', similarly @deva[उपविशालकः] &c. @deva[सौहार्दम्] fr. @deva[सुहृद्], @deva[सौभाग्यम्] from @deva[सुभगम्], &c. When these terminations are added to a Dva. comp. both the words of which are the names of deities, Vṛiddhi is substituted for the initial vowel of both, @deva[आग्निमारुतं कर्म] 'a sacrifice offered to Agni and the Marut deities,' &c.

**(d)** If the initial vowel of a word be preceded by the @deva[य्] and @deva[व्] of a preposition the @deva[य्] or @deva[व्] is first changed to @deva[इय्] or @deva[उव्] before Vṛiddhi substitute can take place; as @deva[व्याकरणम्+अ=वियाकरणम्+अ=वैयाकरणः]; @deva[स्वप्+अ=सुवप्+अ=सौप्तः]; similarly @deva[सौवस्तिक] from @deva[स्वस्ति]; @deva[सौवरम्] fr. @deva[स्वर], &c.

**(e)** Before consonantal Tad. affixes, a final @deva[न्] is generally rejected; the final @deva[न्] with the preceding vowel is sometimes dropped before vowel terminations and before such as begin with @deva[य्]; @deva[युवन्-युवकम्], @deva[राजन्-राजकम्], &c. @deva[आत्मन्-आत्मय-आत्मीयम्]. There are various exceptions to this latter part of the rule; e.g. @deva[राजन्यः] fr. @deva[राजन्] &c.

**N. B.**—Other changes the student will easily note from the instances given.

rules.title: List of Common Taddhita Affixes - Section I
Extended Meanings of Possession Affixes
rules.body:
The affixes given in §. 340 are added in the following senses also, and are therefore called @deva[मत्वर्थीय] 'affixes expressing possession.' These affixes are @deva[मतुप्] (@deva[मत्], @deva[वत्]), @deva[इनि], @deva[इलच्] and @deva[विनि].[^1]

**(1)** In the sense of @deva[गौरवे] 'respectful mention'; @deva[धनवान्] 'possessing wealth', @deva[श्रीमत्] 'possessing glory &c.', @deva[बुद्धिमान्] 'possessing wisdom', @deva[गुणवत्] 'possessing virtue' &c.

**(2)** In the sense of @deva[निन्दायाम्] 'disapprobation'; @deva[दुर्मतिः] 'having a bad mind', 'wicked.'

**(3)** In the sense of @deva[प्रशंसायाम्] 'eulogy'; @deva[सुमनाः] 'having a good mind.'

**(4)** In the sense of @deva[कौशल] 'skill'; @deva[वेदविदः] 'skilled in or knowing the Vedas.'

**(5)** In the sense of @deva[अभावे] 'negation'; @deva[अविद्वान्] 'unlearned', @deva[अबुद्धिमत्] 'not wise' &c.

**(6)** In the sense of @deva[आशिषि] 'blessing'; @deva[आयुष्मान्] 'possessed of long life', @deva[बलिनः] 'possessed of strength' &c.

**(7)** In the sense of @deva[उपमा] 'comparison'; @deva[अश्विव] (= @deva[अश्व इव]) 'like a horse' &c.

---

**N. B.**—When any one of the above seven senses is intended and the base denotes 'time,' then the base takes the affix @deva[अच्] which becomes @deva[अम्] in the Neuter and the word remains indeclinable.[^2]

The words formed in this manner are the following:—@deva[नक्तम्] 'night', and @deva[दिव] 'day'; form @deva[नक्तंदिवम्] 'possessed of night and day', i. e. lasting day and night; @deva[सायम्] 'evening', and @deva[प्रातः] 'morning' form @deva[सायंप्रातः] i. e. lasting evening and morning; @deva[मध्यम्] 'middle' and @deva[दिनम्] 'day' form @deva[मध्यंदिनम्] i. e. lasting from mid-day; @deva[अहन्] 'day' forms @deva[अन्वहम्] 'daily', @deva[संवत्सर] 'year' forms @deva[संवत्सरम्] 'annually.'

**N. B.**—When the base is @deva[वर्ष] 'year' and the following affix has the force of a Past Pass. Part.[^3] i. e. when the idea of expiry is denoted, @deva[पर्युषितम्] 'more than a year old' &c.

**N. B.**—When the base denotes, 'flesh', 'grain', 'water', 'ghee', 'milk', 'food' and the affix also has the sense of the Past Pass. Part. i. e. expresses a past state; @deva[पिशितम्] 'old meat', @deva[धान्यम्] 'old grain', @deva[उदकम्] 'old water', @deva[आज्यम्] 'old ghee', @deva[पयः] 'old milk', @deva[अन्नम्] 'old food.'

The same affix is also added in any of the above senses optionally with @deva[मतुप्] &c., when the base denotes 'sacrificial act', or the base is @deva[गो] 'cow', or any other word, in forming the adjectives @deva[धनिकः] 'rich', and @deva[तपस्विन्] 'an ascetic.'[^4] Thus @deva[गृहमेधी] or @deva[गृहमेधवान्] or @deva[गृहमेधिमान्] or @deva[गृहमेधविन्] 'one who performs the Gṛihamedha sacrifice'; @deva[सोमपः] or @deva[सोमपवान्] or @deva[सोमपिमान्] or @deva[सोमपविन्] 'one who performs the Soma sacrifice'; similarly @deva[वाजिनः], @deva[गोमान्], @deva[धनिकः], @deva[तपस्विन्] &c. &c.[^5]

---

@deva[क] is added in the sense of possession in the following cases:—

**(1)** When the base ends in a long vowel;[^6] @deva[हेमवान्] or @deva[हेमी] or @deva[हेमिमान्] or @deva[हेमविन्] or @deva[हेमकः] 'possessing gold' and so @deva[रत्नवान्] or @deva[रत्नी] &c. or @deva[रत्नकः], @deva[रत्नवत्], &c.

[^1]: By the word "also" in the text, it is implied that these affixes are added to a base in any one of these senses along with the sense of possession. Thus @deva[बुद्धिमान्] 'he who has understanding', 'wise', also conveys the idea of respectful mention.

[^2]: The only exception is @deva[रात्रिःवान्] or @deva[रात्रिमान्] 'lasting a night.'

[^3]: When 'exceeding' or 'more than' is meant to be expressed.

[^4]: The word @deva[तपस्विन्] is irregular because the base ends in a short vowel.

[^5]: Observe, what has been said before applies to this paragraph as well, namely that the idea of possession underlies all these formations.

[^6]: It is really an exception to the dictum that @deva[मतुप्] &c. are affixes of possession.

rules.title: म → व Transformation in Possession Affixes
rules.body:
The @deva[म्] of @deva[मत्] is changed to @deva[व्] before soft letters and vowels.[^1] Thus @deva[धनवत्] 'rich', Nom. @deva[धनवान्], or @deva[धनमत्]; @deva[गुणवत्] 'virtuous' Nom. @deva[गुणवान्] or @deva[गुणमत्], &c.

[^1]: When preceded by a short vowel. When preceded by a long vowel, the @deva[म्] is changed to @deva[व्] in all cases.

rules.title: Adverb-Forming Affixes च्विन् and सात्
rules.body:
The affixes @deva[च्विन्] and @deva[सात्] form adverbial words (@deva[अव्यय]).

## @deva[च्विन्]

Of this affix @deva[च्] and @deva[इन्] disappear and @deva[व्] remains.[^1] It is added to the following roots when preceded by a preposition and meaning 'in honour of.'[^2]

### Roots Taking @deva[च्विन्]

**(1)** The roots @deva[कृ] 'to do', @deva[भू] 'to be', @deva[अस्] 'to be', when preceded by the prepositions @deva[नमस्], @deva[तिरस्], @deva[पुरस्], and @deva[अधि].[^3]

Thus @deva[नमस्+कृ] forms @deva[नमस्कृत्य] 'having saluted'; @deva[तिरस्+कृ] forms @deva[तिरस्कृत्य] 'having dishonoured', 'having neglected'; @deva[पुरस्+कृ] forms @deva[पुरस्कृत्य] 'having placed before', 'having honoured'; @deva[अधि+कृ] forms @deva[अधिकृत्य] 'with reference to', or 'about' or 'concerning,' as @deva[देवदत्तं अधिकृत्य] = 'concerning Devadatta.'

**(2)** The root @deva[क्रम्] 'to step', when preceded by the prep. @deva[परि]; @deva[परिक्रम्य] 'having walked round' or 'round'.

**(3)** @deva[स्था] 'to stand' when preceded by the prep. @deva[उप]; @deva[उपस्थाय] 'having approached', or 'after approaching.'

**(4)** @deva[नम्] 'to bow', when preceded by the prep. @deva[प्र]; @deva[प्रणम्य] 'having bowed to.'

**(5)** @deva[वद्] 'to speak', when preceded by @deva[अभि], in the sense of 'salutation'; @deva[अभिवाद्य] 'having saluted', or 'saluting.'

**(6)** @deva[गम्] 'to go', when preceded by the prep. @deva[अभि]; @deva[अभिगम्य] 'having approached.'

**(7)** @deva[आस्] 'to sit', when preceded by the prep. @deva[परि] and @deva[उप]; @deva[पर्युपास्य] 'having honoured or worshipped.'

**(8)** @deva[ईक्ष्] 'to see', when preceded by the prep. @deva[अव], in the sense of 'consideration'; @deva[अवेक्ष्य] 'having considered, or 'considering.'

**(9)** @deva[धृ] 'to hold', when preceded by @deva[उप], in the sense of 'determining'; @deva[उपधार्य] 'having determined', or 'determining.'

**N. B.**—The words formed by the above rule are indeclinable, and are adverbs. Hence they are also called @deva[अव्यय] 'indeclinables.'[^4]

---

**N. B.**—The affix @deva[ल्यप्] is a synonym of @deva[च्विन्], and like the latter is employed in forming adverbial indeclinables. Here also of the letters @deva[ल्], @deva[य्] and @deva[प्] of the affix @deva[य] alone remains, as @deva[नमस्कृत्य], &c. There is however the following distinction:—When the root is preceded by any other preposition or prepositions than those mentioned above, the affix @deva[ल्यप्] is employed, but not @deva[च्विन्]; @deva[यावत्] + @deva[जीव] form @deva[यावज्जीवम्] 'for life', 'as long as one lives', @deva[समाधिकृत्य] 'including', &c.[^5]

---

## @deva[सात्]

The affix @deva[सात्] may be added in forming the word @deva[मस्तकसात्] from @deva[मस्तक], which means "reducing to atoms, destroying utterly." The words @deva[सततम्], @deva[संततम्] and @deva[संमितम्], meaning 'always', 'for ever', 'together' &c., may optionally take this affix. Thus @deva[सततम्] or @deva[सततसात्]; @deva[संततम्] or @deva[संततसात्]; @deva[संमितम्] or @deva[संमितसात्] respectively. The word @deva[एक] may take this affix @deva[सात्] or @deva[शस्] in forming the word @deva[एकसात्] or @deva[एकशः] which means, 'one by one', 'each one.'

---

**N. B.**—The affix @deva[शस्] may also be added to @deva[शत] 'hundred', @deva[सहस्र] 'thousand', @deva[द्वि] 'two', &c., in the sense of 'a number of.' Thus we have @deva[शतशः] 'by hundreds'; @deva[सहस्रशः] 'by thousands'; @deva[द्विशः] 'by twos.'

---

### Irregular Formations

The following indeclinables are irregularly formed and must be remembered:—@deva[पुनः] 'again', @deva[नमः] 'salutation', @deva[जुषः] 'satisfactorily', @deva[मक्षु] 'quickly', @deva[अधः] 'below', @deva[प्रातः] 'in the morning', @deva[सायम्] 'in the evening' &c.

[^1]: The name of the affix is @deva[क्त्वा].

[^2]: When this affix is used, the root takes weak reduplication in the case of roots of the 3rd class. See §. 511.

[^3]: Before these roots when preceded by these prepositions, the affix @deva[क्त्वा] takes the form @deva[च्विन्], which explains the employment of the latter term in the Sūtra instead of the former.

[^4]: Words ending in @deva[च्विन्] or formed by means of @deva[क्त्वा] are indeclinable, and partake of the nature of the absolutive or gerund.

[^5]: The affix @deva[ल्यप्] is always used when more than one preposition is employed; as @deva[प्रत्युपकृत्य] 'having done a good turn in return.'

rules.title: Introduction to Gender
rules.body:
# Chapter X. Gender

No definite rule can be laid down for the determination of the gender of a noun; but the following general observations will be found useful.

rules.title: Masculine Verbal Derivatives
rules.body:
## I. Masculine

Verbal derivatives formed by the affixes @deva[अच्] and @deva[घञ्] are masculine, as @deva[पाकः] 'cooking', @deva[जयः] or @deva[विजयः] 'victory', @deva[भावः] 'being', &c.

rules.title: Masculine Words Ending in उ and Specific Penultimates
rules.body:
Words ending in @deva[उ] and those having @deva[क], @deva[ट], @deva[ण], @deva[थ], @deva[प], @deva[ष], @deva[ख], @deva[घ], @deva[र], or @deva[स], for their penultimate; as @deva[प्रभुः], @deva[भानुः], @deva[इक्षुः], @deva[स्तबकः] 'a bunch of flowers' &c; @deva[घटः], @deva[पाषाणः], @deva[शोथः] 'a swelling', @deva[फेनः]; @deva[दीपः]; @deva[स्तम्भः]; @deva[रोमः]; @deva[समयः]; @deva[क्षुरः] 'a razor', @deva[अङ्कुरः], @deva[धरः], @deva[वायसः] &c.

**Exceptions:**—Words ending in—

**(a) @deva[उ]**—@deva[धेनु], @deva[रज्जु] (except when it ends a compound, in which case it is both mas. and fem.) @deva[कुहू]—@deva[हू] 'the last day of a lunar month on which the moon is invisible,' @deva[सरयु] 'name of a river,' @deva[तनु], @deva[करेणु] and @deva[विषेणु] 'a kind of creeper,' which are all fem; @deva[इक्ष्वु], @deva[जाठु], @deva[वसु] 'wealth', @deva[अश्रु], @deva[जतु] 'lac,' @deva[त्रपु] 'tin or lead', @deva[तालु], @deva[दारु], @deva[मधु] 'honey,' @deva[स्वादु] 'relish', @deva[वस्तु] and @deva[मस्तु] 'sour cream', which are all neuter.

**(b) @deva[क]**—@deva[चिबुक] 'the chin', @deva[इत्लुक], @deva[प्रातिपदिक], @deva[अंशुक] 'a garment,' @deva[उल्मुक] 'a fire brand.'

**(c) @deva[ट] and @deva[ण]**—@deva[किरीट], @deva[इकुट], @deva[ललाट], @deva[चतुष्पट] 'a place where four roads meet'; @deva[कृण], @deva[लवण], @deva[पर्ण], @deva[उष्ण].

# Chapter XI. Avyayas or Indeclinables

That in an Avyaya whose form remaining the same in all the genders, numbers and cases, undergoes no change.[^2] The Avyayas may be divided into simple and compound ones. The latter are treated of in the chapter on compounds (Avyayībhāvas and a few Bahuvrīhis and Tatpurusha).

The indeclinables comprise (I) Prepositions (II) Adverbs, (III) Particles, (IV) Conjunctions, and (V) Interjections.

Besides these there are in Sanskrit a few nouns having one inflection only which are treated as indeclinable (nipātas); e. g. @deva[अन्यत्] 'another (reason)', @deva[अस्तम्] 'setting', @deva[अस्ति] 'that exists', @deva[ओम्] 'the well-known sacred syllable om', @deva[चनस्] 'satisfaction, food', @deva[चाहु] 'coaxing', @deva[नमस्] 'a bow', @deva[नास्ति] 'non-existence', @deva[भूर्] 'the earth', @deva[भुवर्] 'the sky', @deva[बदि] 'the dark fortnight', @deva[यशस्] 'happiness', @deva[शुदि] or @deva[शुक्ति] 'the bright fortnight', @deva[संवत्] 'a year', @deva[स्वाहा] 'food offered to gods', @deva[स्वधा] 'food offered to the manes', @deva[स्वर्] 'heaven', @deva[स्वस्ति] 'happiness' &c.

## I. PREPOSITIONS

A preposition, styled 'Upasarga or Gati', in Sanskrit is an indeclinable word, having an independent meaning and prefixed to verbs and also to their derivatives. These prepositions modify, intensify and sometimes totally alter the senses of roots[^3]: e. g. @deva[प्रह] 'to strike', @deva[आह] 'to eat, to perform as a sacrifice', @deva[संह] 'to contract', @deva[विह] 'to sport', @deva[परिह] 'to avoid, &c.' Sometimes they are prefixed without any alteration in the sense.

The following are the prepositions (upasargas) commonly prefixed to roots:—

**@deva[अति]**—'beyond, over'; @deva[अतिक्रमः] 'overstepping' or 'going beyond', @deva[अतिसर्जनं] 'a gift, &c.'

**@deva[अधि]**—'over, above, &c.'; @deva[अधिगमः] 'going up, acquisition', @deva[अधिकारः] 'high office or power', @deva[अधिक्षेपः] 'censure', &c.

**@deva[अनु]**—'after, behind, along, &c.' @deva[अनुक्रमणं] 'following', @deva[अनुच्छोति] 'imitation', @deva[अनुग्रहः] 'favour', &c.

**@deva[अप]**—'away from, away.' @deva[अपनयनं] 'the act of taking away', @deva[अपह] 'to plunder, seize' &c., @deva[अपकारः] 'harm, wrong' &c.

**@deva[अधि]** (sometimes **@deva[पि]**)—'near to', 'over', 'taking to', &c.; @deva[अधिगम्] 'to be resolved into or reduced to',[^4] @deva[अधिधानं] or @deva[पिधानं] 'a covering', @deva[अध्ययः] 'destruction', &c.

This prep. is more commonly used as an independent adverb having a cumulative force in classical Sanskrit.

**@deva[अभि]**—'towards, near to', &c; @deva[अभिगम्] 'to go towards', @deva[अभिजनः] 'noble descent or family', @deva[अभिमानः] 'self-respect', @deva[अभिरुच्] 'to defeat', &c.

**@deva[अव]** (sometimes **@deva[व]**; see **@deva[अधि]** and **@deva[अव]**, note)—'away, down', &c. @deva[अव]—or @deva[वगाह] 'to plunge into', @deva[अवतारः] 'descent', @deva[अवगतं] 'reproached', @deva[अवमन्] 'to disrespect', &c.

**@deva[आ]**—'up to, towards, all round, a little', &c.; @deva[आच्छाद्] 'to cover all round', @deva[आकारः] 'form or shape (within due bounds)', @deva[आकाशः] 'that which shines all round' i. e. 'the ether'; @deva[आकम्प] 'to shake a little', &c.

**@deva[उद्]** or **@deva[उत्]**—'upon', &c.; @deva[उद्गम्] 'to go up', @deva[उद्यमः] 'industry', @deva[उत्सर्गः] 'pouring out, hence a gift, a general rule', &c.

**@deva[उप]**—'near to, towards, by the side of', &c.; @deva[उपगा] 'to go near to', @deva[उपकृति] f. 'an obligation', @deva[उपरति] f. 'death', @deva[उपस्थानं] 'praise, worship', @deva[उपमिति] f. 'comparison', &c.

**@deva[दुस्]** or **@deva[दुर्]**—'bad, hard to be done', &c.; @deva[दुराचारः] 'bad conduct', @deva[दुष्कर] 'hard to be done', @deva[दुःसह] 'difficult to be borne', &c.

**@deva[नि]**—'in, into, great, opposed to', &c.; @deva[निड्] 'to insult', @deva[निकेत] 'a house', @deva[निचय] 'a heap, a great collection', @deva[निपीत] 'drunk in', @deva[निदेश] 'a command', &c.

**@deva[निस्]** or **@deva[निर्]**—'out of, away from, without', &c.; @deva[निःसृ] 'to issue out', @deva[निर्गम] 'a passage out', @deva[निर्दोषः] 'out of i. e. free from blame', @deva[निः शंक] 'without doubt', &c.

**@deva[परा]**—'away, back, opposed to', &c.; @deva[पराकृ] 'to reject, to despise', @deva[पराक्रम] 'to act bravely', @deva[परागत] 'gone away', @deva[पराञ्च] 'turn back', @deva[पराजय] 'what is opposed to victory, defeat', &c.

**@deva[परि]**—'all round, about', &c.; @deva[परिधा] 'to place all round i. e. to put on or wear', @deva[परिधिः] 'a wall &c. that surrounds', @deva[परिणामः] 'ripening, maturity', @deva[परिगणना] 'counting all round, i. e. a complete enumeration', &c.

**@deva[प्र]**—(sense to be added from context)

**@deva[प्रति]**—'towards, back, in return, in opposition to', &c.; @deva[प्रतिगम्] 'to go towards', @deva[प्रतिभाषण] 'a speech in return, an answer', @deva[प्रति—वि—कारः] 'an act in opposition to i. e. a remedy' &c.

**@deva[वि]**—'apart, separate from, reverse to', &c.; @deva[विचल्] 'to move apart', @deva[वियुज्] 'to be separated', @deva[विक्री] opp. of @deva[क्री] 'to sell', 'to buy' &c.; sometimes this has an intensive force.

**@deva[सम्]** or **@deva[सं]**—'together with, excellent, full', &c. @deva[संगम्] 'to be united', @deva[संस्कारः] 'perfection', @deva[संस्कृति] 'refinement', @deva[संहारः] 'destruction, contraction', &c.

**@deva[सु]**—'well, thoroughly', &c. (in this sense it is opposed to @deva[दुस्]); @deva[सुकृतं] 'done well', @deva[सुशासित] 'thoroughly trained, well governed', &c. It is also used in the sense of 'very, excessively': @deva[सुमहत्] 'very great.'

Two or more of these prepositions may also be combined and prefixed; e. g. @deva[अभिनिविश्] 'to enter into with resolution', @deva[समुपगम्] 'to come in close contact with', &c.

When used in a compound the verb may be omitted after the prepositions @deva[अति], @deva[अधि], @deva[अनु], @deva[अप], @deva[अव], @deva[अभि], @deva[उप], @deva[परि] and @deva[प्रति]; @deva[अतिक्रान्तो मालां अतिमालः] &c. Vide @ref[232].

There are several other words, also styled Gati by Sanskrit grammarians, used prepositionally. These are prefixed to certain roots only. We give the more important of them below.

**(a)** @deva[अच्छ][^5] 'towards' is prefixed to @deva[वद्] and to roots implying motion; @deva[अच्छगम्य—गत्वा] 'going near', @deva[अच्छपतत्] 'flying towards', @deva[अच्छूद्य] 'having spoken to.'

**(b) (1)** @deva[अन्वाञ्च] 'giving strength to the weak', @deva[अलं] in the sense of 'decorating', @deva[ऊर्ती], @deva[उरर्ती], @deva[उत्ती] all implying 'assent, acceptance or promise', @deva[खात्] and similar imitative sounds, @deva[असत्] and @deva[सत्] in the sense of 'dishonouring or honouring', @deva[प्रास्त] denoting 'fastening', &c. are prefixed to @deva[कृ]; @deva[अन्वाञ्चकरणं], @deva[ऊर्तीकरणं], @deva[असत्कारः], @deva[खात्कृत्य], @deva[खाङ्कृत्य], @deva[प्रास्तकरणं], &c.

**(2)** @deva[नमः], @deva[भाषु], @deva[निष्या], @deva[वशो], @deva[साक्षात्] and some other words may be optionally prefixed to @deva[कृ] or remain separate; @deva[नमस्कारः], @deva[वशोकृ] or @deva[वशो कृ] 'to bring under subjection', @deva[साक्षात् कृ] or @deva[साक्षात्कृ] 'to make manifest', &c.

**(c)** @deva[अन्तर्] is prefixed to roots meaning 'to go', @deva[धा], @deva[भू], and similar roots; @deva[अन्तरित्य] 'having disappeared', @deva[अन्तर्धानं] 'disappearance', @deva[अन्तर्भूत], &c.

**(d)** @deva[अस्तम्] is prefixed to roots implying motion; @deva[अस्तमयः] 'setting', @deva[अस्तंगत] 'set', @deva[अस्तंनी] 'to cause to set, to lead to destruction', &c.

**(e)** @deva[आविः], and @deva[प्रादुः] are prefixed to @deva[कृ], @deva[अस्] and @deva[भू] and @deva[तिरस्] to @deva[भू], @deva[धा] and similar roots, and optionally to @deva[कृ], @deva[आविष्करणं], @deva[आविर्भवनं] 'manifestation', @deva[प्रादुर्]—@deva[आविर्भूत] 'manifested', &c.; @deva[तिरोभूय] 'vanishing out of sight', @deva[तिरोधानं] 'disappearance', &c.

**(f)** @deva[पुरः] is prefixed to @deva[कृ], @deva[भू], @deva[गम्] &c.; @deva[पुरस्कृत] 'placed before, headed by', @deva[पुरोगत] 'gone in the front', &c.

Several nouns, substantive and adjective, may be prefixed to the roots @deva[कृ], @deva[भू], and @deva[अस्] to form what are called in Sanskrit 'chvi-derivatives' (vide chap. IX. Sec. III.) @deva[कृष्णीकरणं] = @deva[कृष्णीकरणं]; @deva[धनी]=@deva[भूत]=@deva[धनीभूतः]. Such nouns are also termed 'Gati.'

Like prepositions may be further used the words to which the Taddhita affix @deva[सात्] is affixed, @deva[अग्निसात्कृ] 'to consign to flames'; @deva[भस्मसात्कृत] 'reduced to ashes', @deva[राजसात्कृत] 'made over to the king', &c. (vide p. 216.)

## II. ADVERBS

Adverbs are either primitive or derived from nouns, pronouns or numerals. | @deva[इत्थम्] | Thus, so, in this manner |
| @deva[इदानीं] | Just now, at this moment |
| @deva[इच्छा] | Truly |
| @deva[इह] | Here |
| @deva[ईषत्] | Slightly, little |
| @deva[उच्चैः] | Loudly |
| @deva[उत्तरम्] | Then |
| @deva[उत्तरेद्युः] | On the day following |
| @deva[उपांशु] | Secretly, in private |
| @deva[उभयतः] | From both sides |
| @deva[उभयद्युः], @deva[उभयेद्युः] | On both days |
| @deva[ऊषा] | Early in the morning, at dawn |
| @deva[ऋतम्], @deva[ऋतेञ्च] | Truly, Truthfully |
| @deva[ऋते] | Without, except |
| @deva[एकत्र] | Together, in one place |
| @deva[एकदा] | Once, once upon a time |
| @deva[एकथा] | In one way, singly, at the same time |
| @deva[एकपदे] | All at once, suddenly |
| @deva[एतर्हि] | Now, at present |
| @deva[एवं] | Just, quite |
| @deva[एवम्] | Thus, so |
| @deva[ओम्] | So be it |
| @deva[काकिद्], @deva[कश्चन] | I trust, hope, &c. |
| @deva[कथम्] | How, in what way |
| @deva[कथञ्चन], @deva[कथाञ्चित्] | With great difficulty, With great effort |
| @deva[कथञ्चिद्] | How indeed, how possibly |
| @deva[कदा] | When, at what time |
| @deva[कदाचित्] | One time, once upon a time |
| @deva[न कदाचित्] | Never |
| @deva[कम्] | Used as an enclitic |
| @deva[कर्हि] | When, at what time? |
| @deva[कर्हिचित्] | At any time |
| @deva[किञ्चन] | What a pity |
| @deva[किञ्च] | Moreover, further, again. Who, what, which? |
| @deva[किंभूत] | How much more? |
| @deva[किञ्चन], @deva[किश्चित्] | To a certain degree, little, somewhat |
| @deva[किसह] | What, how? |
| @deva[किन्तु] | But, yet, nevertheless, however |
| @deva[किन्नु] | What indeed, whether |
| @deva[किन्वा] | Or |
| @deva[किन्विद्] | Whether, how |
| @deva[किल] | Verily, indeed, assuredly |
| @deva[किम्] | What then, how much more, &c. |
| @deva[कुतः] | Whence, from where? |
| @deva[कुत्र] | Where, in which place? |
| @deva[कुत्राचित्] | Somewhere, anywhere |
| @deva[कुविद्] | Much |
| @deva[कृषत्] | In the best manner |
| @deva[कृपत] | In a good manner |
| @deva[कृत्तम्] | Enough, no more of |
| @deva[केवलम्] | Only, merely, simply |
| @deva[क] | Whither, where? |
| @deva[कञ्चित्] | In some place |
| @deva[न कञ्चित्] | Nowhere |
| @deva[खलु] | Certainly, surely, indeed |
| @deva[चिरम्] | A long time. The singular of any of the oblique cases of this word may be used adverbially in the sense of 'long', 'for a long time', as @deva[चिरेण], @deva[चिराय], &c. |
| @deva[चिररात्राय] | For a period of many nights, long |
| @deva[जातु] | Perhaps, sometimes |
| @deva[जोषम्] | Silently |

(The list continues with many more adverbs...)

## III. PARTICLES

The particles are either used as expletives or intensives; some of these are @deva[किल], @deva[खलु], @deva[च], @deva[ह], @deva[इ], @deva[वै], @deva[हि], &c.

The following particles are used with certain words—

**@deva[अह]**—@deva[अद्भुतम्] 'a wonder'.

**@deva[का]**—@deva[कापुरुषः] 'a bad man', @deva[कौष्णम्] 'luke-warm', @deva[काजलम्] 'a little water'.

**@deva[कु]**—@deva[कुकृत्यं] 'a bad deed'.

**@deva[चन]**, **@deva[चित्]**—@deva[किञ्चित्], @deva[कश्चित्], @deva[कञ्चन], @deva[किञ्चन] &c.

**@deva[न]**—is generally changed to @deva[अ] or @deva[अन्] when prefixed to words beginning with a consonant or a vowel respectively. This particle has six different senses:[^6] (1) @deva[सादृश्यं] 'likeness' or 'resemblance'; as @deva[अब्राह्मणः] 'one not a Brāhmaṇa, but resembling a Brāhmaṇa' (wearing the sacred thread, &c.) i. e. 'a Kṣhatriya or a Vaiśya' (2) @deva[अभाव] 'absence or negation'; @deva[अज्ञानं] 'the absence of knowledge', (3) @deva[अन्यत्व] 'difference from'; as @deva[अयं अपटः] 'this is something different from a cloth' i. e. 'a jar' or so; (4) @deva[अल्पता] 'littleness' or 'smallness'; as @deva[अनुदरा कन्या] 'a girl having a slender waist'; (5) @deva[अप्राशस्त्य] 'badness, unfitness', &c.; @deva[अकार्यं] 'something unfit to be done', @deva[अकालः] 'an improper time, not a favourable opportunity', and lastly (6) @deva[विरोध] or 'opposition'; @deva[अनीतिः] 'non-morality'; 'immorality', @deva[असुरः] 'opposed to a god' i. e 'a demon'.

**@deva[म]**—is generally used as an expletive. Used with a form of the present tense of a verb, it gives it the sense of the past tense; as @deva[भवति स्म] i. e. @deva[अभवत्]. When used with the particle @deva[मा] it has an intensive force; as @deva[मा स्म शोकं मनः कुर्याः] &c.

**@deva[स्विद्]**—is added to @deva[कि] and other indeclinables and asks a question or implies a doubt; @deva[किन्विद्], @deva[अहोस्विद्], &c.

**@deva[स्वी]**—is used with @deva[कृ] and its derivatives like a preposition in the sense of 'acceptance'; @deva[स्वीकारः], @deva[स्वीकृतम्], &c.

## IV. CONJUNCTIONS

The following are the principal conjunctions in Sanskrit:—

**(a) Copulative:** @deva[अथ], @deva[अथो], @deva[उत], @deva[च], @deva[किञ्च], &c.

**(b) Disjunctive:** @deva[वा], @deva[वा]...@deva[वा], &c.

**(c) Adversative:** @deva[अथवा], @deva[तु], @deva[किन्तु], @deva[किन्वा], &c.

**(d) Conditional:** @deva[चेत्], @deva[यदि], @deva[यदापि], @deva[नेत्], @deva[नोचेत्], @deva[वेद्] (used in sacrificial ceremonies), &c.

**(e) Causal:** @deva[हि], @deva[तत्], @deva[तेन], &c.

**(f) Interrogative:** @deva[आहो], @deva[अहोस्विद्], @deva[उत], @deva[उताहो], @deva[कि], @deva[किन्नु], @deva[किन्तु], @deva[किञ्चित्], @deva[नञु], @deva[नघा], @deva[नु], &c.

**(g) Affirmatives and negatives:** @deva[अहो], @deva[अथ किम्], @deva[आम्], @deva[अद्धा] &c.

**(h) Conjunctions of time:** @deva[यावत्]—@deva[तावत्], @deva[यदा], @deva[तदा] &c.

**(i)** @deva[अथ] and @deva[इति] are used to mark the beginning and the close of a work respectively.

## V. INTERJECTIONS

"The interjection is not properly a part of speech, as it does not enter into the construction of sentences. It is a sudden exclamation prompted by some strong feeling or emotion. There are various utterances suited to the different emotions of the mind":—Prof. Bain.

**(a)** These are—@deva[अः], @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ए], @deva[ऐ], @deva[ओ], @deva[अहो], @deva[अहहो], @deva[अहो], @deva[बत], @deva[ह], @deva[हा], @deva[हाहा], &c. expressive of wonder, grief or regret, &c.

**(b)** @deva[धिक्], @deva[धिक्] &c. expressive of contempt.

**(c)** @deva[हा], @deva[बत], &c. expressing sorrow, dejection, &c.

**(d)** @deva[हा], @deva[हाहा], @deva[हन्त] showing grief.

**(e)** @deva[आ], @deva[हुम्], @deva[हुम्], &c. expressive of anger, contempt, &c.

**(f)** @deva[हन्त], &c. expressive of joy.

**(g)** There are some interjections used to call attention. Of these,

**(1)** some show respect; such as @deva[अरे], @deva[अये], @deva[अहो], @deva[अहो], @deva[बत], @deva[उ], @deva[ए], @deva[ओ], @deva[भोसु], @deva[भोः], @deva[हंहो], @deva[हे], @deva[हे], @deva[हो], &c.

**(2)** and others, disrespect or contempt; as @deva[अड], @deva[अरे], @deva[अबे], @deva[रे], @deva[रेरे], @deva[अरेरे] &c.

**(3)** The exclamations @deva[श्रौषट्], @deva[वौषट्] and @deva[वषट्] are used when offering oblations to gods or manes; and

**(4)** @deva[स्वाहा] and @deva[स्वधा] when offering oblations to gods and manes respectively.

[^1]: @deva[अष्टौ मुहूर्ता दिवसाता दश पूर्व च सर्वदा। तत्राप्येषो मुहूर्तो यः स कालः कृतघ्नः स्मृतः॥]

[^2]: @deva[सदृशं त्रिषु लिङ्गेषु सर्वासु च विभक्तिषु । वचनेषु च सर्वेषु यन् न व्येति तदव्ययम् ॥] @deva[स्वरादिनिपातमव्ययम्] । Pān. I, 1. 37.

[^3]: @deva[धात्वर्थं भावयते कञ्चित्कञ्चिन्नानुवर्तते । तस्मै विहितस्तस्य उपसर्गागतिविक्रिया ॥] Cf. also Sid. Kau. @deva[उपसर्गेण धात्वर्थो बलादन्यत्र नीयते । प्रहाराहारसंहारविहारपरिहारवत् ॥] Some think that prepositions have no meaning of their own, but they simply bring to light when prefixed to roots their hidden senses. (cf. Sis. X, 15).

[^4]: Cf. @deva[कारणेन अधिगच्छति करणं], &c. Shārīra Bhāshya. According to the grammarian Bhāguri the prepositions @deva[अधि] and @deva[अव] may optionally lose their @deva[अ]—@deva[वावे भागौरिरहोगमबागोरुपसर्गेर्भे:] (Sid.Kau.,...)

[^5]: @deva[अच्छगतेर्यदेषु] । Pāṇ. 1. 4. 69.

[^6]: These are given in the following couplet:— @deva[तद्सादृश्यभावश्च तदन्यत्वं तदल्पता । अप्राशस्त्यं विरोधश्च नञार्थाः षट् प्रकीर्तिताः ॥]

rules.title: Words Feminine and Neuter
rules.body: @deva[स्थूण]—@deva[णा] 'the post or pillar of a house', @deva[अर्चिस्] 'light', and @deva[लक्ष्]—@deva[क्षा] 'one hundred thousand' (according to some n. also).

rules.title: Definition of Avyaya (Indeclinable)
rules.body:
That in an Avyaya whose form remaining the same in all the genders, numbers and cases, undergoes no change.[^1] The Avyayas may be divided into simple and compound ones. The latter are treated of in the chapter on compounds (Avyayībhāvas and a few Bahuvrīhis and Tatpurusha).

[^1]: @deva[सदृशं त्रिषु लिङ्गेषु सर्वासु च विभक्तिषु । वचनेषु च सर्वेषु यन् न व्येति तदव्ययम् ॥] @deva[स्वरादिनिपातमव्ययम्] । Pān. I, 1. 37.

rules.title: Five Categories of Indeclinables
rules.body:
## Five Categories of Indeclinables

The indeclinables comprise:
1. (I) Prepositions
2. (II) Adverbs
3. (III) Particles
4. (IV) Conjunctions
5. (V) Interjections

rules.title: Nouns with Single Inflection Treated as Indeclinables
rules.body:
## Nouns with Single Inflection Treated as Indeclinables

Besides these there are in Sanskrit a few nouns having one inflection only which are treated as indeclinable (nipātas); e.g. @deva[अन्यत्] 'another (reason)', @deva[अस्तम्] 'setting', @deva[अस्ति] 'that exists', @deva[ओम्] 'the well-known sacred syllable om', @deva[चनस्] 'satisfaction, food', @deva[चाहु] 'coaxing', @deva[नमस्] 'a bow', @deva[नास्ति] 'non-existence', @deva[भूर्] 'the earth', @deva[भुवर्] 'the sky', @deva[पदि] 'the dark fortnight', @deva[यशस्] 'happiness', @deva[शुक्ल] or @deva[शुक्लि] 'the bright fortnight', @deva[संवत्] 'a year', @deva[स्वाहा] 'food offered to gods', @deva[स्वधा] 'food offered to the manes', @deva[स्वर्] 'heaven', @deva[स्वस्ति] 'happiness' &c.

---

## I. PREPOSITIONS

rules.title: Definition and Function of Prepositions (Upasarga)
rules.body:
## Definition and Function of Prepositions (Upasarga)

A preposition, styled 'Upasarga or Gati,' in Sanskrit is an indeclinable word, having an independent meaning and prefixed to verbs and also to their derivatives. These prepositions modify, intensify and sometimes totally alter the senses of roots[^1]:

### Examples

- @deva[प्रहृ] 'to strike'
- @deva[आहृ] 'to eat, to perform as a sacrifice'
- @deva[संहृ] 'to contract'
- @deva[विहृ] 'to sport'
- @deva[परिहृ] 'to avoid', &c.

Sometimes they are prefixed without any alteration in the sense.

[^1]: @deva[धात्वर्थं भावयते कञ्चित्कञ्चिन्नानुवर्तते । तस्मै विहितस्तस्य उपसर्गागतिविक्रिया] Cf. also Sid. Kau. @deva[उपसर्गेण धात्वर्थो बलादन्यत्र नीयते । प्रहाराहारसंहारविहारपरिहारवत्] Some think that prepositions have no meaning of their own, but they simply bring to light when prefixed to roots their hidden senses (cf. Śiś. X.15).

rules.title: List of Common Sanskrit Prepositions
rules.body:
## List of Common Sanskrit Prepositions

The following are the prepositions (upasargas) commonly prefixed to roots:

### @deva[अति]

'beyond, over'; @deva[अतिक्रम] 'overstepping' or 'going beyond', @deva[अतिसर्जन] 'a gift', &c.

### @deva[अधि]

'over, above', &c.; @deva[अधिगम] 'going up, acquisition', @deva[अधिकार] 'high office or power', @deva[अधिक्षेप] 'censure', &c.

### @deva[अनु]

'after, behind, along', &c.; @deva[अनुक्रमण] 'following', @deva[अनुच्छोति] 'imitation', @deva[अनुग्रह] 'favour', &c.

### @deva[अप]

'away from, away'; @deva[अपनयन] 'the act of taking away', @deva[अपहृ] 'to plunder, seize', &c., @deva[अपकार] 'harm, wrong', &c.

### @deva[अपि]

(sometimes @deva[पि]) 'near to', 'over', 'taking to', &c.; @deva[अपिगम्] 'to be resolved into or reduced to', @deva[अपिधान] or @deva[पिधान] 'a covering', @deva[अपिधा] 'destruction', &c.[^1]

This prep. is more commonly used as an independent adverb having a cumulative force in classical Sanskrit.

### @deva[अभि]

'towards, near to', &c.; @deva[अभिगम्] 'to go towards', @deva[अभिजन] 'noble descent or family', @deva[अभिमान] 'self-respect', @deva[अभिरुच्] 'to defeat', &c.

### @deva[अव]

(sometimes @deva[व]; see @deva[अपि] and note) 'away, down', &c.; @deva[अव] or @deva[वगाह] 'to plunge into', @deva[अवतार] 'descent', @deva[अवगत] 'reproached', @deva[अवमन्] 'to disrespect', &c.

### @deva[आ]

'up to, towards, all round, a little', &c.; @deva[आच्छाद्] 'to cover all round', @deva[आकार] 'form or shape (within due bounds)', @deva[आकाश] 'that which shines all round' i.e. 'the ether'; @deva[आकम्प] 'to shake a little', &c.

### @deva[उद्]

'upon', &c.; @deva[उद्गम्] 'to go up', @deva[उद्यम] 'industry', @deva[उत्सर्ग] 'pouring out, hence a gift, a general rule', &c.

### @deva[उप]

'near to, towards, by the side of', &c.; @deva[उपगम्] 'to go near to', @deva[उपकृति] f. 'an obligation', @deva[उपरति] f. 'death', @deva[उपस्थान] 'praise, worship', @deva[उपमिति] f. 'comparison', &c.

### @deva[दुस्]

'bad, hard to be done', &c.; @deva[दुराचार] 'bad conduct', @deva[दुष्कर] 'hard to be done', @deva[दुःसह] 'difficult to be borne', &c.

### @deva[नि]

'in, into, great, opposed to', &c.; @deva[निड्] 'to insult', @deva[निकेत] 'a house', @deva[निचय] 'a heap, a great collection', @deva[निपीत] 'drunk in', @deva[निदेश] 'a command', &c.

### @deva[निस्]

'out of, away from, without', &c.; @deva[निःसृ] 'to issue out', @deva[निर्गम] 'a passage out', @deva[निर्दोष] 'out of i.e. free from blame', @deva[निःशङ्क] 'without doubt', &c.

### @deva[परा]

'away, back, opposed to', &c.; @deva[पराकृ] 'to reject, to despise', @deva[पराक्रम] 'to act bravely', @deva[परागत] 'gone away', @deva[पराञ्च] 'turn back', @deva[पराजय] 'what is opposed to victory, defeat', &c.

### @deva[परि]

'all round, about', &c.; @deva[परिधा] 'to place all round i.e. to put on or wear', @deva[परिधि] 'a wall &c. that surrounds', @deva[परिणाम] 'ripening, maturity', @deva[परिगणना] 'counting all round, i.e. a complete enumeration', &c.

### @deva[प्रति]

'towards, back, in return, in opposition to', &c.; @deva[प्रतिगम्] 'to go towards', @deva[प्रतिभाषण] 'a speech in return, an answer', @deva[प्रतिविकार] 'an act in opposition to i.e. a remedy', &c.

### @deva[वि]

'apart, separate from, reverse to', &c.; @deva[विचल्] 'to move apart', @deva[वियुज्] 'to be separated', @deva[विक्री] opp. of @deva[क्री] 'to sell', 'to buy', &c.; sometimes this has an intensive force.

### @deva[सम्]

'together with, excellent, full', &c.; @deva[संगम्] 'to be united', @deva[संस्कार] 'perfection', @deva[संस्कृति] 'refinement', @deva[संहार] 'destruction, contraction', &c.

### @deva[सु]

'well, thoroughly', &c. (in this sense it is opposed to @deva[दुस्]); @deva[सुकृत] 'done well', @deva[सुशासित] 'thoroughly trained, well governed', &c. It is also used in the sense of 'very, excessively': @deva[सुमहत्] 'very great'.

[^1]: Cf. @deva[कारणेन अपिगच्छति करण], &c. Śārīra Bhāṣya. According to the grammarian Bhāguri the prepositions @deva[अपि] and @deva[अव] may optionally lose their @deva[अ]—@deva[वावे भागुरिरहोगमवागोरुपसर्गेर्भे] (Sid. Kau.)

rules.title: Combination of Multiple Prepositions
rules.body:
## Combination of Multiple Prepositions

Two or more of these prepositions may also be combined and prefixed; e.g. @deva[अभिनिविश्] 'to enter into with resolution', @deva[समुपगम्] 'to come in close contact with', &c.

rules.title: Verb Ellipsis After Prepositions in Compounds
rules.body:
## Verb Ellipsis After Prepositions in Compounds

When used in a compound the verb may be omitted after the prepositions @deva[अति], @deva[अधि], @deva[अनु], @deva[अप], @deva[अव], @deva[अभि], @deva[उप], @deva[परि] and @deva[प्रति]; @deva[अतिक्रान्तो मालां] = @deva[अतिमाल], &c. Vide @ref[232].

rules.title: Other Words Used Prepositionally (Gati)
rules.body:
## Other Words Used Prepositionally (Gati)

There are several other words, also styled Gati by Sanskrit grammarians, used prepositionally. These are prefixed to certain roots only. We give the more important of them below.

### (a) @deva[अच्छ]

'towards' is prefixed to @deva[वद्] and to roots implying motion[^1]; @deva[अच्छगम्य] = @deva[गत्वा] 'going near', @deva[अच्छपतत्] 'flying towards', @deva[अच्छूद्य] 'having spoken to'.

### (b) Words Prefixed to @deva[कृ]

**(1)** @deva[अन्वाञ्च्] 'giving strength to the weak', @deva[अलम्] in the sense of 'decorating', @deva[ऊर्ती], @deva[उरती], @deva[उत्ती] all implying 'assent, acceptance or promise', @deva[खात्] and similar imitative sounds, @deva[असत्] and @deva[सत्] in the sense of 'dishonouring or honouring', @deva[प्रास्त] denoting 'fastening', &c. are prefixed to @deva[कृ]; @deva[अन्वाञ्चकरण], @deva[ऊर्तीकरण], @deva[असत्कार], @deva[खात्कृत्य], @deva[खाङ्कृत्य], @deva[प्रास्तकरण], &c.

**(2)** @deva[नमस्], @deva[भागु], @deva[निष्पा], @deva[वशो], @deva[साक्षात्] and some other words may be optionally prefixed to @deva[कृ] or remain separate; @deva[नमस्कार], @deva[वशोकृ] or @deva[वशो कृ] 'to bring under subjection', @deva[साक्षात् कृ] or @deva[साक्षात्कृ] 'to make manifest', &c.

### (c) @deva[अन्तर्]

is prefixed to roots meaning 'to go', @deva[धा], @deva[भू], and similar roots; @deva[अन्तरित्य] 'having disappeared', @deva[अन्तर्धान] 'disappearance', @deva[अन्तर्भूत], &c.

### (d) @deva[अस्तम्]

is prefixed to roots implying motion; @deva[अस्तमय] 'setting', @deva[अस्तंगत] 'set', @deva[अस्तंनी] 'to cause to set, to lead to destruction', &c.

### (e) @deva[आविस्], @deva[प्रादुस्], and @deva[तिरस्]

@deva[आविस्] and @deva[प्रादुस्] are prefixed to @deva[कृ], @deva[अस्] and @deva[भू] and @deva[तिरस्] to @deva[भू], @deva[धा] and similar roots, and optionally to @deva[कृ]; @deva[आविष्करण], @deva[आविर्भवन] 'manifestation', @deva[प्रादुर्—आविर्भूत] 'manifested', &c.; @deva[तिरोभूय] 'vanishing out of sight', @deva[तिरोधान] 'disappearance', &c.

### (f) @deva[पुरस्]

is prefixed to @deva[कृ], @deva[भू], @deva[गम्], &c.; @deva[पुरस्कृत] 'placed before, headed by', @deva[पुरोगत] 'gone in the front', &c.

[^1]: @deva[अच्छगतेर्यदेषु] Pāṇ. I.4.69.

rules.title: Nouns as Gati with Chvi-Derivatives
rules.body:
## Nouns as Gati with Chvi-Derivatives

Several nouns, substantive and adjective, may be prefixed to the roots @deva[कृ], @deva[भू], and @deva[अस्] to form what are called in Sanskrit 'chvi-derivatives' (vide chap. IX. Sec. III.). @deva[कृष्णीकरण] = @deva[कृष्णीकरण]; @deva[धनीभूत] = @deva[धनीभूत]. Such nouns are also termed 'Gati.'

rules.title: Taddhita Affix -sāt Used Prepositionally
rules.body:
## Taddhita Affix -sāt Used Prepositionally

Like prepositions may be further used the words to which the Taddhita affix @deva[सात्] is affixed; @deva[अग्निसात्कृ] 'to consign to flames'; @deva[भस्मसात्कृत] 'reduced to ashes', @deva[राजसात्कृत] 'made over to the king', &c. (vide p. 216.)

---

## II. ADVERBS

rules.title: Formation of Adverbs from Various Cases

rules.title: Particles as Expletives and Intensives
rules.body:
## Particles as Expletives and Intensives

The particles are either used as expletives or intensives; some of these are @deva[किल], @deva[खलु], @deva[च], @deva[ह], @deva[इ], @deva[वै], @deva[हि], &c.

---

## III. PARTICLES

rules.title: Particles Used with Certain Words
rules.body:
## Particles Used with Certain Words

The following particles are used with certain words:

### @deva[अह]

@deva[अद्भुतम्] 'a wonder'

### @deva[का]

@deva[कापुरुष] 'a bad man', @deva[कौष्णम्] 'luke-warm', @deva[काजलम्] 'a little water'

### @deva[कु]

@deva[कुकृत्यम्] 'a bad deed'

### @deva[चन] / @deva[चित्]

@deva[किञ्चित्], @deva[कश्चित्], @deva[कञ्चन], @deva[किञ्चन], &c.

### @deva[न]

is generally changed to @deva[अ] or @deva[अन्] when prefixed to words beginning with a consonant or a vowel respectively. This particle has six different senses:[^1]

1. **@deva[सादृश्य]** 'likeness' or 'resemblance'; as @deva[अब्राह्मण] 'one not a Brāhmaṇa, but resembling a Brāhmaṇa' (wearing the sacred thread, &c.) i.e. 'a Kṣatriya or a Vaiśya'
2. **@deva[अभाव]** 'absence or negation'; @deva[अज्ञान] 'the absence of knowledge'
3. **@deva[अन्यत्व]** 'difference from'; as @deva[अयं अपट] 'this is something different from a cloth' i.e. 'a jar' or so
4. **@deva[अल्पता]** 'littleness' or 'smallness'; as @deva[अनुदरा कन्या] 'a girl having a slender waist'
5. **@deva[अप्राशस्त्य]** 'badness, unfitness', &c.; @deva[अकार्यम्] 'something unfit to be done', @deva[अकाल] 'an improper time, not a favourable opportunity'
6. **@deva[विरोध]** or 'opposition'; @deva[अनीति] 'non-morality; immorality', @deva[असुर] 'opposed to a god' i.e. 'a demon'

### @deva[म]

is generally used as an expletive. Used with a form of the present tense of a verb, it gives it the sense of the past tense; as @deva[भवति स्म] i.e. @deva[अभवत्]. When used with the particle @deva[मा] it has an intensive force; as @deva[मा स्म शोकं मनः कुर्यात्], &c.

### @deva[स्विद्]

is added to @deva[कि] and other indeclinables and asks a question or implies a doubt; @deva[किन्विद्], @deva[अहोस्विद्], &c.

### @deva[स्वी]

is used with @deva[कृ] and its derivatives like a preposition in the sense of 'acceptance'; @deva[स्वीकार], @deva[स्वीकृतम्], &c.

[^1]: These are given in the following couplet: @deva[तद्सादृश्यभावश्च तदन्यत्वं तदल्पता । अप्राशस्त्यं विरोधश्च नञार्थाः षट् प्रकीर्तिताः]

---

## IV. CONJUNCTIONS

rules.title: Principal Conjunctions in Sanskrit
Interjections Expressing Emotions
rules.body:
## Interjections Expressing Emotions

"The interjection is not properly a part of speech, as it does not enter into the construction of sentences. It is a sudden exclamation prompted by some strong feeling or emotion. There are various utterances suited to the different emotions of the mind": Prof. Bain.

### (a) Wonder, Grief, or Regret

These are @deva[अः], @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ए], @deva[ऐ], @deva[ओ], @deva[अहो], @deva[अहहो], @deva[अहह], @deva[बत], @deva[ह], @deva[हा], @deva[हाहा], &c. expressive of wonder, grief or regret, &c.

### (b) Contempt

@deva[धिक्], @deva[धिक्], &c. expressive of contempt.

### (c) Sorrow, Dejection

@deva[हा], @deva[बत], &c. expressing sorrow, dejection, &c.

### (d) Grief

@deva[हा], @deva[हाहा], @deva[हन्त] showing grief.

### (e) Anger, Contempt

@deva[आ], @deva[हुम्], @deva[हुम्], &c. expressive of anger, contempt, &c.

### (f) Joy

@deva[हन्त], &c. expressive of joy.

### (g) Calling Attention

There are some interjections used to call attention. Of these:

**(1)** Some show respect; such as @deva[अरे], @deva[अये], @deva[अहो], @deva[अहह], @deva[बत], @deva[उ], @deva[ए], @deva[ओ], @deva[भोस्], @deva[भोः], @deva[हंहो], @deva[हे], @deva[हे], @deva[हो], &c.

**(2)** And others, disrespect or contempt; as @deva[अड], @deva[अरे], @deva[अबे], @deva[रे], @deva[रेरे], @deva[अरेरे], &c.

**(3)** The exclamations @deva[श्रौषट्], @deva[वौषट्] and @deva[वषट्] are used when offering oblations to gods or manes; and

**(4)** @deva[स्वाहा] and @deva[स्वधा] when offering oblations to gods and manes respectively.

---

## Chapter XII

**CONJUGATION OF VERBS**

rules.title: Introduction to Verbs: Types, Tenses, Moods, and Voices
rules.body:
There are in Sanskrit—

**(a)** Two kinds of verbs, Primitive and Derivative.

**(b)** Six Tenses (@deva[कालः]) and four Moods (@deva[अर्थः]) which are as follow:—[^1]

| TENSES | TECHNICAL NAME | MOODS | TECHNICAL NAME |
|--------|----------------|-------|----------------|
| @deva[वर्तमानः] or Present | @deva[लट्] | @deva[आज्ञा] or Imperative | @deva[लोट्] |
| @deva[भूतः] or Aorist | @deva[लुङ्] | @deva[विधि] or Potential | @deva[विधिलिङ्] |
| @deva[अनद्यतनभूतः] or Imperfect | @deva[लङ्] | @deva[आशीः] or Benedictive | @deva[आशीर्लिङ्] |
| @deva[परोक्षभूतः] or Perfect | @deva[लिट्] | @deva[सत्ता] or Conditional | @deva[लृङ्] |
| @deva[अनद्यतन-भविष्यत्] or 1st Future | @deva[लृट्] | | |
| @deva[भविष्यत्] or 2nd Future | @deva[लुट्] | | |

@deva[लेट्] or the Subjunctive is used only in the Veda and is therefore termed 'The Vedic Subjunctive.'

**Note:**—The ten tenses and moods are technically called the ten Lakaras in Sanskrit grammars.

**(c)** Three Voices (@deva[प्रयोगः]), the Active Voice (@deva[कर्तरिप्रयोगः]) as @deva[पचति], the Passive Voice (@deva[कर्मणिप्रयोगः]), as @deva[पच्यते पक्ति यज्ञः], and the Impersonal Construction (@deva[भावेप्रयोगः]) @deva[तेषां गम्यते].

**(d)** Two sets of personal terminations; the one called 'Parasmaipada' or the Verb Active:—as @deva[भवति] 'he goes'; and the other 'Ātmanepada' or the verb Middle:—as @deva[वर्तते] 'he is'. Some verbs take the former, others the latter, while others take either. Several roots again, though Parasmai, become Ātmanepada in some of the senses they take, or when certain prepositions are prefixed, or in particular tenses. These will be considered in treating of Ātmanepada and Parasmaipada.

**(e)** Derivative verbs are those formed from nouns and those primitive verbs which exist in the language, while primitive verbs are those which are derived from roots given in the Dhātupāṭhas or lexicon of roots.

**(f)** Primitive verbs are conjugated in the Active and Middle, and may be conjugated in the ten tenses and moods given above.

**(g)** Primitive verbs are conjugated in six different ways or conjugations:—

[^1]: These technical names are given in the following Kārikā, @deva[लट् वर्तमाने लेट् वेदे भूते लुङ् लङ् लिटस्तथा । विध्याशिषोर्लिङ् लिङ्लोटौ लुट् लृट् लृङ् च भविष्यति ॥] This terminology of Pāṇini, it will be seen, is artificial. Other grammarians use different names. The ten Lakaras of Pāṇini are according to their nomenclature as follow.—@deva[वर्तती] (@deva[हतिः]), @deva[अवर्तती], @deva[हर्तती], @deva[परोक्षा], @deva[भविष्यती], @deva[भविष्यत्ती], @deva[पञ्चमी], @deva[षष्ठी], @deva[प्रियातिरूपी] and @deva[आशीः]— 'Apte's Guide'.

rules.title: Number and Person in Verbs
rules.body: Primitive verbs or roots are those which originally exist in the language, while derivative verbs are those which may be derived from a parent stock-- a root or a noun.

rules.title: Special Tenses vs. Common Tenses (@[vikaraṇa] vs. @[sakārānta lakāras])
rules.body:
Every verb, in Sanskrit, whether primitive or derivative, is conjugated in the ten tenses and moods given above.

(a). Transitive verbs are conjugated in the Active and Passive voices and intransitive verbs are conjugated in the Active and the Impersonal forms.

rules.title: Conjugation Classification Marker
rules.body: In each tense and mood, there are three numbers, singular, dual, and plural, with three persons in each.

rules.title: Special vs. General Lakāras and Verb Bases
rules.body:
In four of the tenses and moods given above, viz. the Present, the Imperfect, the Imperative and the Potential, the verbs undergo peculiar modifications (@[vikaraṇa]), and these modifications are therefore called Conjugational (@[sārvadhātuka])[^1] or special tenses and moods; and the remaining Non-Conjugational (@[ardhadhātuka]) or general. In the former the characteristic marks and terminations of each are mostly added to a special base formed from the root in various ways, while in the latter they are combined with the root itself.

**(a)** The base (@deva[अङ्ग]) of a root is that form which it assumes before the personal terminations.

[^1]: Strictly the term Sārvadhātuka (belonging to the whole of a root) is given by Pāṇini to the terminations of all tenses in Parasmaipada as opposed to Ātmanepada; also, to the Imperative, the Benedictive, and to the affixes distinguished by @deva[छ] or @deva[श्] denoting agency (kṛt): thus various conjugational signs of the Lakāras (i. e. except that of the @deva[लृट्-लिङ्]), and the terminations of the Present Participle, etc., all in the Ātmanepada terminations are called Sārvadhātuka. Derivative moods and tenses as the Derivative verbs, and its various conjugations, see sūtra of @ref[385] to form the several bases, and a few denominatives, the affixes @deva[झय्], @deva[छु] etc. The other conjugational signs of the lakāras (i. e. the @deva[लृङ्-लिङ्] and the @deva[शतृ], and the Passive and the Frequentative conjugations) and the signs @deva[क्त], @deva[क्त्वा], and other affixes which show that they must be followed by Ātmanepada terminations; also, others are called Ardhadhātuka, the remaining Non-Conjugational (@deva[सकारान्त]).

rules.title: Parasmaipada vs. Ātmanepada Usage
rules.body:
When a root is capable of taking either pada, the Parasmaipada (lit: word for another) should be used when the fruit or result of the action of the verb accrues to any other person or thing than the agent, and the Ātmanepada (lit. word for self) when it refers to the agent. Thus @deva[देवदत्तः यजति] will mean 'Devadatta sacrifices for another (his Yajamāna);' while @deva[देवदत्तः यजते] will mean 'Devadatta sacrifices for himself.'

## SECTION I. ACTIVE VOICE

## I. CONJUGATIONAL OR SPECIAL TENSES AND MOODS

**PRESENT, IMPERFECT, IMPERATIVE and POTENTIAL**

rules.title: Ten Conjugational Classes
rules.body: With reference to the various moods the verbs are divided into ten conjugational classes by Sanskrit grammarians, each class being denominated after the root which begins it viz. (1) @deva[भ्वादि] (2) @deva[अदादि] (3) @deva[जुहोत्यादि], (4) @deva[दिवादि], (5) @deva[स्वादि], (6) @deva[तुदादि], (7) @deva[रुधादि], (8) @deva[तनादि] (9) @deva[क्र्यादि] and (10) @deva[चुरादि].

rules.title: Primitive vs. Derivative Roots
rules.body: The roots contained in the first nine classes and a few of the tenth are primitive roots, while almost all roots of the tenth class, the Causals, Desideratives, Frequentatives, Denominatives, and the roots @[gup], @[dhūp], @[vicch], @[paṇ], @[pan], @[ṛt], and @[kam], are comprised under the head of Derivative roots.

rules.title: Two Groups of Conjugational Classes
rules.body:
These ten classes may again be conveniently divided into two groups, the first comprising the 1st, 4th, 6th and 10th classes, and the second the remaining. In the first the base ends in @deva[अ] and remains unchanged throughout; while in the second it does not end in @deva[अ] and is changeable.

## I. GROUP 1. ROOTS WITH UNCHANGEABLE BASES

(1st, 4th, 6th and 10th classes).

rules.title: First Class (भ्वादि) - Addition of अ (शप्)
Fourth Class (दिवादि) - Addition of य (श्यन्)
rules.body: @deva[य] (@deva[श्यन्]) is added on to the final of a root of the Fourth or @deva[दिवादि] class before the terminations; the radical vowel remains unchanged; e. g. @deva[तुष्+ति=तुष्+य+ति=तुष्यति].

rules.title: Sixth Class (तुदादि) - Addition of अ with Vowel Changes
rules.body: @deva[अ] is added on to the roots of the sixth or @deva[तुदादि] class before which the penultimate vowel remains unchanged, and the final @deva[इ], @deva[उ], short or long, @deva[ऋ] and @deva[ॠ] are changed to @deva[इय], @deva[उव], @deva[रिय] and @deva[रीय] respectively; e. g. @deva[क्षिप्+ति=क्षिप्+अ+ति=क्षिपति]; @deva[धु+ति=धुव+अ+ति=धुवति]; @deva[रि+अ+ति=रियति]; @deva[कृ+अ+ते=क्रियते]; @deva[तृ+अ+ति=तिर्+अ+ति=तिरति], &c.

rules.title: Tenth Class (चुरादि) - Addition of अय with Vṛddhi
rules.body:
Roots of the tenth or @deva[चुरादि] class[^1] add @deva[अय] before the personal terminations. Before @deva[अय] (1) the penultimate short vowel (except @deva[अ]) takes the Guṇa substitute; and the final vowel and the penultimate @deva[अ] not prosodially long, take their Vṛddhi substitute; e. g. @deva[चुर्+ति=चुर्+अय+ति=चोर्+अय+ति=चोरयति]; @deva[धू+अय+ति=धो+अय+ति=धाव+अय+ति=धावयति]; @deva[ताड्+अय+ति=ताड्+अय+ति=ताडयति]; but @deva[दण्ड्+अय+ति=दण्डयति], &c.

[^1]: This class contains a few primitive verbs, almost all the roots belonging to it being derivative; besides, all Causals and some Nominal verbs may be regarded as belonging to this class.

rules.title: Lengthening of अ and Elision Before Terminations
rules.body:
**(a)** The preceding @deva[अ] is lengthened before a conjugational termination beginning with a semivowel, a nasal or @deva[म्] or @deva[य्]; e. g. @deva[नयामि] &c.[^1]

**(b)** The final @deva[अ] is dropped before terminations beginning with @deva[अ]; @deva[नय+अन्ति=नयन्ति], &c.

The augment @deva[अ] is prefixed to roots in this tense. This @deva[अ] is replaced by @deva[आ] in the case of roots beginning with a vowel[^1]; this @deva[आ] forms Vṛddhi with an initial vowel; e. g. @deva[अ+ईक्ष्+त्=आ+ईक्ष्+अ+त्=ऐक्षत्]; similarly @deva[ईक्ष्]—@deva[ऐक्षत्]; @deva[उक्ष्]—@deva[औक्षत्]; @deva[ऊह्]—@deva[औहत्]; @deva[ऋच्छ्]—@deva[आर्च्छत्] &c.

**(a)** When a preposition (@deva[उपसर्ग]) is prefixed to a root, the augment @deva[अ] or @deva[आ] comes between the prep. and the root; e. g. @deva[हृ] with @deva[प्र], @deva[प्राहरत्].

rules.title: Changes of Long ऋ to इर् or उर्
rules.body:
The @deva[ऋ] (long) of a root, penultimate or final, when it does not take Guṇa or Vṛddhi, is changed to @deva[इर्], and to @deva[उर्] if a labial or @deva[व्] precedes; and the @deva[इ] or @deva[उ] is lengthened when @deva[इर्] or @deva[उर्] is followed by a consonant; e. g. @deva[कॄ] 4. P. 'to become old,' @deva[कीर्यति]; @deva[वृ] P. Â., @deva[कुर्वीत], &c; @deva[हृ] 6. P. @deva[हिरति], &c; here @deva[इ] does not become @deva[दीर्घ] as @deva[रि] is followed by @deva[अ]; @deva[चुर्] 10. P. Â. @deva[चोरयति]; @deva[अचोरयत्], @deva[अचोरीत्], &c.[^1]

[^1]: @deva[ऋत इदुतः] । @deva[उरण् रपरः] । Pāṇ. VII. 1. 100, 1. 1. 51. @deva[इतो वा] VI. Pāṇ. VII. 2. 17.

rules.title: Lengthening of Penultimate Vowels and Irregular First Class Roots
rules.body:
The penultimate @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ] or @deva[ऌ] of a root, followed by @deva[व्] or @deva[य्] is lengthened when a consonant follows;[^1] e. g. @deva[जृम्भ्] 1. Â. to measure out, @deva[जृम्भते]; @deva[छुर्] to sprinkle, @deva[फुर्] to act dishonestly, to be crooked, @deva[हुम्फ्] to faint, @deva[फुर्] to spread, to forget; @deva[दृम्भ्] to thunder, to shine; @deva[जुर्व्], @deva[तुर्व्], @deva[वुर्व्], @deva[दुर्व्], @deva[मुर्व्] all meaning to kill, @deva[लृम्भ्] to try, @deva[हुम्], &c., all Parasm. and belonging to the 1st class, lengthen their penultimate vowel; @deva[दिव्] 4. P. @deva[दीव्यति]; similarly @deva[तिर्] has @deva[तीर्यति], @deva[सिव्], @deva[शीव्यति], &c.

rules.title: Seven Roots Forming Bases Like Desiderative
rules.body: The following seven roots form their bases like the Desiderative in the senses indicated. These are:—@deva[किण्] to administer medicine, to treat as a patient, @deva[चिकीर्षति]; @deva[तिकित्] to censure, @deva[जुगुप्साते]; @deva[तिज्] to bear, to forgive, @deva[तितिक्षति]; @deva[विद्] to abhor, to act loathsomely, @deva[विविक्षति]; @deva[दीष्] to make straight, @deva[दीदिषति]-@deva[ते]; @deva[मान्] to reason, to think, @deva[मीमांसते]; @deva[शिष्] to sharpen, @deva[शीषाषति]-@deva[ते]. But @deva[किण्] to desire @deva[कैकषति]; to dwell, @deva[किकीषति]; @deva[दीष्] to cut @deva[दीदिषति]-@deva[ते] &c.

rules.title: Roots Adding Penultimate Nasal and Irregular Fourth Class Roots
rules.body:
There are a few roots which add a penultimate nasal in the Special Tenses and Moods necessarily; e. g. @deva[चिद्] to cut @deva[चिनत्ति], @deva[चन्] to go @deva[अचनत], @deva[पिष्] to roll into a ball @deva[पिण्डति], @deva[शुर्] to purify, to go @deva[शुञ्जति] &c; and a few more which do so optionally, e. g. @deva[दुह्] to be firm @deva[चुणत्ति]-@deva[दुहत्ति]; @deva[दुर्] or @deva[सुर्] to go @deva[सुरति]-@deva[सुञ्चति], @deva[उपसर्गरहितगम्] @deva[रुञ्जति]; @deva[लुच्] to pluck @deva[लुञ्जति], @deva[लुचति] all P; @deva[गुञ्ज्] Â. to hum @deva[गुञ्जते], @deva[गुनति]; @deva[गर्ज्] P. to roar @deva[गर्जति], @deva[गजति] and others less important.

## II. GROUP II.

## ROOTS WITH CHANGEABLE BASES.

**(2nd, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 8th, and 9th Classes.)**

rules.title: Personal Terminations for Group II (Changeable Bases)
rules.body:
## Terminations:—

### Parasmaipada.

The terminations of the Present, the Imperfect and the Imperative are the same as those of the first group, the termination of the 2nd per. sing. of the Imperative is @deva[हि]. The terminations of the Potential are as follow:—

| 2. | @deva[यास्] | @deva[यातम्] | @deva[यात] |
| 3. | @deva[यात्] | @deva[याताम्] | @deva[युस्] |

### Ātmanepada.

rules.title: Strong and Weak Terminations for Group II
rules.body:
The base of the roots of the 2nd group of Conjugational classes undergoes many modifications with regard to which the terminations are divided into sets, one set is called 'strong', the other 'weak.' The base taking the strong terminations may be called 'The strong base;' and that taking the weak ones 'The weak base'.

**(a)** The strong terminations are:—

The singulars of all persons of the Present and the Imperfect, the third person singular and all numbers of the first person of the Imperative, in the Parasmaipada, and all numbers of the first person of the Imperative in the Ātmanepada.

**(b)** The rest are weak.

rules.title: Guṇa Substitution Before Strong Terminations - Fifth, Eighth, and Ninth Classes
rules.body:
Before strong terminations the penultimate short and the final vowel of the base take their Guṇa substitute.

**Fifth, Eighth and Ninth classes**

rules.title: Addition of नु and उ to Fifth and Eighth Classes
rules.body:
@deva[नु] and @deva[उ] are added on to the roots of the 5th and 8th classes respectively before the terminations.[^1]

[^1]: @deva[स्वादिभ्यो नु:] । @deva[तनादिकृणोतः उ:] । Pāṇ. III. 1. 73, 79.

rules.title: Rules for Final नु Changes in Fifth Class
rules.body: The final @deva[नु] of the base is optionally dropped before @deva[म्] and @deva[व्] if it is not preceded by a conjunct consonant. It is changed to @deva[ण] before a weak termination beginning with a vowel, if preceded by a conjunct consonant and to @deva[न] in other cases. The @deva[हि] of the Imperative 2nd per. sing. is dropped after @deva[नु] not preceded by a conjunct consonant.

rules.title: Insertion of न in Ninth Class
rules.body:
In the ninth class @deva[न] is inserted between the root and the terminations. @deva[न] becomes @deva[ण] before the weak terminations beginning with a vowel, and @deva[नी] before the weak terminations beginning with a consonant.[^1]

[^1]: @deva[क्र्यादिभ्यो न:] @deva[।] Pāṇ. III. 1. 81.

rules.title: Fifth and Eighth Class Paradigms - Complete Conjugation Tables
rules.body:
**(a)** The penultimate nasal of a root is dropped before @deva[न] &c. as @deva[युनक्ति], @deva[युञ्जत], @deva[युञ्जन्ति] &c. from @deva[युज्] 'to arrange, put together.'

**(b)** In the case of roots ending in a consonant, the imperative second person singular termination is @deva[आन] instead of @deva[हि]; as @deva[सुनान] from @deva[सु] 'to press out juice'.

---

rules.title: Special Rule for ज्ञप् - न Not Changed to ण
rules.body: In the case of the root @deva[ज्ञप्] the @deva[न] of @deva[ना] is not changed to @deva[ण]; as @deva[ज्ञपनाति], @deva[ज्ञपनीतः], @deva[ज्ञपनन्ति], &c.

rules.title: Irregular Forms of ज्ञा and ज्या
rules.body: The roots @deva[ज्ञा] 'to know' and @deva[ज्या] 'to become old' assume the forms @deva[ज्ञ] and @deva[जि] respectively; as @deva[जानाति]-@deva[नीते], @deva[जिनाति], &c.

rules.title: Irregular Form of गृह - न Changed to ह
rules.body: The @deva[न] of @deva[गृह] is changed to @deva[ह]; as @deva[गृहाति]; @deva[अगृहाम्], @deva[अगृहीत], @deva[अगृहीम], &c. Imperf. 1st, pers.

The roots @deva[स्कु] 'to go by leaps, to raise,' @deva[स्तम्भ्] 'to obstruct,' @deva[स्तम्भ्] 'to stop,' @deva[स्कम्भ्] and @deva[स्कुम्भ्] 'to obstruct' belong to the 5th and 9th classes; as @deva[स्कुनोति], @deva[स्कुनुते], @deva[स्कुनाति], @deva[स्कुनीते], &c.

---

**Second, Third and Seventh Classes.**

rules.title: Special Sandhi Rules for Group II - Nine Rules
rules.body:
## Special rules of Sandhi of the finals of roots and the initial letters of terminations:—

**(1)** The ending @deva[आ] of a root takes its Vṛddhi substitute when followed by a consonantal strong termination; as @deva[आ+ति=आति].

**(2)** The final @deva[इ] or @deva[उ], short or long, of a root is changed to @deva[इय्] or @deva[उव्] before a vowel weak termination.

**(3)** The ending @deva[ह्] of roots is changed to @deva[ढ] when followed by any consonant, except a nasal or a semivowel, or by nothing; and that of roots beginning with @deva[द्] to @deva[त्] under the same circumstances.

**(4)** The initial @deva[त] or @deva[थ] of a termination is changed to @deva[च] after a soft aspirate (4th letter of a class).

**(5)** @deva[द्] or @deva[ध्] followed by @deva[स] is changed to @deva[त्].

**(6)** @deva[द्] and @deva[ध्] when followed by a consonant are changed to the nasal of the class to which the following consonant belongs, and to an anusvāra when followed by @deva[श्], @deva[ष्], @deva[स] or @deva[ह].

**(7)** The ending @deva[इ] of a root, short or long, not preceded by a conjunct consonant is changed to @deva[य] before vowel weak terminations, when the base consists of more than one syllable.

**(8)** The ending @deva[इ] of a root is optionally changed to @deva[र्] or Visarga in the Imperfect second pers. sing. and the ending @deva[द्] to @deva[त्] or @deva[ढ्] before the termination @deva[स्] and optionally before @deva[थ्].

**(9)** When a conjunct consonant having @deva[श्] or @deva[ष्] for its first member is at the end of a word or is followed by a consonant except a nasal or a semivowel, the @deva[श्] or @deva[ष] is dropped.

**N. B.**—The usual Sandhi rules i. e. those given in the 2nd and 3rd Chapters should be observed.

rules.title: Second Person Singular Imperative Termination हि
rules.body:
(I) The second person sing. termination of the Parasm. Imperative is @deva[हि] when the base ends in any consonant except a nasal or a semivowel; also in the case of the root @deva[यज्] 3. P. 'to sacrifice.'[^1]

[^1]: @deva[दुङालभौ हेचिः] @deva[।] Pāṇ. VI. 4. 101

rules.title: Dropping of स and त in Imperfect - Introduction to Second Class
rules.body:
The @deva[स] and @deva[त] of the Imperfect 2nd and 3rd per. sing. are dropped after a consonant.

---

**Second (or @deva[अदादि]) Class.**

rules.title: Direct Addition of Terminations in Second Class
rules.body: In this class the terminations are directly added to the root.

rules.title: Second Class Paradigm - या and Roots Ending in आ
rules.body:
