rules.title: Perfect Forms in Passive Voice
rules.body:
## Perfect Forms in Passive Voice

### (a) Reduplicative Perfect

The Reduplicative Perfect of a root in the Passive is formed like that of the Active, except in that the Auxiliary verb @deva[भू] is used instead of @deva[अस्].

**Example:**
@deva[क्रीयते]—@deva[क्रीयां बभूव] &c.

### (b) Periphrastic Perfect

The Periphrastic Perfect of the Passive does not differ from that of the Active, except in that the Auxiliary verb @deva[भू]—@deva[चकार] is used.

**Examples:**
- @deva[क्रीयते]—@deva[क्रीयां चकार]
- @deva[पूज्यते]—@deva[पूजां चकार]

And before it @deva[इस्] is used.

rules.title: Futures, Conditional and Benedictive in Passive
rules.body:
## Futures, Conditional and Benedictive in Passive

### (a) Forms in Impersonal Passive

The forms of the two Futures, Conditional and also the Benedictive (especially @deva[भावे]—Passive, briefly stated below.

### (b) Optional Forms with Vṛddhi

The Aorist optionally forms the Futures, Conditional as well as the Benedictive of the Passive by changing their vowels to Vṛddhi and then by @deva[आ] regarded to them invariably; in the case of roots ending in a vowel, the vowel is lengthened before @deva[इ]; and the @deva[य्] inserted between the root and this @deva[इ].

**Examples:**
- @deva[दा]—@deva[दायिष्यते], @deva[दायि], @deva[दायात्]
- @deva[वच्]—@deva[वच्य]@deva[च्यते]
- @deva[युज्]@deva[यते]—@deva[युज्+य]
- @deva[चकरे] 'to do'—@deva[कारिष्यते], @deva[कारि], @deva[कार्यात्]

@note[type=exception]{See @ref[468]; these forms strictly forbidden with them; only @deva[इस्] used.}

### (c) Additional Forms

The First Future, Conditional and the 5th Variety of the Aorist containing a nasal or a @deva[र्], @deva[त्], @deva[स्] of the Passive, &c.

rules.title: Aorist Passive Formation Rules
rules.body:
## Aorist Passive Formation Rules

### (a) Fourth, Fifth and Seventh Varieties

The Passive of the Aorist of roots belonging to the 4th, 5th and 7th Varieties is made up similarly by appending the Ātmanepada terminations to the base.

**Examples:**
- @deva[भू]—@deva[अभाविषि]
- @deva[कृ]—@deva[अकारिषि]
- @deva[धा]—@deva[अधिषि]
- @deva[पच्]—@deva[अपक्षि]
- @deva[दिश्]—@deva[अदिक्षि]
- @deva[द्विष्]—@deva[अद्विक्षि], &c.

### (b) Varieties Taking Fourth, Fifth or Seventh Form

Roots belonging to the first, second, third and sixth Varieties take the fourth, fifth or seventh Variety in the Passive, in accordance with the general rules.

**Examples:**
- @deva[स्था]—@deva[अस्थिषि] 1 sing.
- @deva[ह्वा]—@deva[अह्वासि]
- @deva[जॄ]—@deva[अजरिषि]
- @deva[श्रि]—@deva[अश्रायिषि]
- @deva[स्तु]—@deva[अस्तोषि]
- @deva[नम्]—@deva[अनंसि], &c.

### (c) Third Person Singular with @deva[इ]

The third per. sing. of the Aorist Passive of all roots is formed by adding @deva[इ]—

#### (1) Guṇa and Vṛddhi Substitution Rules

Before this @deva[इ] the penultimate (prosodially) short vowel takes its Guṇa substitute, and penultimate @deva[अ] except that of @deva[जन्] and of Seṭ roots ending in @deva[अम्] except @deva[चम्] with @deva[आ], @deva[कम्], and @deva[वम्], and the final vowel take their Vṛddhi substitute.

**Examples:**
- @deva[भिद्]—@deva[अभेदि]
- but @deva[निन्द्]—@deva[अनिन्दि]
- @deva[तुद्]—@deva[अतोदि]
- @deva[कृष्]—@deva[अकार्षि]
- @deva[वद्]—@deva[अवादि]
- @deva[पद्]—@deva[अपादि]
- but @deva[जन्]—@deva[अजनि]
- @deva[गम्]—@deva[अगामि]
- but @deva[दम्]—@deva[अदमि], &c.
- @deva[चम्] with @deva[आ]—@deva[आचामि]
- @deva[कम्]—@deva[अकामि], &c.
- @deva[नी]—@deva[अनायि]
- @deva[स्तु]—@deva[अस्तावि]
- @deva[लू]—@deva[अलावि]
- @deva[कॄ] or @deva[कृ]—@deva[अकारि]

#### (2) Roots Ending in @deva[आ]

Roots ending in @deva[आ] original or substituted (i. e. of roots in @deva[ए], @deva[ऐ], @deva[ओ]) insert @deva[य्] before this @deva[इ].

**Examples:**
- @deva[दा]—@deva[अदायि]
- @deva[धे]—@deva[अधायि]
- @deva[गै]—@deva[अगायि]
- @deva[शो]—@deva[अशायि], &c.

#### (3) Nasal Insertion

@deva[रध्], @deva[जभ्] and @deva[रभ्] insert a nasal before their final consonant, so that their penultimate @deva[अ] cannot take Guṇa or Vṛddhi substitute.

**Examples:**
- @deva[अरन्धि]
- @deva[अजम्भि]
- @deva[अरम्भि]

#### (4) @deva[लभ्] Rules

@deva[लभ्] without a preposition does the same optionally and with a preposition necessarily.

**Examples:**
- @deva[अलम्भि], @deva[अलाभि]
- but @deva[प्रालम्भि]

#### (5) Special Forms

@deva[भञ्ज्] 'to break' forms @deva[अभञ्जि] or @deva[अभाजि]; @deva[शम्]—@deva[अशमि] and @deva[अशामि] in the sense of 'to observe (10 Â.).'

#### (6) @deva[मृज्] and @deva[गृह्]

@deva[मृज्] takes Vṛddhi; @deva[गृह्] lengthens its vowel; @deva[अमार्जि], @deva[अग्राहि].

#### (7) @deva[इ] Forms

@deva[इ] 'to go' has @deva[अगायि]; with @deva[अधि] Â., @deva[अध्यायि] or @deva[अध्यगायि].

### (d) Roots at § 461

The roots at @ref[461] will have two forms.

**Examples:**
- @deva[गुप्]—@deva[अगोपि], @deva[अगोपायि]
- @deva[विच्छ्]—@deva[अविच्छि], @deva[अविच्छायि] &c.
- @deva[ऋत्]—@deva[आर्ति] or @deva[आर्तियि] 3 sing.

### (e) Optional Forms

@ref[596] (b) holds good in the Passive Aorist except in the 3rd sing.; the optional forms must be made up by appending the Ātm. terminations of the 5th Variety as the roots necessarily take @deva[इ].

**Examples:**
- @deva[दा]—@deva[अदिषि], @deva[अदायिषि]
- @deva[नी]—@deva[अनेषि], @deva[अनायिषि]
- @deva[कृ]—@deva[अकृषि], @deva[अकारिषि]
- @deva[हन्]—@deva[आहसि], @deva[अघानिषि]; @deva[अवधिषि] 1 sing.
- @deva[ग्रह्]—@deva[अग्रहीषि], @deva[अग्राहिषि] 1 sing. &c.

rules.title: Passive Forms of Tenth Class Roots
rules.body:
## Passive Forms of Tenth Class Roots

### (a) Optional Dropping of @deva[अय्]

The @deva[अय्] (i. e. @deva[अय] with the final @deva[अ] dropped) is optionally dropped in the General Tenses, except the Perfect. The Aorist forms, except that of the 3rd sing., are made up by adding the terminations of the Fifth Form.

**Examples (@deva[चुर्] 1 sing.):**
- @deva[चोरयांचक्रे]-@deva[बभूवे], @deva[चोरयामासे] Perf.
- @deva[चोरयिताहे], @deva[चोरिताहे] 1st Fu.
- @deva[चोरयिष्ये], @deva[चोरिष्ये] 2nd Fu.
- @deva[अचोरयिषि], @deva[अचोरिषि] Aor.
- @deva[चोरयिषीय], @deva[चोरिषीय] Ben.

### (b) Optional Lengthening

Roots which do not lengthen their penultimate @deva[अ] (see also @ref[603]) lengthen it optionally in the general Tenses of the Passive, except in Perf., when @deva[अय्] is dropped.

**Example:**
@deva[कथ्]—@deva[अकथयिषि], @deva[अकथिषि] Aor. 1 sing., &c.

### (c) Third Person Singular

The 3 per. sing. of the Pass. Aorist is formed by dropping @deva[अय्] necessarily and adding @deva[इ].

**Examples:**
- @deva[चोरय]—@deva[अचोर्]—@deva[अचोरि]
- @deva[पीड्]—@deva[अपीडि]
- @deva[पॄ]—@deva[अपारि], &c.
- @deva[रह्]—@deva[अरहि], @deva[अराहि] Aor. 3 sing.
- @deva[रम्]—@deva[अरमि], @deva[अरामि] Aorist, 3rd sing. &c.

### Paradigms

#### @deva[बुध्] 1 P. 'to know'

##### Perfect

| | Singular | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | @deva[बुबुधे] | @deva[बुबुधिवहे] | @deva[बुबुधिमहे] |
| 2. | @deva[बुबुधिषे] | @deva[बुबुधाथे] | @deva[बुबुधिध्वे] |
| 3. | @deva[बुबुधे] | @deva[बुबुधाते] | @deva[बुबुधिरे] |

##### 1st Future

| | Singular | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | @deva[बोधिताहे] | @deva[बोधितास्वहे] | @deva[बोधितास्महे] |
| 2. | @deva[बोधितासे] | @deva[बोधितासाथे] | @deva[बोधिताध्वे] |
| 3. | @deva[बोधिता] | @deva[बोधितारौ] | @deva[बोधितारः] |

##### 2nd Future

| | Singular | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | @deva[बोधिष्ये] | @deva[बोधिष्यावहे] | @deva[बोधिष्यामहे] |
| 2. | @deva[बोधिष्यसे] | @deva[बोधिष्येथे] | @deva[बोधिष्यध्वे] |
| 3. | @deva[बोधिष्यते] | @deva[बोधिष्येते] | @deva[बोधिष्यन्ते] |

##### Conditional

| | Singular | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | @deva[अबोधिष्ये] | @deva[अबोधिष्यावहि] | @deva[अबोधिष्यामहि] |
| 2. | @deva[अबोधिष्यथाः] | @deva[अबोधिष्येथाम्] | @deva[अबोधिष्यध्वम्] |
| 3. | @deva[अबोधिष्यत] | @deva[अबोधिष्येताम्] | @deva[अबोधिष्यन्त] |

##### Aorist

| | Singular | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | @deva[अबोधिषि] | @deva[अबोधिष्वहि] | @deva[अबोधिष्महि] |
| 2. | @deva[अबोधिष्ठाः] | @deva[अबोधिषाथाम्] | @deva[अबोधिध्वम्] |
| 3. | @deva[अबोधि] | @deva[अबोधिषाताम्] | @deva[अबोधिषत] |

##### Benedictive

| | Singular | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | @deva[बोधिषीय] | @deva[बोधिषीवहि] | @deva[बोधिषीमहि] |
| 2. | @deva[बोधिषीष्ठाः] | @deva[बोधिषीयास्थाम्] | @deva[बोधिषीध्वम्] |
| 3. | @deva[बोधिषीष्ट] | @deva[बोधिषीयास्ताम्] | @deva[बोधिषीरन्] |

@note[type=note]{The Passive forms of roots of the tenth class differ from the Passive forms of Causals for which see @deva[बुध्] cau. Pass. given in the next section.}

---

**SECTION III.**

**DERIVATIVE VERBS** (@deva[प्रत्ययान्तधातवः])
and
**THEIR CONJUGATION.**

rules.title: Classification of Derivative Verbs
rules.body:
## Classification of Derivative Verbs

The Derivative Verbs are divided into four classes:

1. **Causals or Nijantas** (@deva[णिजन्तः])
2. **Desideratives or Sanantas** (@deva[सन्नन्तः])
3. **Frequentatives or Yanantas** (@deva[यङन्तः])
4. **Denominatives or Nāmadhātus** (@deva[नामधातवः])

The formation and the conjugation of these will be given in the present section.

---

**I CAUSALS.**

rules.title: Causal Forms of Roots
rules.body:
## Causal Forms of Roots

Any root belonging to any one of the Conjugational classes may have causal form which is conjugated like a root of the Tenth class.

rules.title: Meaning and Use of Causals
rules.body:
## Meaning and Use of Causals

The Causal of a root implies that a person or a thing causes or makes another person or thing to perform the action denoted by the root. It is also employed, sometimes, to convert an intransitive verb into a transitive one.

**Formation of the Causal Base.**

rules.title: Formation of Causal Base Like Tenth Class
rules.body:
## Formation of Causal Base Like Tenth Class

The Causal Base of a root is formed like that of a root of the Tenth class. In the case of roots of the Tenth class the causal form is identical with the primitive. The Causal form takes either pada.

**Examples:**
- @deva[बुध्]—causal base @deva[बोधय], @deva[बोधयति] 'he causes to know'
- @deva[क्षुभ्]—@deva[क्षोभयति] 'he shakes or agitates'
- @deva[गण]—@deva[गणयति] 'he causes to count'
- @deva[नी]—@deva[नाययति] 'he makes another lead or to carry'
- @deva[कृ] 'to call' or 'to scatter'—@deva[करयति] 'he causes to do or scatter'
- @deva[कूद्]—@deva[कूदयति], &c.

rules.title: Vowel Shortening Before Vṛddhi in Causals
rules.body:
## Vowel Shortening Before Vṛddhi in Causals

Roots ending in @deva[अय्], except @deva[अय्] 'to go' &c., @deva[कथ्] 'to love,' @deva[वस्] 'to eat,' @deva[दृश्] when it means 'to see' and @deva[यस्] when it does not mean 'to eat,' and the roots[^1] marked with an indicatory @deva[ङ्] (e. g., @deva[वण्], &c.), shorten their vowel before taking its Vṛddhi substitute.

**Examples:**
- @deva[पन्]—@deva[पानयति]
- @deva[कथ्]—@deva[कामयति]
- @deva[वद्]—@deva[वन्दयति]
- @deva[जन्]—@deva[जन्वयति]
- @deva[क्रय्]—@deva[क्रयापयति]
- @deva[दुह्]—@deva[दुःपयति]
- @deva[आक्]—@deva[आकपयति]
- @deva[जा]—@deva[जंपयति], &c.

**Exceptions:**
- @deva[इम्]—@deva[इमायति]
- @deva[चक्ष्]—@deva[चक्षयति]
- @deva[शुश्] 'to see'—@deva[शुशयति], but @deva[इमयति] in other cases
- @deva[पम्]—@deva[पामयति], &c.
- @deva[यश्] 'to eat'—@deva[यशयति]

### (c) Optional Lengthening

The roots @deva[पत्], @deva[नम्], @deva[वद्], @deva[ग्रन्थ्], @deva[रुद्], and @deva[इर्], lengthen their vowel optionally when not preceded by a preposition.

**Examples:**
- @deva[नमयति], @deva[नामयति]
- with preposition: @deva[प्रणमयति], &c.

---

[^1]: These are: @deva[वद्], @deva[व्यध्], @deva[प्लुट्], @deva[प्रथ्], 'to spread,' @deva[वृ] 'to pound,' @deva[स्वद्] 1 Â. 'to destroy, to cut,' @deva[अञ्ज्] 1 Â. 'to go,' @deva[दुश्], @deva[कुश्] 1 Â. 'to pity,' @deva[कथ्], @deva[हृद्] 1 Â., @deva[त्वर्], @deva[ज्वर्], @deva[नन्] 1 Par. 'to distil,' @deva[वृद्] 'to surround,' @deva[मद्] 'to speak,' @deva[नृद्] 'to dance,' @deva[कृद्] 1 P. 'to resist,' @deva[शाय्] 1. P. Â. 'to lie down'; @deva[नृत्] 'to dance'; @deva[प्रुच्] 1 P. to shine,' 1 to 'to cling to', @deva[वृ], @deva[प्लु], @deva[स्पृ], @deva[स्पु], all meaning 'to cover,' @deva[वु], @deva[अट्], @deva[अट्] 'to move in a zigzag manner,' @deva[कण्], @deva[एण्] P. 'to go,' @deva[वण्], @deva[युण्], @deva[भुण्].

rules.title: Augment व् in Causals of Roots Ending in आ
rules.body:
## Augment @deva[प्] in Causals of Roots Ending in @deva[आ]

Roots ending in @deva[आ] (@deva[ए], @deva[ऐ] or @deva[ओ] changeable to @deva[आ]; see @ref[459]) and the roots @deva[ऋ] 'to go,' @deva[ह्री] 'to be ashamed,' @deva[री] 'to go' (9 cl.), 'to flow' (4. cl. Â.) and @deva[व्ली] 'to choose, to go,' insert the augment @deva[प्] before @deva[अय] and their vowel takes Guṇa substitute.

**Examples:**
- @deva[दापयति] fr. @deva[दा], @deva[दे] or @deva[दो]
- @deva[धापयति] fr. @deva[धे]
- @deva[गापयति] fr. @deva[गै], &c.
- @deva[ऋ]—@deva[अर्पयति]
- @deva[ह्री]—@deva[ह्रेपयति]
- @deva[री]—@deva[रेपयति]
- @deva[व्ली]—@deva[व्लेपयति]

rules.title: Special Causal Forms with व् Augment
rules.body:
## Special Causal Forms with @deva[प्] Augment

### (a) Roots Changing Final Vowel to @deva[आ]

@deva[मि] 'to throw,' @deva[मी] 'to destroy,' @deva[दी] 'to perish,' @deva[जि] 'to conquer,' and @deva[क्री] 'to buy,' also insert @deva[प्], but after changing their final vowel to @deva[आ].

**Examples:**
- @deva[मापयति]
- @deva[दापयति]
- @deva[जापयति]
- @deva[क्रापयति]

### (b) Vowel Shortening Before @deva[प्]

The roots @deva[क्षै], @deva[ज्ञा], @deva[श्रा] or @deva[श्रै] 'to cook' and @deva[ज्ञा] (mit.), shorten their vowel necessarily, and @deva[ग्लै] and @deva[स्ना] optionally, before the inserted @deva[प्] when not preceded by prepositions.

**Examples:**
- @deva[क्षपयति], &c.
- @deva[ज्ञपयति] (@deva[पशुं संज्ञपयति] 'slays'; @deva[प्रज्ञपयति] @deva[शरं] &c.)
- but @deva[ज्ञापयति], @deva[ग्लपयति], @deva[ग्लापयति]; @deva[स्नपयति], @deva[स्नापयति]

**With prepositions:**
- @deva[प्रग्लापयति], @deva[उपस्नापयति] only

rules.title: Causals with प and ञ् Augments
rules.body:
## Causals with @deva[य्] and @deva[ल्]/@deva[ज्] Augments

@deva[शो] 'to pare, to sharpen,' @deva[छो] 'to cut,' @deva[सो] 'to finish,' @deva[दे] P. 'to give,' @deva[अर्थ्], @deva[कथ्], @deva[कुथ्], @deva[कुथ्], all P. and meaning 'to injure,' 'to kill,' @deva[चन्] 'to kill,' @deva[वन्] P. 'to honour,' @deva[ज्वल्] 'to shine,' @deva[ह्वल्], @deva[ह्मल्] 'to shake, to move,' @deva[स्मृ], @deva[दृ] 1 P. 'to fear,' @deva[नी] 'to guide,' @deva[श्रा] 'to cook, to boil,' @deva[ज्ञा] 'to kill, to gratify, to sharpen, to manifest,' @deva[चल्], @deva[छद्] 'to live or to be' (@deva[छादयति] in other senses), @deva[लड्] 'to sport, to loll the tongue,' @deva[मद्] 'to be poor, to reduce,' @deva[ध्वन्], @deva[स्वन्], @deva[जन्], @deva[जॄ], @deva[रुष्] 'to be crooked, to shine,' @deva[रञ्ज्], @deva[रम्], @deva[क्रम्], @deva[गम्], and @deva[फण्] 1 P. 'to go,' 'to call,' @deva[व्ये] 'to cover,' @deva[वे] 'to weave,' @deva[सै] 'to waste away,' and @deva[पा] 'to drink' insert @deva[य्] instead of @deva[प्].

**Examples:**
- @deva[शाययति]
- @deva[साययति]
- @deva[वाययति]
- @deva[पाययति], &c.

### (a) Special Augments

@deva[पा] 'to protect' and @deva[वे] when it means 'to shake,' insert @deva[ल्] and @deva[ज्] respectively before @deva[अय].

**Examples:**
- @deva[पालयति] 'he protects'
- @deva[वाजयति] 'he shakes'

---

[^1]: See @ref[605] (b).

rules.title: Nasal Insertion in Causals
rules.body:
## Nasal Insertion in Causals

The roots @deva[गृभ्], @deva[स्तभ्], @deva[स्तम्भ्], and @deva[लभ्] insert a nasal before their final.

**Examples:**
- @deva[गृभ्]—@deva[गृम्भयति-ते]
- @deva[रम्भयति-ते], &c.

rules.title: Roots with Two Causal Forms
rules.body:
## Roots with Two Causal Forms

The roots @deva[युज्], @deva[विच्छ्], @deva[भुज्], @deva[पुष्], @deva[पन्], and @deva[कुद्] have two forms in the causal.

**Examples:**
- @deva[युज्]—@deva[युज्यति-ते], @deva[योजापयति-ते]
- @deva[विच्छ्]—@deva[विच्छयति-ते], @deva[विच्छाययति-ते], &c.

rules.title: Final Vowel Elision in Causals
rules.body:
## Final Vowel Elision in Causals

@deva[दीपी], @deva[वेपी] and @deva[दरिद्रा] drop their final vowel before @deva[अय्].

**Examples:**
- @deva[दीपयति-ते]
- @deva[वेपयति-ते]
- @deva[दरिद्रयति-ते]

rules.title: Anomalous Causal Forms
rules.body:
## Anomalous Causal Forms

The following roots form their Causal base anomalously:

rules.title: Conjugation of Causal Base Like Tenth Class
rules.body:
## Conjugation of Causal Base Like Tenth Class

The Causal base is conjugated like the base of a root of the 10th or Churādi class in all the ten Tenses and Moods of the Parasmaipada, the Ātmanepada and the Passive.

The @deva[अय्] (i. e. @deva[अय्] with the final @deva[अ] dropped) is retained, as remarked before, in the General Tenses, except the Aorist and the Benedictive, and is dropped before the @deva[य] of the Passive.

The formation of the Aorist of causals has been fully explained along with that of the roots of the Tenth class, at @ref[548]-@ref[556].

rules.title: Complete Paradigms of Causal बोधय्
rules.body:
## Complete Paradigms of Causal @deva[बोधय्]

Paradigms of all the Tenses and Moods in the Par. Ātm. and Pass. of @deva[बुध्], Causal base @deva[बोधय्].

### Special Tenses

#### Present

**Parasmaipada:**

rules.title: Formation of Desiderative Forms
rules.body:
## Formation of Desiderative Forms

Any primitive root of the ten classes, and also the causal base, may optionally[^1] take a Desiderative form, which, like the causal base, is conjugated in all the ten Tenses and Moods of three voices.

---

[^1]: Or the notion of desire may be conveyed by means of a periphrase; i. e. @deva[पिपठिषति] or @deva[पठितुमिच्छति] 'he wishes to read.'

rules.title: Meaning of Desiderative Forms
rules.body:
## Meaning of Desiderative Forms

The Desiderative expresses the notion that a person or thing wishes (or is about) to perform the action, or to be in the condition denoted by the root or the desiderative base.

**Examples:**
- @deva[पिपठिषति] 'he wishes to study' from @deva[पठ्]
- @deva[मुमूर्षति] 'he is about to die' from @deva[मृ], &c.

rules.title: Desiderative Forms Without Desiderative Sense
rules.body:
## Desiderative Forms Without Desiderative Sense

There are a few primitive roots, which, though they take a Desiderative form, do not convey a desiderative sense (See @ref[39]. b). As has been looked upon as primitive roots, the Desiderative bases may be derived from them according to the rules given below.

**Example:**
@deva[जुगुप्सिषत] 'he wishes to censure' from @deva[जुगुप्स्] &c.

rules.title: Formation of Desiderative Base by Reduplication
Prefixing Augment इ to Desiderative स्
rules.body:
## Prefixing Augment @deva[इ] to Desiderative @deva[स्]

To this @deva[स्] the augment @deva[इ] is to be prefixed after Seṭ roots, optionally after Veṭ ones and not after those that are Aniṭ, subject to the following exceptions:—

### (1) Roots Ending in @deva[उ], @deva[ऊ], @deva[ऋ], @deva[ऌ]

Roots ending in @deva[उ] or @deva[ऊ], @deva[ऋ] and @deva[ऌ] short, and the roots @deva[ग्रह्] and @deva[गुह्] do not take @deva[इ]; @deva[नु]—@deva[नुनूष्] (Vide @ref[618]. (d)); @deva[भू]—@deva[बुभूष्], &c.

**Exceptions:**
@deva[ऋ] 'to go,' @deva[ऋ] Ā. 'to respect,' @deva[धृ] 6 Ā. 'to hold,' and @deva[पू] Ā. 'to purify,' admit of @deva[इ] (see also 4 below)

### (2) Roots Taking @deva[इ] Necessarily

@deva[स्मि], @deva[अञ्ज्], @deva[प्रच्छ्], @deva[अश्] take @deva[इ] necessarily.

### (3) Roots Differing in Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada

@deva[वृत्], @deva[वृध्], @deva[वृध्], @deva[स्यन्द्] and @deva[क्लृप्] do not admit of @deva[इ] in the Par. (see @ref[484]). In the Ātm. they admit @deva[इ], the last two do so optionally.

**Examples:**
- @deva[वृत्]—@deva[विवृत्सति], @deva[विवर्तिषते], &c.

### (4) Roots with Optional @deva[इ]

Roots ending in long @deva[ऋ] and @deva[ॠ] and the roots @deva[दरिद्रा], @deva[श्रि], @deva[ऊर्णु], @deva[यु], @deva[भृ], @deva[दृ], @deva[स्तृ], @deva[ऋध्] 'to prosper,' @deva[दम्भ्], @deva[भ्रस्ज्], @deva[ज्ञप्] (i. e. @deva[ज्ञप्] of the 10 cl. and optional Cau. Base of @deva[ज्ञा]), @deva[सन्] 'to give,' @deva[तन्], @deva[पन्], @deva[क्षण्], @deva[चुर्], @deva[छृद्], @deva[तृद्], and @deva[नृत्] (Vide @ref[485].) take @deva[इ] optionally.

**Exceptions:**
@deva[कॄ] 'to scatter,' @deva[गॄ] 'to swallow,' take @deva[इ] necessarily. The intermediate @deva[इ] is not lengthened in the case of these roots; @deva[चिकरिष्], &c.

### (5) Roots Differing by Voice

The roots @deva[क्रम्], @deva[गम्] and @deva[सु] take @deva[इ] in the Par. and reject it in the Ātm.

rules.title: Radical Vowel Changes Before स् in Desideratives
rules.body:
## Radical Vowel Changes Before @deva[स्] in Desideratives

The radical vowels undergo the following changes before @deva[स्]—

### (a) Strong and Weak Forms

The @deva[स्] with @deva[इ] is strong and without @deva[इ] weak.

The usual rule as to Guṇa substitute holds good in the one case and does not in the other.

**Examples:**
- @deva[वृत्]—@deva[विवर्तिष्], @deva[विवृत्स्]
- @deva[दृ]—@deva[दिदरिष्], &c.

### (b) Lengthening and @deva[ऋ] Changes

The final @deva[इ] and @deva[उ] and the penultimate @deva[अ] of @deva[गम्] and @deva[गम्] (substituted for @deva[इ] 2 Par. 'to go,' and for @deva[इ] with @deva[अधि] 'to remember' or 'to study') are lengthened and final @deva[ऋ], short or long, changed to @deva[ईर्], or to @deva[ऊर्] after labials or @deva[व] when the @deva[स्] is unaugmented.

**Examples:**
- @deva[जि]—@deva[जिगीष्]
- @deva[दु]—@deva[दुदूष्]
- @deva[कृ]—@deva[चिकीर्ष्]
- @deva[तॄ]—@deva[तितीर्ष्]
- @deva[मृ]—@deva[मुमूर्ष्]
- @deva[पॄ]—@deva[पुपूर्ष्], &c.

### (c) Exceptions

The roots @deva[रुद्], @deva[विद्] and @deva[मुष्] do not change their vowel to Guṇa; and the roots @deva[ग्रह्], @deva[स्वप्] and @deva[प्रच्छ्] take Samprasāraṇa.

**Examples:**
- @deva[रुरुदिष्]
- @deva[विविदिष्]
- @deva[मुमुषिष्]
- @deva[जिघृक्ष्]
- @deva[सुषुप्स्]
- @deva[पिपृच्छिष्]

### (d) Optional Guṇa when @deva[इ] is Prefixed

Roots with an initial consonant, and having @deva[इ] or @deva[उ] short for their penultimate, and ending in any consonant, except @deva[य्] or @deva[व्], change their vowel to Guṇa optionally when @deva[इ] is prefixed to @deva[स्].

**Examples:**
- @deva[द्युत्]—@deva[दिद्युतिष्], @deva[दिद्योतिष्]
- @deva[मुद्]—@deva[मुमुदिष्] or @deva[मुमोदिष्] &c.

rules.title: Desideratives of Causals and Tenth Class Roots
rules.body:
## Desideratives of Causals and Tenth Class Roots

The formation of Desiderative bases of causals and of roots of the Tenth class does not differ from that of primitive roots.

Art @ref[550]. should be attended to in forming Desideratives from Causals and roots of the Tenth class.

rules.title: Pada Selection in Desideratives
rules.body:
## Pada Selection in Desideratives

Roots in their Desiderative forms take the same terminations, Parasmai or Ātmane, that they do in the primitive. The roots @deva[वृ], @deva[मृ], @deva[हु] and @deva[टनु] take Ātm. terminations in the Desiderative.

rules.title: Conjugation of Desiderative Base in Conjugational Tenses
Non-Conjugational Tenses of Desideratives
rules.body:
## Non-Conjugational Tenses of Desideratives

### (a) Perfect

The Perfect is formed by adding @deva[आम्] to the base and appending the Perfect forms of the auxiliary verbs @deva[अस्], @deva[भू], and @deva[कृ] (see @ref[490], @ref[526]).

### (b) Aorist

In the Aorist the Desiderative Bases take the terminations of the 5th Variety.

### (c) Benedictive

In the Benedictive the Parasm. terminations are added without @deva[इ] and the Atm. ones with the intermediate @deva[इ].

### (d) Remaining Tenses

The remaining tenses have no peculiarities.

**III. FREQUENTATIVES** (@deva[यङन्तः])

rules.title: Formation and Use of Frequentatives
rules.body:
## Formation and Use of Frequentatives

A Frequentative or Intensive form may be derived from any monosyllabic root of the first nine classes, beginning with a consonant. The Frequentative or Intensive is used to signify the repetition or the intensity of the action denoted by the verb from which it is derived.

**Exceptions:**

rules.title: Exceptions and Special Uses of Frequentatives
rules.body:
## Exceptions and Special Uses of Frequentatives

### (a) Exceptional Roots

A Frequentative may be formed from @deva[इ] 'to go', @deva[ऋ] 'to go', @deva[अन्] 'to eat' and @deva[जुप्] 'to conceal', though these begin with a vowel; and from @deva[सत्त्] cl. 10 'to hint', @deva[दूष्] cl. 10 'to string together', and @deva[मुख्] cl. 10, though they belong to the 10th class.

### (b) Special Semantic Uses

The Frequentative of roots signifying motion conveys the notion of tortuous motion and not of repetition.

The Frequentative of roots @deva[छुअ्] 'to cut', @deva[सद्] 'to sink down', @deva[वत्] 'to go', @deva[गम्] 'to mutter prayers', @deva[यच्] 'to yawn', @deva[दह्] 'to burn', @deva[दंश्] 'to bite', and @deva[गृ] 'to swallow' imply reproach on the manner of doing the act: @deva[अडोलच्छति] 'he cuts awkwardly', @deva[सासत्यते] 'falls down badly', @deva[संवद्यते], etc.

rules.title: Two Types of Frequentative Bases
rules.body:
## Two Types of Frequentative Bases

There are two kinds of Frequentative bases derived from roots; both are formed by a peculiar reduplication of the root:

1. **Ātmanepada Frequentative**: The suffix @deva[य] (@deva[यङ्]) is added to the root before reduplication takes place, and the base is conjugated in the Ātmanepada alone.

2. **Parasmaipada Frequentative**: The suffix @deva[य] is dropped (@deva[यङलुङ्]) and the base is conjugated in Parasmaipada only (in the Ātmanepada also, according to some grammarians).

It will be convenient to call one the Ātm. Frequentative, and the other the Parasm. Frequentative.

---

**ĀTMANEPADA-FREQUENTATIVE**

rules.title: Formation of Ātmanepada Frequentative Base
Reduplication in Ātmanepada Frequentatives
rules.body:
## Reduplication in Ātmanepada Frequentatives

The reduplication syllable is formed between the reduplicative syllable and the radical consonant:

@deva[पृट्]—@deva[पूर्यंय] = @deva[पुपूर्यंयते]

@deva[भञ्ज्]—@deva[भुञ्जय] = @deva[पुञ्जयते]

@deva[पृञ्]—@deva[परीयते]

@deva[मृड्] = @deva[मरीयते]

---

### Conjugation of the Ātm. Freq. Base

In the Conjugational Tenses the Ātm. Freq. Base is conjugated like the Conjugational base of the 4th class in Ātmanepada. In the General Tenses, and in all the Tenses of the Passive, the base loses its final @deva[य] when the base + @deva[अ] is preceded by a vowel and drops the @deva[य] itself when it is preceded by a consonant.

As regards the Perfect, the Freq. Base takes the Periphrastic Perfect. In the Aorist the Ātm. terminations of the 5th form are added. In the remaining Tenses the Ātm. terminations with the intermediate @deva[इ] prefixed to them are added as usual. The Passive is also formed like the Passive of derived verbs.

### Paradigms

The 3rd sing. of @deva[बोबुध्] the Ātm. Freq. Base of the root @deva[बुध्] and @deva[देदीय] that of the root @deva[द्या]:

| Imperative | @deva[बोबुध्यताम्] | @deva[देदीयताम्] | @deva[बोबुध्यताम्] | @deva[देदीय्यताम्] |

## Conjugation of Ātmanepada Frequentative Base

### Conjugational Tenses

In the Conjugational Tenses the Ātm. Freq. Base is conjugated like the Conjugational base of the 4th class in Ātmanepada.

### General Tenses

In the General Tenses, and in all the Tenses of the Passive, the base loses its final @deva[य] when the base + @deva[अ] is preceded by a vowel and drops the @deva[य] itself when it is preceded by a consonant.

### Perfect

As regards the Perfect, the Freq. Base takes the Periphrastic Perfect.

### Aorist

In the Aorist the Ātm. terminations of the 5th form are added.

### Remaining Tenses

In the remaining Tenses the Ātm. terminations with the intermediate @deva[इ] prefixed to them are added as usual.

### Passive

The Passive is also formed like the Passive of derived verbs.

**PARASMAIPADA FREQUENTATIVES**

The Parasm. Frequentative is peculiar to the Veda. Its forms are very rarely to be met with in Classical composition.

Conjugation of Parasmaipada Frequentatives
rules.body:
## Conjugation of Parasmaipada Frequentatives

### Conjugational Tenses

In the Conjugational Tenses the Parasm. Frequentative is conjugated like a root of the second class.

### General Tenses

In the General Tenses, it is conjugated like a primitive root, Ātm. base taking, however, Ātm. terminations (see @ref[485], @ref[486]).

rules.title: Semantic Distinction in Parasmaipada Frequentatives
Paradigms and Irregular Frequentatives
rules.body:
## Paradigms and Irregular Frequentatives

### Paradigms: Parasmaipada Frequentatives

The Third persons of the Parasmaipada Frequentative of @deva[कृ] 'to do', @deva[पृच्] 'to fill', and @deva[कृष्] 'to draw furrows'.

All those tenses of this Intensive in which the weak form of the base is used (vide @ref[485], @ref[486]) substitute @deva[चकृ] for @deva[कृ] 'to do'; @deva[पूर्य] 'to fill up', and @deva[कृष्य] 'to draw furrows' respectively.

If in any weak form of an Intensive the root has a final consonant, @deva[र्] is inserted between the Guṇa of the root and the termination (see @ref[640]).

#### Special Tenses

**Conjugation in Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada**

| Tense | Par. | Ātm. |
|-------|------|------|
| **Present** |

rules.title: Complete Paradigms of Parasmaipada Frequentatives and Introduction to Nominal Verbs
rules.body:
## Complete Paradigms of Parasmaipada Frequentatives and Introduction to Nominal Verbs

### Optional @deva[इ] Before Terminations

When the roots of the Parasm. Frequentative base follow the conjugation of the special base of a root of the 3rd class, @deva[इ] is optionally prefixed to the terminations of the singulars of the Present, of the 2nd and 3rd singulars of the Imperfect and of the 3rd singular of the Imperative; when @deva[इ] is prefixed to these, a penultimate short vowel does not take Guṇa:

@deva[दा]—@deva[दादाति] or @deva[दादेति]

@deva[वृत्]—@deva[वर्वर्ति] or @deva[वरिवर्ति] or @deva[वरीवर्ति] or @deva[वर्वृतीति] or @deva[वरिवृतीति] or @deva[वरीवृतीति]

@deva[कृ]—@deva[चर्कर्ति] or @deva[चर्करीति], @deva[चरिकर्ति] or @deva[चरिकरीति], @deva[चरीकर्ति] or @deva[चरीकरीति]

### Non-Conjugational Tenses

As regards the formation of the Non-conjugational tenses grammarians seem to be at variance. The Perfect follows the usual rules for the polysyllabic roots. In the remaining tenses the augment @deva[इ] is always prefixed except in the Benedictive.

As this form of the Freq. is mostly confined to the Veda, details are not given here.

### Paradigms: @deva[बोभू] or @deva[बोभव्] from the root @deva[भू]

| | @deva[अबोभवीत्, अबोभूत्] | @deva[अबोभूताम्] | @deva[अबोभुवुः] |

### Ātmanepada and Passive Forms (3rd sing.)

| Tense | Ātmanepada | Passive |
|-------|------------|---------|
| Present | @deva[बोभूते] | @deva[बोभूयते] |
| Imperfect | @deva[अबोभूत] | @deva[अबोभूयत] |
| Imperative | @deva[बोभूताम्] | @deva[बोभूयताम्] |
| Potential | @deva[बोभूयीत] | @deva[बोभूयते] |
| Perfect | @deva[बोभवाञ्चक्रे], etc. | @deva[बोभवाञ्चक्रे] |
| 1st Future | @deva[बोभविता] | @deva[बोभविता] or @deva[बोभाविता] |
| 2nd Future | @deva[बोभविष्यते] | @deva[बोभविष्यते] or @deva[बोभाविष्यते] |
| Conditional | @deva[अबोभविष्यत] | @deva[अबोभविष्यत] or @deva[अबोभाविष्यत] |

---

**IV. NOMINAL VERBS**

Verbs are formed from nominal bases by means of certain affixes. These are not very much in common use and are generally used in the Present Tense. They have various meanings. They sometimes convey the notion of performing, practising, or using, or treating like the thing or quality expressed by the noun and are used transitively; sometimes they express the idea of acting, behaving or becoming like the person or thing expressed by the noun; and at others they yield the sense of wishing or wishing for the thing expressed by the noun.

These will be arranged here under four heads, according to the affixes by which they are derived.

### (a) By means of the affix @deva[य] (@deva[क्यच्]) and Conjugated in Parasmaipada

rules.title: Formation of Nominal Verbs Expressing Wish (क्यच्)
rules.body:
## Formation of Nominal Verbs Expressing Wish (@deva[क्यच्])

When the sense of 'wish' is to be expressed, a nominal verb may be derived from any Subanta or nominal stem by affixing @deva[य] to it. The derivative verbal base derived in this manner is conjugated in the Parasmaipada only.

rules.title: Vowel Changes Before य in Nominal Verbs
Insertion of स् and अस् in Nominal Verbs
Restriction on य Affix with स्-Ending Nouns
Exceptional Forms with Double Meanings
rules.body:
## Exceptional Forms with Double Meanings

### @deva[अशन]

@deva[अशन] has:
- @deva[अशनायति] 'he wishes to eat'
- @deva[अशनीयति] 'he wishes to possess food'

### @deva[उदक]

@deva[उदक] has:
- @deva[उदन्यति] 'he wishes to drink water'
- @deva[उदकीयति] 'he wishes to possess water'

### @deva[धन]

@deva[धन] has:
- @deva[धनायति] 'he wishes to acquire money'
- @deva[धनीयति] 'he wishes to be wealthy'

rules.title: Non-Desiderative Uses of य Nominal Verbs
Dropping of य in General Tenses
rules.body:
## Dropping of @deva[य] in General Tenses

In the general tenses the affix @deva[य] (@deva[क्यच्] and @deva[क्यङ्] to be given hereafter) is dropped when preceded by a consonant:

@deva[समिधांचकार] Perf. 1 sing.

@deva[समिधिता], @deva[समिधिष्यति] 1st and 2nd Fu. 3 sing. from @deva[समिध्यति]

But @deva[पुत्रीयांचकार] from @deva[पुत्रीयति]

---

### (b) By means of the affix @deva[काम्य] (@deva[काम्यच्]) and conjugated in Par.

rules.title: Formation with काम्य Affix
Exception to § 644 for काम्य Affix
rules.body:
## Exception to § 644 for @deva[काम्य] Affix

The restriction given at @ref[644] does not hold good in the case of this affix:

@deva[किंकाम्यति], @deva[स्वःकाम्यति]

---

### (c) By means of the affix @deva[क्विप्] (o) and conjugated in Par.

rules.title: Nominal Verbs Without Added Affix
rules.body:
## Nominal Verbs Without Added Affix

Nominal bases are formed without the addition of any affix, the characteristic signs of the tenses and moods and the personal terminations being added immediately to the nominal base.

The bases thus derived convey the notion of acting or behaving like that which is expressed by the noun, and are conjugated in the Parasmaipada.

rules.title: Vowel Changes in Nominal Verbs Formed Without an Affix
Formation with क्यङ् Affix
rules.body:
## Formation with @deva[क्यङ्] Affix

The affix @deva[य] (@deva[क्यङ्]) is added in the same sense as above to nominal stems and the nominal verbs so derived are conjugated in the Ātmanepada.

rules.title: Vowel Changes Before क्यङ्
य Affix for 'Becoming What It Was Not Before'
Special Uses of क्यच् Affix
Formation with क्यष् (य) Affix
rules.body:
## Formation with @deva[क्यष्] (@deva[य]) Affix

The affix @deva[य] is added to @deva[लोहित] and some other words and to words ending in the affix @deva[आ] (@deva[डाच्]) and the nominal base thus formed is conjugated in the Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada:

### Examples

@deva[लोहित]—@deva[लोहितायति]-@deva[ते] 'becomes red'

@deva[पटपटायते] 'utters the sound Paṭpaṭ'

---

### (f) By means of the affix @deva[इ] (@deva[णिङ्] and @deva[णिच्]) and conjugated in Parasm. and Ātm.

rules.title: Formation with इ Affixes (णिङ् and णिच्)
Change of इङ् to आकिङ्
Additional Uses of इङ् Affix
Roots That Are Also Prātipadika (यङ् Derivatives)
rules.body:
## Roots That Are Also Prātipadika (@deva[यङ्] Derivatives)

There are several roots[^1] which are also Prātipadikas and which may be regarded as Nominal verbal bases derived from those Prātipadikas by means of the affix @deva[य] (@deva[यङ्]).

The more important of these are given below:

| Root | Form | Meaning |
|------|------|---------|
| @deva[दयुष्] | @deva[दयुषति-ते] | he scratches |
| @deva[सुशूष्] | @deva[सुशूष्यति] | he worships |
| @deva[मन्द] | @deva[मंदयति] | he offends against, he becomes angry |
| | @deva[मंदयते] | (according to Candra) |
| @deva[निवञ्ज] | @deva[निवञ्जयति] | treats medically |
| @deva[इषुध] | @deva[इषुध्यति] | it contains arrows |
| @deva[गद्द] | @deva[गद्दयति] | he stammers |
| @deva[क्ला] | @deva[क्लायति] | is delighted |
| @deva[कैल], @deva[सैल] | @deva[कैलायति], @deva[सैलायति] | he sports, he becomes merry |
| @deva[अङ्ग] | @deva[अङ्गयति-ते] (@deva[शुस्यति]) | he is jealous, he envies, etc. |
| @deva[कुप्णि] | @deva[कुप्णायति] | he is angry or feels ashamed |

---

### (h) No affixes added to certain nominal bases

---

[^1]: In the Kaumudī these roots are classed separately under the head of '@deva[कुप्णादिगण]' or the group of roots beginning with @deva[कुप्णि].

rules.title: Nominal Stems Used as Verbs Without Affixes
rules.body:
## Nominal Stems Used as Verbs Without Affixes

A few nominal stems are used as verbs without the addition of any special affix as given above. They are called '@deva[कर्मव्यर्थे वर्णाः]'.

rules.title: Expressing Desire by Adding Root to Root
Optional Formation from Specific Words
rules.body:
## Optional Formation from Specific Words

Verbs may be formed optionally from the words @deva[स्फातयि], @deva[चयायति], @deva[भूरि], and @deva[अर्थ] by means of regular affixes, or without the help of any affixes as given in the last paragraph.

### Three Methods of Formation

The special affixes are @deva[क्यच्], @deva[चङ्कच्] or @deva[णिच्]; so these four words may be used in three ways:

1. As nominal verbs with the affixes added
2. As verbs used transitively without affixes
3. As nominal verbal bases not requiring any affixes for their use

### Examples

From @deva[स्फातयि]: @deva[स्फातयि], @deva[स्फातयति], @deva[स्फातययति] 'to use salt'

From @deva[आत्मन्]: @deva[आत्मनि], @deva[आत्मायति], @deva[आत्मायते] respectively

Similarly from @deva[अम्बस्], @deva[पयस्], @deva[शुचि]: @deva[अम्बयन्ति], @deva[पयस्यति], etc.

In all these cases the root affix may be taken to be @deva[णिच्] or @deva[णिच्].

rules.title: Suffixes Conveying Reproach
rules.body:
## Suffixes Conveying Reproach

By means of the suffixes @deva[कुङ्], @deva[किय], @deva[णिच्] and @deva[कुण] the sense of reproach is conveyed:

### Examples

@deva[स्तेनकुयति], @deva[स्तेनकियति] 'to call a person a thief'

@deva[भृत्येयति] 'to call a person a servant'

Similarly @deva[किंकरेयति]

---

**CHAPTER XIII**

**CONJUGATION OF ROOTS**

rules.title: Alphabetical Arrangement and Nominal Verb Examples
rules.body:
## Alphabetical Arrangement and Nominal Verb Examples

In the following pages roots have been arranged according to their initial letters. It will be convenient to follow an alphabetical arrangement in stating the order in which they would be given in this chapter. This chapter will follow the following sequence:

### Examples of Nominal Verbs

| Form | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| @deva[छेदा]—@deva[छेदायति] | he shines |
| @deva[रेखा]—@deva[रेखायति] | he approaches |
| @deva[उषप्]—@deva[उषपायति] | it dawns |
| @deva[मही]—@deva[महीयते] | he is adored, etc. |
| @deva[मेधा]—@deva[मेधायति] | he is quick in understanding |
| @deva[तिरस्]—@deva[तिरस्यति] | he disappears |
| @deva[सुख्]—@deva[सुख्यति] | feels happy |
| @deva[अशुद्]—@deva[अशुद्यति] | he becomes healthy |
| @deva[दुख्]—@deva[दुख्यति] | feels unhappy |
| @deva[उरस्]—@deva[उरस्यति] | he becomes powerful |
| @deva[पयस्]—@deva[पयस्यति] | it spreads |

---

**CHAPTER XIII**

**Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada**

**Note**: This rule spans pages 396-405 and contains extensive material on when roots take Parasmaipada vs. Ātmanepada with various prepositions. The detailed content covers specific rules for individual roots with their prepositional combinations and semantic conditions.

rules.title: Unādi Affixes and Introduction to Participles
rules.body:
## Unādi Affixes and Introduction to Participles

There is a peculiar class of Kṛt or Primary affixes technically designated by Sanskrit grammarians—Unādi or those beginning with the affix @deva[उण्], i.e. the affix @deva[उ] with the signs or indicatory letter @deva[न्].

### Characteristics of Unādi Affixes

These Unādi affixes form primary nouns, like other Kṛt affixes form verbal roots, but are classed separately because:

1. Their application is limited
2. The nouns derived by their means are either formed irregularly
3. The connection between their senses and the meanings of roots from which they are supposed to be derived is not so clearly discernible as in the case of other primary derivatives

### Examples

@deva[अश्व] 'a horse' which is derived either from:
- @deva[आस्] 'to pervade', or
- @deva[अश्व] 'road'

@deva[काड्] 'an artisan' from @deva[कृ] 'to do', etc.

---

**SECTION I**

**PARTICIPLES (Declinable and Indeclinable)**

### 1. Participles (Declinable)

### (a) Participles of the Present Tense

rules.title: Formation of Present Parasmaipada Participle
rules.body:
## Formation of Present Parasmaipada Participle

The participle of the present Parasmaipada is formed by the addition of the affix @deva[अत्] to that form of a root, primitive or derivative, which it assumes before the third person plural termination of the Present Tense. If the base ends in @deva[अ], the @deva[अ] is dropped.

### Examples

| Root (Class) | 3rd Pl. Present | Participle | Meaning |
|--------------|-----------------|------------|---------|
| @deva[भू] (1) | @deva[भव] + @deva[अन्ति] | @deva[भव] + @deva[अत्] = @deva[भवत्] | being |
| @deva[स्था] (1) | @deva[तिष्ठ] + @deva[अन्ति] | @deva[तिष्ठ] + @deva[अत्] = @deva[तिष्ठत्] | standing |
| @deva[द्विष्] (2) | @deva[द्विष्] + @deva[अन्ति] | @deva[द्विष्] + @deva[अत्] = @deva[द्विषत्] | hating |
| @deva[अद्] (2) | — | @deva[अदत्] | eating |
| @deva[या] (2) | — | @deva[यात्] | going |
| @deva[हु] (3) | — | @deva[जुह्वत्] | sacrificing |
| @deva[दिव्] (4) | — | @deva[दीव्यत्] | playing |
| @deva[सु] (5) | — | @deva[सुन्वत्] | extracting |
| @deva[तुद्] (6) | — | @deva[तुदत्] | giving pain |
| @deva[रुध्] (7) | — | @deva[रुन्धत्] | preventing |
| @deva[कृ] (8) | — | @deva[कुर्वत्] | doing |
| @deva[तन्] (8) | — | @deva[तन्वत्] | stretching, etc. |
| @deva[क्री] (9) | — | @deva[क्रीणत्] | buying |
| @deva[मुष्] (9) | — | @deva[मुष्णत्] | stealing, etc. |
| @deva[चुर्] (10) | — | @deva[चोरयत्] | stealing |

### Derived Forms

@deva[बोधय्] cau. of @deva[बुध्]: @deva[बोधयत्] 'causing to know'

@deva[बुबोधिष्] desid. of @deva[बुध्]: @deva[बुबोधिषत्] 'desiring to know'

@deva[दित्स्] desid. of @deva[दा]: @deva[दित्सत्] 'desiring to give'

@deva[चेक्षिप्] freq. of @deva[क्षिप्]: @deva[चेक्षिपत्] 'throwing again and again', etc.

### (a) Optional @deva[वस्] Form

The termination @deva[अत्] is optionally changed to @deva[वस्] when added to the root @deva[विद्]: @deva[विदत्] or @deva[विद्वस्] 'knowing'

### (b) Agent Sense

The affix @deva[अत्] when added to @deva[द्विष्] and @deva[सु] 'to extract Soma juice in a sacrifice' has the sense of an agent: @deva[द्विषत्] m. 'an enemy'; @deva[यज्ञे सर्वे सुन्वन्तः] 'all are the extractors of Soma juice in a sacrifice'

### (c) Fitness, Respect

When affixed to @deva[अर्ह्] it has the sense of 'fitness, respect': @deva[अर्हत्] 'one deserving respect, respectable'

### (d) Ease vs. Difficulty

@deva[इ] 2 P. and @deva[धृ] cau. take the affix @deva[अत्] when the idea of difficulty is not present: @deva[अधीयत्] 'studying without experiencing any difficulty', @deva[धारयत्] 'holding or bearing with ease'; but @deva[कृच्छ्रेण अधीते], @deva[कृच्छ्रेण धारयति].

rules.title: Declension of अत् Participles
rules.body:
## Declension of @deva[अत्] Participles

The declension of the Participles in @deva[अत्] has been treated of in @ref[116].

rules.title: Formation of Present Ātmanepada Participle
rules.body:
## Formation of Present Ātmanepada Participle

The participle of the Present Ātmanepada is formed by adding @deva[आन] to the root which undergoes the same changes before it, as before the termination @deva[अते] or @deva[अन्ते] of the 3rd plural present.

### @deva[आन] → @deva[मान] Substitution

@deva[आन] is changed to @deva[मान] in the case of roots of the 1st, 4th, 6th and 10th classes, and all derived roots — or rather, when the base ends in @deva[अ], before which the @deva[अ] of the base remains unchanged.

### Examples

| Root (Class) | Participle | Meaning |
|--------------|------------|---------|
| @deva[एध्] (1) | @deva[एधमान] | growing |
| @deva[वन्द्] (1) | @deva[वन्दमान] | saluting |
| @deva[शी] (2) | @deva[शयान] | lying down |
| @deva[द्विष्] (2) | @deva[द्विषाण] | hating |
| @deva[हन्] with @deva[आ] (2) | @deva[आघ्नान] | killing |
| @deva[धा] (3) | @deva[दधान] | holding |
| @deva[हु] (3) | @deva[जुह्वाण] | sacrificing |
| @deva[दिव्] (4) | @deva[दीव्यमान] | playing |
| @deva[सु] (5) | @deva[सुन्वान] | extracting |
| @deva[तुद्] (6) | @deva[तुदमान] | giving pain |
| @deva[रुध्] (7) | @deva[रुन्धान] | obstructing |
| @deva[कृ] (8) | @deva[कुर्वाण] | doing |
| @deva[तन्] (8) | @deva[तन्वान] | stretching |
| @deva[क्री] (9) | @deva[क्रीणान] | buying |
| @deva[चुर्] (10) | @deva[चोरयमाण] | stealing, etc. |

### Derived Forms

@deva[बुध्] (1 cl.) cau.: @deva[बोधयति]—@deva[बोधयमान] 'causing to know'

Desiderative: @deva[बुबोधिषति]—@deva[बुबोधिषमाण] 'being desirous to know', etc.

rules.title: Special Forms of आन Participles
Extended Use of आन for Habit and Capacity
Formation of Present Passive Participle
rules.body:
## Formation of Present Passive Participle

The participle of the Present Passive is formed by adding @deva[मान] to the Passive base in @deva[य]:

### Examples

| Root | Participle | Meaning |
|------|------------|---------|
| @deva[बुध्] | @deva[बुध्यमान] | who or what is known |
| @deva[अद्] | @deva[अद्यमान] | what is eaten |
| @deva[दा] | @deva[दीयमान] | who or what is given |
| @deva[चि] | @deva[चीयमान] | who or what is gathered |
| @deva[कृ] | @deva[क्रियमाण] | what is done |
| @deva[कृ] | @deva[कीर्यमाण] | what is scattered |
| @deva[चोर्] | @deva[चोर्यमाण] | who or what is stolen |

### Derived Forms

@deva[बुध्] cau. Pass.: @deva[बोध्यमान] 'who or what is caused to know'

@deva[बुध्] Des. Pass.: @deva[बुबोधिषयमाण] 'who or what is desired to know', etc.

rules.title: Declension of मान Participles
rules.body:
## Declension of @deva[मान] Participles

The participles formed according to @ref[669] are declined like nouns ending in @deva[अ] m., f. and n.

---

### (b) Participles of the Perfect

rules.title: Weak Terminations in Perfect and Past Participles
rules.body:
## Weak Terminations in Perfect and Past Participles

The terminations of the Perfect and the Past participles are weak, and therefore the radical vowel does not take its Guṇa substitute before these.

The penultimate nasal is generally dropped before these (See @ref[534]).

rules.title: Formation of Perfect Participles
rules.body:
## Formation of Perfect Participles

The participle of the Perfect Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada is formed by adding @deva[वस्] and @deva[आन] generally to that form of the root which it assumes before the termination of the 3rd person plural.

### Rules for @deva[इ] Insertion

If this form consists of one syllable only or when the root ends in @deva[आ], @deva[वस्] has the intermediate @deva[इ] added to it.

@deva[इ] is optionally prefixed to @deva[वस्] in the case of the roots @deva[गम्], @deva[हन्], @deva[दृश्], @deva[विश्] and @deva[विद्] (6 cl.).

@deva[जन्] and @deva[खन्], and @deva[गम्] and @deva[हन्], when they do not take @deva[इ], form this participle from that base which they would assume before the 2nd person singular termination.

### PARASMAIPADA

| Root | Meaning | Perf. Base (3rd pl.) | Perf. Participle | Translation |
|------|---------|---------------------|------------------|-------------|
| @deva[इ] | to go | @deva[ईयु] | @deva[ईयिवस्] | who or what went |
| @deva[ऋ] | " | @deva[आरु] | @deva[आरिवस्] | " " |
| @deva[नी] | to carry | @deva[निनी] | @deva[निनीवस्] | who or what carried |
| @deva[पच्] | to cook | @deva[पेच्] | @deva[पेचिवस्] | " cooked |
| @deva[वच्] | to speak | @deva[ऊच्] | @deva[ऊचिवस्] | " spoke |
| @deva[यज्] | to sacrifice | @deva[ईज्] | @deva[ईजिवस्] | " sacrificed |
| @deva[भञ्ज्] | to break | @deva[बभञ्ज्] | @deva[बभञ्ज्वस्] | " broke |
| @deva[अस्] | to throw | @deva[आस्] | @deva[आसिवस्] | " threw |
| @deva[स्तु] | to praise | @deva[तुष्टु] | @deva[तुष्टुवस्] | " praised |
| @deva[कृ] | to do | @deva[चक्र्] | @deva[चक्रवस्] | " did |
| @deva[भिद्] | to split | @deva[बिभिद्] | @deva[बिभिद्वस्] | " split |
| @deva[दा] | to give | @deva[दद्] | @deva[ददिवस्] | " gave, etc. |
| @deva[घस्] | to eat | @deva[जक्ष्] | @deva[जक्षिवस्] | " ate |
| @deva[दृश्] | to see | @deva[ददृश्] | @deva[ददृशिवस्] or @deva[ददृश्वस्] | " saw |
| @deva[विद्] | to know, etc. | @deva[विविद्] | @deva[विविद्वस्] or @deva[विविदिवस्] | " knew, etc. |
| @deva[विश्] | to enter | @deva[विविश्] | @deva[विविशिवस्] or @deva[विविश्वस्] | " entered |

### Special Forms

@deva[जन्] has @deva[जजन्वस्]

@deva[खन्]—@deva[चखन्वस्]

@deva[गम्]—@deva[जग्मिवस्] or @deva[जगन्वस्]

@deva[हन्]—@deva[जघ्निवस्] or @deva[जघन्वस्]

### (I) Roots Beginning with @deva[अ]

In the case of roots beginning with @deva[अ], @deva[न्] is not inserted, as it is in the Perfect: @deva[अञ्ज्]—@deva[आञ्जिवस्]

### (a) Declension

For the declension of these participles see @ref[124].

### ĀTMANEPADA

| Root | Meaning | Perf. Base (3rd pl.) | Perf. Participle |
|------|---------|---------------------|------------------|
| @deva[नी] | to carry | @deva[निनी] | @deva[निन्यान] |
| @deva[दा] | to give | @deva[दद्] | @deva[ददान] |
| @deva[पच्] | to cook | @deva[पेच्] | @deva[पेचान] |
| @deva[यज्] | to sacrifice | @deva[ईज्] | @deva[ईजान] |
| @deva[कृ] | to do | @deva[चक्र्] | @deva[चक्राण] |
| @deva[वच्] | to speak | @deva[ऊच्] | @deva[ऊचान] |
| @deva[स्तु] | to praise | @deva[तुष्टु] | @deva[तुष्टुवान] |
| @deva[श्रु] | to hear | @deva[शुश्रु] | @deva[शुश्रुवाण] |

### (b) Declension

These are declined like nouns ending in @deva[अ] m., f., n.

rules.title: Irregular Perfect Participles from ऋ-Ending Roots
Frequency of Perfect Participle Usage
rules.body:
## Frequency of Perfect Participle Usage

The Perfect participle is not frequently used. The only participles that are most common to be met with are those formed from the roots @deva[सम्भू], @deva[वद्], @deva[स्था] and @deva[श्रु].

rules.title: Periphrastic Perfect Participles
rules.body:
## Periphrastic Perfect Participles

The participles of the Periphrastic Perfect Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada are formed by the addition of the Perfect Participal forms of the auxiliary verbs @deva[कृ], @deva[अस्] or @deva[भू] to the base in @deva[आम्].

### Examples

@deva[दयालासिवस्], @deva[ञ्चत्रिषिवस्]

@deva[गण्]—@deva[गणयामासिवस्], @deva[गणयामचक्रुवस्], etc.

---

### (c) Past Passive Participles

rules.title: Formation of Past Passive Participle
rules.body:
## Formation of Past Passive Participle

The Past Passive Participle is formed by the addition of the affix @deva[त्] to the root.

### Examples

| Root | Participle | Meaning |
|------|------------|---------|
| @deva[स्ना] | @deva[स्नात] | bathed |
| @deva[जि] | @deva[जित] | conquered |
| @deva[नी] | @deva[नीत] | carried |
| @deva[श्रु] | @deva[श्रुत] | heard |
| @deva[भू] | @deva[भूत] | become |
| @deva[हृ] | @deva[हृत] | taken away |
| @deva[त्यज्] | @deva[त्यक्त] | abandoned |
| @deva[चिन्त्] | @deva[चिन्त्] | thought or meditated upon, etc. |

rules.title: Samprasāraṇa Before त् Affix
rules.body:
## Samprasāraṇa Before @deva[त्] Affix

Roots capable of taking Samprasāraṇa take it before the affix @deva[त्].

rules.title: Affix त् Is Weak with Exceptions
rules.body:
The affix @deva[त्] is weak.

**Exceptions:—**

(a) The roots @deva[नी], @deva[विद्] 1 cl., @deva[दिश्], @deva[विष्टर्], @deva[प्रुष्] and @deva[भृष्] admit of the Guṇa change before @deva[त्] when @deva[इ] is prefixed to it; @deva[या] I. A also does the same when it takes @deva[इ] (see @ref[686]b),

(b) Such of the roots of the 1st class as have @deva[उ] for their penultimate change their vowel to Guṇa optionally, when the affix @deva[त्] is added with the Intermediate @deva[इ], and in P. P. Participle as used impersonally, or when it conveys the sense of beginning to perform the action or undergoing the condition expressed by the root; @deva[मुद्] 'to delight' @deva[मुदित], but 'to begin to delight' @deva[मुदित] or @deva[प्रमुदित]: @deva[म्हुदित] or @deva[प्रमोदित रामयुः]: @deva[प्रहुद्दितः] or @deva[प्रमोदितः मायुः], &c. similarly; @deva[बुद]-@deva[प्रबुदित] or @deva[प्रबोदित] &c.

rules.title: Penultimate Radical Nasal Generally Dropped
rules.body: The Penultimate radical nasal is generally dropped. (See @ref[674]).

rules.title: Augment इ Prefixed to त् in Certain Roots
rules.body: The augment @deva[इ] is prefixed to this @deva[त्] in the case of certain roots, optionally in the case of some and not at all in the case of others.

rules.title: Roots Not Taking इ Before त् with Examples
rules.body:
As a general rule, all roots ending in a vowel, and such as take the @deva[इ] optionally before any termination, and Aniṭ roots ending in consonants generally, do not take @deva[इ]; the rules of Sandhi given in the foregoing chapters that are applicable in particular cases ought to be observed,—

| Roots. | P. P. Ptc | | Roots. | P. P. Ptc. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[पा] | @deva[पात] protected | | @deva[त्यज] | @deva[त्यक्त] abandoned. |
| @deva[क्षि] | @deva[क्षित] resorted to | | @deva[भुञ्ज] | @deva[भुग्ध] fried. |
| @deva[नी] | @deva[नीत] carried. | | @deva[यज्] | @deva[इष्ट] sacrificed |
| @deva[श्रु] | @deva[श्रुत] heard. | | @deva[दुश्] | @deva[दुष्ट] awakened. |
| @deva[भू] | @deva[भूत] become. | | @deva[विध्] | @deva[विद्ध] pierced. |
| @deva[कृ] | @deva[कृत] done. | | @deva[स्तृ] | @deva[स्तृत] spread. |
| @deva[ऊर्णु] | @deva[ऊर्णुत] covered. | | @deva[लभ] | @deva[लब्ध] obtained. |
| @deva[वै] | @deva[ऊत] woven | | @deva[बन्धु] | @deva[बद्ध] bound. |
| @deva[व्ये] | @deva[वीत] covered | | @deva[दृष] | @deva[दृष्ट] seen. |
| @deva[हे][^1] | @deva[हूत] called &c., | | @deva[हिद] | @deva[छिद्ध] cut out &c. |

| Roots. | P. P. Ptc. | | Roots. | P. P. Ptc. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[वच्] | @deva[उक्त] spoken | | @deva[दंश्] | @deva[दष्ट] bitten |
| @deva[गुह्] | @deva[गूढ] concealed | | @deva[द्विष्] | @deva[द्विष्ट] hated, &c. |
| @deva[मृज्] | @deva[मृष्ट] wiped off, &c. | | @deva[शास्] | @deva[शिष्ट] governed |
| @deva[सिध्] | @deva[सिद्ध] accomplished, &c. | | @deva[दह्] | @deva[दग्ध] burnt |
| @deva[तृप्] | @deva[तृप्त] satisfied | | @deva[वह्] | @deva[ऊढ] borne |
| @deva[नश्] | @deva[नष्ट] perished, &c. | | @deva[सह्] | @deva[सोढ] endured |
| @deva[वृध्] | @deva[वृद्ध] grown | | @deva[क्षुध्] | @deva[क्षुस्त] destroyed |
| @deva[भू] | @deva[भूत] happened, completed, &c. | | @deva[लिह्] | @deva[लीढ] licked |
| @deva[शक्] | @deva[शक्त] able | | @deva[मुह्] | @deva[मुग्ध] or @deva[मूढ] faint |
| @deva[सिच्] | @deva[सिक्त] sprinkled | | @deva[नह्] | @deva[नद्ध] bound |
| @deva[पृच्छ] | @deva[पृष्ट] asked | | @deva[क्षिप्] | @deva[क्षिप्त] dropped |

**Exceptions:—**

(a) @deva[ज्ञा], @deva[जाग्], @deva[स्था] and @deva[आस्य] take @deva[इ]; the final vowel of the first two takes Guṇa substitute, and the last two drop their final; @deva[ज्ञायित], @deva[जागरित]; @deva[स्थित], @deva[आस्यदित].

(b) @deva[पत्] takes @deva[इ] though it admits of @deva[इ] optionally in Desiderative; @deva[पतित].

(c) The Anit roots @deva[वस्] and @deva[श्लिष्] admit @deva[इ] before @deva[त्]; @deva[उषित], @deva[शुषित].

[^1]: @deva[हे] substitutes @deva[ह] for its @deva[इ].

rules.title: Seṭ Roots and Derivative Bases Admitting इ
rules.body:
Seṭ roots (subject to @ref[684]), and all derivative bases admit of @deva[इ]; roots of the Tenth Class and causals reject their final @deva[अय], Par. Frequentatives their final @deva[अ], and Ātm. Frequentatives their @deva[य]:—

| Roots. | P. P. Ptc. | | Roots. | P. P. Ptc. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[शङ्क्] | @deva[शङ्कित] 'suspected.' | | @deva[कथ्] | @deva[कथित] 'told.' |
| @deva[उद्] | @deva[उदित] 'spoken.' | | @deva[प्रथ्] | @deva[प्रथित] 'spread.' |

| Roots. | P. P. Ptc. | | Roots. | P. P. Ptc. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[एष्] | @deva[एषित] 'increased.' | | @deva[बोधय्] cau. Base of @deva[बुध्], @deva[बोधित] 'made to know.' |
| @deva[कम्प्] | @deva[कम्पित] 'shaken.' | | @deva[चिकीर्ष] des. b. of @deva[कृ]; @deva[चिकीर्षित] 'desired to do.' |
| @deva[चुर्] | @deva[चोरित] 'stolen, deceived.' | | @deva[बोबुध्] Ātm. Fre. Base of @deva[बुध्], @deva[बोबुधित] 'frequently known.' |
| @deva[मृश्] | @deva[मृशित] 'taken.' | | @deva[बोभूय]—Par. Fre. Base of @deva[भू], @deva[बोभूत] &c. |

**Exceptions:—**@deva[इष्], @deva[उष्], @deva[चष्], 'to go, to till,' &c., @deva[चित्] 'to know to observe,' &c., @deva[विद्], @deva[मिद्], @deva[स्तृ], @deva[भृत्], @deva[भृष्], @deva[भी], @deva[पी], @deva[हीय], @deva[स्यै], @deva[प्रिह्य], @deva[चुष्], @deva[डूष्], @deva[दुष्], @deva[सुष्], @deva[रुष्].

N. B. There are many Seṭ roots which reject the intermediate @deva[इ] but as some of them form their P. P. participles in @deva[न] and others irregularly, they will be given in their proper places.

rules.title: Roots Inserting इ Optionally Before त्
rules.body:
The following roots insert @deva[इ] optionally:—

(a) @deva[मुष्], @deva[सन्], @deva[पुष्], @deva[दुष्], @deva[षुष्], @deva[क्षुष्], @deva[जुष्], @deva[सुष्], @deva[अष्य], @deva[शुष्], with @deva[स्तु], @deva[स्वप्] with @deva[आ], and @deva[हृष्] 4. 1. Par. when used with @deva[लोमन्] 'the hair,' or when it means 'to be surprised or disappointed,' @deva[मुषितः], @deva[इत्यायः], (see @ref[696] a), @deva[चलितः], @deva[कुलितः], @deva[कुद्र]. Bh. VIII. 8; @deva[स्वै], @deva[शूष्] 'to do, 'wasted, perished,' @deva[द्रोषित]; @deva[स्पृष्ट], @deva[स्पृशित]; @deva[क्षुष्], @deva[क्षुषित]; @deva[शून्], @deva[ज्वरितः]; @deva[रुष्], @deva[रुषित]; @deva[आह्] (See @ref[696] a), @deva[मुघवत्] or @deva[हुषित]; @deva[आस्वाप्तः], @deva[आस्वपित]; @deva[हृष्ट]—@deva[हर्षित]—@deva[लोमन्] 'horripilated with joy,' @deva[हृष्ट]—@deva[हर्षितः लोमः] @deva[हृष्य्]—@deva[हृषितो धीवान्] 'disappointed.'

(b) @deva[क्षिप्] and @deva[भ] take @deva[इ] optionally before @deva[त्] and @deva[स्य]; @deva[क्षिप्तः], @deva[क्षिपित]; @deva[भूतः], @deva[भवित].

(c) The following roots admit of @deva[इ] optionally before @deva[त्] when the P. P. Participle is used impersonally, or when it conveys the sense of beginning to perform the action or to undergo the condition expressed by the root; @deva[मुद्], @deva[स्मर्], @deva[पुष्], @deva[फल्], @deva[शिक्ष्], @deva[वृत्], @deva[स्पृश्], I. 4. cl. @deva[स्मुर्]-@deva[स्पृष्ट], @deva[एज्]-@deva[स्फार्], @deva[क्षिद्] and @deva[स्विदु] I. 4. P. I. A.; @deva[स्मृद्]—@deva[प्रस्मृदितः] or @deva[प्रस्वेदितः चैत्रः] 'Chaitra has begun to perspire;' @deva[प्रस्वेदितं] or @deva[प्रस्वेदितमनेन] 'he has perspired,' &c.; @deva[स्वेदु] 4. cl. has @deva[स्वेदित] also.

**N. B.** When the participle is not used in the sense given above these roots reject @deva[इ]; @deva[स्पृष्टः]—@deva[स्पृष्ट]; 'perspired, sounded inarticulately,' &c.

rules.title: Special Rules for अञ्च्, युज्, and शुष्
rules.body:
(a) @deva[अञ्च्] in the sense of 'to worship' takes @deva[इ]; @deva[अञ्चित] (b) @deva[गम्] 'bent' not in the sense of worship @deva[गुप्तः] with @deva[सम्]—@deva[समूढः] (@deva[समुङ्गिरे शबरीति पदै]).

(b) @deva[युज्] and @deva[शुष्] reject @deva[इ] when they express the idea of 'immoderation' or 'rudeness;' @deva[युष्टः] 'rude,' @deva[विषृष्टः] 'ill-mannered;' but @deva[युजितः] 'overpowered, trifled with,' &c., @deva[विश्रुषित] 'tormented or ill-treated.'

rules.title: Substitution of न for त् After इ or ऋ
rules.body:
@deva[न][^1] is substituted for @deva[त्] when it immediately follows a final @deva[इ] or @deva[ऋ]; this final @deva[इ] is also changed to @deva[ई]; @deva[शि]—@deva[शीन], @deva[ऋ]—@deva[ऋण]; @deva[पुल्]—@deva[पूर्ण] (See @ref[693]).

**Exceptions:—**

(a) @deva[शीग्] has @deva[शीतं] when it means 'a part, a portion,' @deva[शीनं] in other senses.

(b) @deva[विङ्] 6. P. A. takes @deva[त्] in the sense of 'fit for enjoyment or famous,' @deva[विक्तः] 'wealth, property,' @deva[विकः] 'famous'; @deva[विनः] in other cases.

(c) @deva[भृङ्], @deva[पूर्] and @deva[चुस्छु]; @deva[भृतः], @deva[पूर्णः] 'filled,' (also @deva[पूतः] when it means the same as @deva[अत्]), @deva[चुस्छुः].

[^1]: @deva[इदुपधावो न्पनादौ नः पुशिप्य च हि ।] @deva[परयोप्यस्तोऽसत्त्वानुपेत्य च ।] @deva[स्यादियूस् ।] Pāṇ. VIII. 2. 42–44.

rules.title: Roots with Conjunct Consonants Substituting न for त्
rules.body:
Roots ending in @deva[ऋ][^1] (@deva[ऋ], @deva[लृ] and @deva[ओ] changeable to @deva[आ]) and beginning with a conjunct consonant containing a semi-vowel also substitute @deva[न्] for @deva[त्]; @deva[ह्रु] 'to run, to sleep,' @deva[प्राणः]; @deva[म्लै] 'to fade,' @deva[म्लानः]; @deva[स्रु]—@deva[स्त्राणः] 'collected to a mass,' &c.

**Exceptions:—**@deva[ग्रै] 'to name,' &c., @deva[स्वै] 'to contemplate,' @deva[ग्राणः] and @deva[प्लै]; @deva[स्वितः], @deva[स्वानः], @deva[ग्रातः] and @deva[प्रातः].

[^1]: @deva[पूर्वरुषाद्रुषुतैः ।] Pāṇ. VIII. 2. 19.

rules.title: Roots from § 414 and ज्ञा Substituting न for त्
rules.body:
The roots given at @ref[414] and @deva[ज्ञा] substitute @deva[न्] for @deva[त्].

| Roots | | P. P. Ptc. | Roots | | P. P. Ptc. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[री] | to flow, to move | @deva[रीणः] | @deva[जू] | to grow old | @deva[जीर्णः] |
| @deva[ली] | to melt, etc. | @deva[लीनः] | @deva[दृ] | to tear | @deva[दीर्णः] |
| @deva[श्ली] | to go, to hold | @deva[श्लीनः] | @deva[नी] | to lead | @deva[नीर्णः] |
| @deva[श्ली] | to go, to move | @deva[श्लीनः] | @deva[पू] | to fill, to gratify | @deva[पूर्णः] |
| @deva[धू] | to shake | @deva[धूनः] | @deva[भृ] | to bear, to nourish | @deva[भूर्णः] |
| @deva[नू] | to destroy | @deva[नूनः] | @deva[मृ] | to hurt, to kill | @deva[मूर्णः] |
| @deva[लू] | to cut | @deva[लूनः] | @deva[वृ] | to choose | @deva[वूर्णः] |
| @deva[इ] | to go | @deva[ईणः] | @deva[श्रि] | to tear asunder | @deva[शीर्णः] |
| @deva[कू] | to scatter | @deva[कीर्णः] | @deva[स्तृ] | to scatter | @deva[स्तीर्णः] |
| @deva[गृ] | to utter a sound, to praise, etc. | @deva[गीर्णः] | @deva[ज्ञा] | to grow old | @deva[ज्ञीणः] |

rules.title: हृ and गृ Substituting न for त् with Vowel Lengthening
rules.body: @deva[हृ] and @deva[गृ] 'to sound indistinctly,' substitute @deva[न] for @deva[त्] and lengthen their vowels; @deva[हीनः] 'gone,' @deva[गीनः].

rules.title: Comprehensive List of Roots Substituting न् for त्
rules.body:
The following roots substitute @deva[न्] for @deva[त्]:—

| Roots | | P. P. Ptc. | Roots | | P. P. Ptc. |

| @deva[ह्नु] | to torment | @deva[ह्नूनः] | @deva[त्री] | 4. A. to move, to cover | @deva[त्राणः] |
| @deva[धी] | to hold, to accomplish | @deva[धीनः] | @deva[स्पि] | I. P. to grow, to swell | @deva[स्पानः] |
| @deva[ल्यी] | 4. A. | @deva[लीनः] | @deva[सू] | 4. A. to bring forth, to produce | @deva[सूनः] |
| @deva[मी] | 4. A. to give pain | @deva[मीनः] | @deva[भज्] | to break | @deva[भग्नः] |
| @deva[नै] | to perish, to waste | @deva[नीनः] | @deva[सुज्] | 6. P. | @deva[सुग्नः] |

| @deva[ह्रु] | to go | @deva[ह्रुनः] | @deva[रुज्] | to break | @deva[रुग्नः] |
| @deva[हा] | to abandon | @deva[हीनः] | @deva[लज्] | 6. A. to be ashamed | @deva[लग्नः] |
| @deva[विज्] | | @deva[विग्नः], @deva[उद्विग्नः] | @deva[स्कन्द्] | with @deva[वि] | @deva[विस्कन्नः] |
| @deva[त्रुस्य] | | @deva[त्रुग्नः] | @deva[स्कन्द्] | with @deva[परि] | @deva[परिस्कन्नः]-@deva[स्कुनः] |
| @deva[स्फुर्] | I. P. | @deva[स्फुर्णः] | @deva[विद्] | 4. A. | @deva[विन्नः] |

rules.title: Contextual Substitution of न for त् - Special Rules
rules.body:
(a) @deva[ऋण][^1] when it means 'to incur debt' substitutes @deva[न्]; @deva[ऋणः] 'debt;' but @deva[ऋतः], 'gone.'

(b) @deva[क्षि], when the P. P. Participle has an active sense, substitutes @deva[न] and lengthens its @deva[इ]; @deva[क्षीणः], reduced, emaciated; but when a curse is implied, or pity expressed, the change is optional; @deva[क्षीणश्चायं] or @deva[क्षितश्चायं भिक्षुः] i. e. 'die;' @deva[क्षीणः] or @deva[क्षितः भिक्षुः सत्येतरे] 'oh, the poor ascetic is reduced thin;' but @deva[अन्यः क्षितः ऋतः].

(c) @deva[द्युत्][^2] takes @deva[न] when it does not mean 'to gamble;' @deva[द्युनः] 'a sport in which nothing is staked,' but @deva[द्युतः] 'gambling.'

(d) @deva[शा][^2] with @deva[निस्] takes @deva[न] except when it has @deva[शाकः] for its subject; @deva[निर्शानोऽग्निः] 'the fire is extinguished;' @deva[निर्शानः ऋषिः] 'the sage is absolved;' but @deva[निर्शितः शाकः]

(e) @deva[स्पृश्] takes @deva[न] when the notion of touch is not present; @deva[संस्पृतः वृश्चिकः] 'a scorpion contracted through cold;' when it means 'to be oppressed by or cold' @deva[स्पृष्टोऽयमुकेन अयं मृदानुकूल (की) स्पृष्ट-कृतः], but @deva[अग्निना स्पृष्टः] and not @deva[अग्नीन] as the idea of touch is present and also when preceded by @deva[परि]; @deva[परिस्पृष्टः युधि], &c.; with @deva[अनि] and @deva[अव] the change is optional; @deva[अनिस्पृषः] or @deva[अनिस्पृग्नः युधि], @deva[अवस्पृष्ठ] or @deva[अवस्पृनः व्यूहस्पृशः]; but @deva[समवस्पानः]

[^1]: @deva[ऋणुमाङ्घयुमात्रशुवै ।] Pāṇ. VIII. 2. 60.

[^2]: @deva[दिवितोऽक्तिजिर्मीमेतु; निशानोऽन्यैः ।] Pāṇ. VIII. 2. 49–50.

rules.title: Roots Optionally Taking न or त्
rules.body: The roots @deva[मुद्], @deva[विद्य], 6. A., @deva[ज्ञद्], @deva[शा], @deva[हा] and @deva[हा] take @deva[न] or @deva[त्]; @deva[मुग्नः] or @deva[मुतः]; @deva[विनः] or @deva[वितः], @deva[ज्ञानः] or @deva[ज्ञातः], @deva[शानः] or @deva[शातः] and @deva[ह्रानः] or @deva[ह्रातः].

rules.title: Special Rules for पीयः with Contextual Conditions
rules.body: @deva[पीयः] has @deva[पूतः] when it is used with 'one's own limbs.' @deva[पूतं क्षौमं], and @deva[पीयः] or @deva[पूनः] in other cases, as @deva[पीयः] or @deva[पूनः रथः]; when it is preceded by a preposition, @deva[इ] is not substituted, and the vowel; @deva[प्रस्यातः]; but when it is used with @deva[अङ्गै] or @deva[ज्चृपतु] with the preposition @deva[आ], @deva[इ] is necessarily substituted; @deva[आपीतः अस्यः]; @deva[भूयौनं ज्चृषै].

rules.title: Nasal-Ending Roots - Vowel Lengthening and Nasal Dropping
rules.body:
(a) Roots ending in a nasal lengthen their penultimate vowel before a weak termination beginning with any consonant except a nasal or a semivowel, or before the affix @deva[किन्] @deva[चर्]—@deva[चारिन्], @deva[तर्]—@deva[तारिन्], &c.

(b) Anit roots ending in a nasal, the root @deva[वन्] 1. P. and the eight roots of the 8th class—@deva[तन्] and others (see p. 355) drop their nasal before a weak termination beginning with any consonant except a nasal or a semivowel:—

| Roots | | P. P. Ptc. | Roots | | P. P. Ptc. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[मन्] | 'to think', &c. | @deva[मतः] | @deva[नम्] | 'to bow' | @deva[नतः] |
| @deva[ङृह्] | 'to strike,' | @deva[हतः] | @deva[यम्] | 'to restrain' | @deva[यतः] |
| @deva[एघ्] | 'to sport' | @deva[हतः] | @deva[वन्] | 1. P. 'to sound, to serve,' &c. | @deva[वतः] |
| @deva[गच्] | 'to go' | @deva[गतः] | @deva[युष्] | 'to shine' | @deva[युतः] |
| @deva[तन्] | | @deva[ततः] | @deva[वुच्] | 'to graze' | @deva[वतः] |
| @deva[क्षुण्] | | @deva[क्षुतः] | @deva[नुद्] | 'to beg' | @deva[नतः] |
| @deva[सम्प्] | | @deva[सप्तः] | | | |

rules.title: हन्, जन्, सन् Dropping Nasal with Vowel Lengthening
rules.body: The roots @deva[हन्], @deva[जन्] and @deva[सन्], drop their nasal and at the same time lengthen their vowel; @deva[हातः], @deva[जातः], @deva[सातः].

rules.title: Radical इ Changing to ऊ Before त् or न्
rules.body: A radical @deva[इ] preceding or following a vowel is sometimes changed to @deva[ऊ] before @deva[त्] or @deva[न्]; when it is preceded by @deva[य] it is dropped; @deva[इङ्]—@deva[इतः], @deva[ऊतः]; @deva[पुरीत्], @deva[पुङ्]—@deva[पूर्णः], @deva[नीरु]—@deva[लीणः], @deva[पु]—@deva[पूतः], @deva[द्युतः] (See @ref[693], c.).

rules.title: Roots Rejecting इ in Limited Senses
rules.body:
The following roots (some forming their P. P. P. irregularly) reject @deva[इ] in the limited sense attached to each:—

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[चुष्]—@deva[चुष्टः] | 'a churning handle.' | @deva[विसर्]—@deva[विसृटः] | 'a note.' |
| @deva[स्मरु]—@deva[स्मृतः] | 'the mind.' | @deva[कृष्]—@deva[फृष्टः] | 'a decoction easily prepared.' (@deva[अनासासमासो: कदाचिदुक्तः] Sid. Kau.) |
| @deva[स्थुप्]—@deva[स्थातः] | 'darkness.' | | |
| @deva[लग्]—@deva[लग्नः] | 'attached.' | @deva[चाहृ]—@deva[चाटः] | 'much.' |
| @deva[स्वैत्]—@deva[स्वातः] | 'indistinct.' | | |

In their usual senses they have @deva[हृषितः], @deva[स्पर्शितः], @deva[क्षमितः], @deva[म्लेश्छितः], @deva[विरञ्जितः], @deva[फणितः] and @deva[वाह्यितः].

rules.title: दा and धा - Special त् Dropping After Vowel-Ending Prepositions
rules.body: @deva[दा] 'to give,' and @deva[धा], form their P. P. Ptc. as @deva[दत्तः]; the @deva[त्] of @deva[दत्तः] is dropped after a preposition ending in a vowel; @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्रदत्तः]; but in this latter case the preceding @deva[इ] or @deva[उ] is lengthened; @deva[नीदत्तः], @deva[दत्तः], &c.; @deva[त्] may optionally be retained also; @deva[अवदत्तः], @deva[अवदत्], @deva[प्रदत्तः], &c.

rules.title: Comprehensive List of Irregular Past Passive Participles
rules.body:
The following roots form their P. P. Participles irregularly:—

| Roots | | P. P. Ptc. | Roots | | P. P. Ptc. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

rules.title: Roots इ and यज् Taking Affix वत् in Active Sense
rules.body: (a) The roots @deva[इ] and @deva[यज्] take the affix @deva[वत्] like @deva[त्] in an active sense; @deva[इत्वत्] 'one who extracted Soma juice;' @deva[यजत्वत्] 'one who has offered a sacrifice;' @deva[अत्] is added to @deva[जु] optionally in the same sense; @deva[जीर्णः] or @deva[जग्वतः] 'one who has become old' (also @deva[जग्मिवत्]).

rules.title: Declension of Participles in त् or न् and Note on Passive Force
rules.body:
The participles in @deva[त्] or @deva[न] follow the Declension of nouns in @deva[अ].

**Note:** The P. P. participles have not always a passive force:—

rules.title: Affix त् Showing Place of Habitual Action
rules.body:
The affix @deva[त्][^1] added to roots having the sense of 'staying,' or 'going' shows the place where the action usually takes place; @deva[अत्र मुकुन्दस्य आसितं] 'this is the place where Mukunda to sit;' @deva[इदं गतं रामस्य] 'this is the path by which the husband of Rāmā used to pass;' @deva[अत्रुहौ एतत् अस्य] 'this is the place where Anaṅta took his food,' &c.

[^1]: @deva[अधिकरणे च क्तोऽयुद्धिस्मृत्यसौत्कारुयृत्त: ।] Pāṇ. III. 4. 48.

rules.title: Past Passive Participles with Active Sense
rules.body: (a) The P. P. Participles of roots implying motion, of intransitive roots, and of the roots @deva[शी], @deva[छुत्], @deva[स्था], @deva[आस्], @deva[द्युल्] 'to dwell,' @deva[जन्], @deva[सुप्], and @deva[जु] 4. cl. have an active sense; @deva[गतोऽहं मद्रापुरं] 'I went to Madras;' @deva[स्थगनः भवः] 'the boy has become languid,' @deva[क्षीणा धृता: ह्रारिः] 'Hari embraced Lakshmi;' @deva[शेषोऽग्रिशयात्रि:] 'slept on Sesha;' @deva[वैकुण्ठे-मविष्टितः] 'dwelt in Vaikuṇṭha;' @deva[शिनुषुदुवसितः] 'served Shiva,' @deva[हरिदिनेऽद्य उपोषितः] 'observed a fast on the day sacred to Hari,' @deva[रामजुञु जातः] 'was born after Rāma;' @deva[गङ्गासुस्यतः] sat on Garuḍa; @deva[विश्चैतनुधीर्ह्रातः] 'grown after this,' &c.

rules.title: Past Passive Participles as Neuter Abstract Nouns
rules.body: P. P. Participles have sometimes the sense of neuter abstract nouns; as @deva[वचितं] 'speech', @deva[शयितं] 'sleep', @deva[हसितं] 'laughing,' similarly @deva[स्थितं], @deva[गतं], etc.; See Bhaṭṭ. VII. 125.

rules.title: Past Passive Participles with Present Tense Sense
rules.body:
The P. P. Participles of roots meaning 'to think or to wish,' 'to know,' 'to adore,' and of the roots @deva[हन्], @deva[भू] etc. have the sense of the present Tense; @deva[राज्ञा मतः] 'he is honoured by the king;' @deva[सत्त्रैष आरुत्रेः द्युतः तथा] the root is kindled;' so @deva[भूतः] etc.

---

## (d) Past Active Participles.

rules.title: Formation of Past Active Participles
rules.body:
Past Active participles are derived from the P. P. Passive Participle in @deva[त्] or @deva[न] by changing it to them the affix @deva[वत्]; e.g.

| Roots | | P. P. Ptc. | P. Ac. Ptc. | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[भू] | to be | @deva[भूतः] | @deva[भूतवत्] | one or that has been |
| @deva[कृ] | to do | @deva[कृतः] | @deva[कृतवत्] | „ „ done |
| @deva[कृ] | to scatter | @deva[कीर्णः] | @deva[कीर्णवत्] | „ „ scattered |
| @deva[दिद्] | to cut | @deva[दिन्नः] | @deva[दिन्नवत्] | „ „ cut |
| etc. | | etc. | etc. | etc. |

---

## (e) Participle of the Future Tense.

rules.title: Formation of Future Tense Participles
rules.body:
The Participle of the Simple Future, Active as well as Passive, is formed from the third person singular form of the Second Future of a root. The Parasm. Ptc. is formed simply by dropping the final @deva[इ], and the Atm. and the Passive one by substituting @deva[मान] for the final @deva[इ]; e. g.

**Participles.**

| Roots | Par. | Atm. | Passive |
|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[दा]— | @deva[द्रास्यत्] | @deva[द्रास्यमाणः] | @deva[द्रास्यमाणः] or @deva[द्रायिष्यमाणः] |
| @deva[भू]— | @deva[भविष्यत्] | @deva[भविष्यमाणः] | @deva[भविष्यमाणः] or @deva[भाविष्यमाणः] |

---
