|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[चुर्]— | @deva[चोरयिष्यत्] | @deva[चोरयिष्यमाणः] | @deva[चोरयिष्यमाणः] or @deva[चोरिष्यमाणः] |
| @deva[गम्]— | @deva[गमिष्यत्] | @deva[विगमिष्यमाणः] | @deva[गम्यमाणः] |
| @deva[जि]— | @deva[जेष्यत्] | @deva[विजेष्यमाणः] | @deva[जेष्यमाणः], @deva[जायिष्यमाणः] |
| @deva[कृ]— | @deva[करिष्यत्] | @deva[करिष्यमाणः] | @deva[कारिष्यमाणः], @deva[कारिष्यमाणः] |
| @deva[श्रु]— | @deva[श्रोष्यत्] | @deva[विश्रोष्यमाणः] | @deva[श्रोष्यमाणः], @deva[श्राविष्यमाणः] |
| @deva[एष्]—A. | | @deva[एषिष्यमाणः] | @deva[एषिष्यमाणः] |
| @deva[वद्]— | @deva[वोत्स्यत्] | @deva[वोत्स्यमाणः] | @deva[वोत्स्यमाणः] |

Similarly @deva[पिपाटु] Desi. Base of @deva[पट्]—@deva[पिपटिष्यत्], @deva[पिपटिष्यमाणः] &c.; @deva[बोबुध्] Fre. B. of @deva[बुध्]—@deva[बोबुधिष्यत्], @deva[बोबुधिष्यमाणः], &c.

rules.title: Declension of Future Participles
rules.body:
These Participles are declined like words ending in @deva[त्] and @deva[अ].

---

## (f) Potential Participles (and Verbal Adjectives).

rules.title: Introduction to Potential Participles
rules.body:
The Potential Participle is formed by means of the affixes @deva[तव्य], @deva[अनीय], @deva[य] and rarely @deva[एलिम्], added to a root or derivative verb. This is Passive when the verb is transitive and impersonal when the verb is intransitive. It is also used like an adjective when denoting fitness, &c.

---

## (1) Participles in @deva[तव्य] and @deva[अनीय].

rules.title: Formation of Participles in तव्य and अनीय
rules.body:
The affixes @deva[तव्य] or @deva[अनीय][^1] are added to roots or derivative bases in the sense of 'must be fit to be,' &c. Before these the ending vowel and the penultimate short of a root take their Guṇa substitute. Before @deva[तव्य] Seṭ roots take @deva[इ], Anit roots do not, and Veṭ roots take it optionally. Before @deva[अनीय] penultimate @deva[ऋ] is always changed to @deva[अर्] and not to @deva[ऋ] (as it sometimes does); e. g.

| Roots | | Pot. Ptc. |
|---|---|---|
| @deva[दा]— | @deva[दातव्यः], @deva[दानीयः] | what must or ought to be given. |
| @deva[चि]— | @deva[चेतव्यः], @deva[चयनीयः] | what must or ought to be searched into, &c. |
| @deva[नी]— | @deva[नेतव्यः], @deva[नयनीयः] | „ „ carried. |
| @deva[श्रु]— | @deva[श्रोतव्यः], @deva[श्रवणीयः] | „ „ heard. |
| @deva[भू]— | @deva[भवितव्यः], @deva[भवनीयः] | „ „ been. |
| @deva[कृ]— | @deva[कर्तव्यः], @deva[करणीयः] | „ „ done. |
| @deva[बुध्]— | @deva[बोद्धितव्यः], @deva[बोधनीयः], @deva[बोद्धव्यः] | „ „ known. |
| @deva[मुच्]— | @deva[मोक्तव्यः], @deva[मोचनीयः] | „ „ released. |
| @deva[मृज्]—[^2] | @deva[मार्ष्टव्यः], @deva[मार्जनीयः] | „ „ wiped. |
| @deva[सृज्]— | @deva[स्रष्टव्यः], @deva[सर्जनीयः] | „ „ created. |
| @deva[भृज्]— | @deva[भर्ष्टव्यः], @deva[भर्जनीयः], @deva[भृष्टव्यः], @deva[भर्जनीयः] | „ „ fried. |
| @deva[भिद्]— | @deva[भेत्तव्यः], @deva[भेदनीयः] | „ „ split. |
| @deva[निन्द्]— | @deva[निन्दितव्यः], @deva[निन्दनीयः]; | „ „ censured. |
| @deva[गुह्]—[^3] | @deva[गोहितव्यः], @deva[गूहनीयः], @deva[गुहितव्यः] | „ „ concealed. |

[^1]: @deva[तव्यस्त्रैयंथनीय्यै: ।] Pāṇ. III. 1. 96. @deva[क्तेऽन्यतरस्याम् उपसंश्यानं ।] Vārtika.

[^2]: The @deva[ऋ] of @deva[मृज्] is changed to @deva[आर्] against § 712.

[^3]: The @deva[उ] of @deva[गुह्] is lengthened instead of being Guṇated before a strong termination beginning with a vowel.

rules.title: Participles in अनीय for Causals, Frequentatives, and Desideratives
rules.body:
The final @deva[अय] of roots of the tenth class and of causals, the final @deva[अ] of Atm. Freq. Bases, when the @deva[य] is preceded by a vowel and the whole @deva[य] when it is preceded by a consonant, are dropped before @deva[अनीय]. To Desiderative bases it is added without any change; e. g.

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| @deva[कथ्]— | @deva[कथनीयः] | what must, or ought to be told. |
| @deva[चुर्]— | @deva[चोरणीयः] | „ „ stolen. |
| @deva[बोधय] cau. of @deva[बुध्]— | @deva[बोधनीयः] | „ „ made to know. |
| @deva[बोबुध्] Atm. Freq. Base of „ | @deva[बोबुधनीयः] | „ „ known frequently. |
| @deva[बोबुष्य]—Atm. freq. Base of @deva[बुध्]— | @deva[बोबुष्यनीयः] | what must or ought to be frequently. |
| @deva[बुबूधिष] Desi. Base of @deva[बुध्] | @deva[बुबूधिषितव्यः] | „ „ desired to know. |

---

## (2) Participles in @deva[य] (@deva[यत्], @deva[क्यप्] and @deva[घ्यत्]).

**By means of @deva[यत्] (@deva[य]).**

rules.title: Affix य (यत्) for Vowel-Ending Roots
rules.body:
The affix @deva[य] (@deva[यत्]) is added on to roots ending in a vowel in the sense of 'fit to be, or ought to be.' Before this @deva[य] the radical vowel undergoes Guṇa substitute and final @deva[आ] (@deva[इ], @deva[ऋ] and @deva[ओ] changeable to @deva[आ]) is changed to @deva[ए].

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| @deva[दा]— | @deva[देयः] | what is fit or ought to be given. |
| @deva[पा]— | @deva[पेयः] | „ „ sucked. |
| @deva[गै]— | @deva[गेयः] | „ „ sung. |
| @deva[भो]— | @deva[भोयः] | „ „ cut. |
| @deva[ग्रथ्]— | @deva[ग्रैयः] | „ „ collected. |
| @deva[नी]— | @deva[नेयः] | „ „ led or carried. |

rules.title: Affix य for Roots with Penultimate अ and Labial Ending
rules.body:
Roots having @deva[अ] for their penultimate and ending in a consonant of the labial class take the affix @deva[य]; @deva[शाप्]—@deva[शाप्यः]; @deva[दुष्]—@deva[दुष्यः]; @deva[रप्]—@deva[रप्यः], &c.

(a) When @deva[वध्] is preceded by @deva[अपि], @deva[य्] (changed to @deva[इ]) is inserted between @deva[इ] and @deva[प्]; @deva[अपिवधो]—@deva[आपेधयः] 'what ought or is fit to be killed;' @deva[य] is also inserted when @deva[द्रुष्] is preceded by @deva[उप] if the meaning be 'to praise;' @deva[उपद्रुष्यः साधुः] 'a Sādhu ought to be praised;' but @deva[उपकुष्यं धनं] 'wealth ought to be acquired.'

rules.title: Specific Roots Taking Affix य
rules.body: The roots @deva[हस्] 'to laugh at,' @deva[भाष्] 'to kill,' @deva[पृच्] 'to go on,' or 'ask,' @deva[यत्] 'to strive,' @deva[जय्], @deva[भक्] and @deva[शक्] take the affix @deva[य]; @deva[हस्यं] 'what is fit to be laughed at,' @deva[भाष्यं] 'what ought to be killed;' &c.

rules.title: गद्, पद्, वद्, यम् Taking य Without Preposition
rules.body:
The roots @deva[गद्], @deva[पद्], @deva[वद्] and @deva[यम्], take the affix @deva[य][^1] when not preceded by a preposition; @deva[गद्]—@deva[गद्यः] 'what ought to be spoken or told;' @deva[पद्यः], @deva[वद्यः], @deva[यम्यः]. @deva[वद्] with @deva[आ] may take this affix, if it does not mean 'a preceptor;' in which case it takes the affix @deva[एयत्] (@deva[य]) @deva[आवद्यः देशः] 'a country fit to be gone to,' but @deva[आचार्यः] 'a preceptor.'

[^1]: @deva[अचे यत्।] Pāṇ. III. 1. 97.

rules.title: वच्, पण्, and वृ Taking य with Semantic Conditions
rules.body: The roots @deva[वच्] implying reproach, @deva[पण्] meaning 'to transact business,' and @deva[वृ] 9. Atm. not denoting limit or restraint, take the affix @deva[य]; @deva[इ] @deva[य] is prefixed to @deva[वच्] if it hints reproachingly or demnation; but @deva[अनुप] (@deva[अन्+वच्+क्यप्] i. e. @deva[य]) @deva[गुरोः] 'the name of a preceptor ought not to be uttered (out of respect),' @deva[पण्यः गौः] 'a cow is saleable;' but @deva[पाण्यः] (@deva[पण्+एयत्] i. e. @deva[य]) @deva[ब्राह्मणः] 'a Brāhmaṇa deserving praise;' @deva[वर्यः] (that can be chosen or sought after)' a title of @deva[विष्णु]. @deva[शतेन वरा] 'hundred men (i. e. any one) can seek the hand of a girl;' but @deva[वार्या] (@deva[वृ+क्यप्] i. e. @deva[य]) @deva[कन्या] 'to be married by a particular man.'

rules.title: वह् and ऋ Taking य in Specific Senses
rules.body: The root @deva[वह्] not denoting an instrument for carrying, and @deva[ऋ] in the sense of 'a master or a Vaishya' take @deva[य]; @deva[वह्यं] 'a carriage or a vehicle;' but @deva[वाह्यः] (@deva[वह्+एयत्]) 'what can be borne,' @deva[आर्यः] 'a master or a Vaishya;' but @deva[आर्येः] (@deva[ऋ+एयत्]) 'fit to be approached or adored.'

rules.title: भू with जम् Taking य for Conception Sense
rules.body: @deva[भू] with @deva[जम्] in the senses of 'being conceived' takes the affix @deva[य]; as @deva[उपुरग्नः गौः संभावयमानां तेन गर्भेण संभोज्यते] (Sid. Kau.) but @deva[उभूसंभावनीयः] (@deva[उभू+एयत्]) @deva[कादाचिः साधुस्य उपक्षये] (Sid. Kau.).

rules.title: जृ Taking य with Negative Particle
rules.body: @deva[जृ] takes this affix with the negative particle prefixed to it and forms @deva[अजर्यं] 'what cannot grow old;' but this must qualify @deva[संगतं] 'friendship;' cf. @deva[तेन संगतमेण रामयोरयं कथं जरति।] Bhaṭṭi. VI. 53. In @deva[अत्रैरर्जर्यं जरसंबोध्यमानेन नित्यसंगत्वात्] Aṅg. XVIII. 7, the word @deva[अजर्यं] can be construed as an adverb; but if does not qualify @deva[संगतं], it will take the affix @deva[य]; as @deva[अजरिता कन्या].

rules.title: हन् Taking यत् or एयत् Optionally
Roots Taking Affix क्यप् (य)
rules.body: The roots @deva[इ] 1. 2. P. 'to go,' @deva[स्तु], @deva[शास्], @deva[इ] 5. P. A. @deva[ह्व], @deva[दुह्], and roots having @deva[ऋ] short for their penultimate, except @deva[कृष्] and @deva[वृत्], take the affix @deva[क्यप्] (@deva[य]) in the same sense as @deva[यत्]. When a root ends in a short vowel, @deva[त्] is inserted between the final vowel of the root; e. g. @deva[इ+य=ए+त्+य]='worthy of being served;' @deva[स्तुत्यः] 'deserving praise;' @deva[शास्]—@deva[शिष्यः] 'fit to be instructed;' @deva[दुह्]—@deva[दुह्यः]; @deva[इ]—@deva[आइत्यः]; @deva[दुह्]—@deva[दुह्यः] 'worthy of being served;' @deva[भृ]—@deva[भृत्यः]; @deva[दृश्]—@deva[दृश्यः] 'fit to be increased as wealth, &c.' but @deva[कल्पः] (@deva[कृष्+य]) 'able;' @deva[वद्]—@deva[वर्यः] (@deva[वृत्+एयत्]) 'that ought to be told or said.'

rules.title: स्तु, ह्व, वह् Taking यत् According to Vāmana and Pāṇini
rules.body: According to Vāmana, the roots @deva[स्तु], @deva[ह्व] and @deva[वह्] take @deva[इ]. @deva[यत्]. According to Pāṇini the roots @deva[स्तु]—@deva[स्तुत्यः] 'praiseworthy;' @deva[ह्वे]—@deva[ह्वेत्यः]; @deva[वह्]—@deva[वह्यः]; optionally they take the affix @deva[एयत्] (to be given hereafter); @deva[स्तव्यः], @deva[ह्वायः], @deva[वाह्यः].

rules.title: शुच् Taking क्यप् or एयत् Optionally
rules.body: @deva[शुच्] also takes this affix optionally; @deva[शुच्यः] 'what is fit or ought to be cleansed;' optionally it takes @deva[एयत्] before which the final @deva[च्] is changed to @deva[त्]; @deva[शोच्यः].

rules.title: भू and वह् with Subanta Taking क्यप्
rules.body:
(a) @deva[भू] when it has a Subanta prefixed to it and is without a preposition takes the affix @deva[क्यप्] impersonally; @deva[ब्रह्मणि भावः ब्रह्मभूयं] 'identity with Brahman.' When no Subanta is used prepositionally with it, it takes the affix @deva[यत्]; @deva[भव्यः] or @deva[भूयम्].

(b) @deva[वह्] under similar circumstances takes either @deva[क्यप्] or @deva[एयत्] in a passive sense in the Veda, namely: @deva[वाह्यं] or @deva[वहयेत्] 'expounding the Veda;' (@deva[वहतेवेदः तस्य वेदित्] Sid. Kau.).

rules.title: खद् Taking क्यप् with द् Dropping and ट् Addition
rules.body: @deva[खद्] takes this affix, but drops its @deva[द्] and adds @deva[ट्] to its penultimate vowel; @deva[खद्+य=ख+य=खट्+य=खेय्यः] 'what is fit or ought to be dug or excavated.'

rules.title: भृ 1. cl. Taking क्यप् When Not Forming a Name
rules.body:
@deva[भृ] I. cl. takes this affix when the participle so derived does not form a name; @deva[भृत्याः] 'those who ought to be nourished or maintained,' hence 'soldiers,' &c.; but @deva[भार्याः] (@deva[भृ+एयत्]) 'a class of Kshatriyas;' when @deva[सम्] precedes @deva[भृ], @deva[क्यप्] and @deva[एयत्] are added optionally; @deva[संभृत्याः] or @deva[संभार्याः].

**N. B.** The word @deva[भार्या] meaning 'a wife' ought to be derived from @deva[भृ] of the 3rd class and affix @deva[एयत्].

rules.title: Seven Irregular Words with क्यप्
rules.body: The following seven words are irregularly formed with the affix @deva[क्यप्] in the sense given in each case—@deva[राजसूय] (@deva[राजन्+सू+क्यप्]) @deva[राजा शोभते जनिभवतीत्यर्थः निवपनेयक्तिबहव। यत्र स्तुतम्भक्तः सोमः राजा यत्र तत् कल्प्यते। लोशः उच्चाटनार्थः कर्मा। विक्रयार्थेन तन्तुस्तुतं सेवते रूप्यगुणो उद्यातनागीवप्रतिमति], (@deva[केचिदाचार्याश्चाः]) or @deva[राज-सूय्+क्यप्]) @deva[सूक्तं आयूषि। कश्चित् क्यप्, निगोतनुर्देवेशं। यत्र यत् प्रेत्यागतः: द्युर्णात्? 'घृषीति कर्मणि लोके प्रस्यर्ति क्यप्रं रट्। युष्य] 'falsehood' (from @deva[युष्+क्यप्+क्यप्]); @deva[मृषोक्तिः इति रत्नः]; @deva[कुल्यं] (any base metal) fr. @deva[कुप्+क्यप्।] @deva[यदयोतिः कुल्यं च याद्राशाभ्य। डुयुणीरुजरतिङोतुं धनं उन्नयते।] Cf. Kir. I. 35, Manu. VII. 96. @deva[युष्] in other cases takes the affix @deva[एयत्]; @deva[गोप्यं] 'what ought to be concealed;' @deva[क्षेत्रं श्रूयते पुल्मनं गुरुगोष्यात्रः गुघुरिवाद्यित्येतत्। क्षयष्ट्य ङु कर्मणि गुरुदातिभाः] 'growing in cultivated ground;' @deva[त क्यत्र्तै अनुल्पेता:] 'too feeble verb.'

rules.title: River Names and Constellation Names with क्यप्
rules.body:
(a) The following two words which are the names of two rivers are derived by means of this affix; @deva[भिवर्ति कुवं विषः] from @deva[छिद्+क्यप्]; @deva[जलपूर्णां नाम्ना:], @deva[उञ्जुद्+क्यप्]; see Rāg. XI. 8. In other cases these roots take the affix @deva[त्]; @deva[भेत्तुंः], @deva[उन्चिद्धता].

(b) Similarly the words @deva[पुष्य:] and @deva[विष्णुप्]; both the names of the constellation Pushya, are derived from @deva[एष्] and @deva[तिष्] respectively with the affixes @deva[क्यप्]; (verging towards, @deva[विष्णुः], @deva[तिष्ठेत्युच्यते])

rules.title: यज्, नी, जि with वि Taking क्यप् in Specific Contexts
rules.body:
The roots @deva[यज्], @deva[नी] and @deva[जि], preceded by @deva[वि], take this affix, when they are connected with the words @deva[मुञ्ज], @deva[कट्यक] and @deva[उदुक] respectively, @deva[विषण्णो मुञ्जः] 'The Munja grass to be prepared for weaving into a rope' (@deva[मुञ्जानृत्युर्णाय शोधनीयस्य इत्यर्थः] Sid. Kau.); @deva[निवेय: कट्यकः] 'the girdle ought to be destroyed;' @deva[विश्वेञ्चुत् वृषेः] 'The plough to be pulled with great force,' @deva[चलेन कट्यक्षः]; in other cases these take the affix @deva[यत्]; @deva[विजेयः], @deva[नीतव्यः], @deva[जेयः].

[^1]: @deva[राजसूयमुषयक्षत्र-पद्यो-सूयगुयक्षुद्यस्यङ्कः।] Pāṇ. III. I. 114. Vide Sid. Kau. on the same.

[^2]: Cf. @deva[निजं जनुष्योसपाति हृवानो], &c. Rig. III. 59. 1.

rules.title: Words Derived from यह् with क्यप्
rules.body: The following words are derived from the root @deva[यह्] with the affix @deva[क्यप्]—@deva[अवयह्यः]; @deva[प्रयह्यः], @deva[पदे] 'two technical terms in grammar;' @deva[पयुक्तः] 'birds restrained from free motion, such as parrots, &c.' @deva[प्रवायुरेव्येन परोहत्राक्ता उपक्षये।] Sid. Kau. @deva[ग्रामयुद्धे सेना] 'an army stationed outside a village;' @deva[आर्युवाहास्ते आयुयुद्धे: तिर्व्यामुद्धीव उत्यर्थः] (Sid. Kau.) 'siding with the noble.' See Rāg. II. 43.

rules.title: कृ and दृ Taking Both क्यप् and एयत्
rules.body: The roots @deva[कृ] and @deva[दृ] take both @deva[क्यप्] and @deva[एयत्]; @deva[कृत्यः], @deva[कार्यः]; @deva[दृत्यः]; @deva[दार्यः] 'what ought to be chosen, best,' &c.

rules.title: युज् Taking क्यप् with Final Consonant Change
Affix घ्यत् (य) for ऋ-Ending and Consonant-Ending Roots
rules.body:
Roots ending in @deva[ऋ], and those ending in a consonant take the affix @deva[घ्यत्] (@deva[य]) in the same sense as @deva[क्यप्]. Before this affix the ending @deva[चु] and @deva[व] of a root are changed to @deva[ऋ] and @deva[यु] respectively and the final vowel and the penultimate @deva[अ] take Vṛiddhi substitute; any other penultimate vowel generally takes Guṇa.

@deva[कृ]—@deva[कार्यं] 'what ought to be done,' @deva[धृ]—@deva[धार्यं] 'what ought to be worn,' @deva[दा]—@deva[देयः]; @deva[हृ]—@deva[हार्यं]; @deva[पद्]—@deva[दृदु]—@deva[पार्यः] 'what is to be thought of,' &c.; @deva[वच्]—@deva[वाच्यं] 'what is meant in a sentence,' @deva[पच्]—@deva[पाच्यं] 'what is to be cooked,' @deva[वुज्]—@deva[भोज्यं] 'what is to be purified,' &c.

rules.title: पद् with अमा Taking घ्यत् and युज् with Special Prefixes
rules.body:
The root @deva[पद्] when preceded by @deva[अमा] 'with' takes the affix @deva[घ्यत्] before which the penultimate @deva[अ] is optionally changed to Vṛiddhi; @deva[अमा रुङु गुवातोऽव्या चन्द्रा:शो अवतिब्धुवा] or @deva[वाश्या] 'the day on which the sun and the moon are with each other' i. e. are in conjunction.'

(a) @deva[युज्] when preceded by @deva[पाणिं] or the preposition @deva[समत्] takes the affix @deva[घ्यत्]; as @deva[पाणिस्यो डुयुयोऽ पाणिगुम्योऽ यृज्यः]; similarly @deva[समवसुयुर्यं].

rules.title: Roots Not Changing ऋ or व Before घ्यत्
rules.body:
(a) The roots @deva[युज्], @deva[याच्], @deva[रुच्], @deva[प्रथ्], @deva[स्पृश्], and @deva[एच्] do not change their @deva[ऋ] or @deva[व] to @deva[वृ] or @deva[यु] before @deva[घ्यत्]; @deva[योज्यं] @deva[याच्यं]; @deva[रोच्यं], @deva[प्रथ्यंयुम्] (@deva[प्रत्यशीतव्यः]), @deva[ज्ञेय्यं], @deva[स्पश्यं], @deva[गाच्यं].

(b) @deva[वच्] does not change its @deva[चु] to @deva[ऋ] before @deva[घ्यत्] when the meaning is 'what ought to be spoken out, speech,' @deva[वाच्यं]; but @deva[वाक्यं]; 'a sentence.'

(c) @deva[पञ्च्] when it means 'to go' does not change @deva[चु] its to @deva[ऋ]; @deva[पञ्च्यं]; when it means 'to bend' the @deva[चु] is changed to @deva[ऋ]; @deva[पञ्कुवं शरीरं].

(d) @deva[युज्] when it is preceded by @deva[प्र] and @deva[वि], takes the affix @deva[एयत्] in the sense of 'what is possible or capable of;' and does not change its @deva[ऋ] to @deva[यु]; @deva[प्रयुङ्कुम् शक्यं प्रयोज्यं]; @deva[निवौङुकुम् शक्यः निवौज्यः]; @deva[शङुयः]!

(e) @deva[भुज्] has @deva[भोजं] meaning 'food,' and @deva[भोज्यं] 'what is fit to be enjoyed.'

rules.title: Affix एलिम् for ऋ-Ending Roots and Selected Consonant-Ending Roots
rules.body:
Roots ending in @deva[ऋ], short or long, take the affix @deva[एलिम्] in the sense of 'what ought or must necessarily be done;' @deva[कृ]—@deva[कर्तुं] 'what must necessarily be cut off,' @deva[पाक्तुं] 'what must necessarily be cooked,' @deva[दा] to be with @deva[आ]—@deva[आत्तुं]; @deva[प्र] 'to mix,' @deva[यात्], &c.

(a) The roots @deva[वच्], @deva[प्रथ्], @deva[द्युत्], @deva[भृत्] and @deva[वद्] also do the same, @deva[वाच्यं] 'what must necessarily be on;' @deva[प्रथ्युत्] 'what must be spoken of distinctly;' @deva[द्युत्युत्], @deva[भात्युत्], @deva[वात्युत्].

rules.title: Comprehensive Coverage: Irregular Potential Participles and Indeclinable Participles
rules.body:
## § 739. Irregular Words Derived with Affix @deva[घ्यत्]

The following words are irregularly derived by means of the affix @deva[घ्यत्]; @deva[आहात्यं] 'what ought to be brought from the Gārhapatya i. e. the Dakshiṇā-gni;' (fr. @deva[नी] with @deva[आ]) @deva[विद्युणामाविनांगे दृत्युतृद। य हि गाहपत्युगाम्यानात्रोऽक्षिनां स्य तत्संतप्रत्र्यूतोगाम्।] (Sid. Kau.); but @deva[नायं] in other senses 'to be led, &c.' @deva[मोपुनुमार्यं] (fr. @deva[नी] with @deva[मो]) @deva[चौरः मेनोवनुहे डुर्युथुर्येः] (Sid. Kau.); 'disgusted with worldly pleasures;' as @deva[प्रणायुयूनैवोचारो विरक्तो डुर्युथुर्येः।] but @deva[प्रणेयं] in other cases.

(a) @deva[गीतोत्यं अनेन इति भाव्यं] 'a sacrifice' (fr. @deva[या]); @deva[समुयक् तिङुवं होमवशुम्भरोर्यति इति भाज्यार्यं] (from. @deva[नी] with @deva[सम्]) @deva[द्वाविविकोर:] 'a kind of offering (See Śīs. XI. 41)'; @deva[तिन्नीविरोऽक्षिम्युणागुवत्कै निवुद्धुत्यः निवुत्ता:] (fr. @deva[वध्] with @deva[नि]); @deva[शुसीत अनेन संदाध्यते घाश्यः] (fr. @deva[धा]) @deva[चरुख:]; @deva[कुपुष्यन पाष्ये (अनिमित्रा सोम:) कुपुष्यार्यख: कृत्:]; @deva[संज्योषैविरोत्य: संज्यास्यु:] (a sacrifice); @deva[परिज्ञात्यं], @deva[उपत्युत्यं]; @deva[स्वयुत्यत्: पूनिष्पाषैविकायिनोङुयुते] (rites for depositing the sacrificial fire); @deva[परिचेत्युत्], @deva[डुयुचेत्युत्], @deva[संवूत्युत्] in other cases; @deva[चौवूते अतीं तिस्युत: आर्जते]; @deva[अतीरे चयनं आश्वातिस्युत्].

---

## @ref[741]. Participles with Active Sense

The roots @deva[भू] and @deva[गै] take the affix @deva[यत्]; @deva[भव्यः] and @deva[स्था] take @deva[अनीय]; and @deva[वद्], @deva[वृ] and @deva[पच्] take @deva[घ्यत्], in an active sense; @deva[अदेर्तो भव्यं] (also @deva[भव्युभूतनं]); @deva[गायुवो गेवः] 'one who sings' (also @deva[गेयं राम अनेनै]); @deva[प्रवचनीयः] 'one who speaks' @deva[उदु], @deva[वानीयः] 'one who stands for,' @deva[स्तुत्य], @deva[पुचोय युरितिय्येः], @deva[पाच्युयुं] 'food.'

---

## (3) By means of @deva[केलिमुर्] (@deva[एलिम्]).

## @ref[742]. Affix @deva[एलिमुर्] for Transitive Roots

A few transitive roots take the affix @deva[एलिमुर्] having the same force as the affix @deva[यत्]; @deva[पचेलिमः] fr. @deva[पच्], 'fit to ripen or to be cooked; as @deva[पचेलिमा भावनः]; @deva[भिदेलिमाः] (fr. @deva[भिद्]) @deva[स्तम्बाः] 'the pine tress ought to be felled,' &c.

## @ref[743]. Declension of Potential Participles

The declension of these Participles follows that of nouns ending in @deva[अ].

---

## II. INDECLINABLE PARTICIPLES

## (a) Indeclinable Past Participles.

## @ref[744]. Introduction to Indeclinable Past Participles (Gerunds)

The Indeclinable Past Participles are of the nature of gerunds. They fall under two heads:—(1) Those derived by affixing @deva[क्त्वा] to the simple root, and (2) Those derived by means of @deva[य] affixed to the root compounded with prepositions or words used prepositionally; @deva[गम्]—@deva[गत्वा] 'having gone,' @deva[भू] with @deva[परिदेवस्त्र] 'having' 'having served;' &c.

## I. Indeclinable Participles formed with @deva[क्त्वा].

## @ref[745]. Formation of Gerund in @deva[क्त्वा]

The Indeclinable Past Participle or gerund in @deva[क्त्वा] is formed of all roots or derivative verbal bases to which a preposition (nor a prepositional word) is prefixed. The affix @deva[क्त्वा] is of the same nature as the @deva[त्] of the Past Passive Participle, so that all the changes that take place before @deva[त्] generally take place before @deva[क्त्वा]. In other words from the P. P. Ptc. in @deva[त्] or @deva[न] separate the @deva[त्] or @deva[न] from it, add @deva[क्त्वा] instead, and this will be the form of the gerund in @deva[क्त्वा]; e. g.

| Roots | | P. P. Ptc. | Ind. P. Ptc. |
|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[ज्ञा] | to know | @deva[ज्ञातः] | @deva[ज्ञात्वा] |
| @deva[दा] | to give | @deva[दत्तः] | @deva[दत्त्वा] |
| @deva[स्था] | to stand | @deva[स्थितः] | @deva[स्थित्वा] |
| @deva[ह्रु] | to go | @deva[ह्रुणः] | @deva[ह्रुण्त्वा] |
| @deva[हा] | to abandon | @deva[हीनः] | @deva[हीत्वा] |

| @deva[जि] | to conquer | @deva[जितः] | @deva[जित्वा] |
| @deva[पू] | to purify | @deva[पवितः] or @deva[पूतः] | @deva[पवित्वा] or @deva[पूत्वा] |
| @deva[भू] | to be | @deva[भूतः] | @deva[भूत्वा] |
| @deva[कृ] | to do | @deva[कृतः] | @deva[कृत्वा] |
| @deva[तृ] | to cross | @deva[तीर्णः] | @deva[तीर्त्वा] |
| @deva[पूर्] | to fill | @deva[पूर्णः] | @deva[पूर्त्वा] |

| @deva[मुच्] | to release | @deva[मुक्तः] | @deva[मुक्त्वा] |
| @deva[अद्] | to eat | @deva[जग्धः] | @deva[जग्ध्वा] |
| @deva[छो] | to cut | @deva[छातः], @deva[छितः] | @deva[छात्वा], @deva[छित्वा] |

| @deva[वस्] | to dwell | @deva[उषितः] | @deva[उषित्वा] |
| @deva[वच्] | to speak | @deva[उक्तः] | @deva[उक्त्वा] |

## @ref[746]. Guṇa Before Intermediate @deva[इ]

When the intermediate @deva[इ] is inserted, the preceding vowel takes its Guṇa substitute; @deva[शि]—@deva[शयित्वा], @deva[कु]—@deva[कवित्वा], @deva[जाग्]—@deva[जागरित्वा], &c.

(a) The roots @deva[तृप्], @deva[द्विष्], @deva[हृष्] and @deva[कुल्] take Guṇa optionally; @deva[तृपित्वा] or @deva[तृप्त्वा], @deva[द्विषित्वा] or @deva[द्विप्त्वा], @deva[हृषित्वा] or @deva[हृष्त्वा], @deva[कुल]—@deva[कवित्वा] or @deva[कुलित्वा].

(b) But the roots @deva[युध्], @deva[पुष्], @deva[द्युत्], @deva[कुश्], @deva[इष्], and @deva[किञ्छु], the roots mentioned at @ref[493] (i. e. @deva[किच्], &c.) do not take Guṇa; @deva[इष्]—@deva[युधित्वा] 'having rejoiced;' @deva[युध्]—@deva[पुषित्वा], @deva[द्युत्]—@deva[द्युतित्वा] 'having covered,' @deva[कुशित्वा], @deva[इङुषित्वा], @deva[किञ्छु]—@deva[किङ्छित्वा] or @deva[किद्युष्युः] @deva[कुर्]—@deva[कुदित्वा], @deva[विख्य]—@deva[विनित्वा]; &c.

## @ref[747]. Veṭ Roots and Optional @deva[इ]

Veṭ roots, except @deva[प्रच्छु] which takes @deva[इ] necessarily, and @deva[रुच्], @deva[पूर्] which reject @deva[इ], the five roots given under @ref[472] and the roots marked with an indicatory @deva[उ] admit of @deva[इ] optionally before @deva[क्त्वा] e. g.

| Roots | | Ind. P. Ptc. or Ger. |
|---|---|---|
| @deva[मृज्] | to cleanse | @deva[मृजित्वा], @deva[मृष्ट्वा] |
| @deva[गो] | to enter | @deva[गाहित्वा], @deva[गाढ्वा] |
| @deva[गुह्] | to conceal | @deva[गूहित्वा], @deva[गुहित्वा], @deva[गूढ्वा] |
| @deva[गोप्] | to protect | @deva[गोपायित्वा], @deva[गोपित्वा], @deva[गुप्त्वा], @deva[गुप्त्वा] |
| @deva[दृश्] | to desire | @deva[एषित्वा] or @deva[दृष्ट्वा] |
| @deva[सह्] | to endure | @deva[सोढित्वा] or @deva[सोढ्वा] |
| @deva[अर्ह्] | to covet | @deva[अर्हित्वा] or @deva[हृष्ट्वा] |
| @deva[अञ्च्] | to go, to worship | @deva[अक्त्वा] having gone, @deva[अर्चित्वा] having worshipped |
| @deva[क्षण्] | to kill | @deva[क्षत्वा], @deva[क्षणित्वा] |
| @deva[खन्] | to dig | @deva[खनित्वा], @deva[खात्वा] |
| @deva[तन्] | to stretch | @deva[तनित्वा], @deva[तत्वा] |
| @deva[व्रश्] | to tame | @deva[व्रशित्वा], @deva[व्रात्वा] |
| @deva[शाम्] | to pacify | @deva[शामित्वा], @deva[शान्त्वा] |
| @deva[कृष्] | to go &c. | @deva[कृषित्वा], @deva[कृष्ट्वा], @deva[क्रान्त्वा] |
| @deva[वर्ष्] | 4. P. to be straight, &c. | @deva[वर्षित्वा], @deva[वृष्ट्वा] |
| @deva[वह्] | I. A. to be | @deva[वहित्वा] or @deva[उच्चवा] &c. &c. |

But @deva[मृज्]—@deva[मार्जित्वा], @deva[रुच्]—@deva[रुढ्वा], @deva[यू]—@deva[युयुत्वा], @deva[गृ]—@deva[गुरुत्वा].

## @ref[748]. Set Roots and Roots of the 10th Class

The roots @deva[शि], @deva[वी], @deva[सी], @deva[गृ] and @deva[ज्ञा], Seṭ roots ending in consonants, roots of the 10th class and all derivative verbs, admit @deva[इ] before @deva[क्त्वा]; roots of the 10th cl. preserve their @deva[अय] before @deva[क्त्वा]; @deva[शि]—@deva[शयित्वा], @deva[वी]—@deva[वयित्वा], @deva[ज्ञा]—@deva[ज्ञरित्वा] or @deva[जारित्वा], @deva[पद्]—@deva[पदित्वा], @deva[वि]—@deva[विचित्वा], @deva[गुरुच्]—@deva[गुरुचित्वा], @deva[जागृ]—@deva[जागरित्वा], &c., @deva[चुर्]—@deva[चोरयित्वा], @deva[कम्प]—@deva[कम्पयित्वा], @deva[बुध्]—cau. @deva[बोधयित्वा], desi. @deva[बुबुधिषित्वा]; Atm. fre. @deva[बोबुधयित्वा], &c.

## @ref[749]. Nasal Dropping Rules

(a) The roots @deva[स्कन्द्] and @deva[स्वृज्] do not drop their nasal; @deva[स्कन्दित्वा]—@deva[स्कद्य]—@deva[स्कन्दित्वा]; @deva[स्वृञ्जित्वा].

(b) The penultimate nasal of roots ending in @deva[म्] or @deva[न्] and that of @deva[वञ्च्] 'to roam abroad,' 'to deceive' and @deva[लुञ्च्] 'to tear out,' are optionally dropped, @deva[यम्]—@deva[यमित्वा], @deva[यतित्वा], @deva[भुज्]—@deva[भुक्त्वा], @deva[यक्षित्वा]; @deva[वञ्च्]—@deva[वञ्चित्वा], @deva[वचित्वा], @deva[वत्त्वा]; @deva[लुञ्च्]—@deva[लुञ्चित्वा], @deva[लुचित्वा].

(c) Roots ending in @deva[ञ्च्] such as @deva[भुञ्ज्], @deva[रञ्च्], @deva[सृज्], @deva[स्पृश्] &c. and the root @deva[तुञ्ज्] optionally drop their nasal before @deva[क्त्वा]; @deva[भुञ्ज्]—@deva[भुङ्क्त्वा] or @deva[भुक्त्वा], @deva[रञ्च्]—@deva[रङ्क्त्वा] or @deva[रक्त्वा]; @deva[अञ्ज्]—@deva[अङ्कित्वा], @deva[अक्त्वा] or @deva[अक्त्वा].

(d) @deva[मृज्] and @deva[नञ्च्] insert a nasal optionally; @deva[मार्क्त्वा] or @deva[मृष्ट्वा]; @deva[नश्कित्वा], @deva[नष्ट्वा] or @deva[नष्ट्वा].

## @ref[750]. Guṇa for Penultimate @deva[इ] and @deva[उ]

Guṇa is optionally substituted for the penultimate @deva[इ] and @deva[उ], roots beginning with any consonant and ending in any except @deva[ऋ] or @deva[व] when @deva[क्त्वा] has @deva[इ] prefixed to it; @deva[सिध्]—@deva[क्षुधित्वा] or @deva[क्षुद्धित्वा]; @deva[रुज्]—@deva[र्षुधिर] or @deva[क्षुदरित्वा।] also @deva[क्षुरित्त्वा।]; @deva[क्षुध्]—6. P. @deva[क्षुधित्वा] or @deva[क्षुधित्वा]; @deva[स्पृश्] @deva[यादितः] or @deva[निदुकोनिवदा]; @deva[पिष्]—@deva[निषित्वा], @deva[गुनित्वा] and @deva[निप], or @deva[रुप्], &c., but @deva[विद्]—@deva[वेदित्वा], @deva[मुत्वा].

## 2. Indeclinable Participles formed with @deva[य].

## @ref[751]. Formation of Gerund in @deva[य]

When a root is compounded with one or more prepositions or words prefixed to verbs like prepositions, the indeclinable participle is formed by affixing @deva[य] immediately to it; the @deva[य] is changed to @deva[त्य] after a short radical vowel (even when it combines with the final vowel of a preposition to a long vowel); e. g.

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[दा] with @deva[आ]—@deva[आदाय] | @deva[प्र] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्रेत्य] |
| @deva[मिद्] with @deva[विश्]—@deva[विज्ञाय] | @deva[कृ] with @deva[सम्]—@deva[संस्कृत्य] |
| @deva[जि] with @deva[परा]—@deva[पराजित्य] | @deva[कृ] with @deva[विश्]—@deva[विभक्त्य] |
| @deva[नी] with @deva[वि]—@deva[विनीय] | @deva[वद्] with @deva[नि]—@deva[निवाच्य] |
| @deva[भू] with @deva[अनु]—@deva[अनुभूय] | @deva[मद्] with @deva[उत्]—@deva[उत्पद्य] |
| @deva[इ] with @deva[अभि]—@deva[अभीत्य] | &c. | &c. | &c. |

## @ref[752]. Application of Previous Rules

The rules given at @ref[394], @ref[395], @ref[459], @ref[502] and @ref[587] apply to the roots also in the gerund in @deva[य]:—

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[विद्] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्रवीद्य] | @deva[अच्] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्राच्य] |
| @deva[कृ] with @deva[अव]—@deva[अवकीर्य] | @deva[वस्] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्रोष्य] |
| @deva[युज्] with @deva[आ]—@deva[आयुज्य] | @deva[शङ्ख्] with @deva[वि]—@deva[विशङ्ख्य] |
| @deva[बन्ध्] with @deva[नि]—@deva[निबध्य] | @deva[धा] with @deva[आ]—@deva[आहूय] |
| @deva[हि], @deva[नी], @deva[मा] and @deva[गृ] with @deva[अनु]—@deva[अनुदाय] | @deva[दा] with @deva[उद्]—@deva[उद्दाय] |
| @deva[रुष्] with @deva[परि]—@deva[परिरुष्य] | @deva[धो] with @deva[वि]—@deva[विधाय] or @deva[विद्धाय] |
| @deva[वै] with @deva[आ]—@deva[आदुष्य] | &c. | &c. | &c. |

## @ref[753]. Nasal Dropping for 8th Class Roots

Roots of the 8th class ending in a nasal, except @deva[यम्] and the roots @deva[मन्], @deva[यन्] and @deva[हन्], drop their nasal necessarily; @deva[तक्], @deva[तन्य], @deva[यम्य] and @deva[रुम्] do it optionally; @deva[तन्] with @deva[वि]—@deva[वितत्य]; @deva[म्रुष्] with @deva[प्रति]—@deva[प्रतिम्रुष्य]; @deva[तन्य] with @deva[वि]—@deva[वितन्य] or @deva[विततुम्]; @deva[रुम्] with @deva[वि]—@deva[विरुम्य] or @deva[विरत्य]; @deva[मन्] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्रणम्य] or @deva[प्रणत्य], &c.

## @ref[754]. Special Forms for @deva[सन्], @deva[जन्], @deva[सन्]

The roots @deva[सन्], @deva[जन्] and @deva[सन्] have respectively @deva[निसत्युम्]—@deva[निसाय]; @deva[प्रजन्य]—@deva[प्रजाय]; and @deva[प्रसन्य]—@deva[प्रसाय].

## @ref[755]. @deva[द्विष्] and @deva[जागृ]

@deva[द्विष्] lengthens its @deva[इ] before the affix @deva[य] and @deva[जागृ] changes its final vowel to Guṇa; @deva[प्रदीय]; @deva[प्रजाय्य].

## @ref[756]. Samprasāraṇa Rules

(a), @deva[च्युत्] and @deva[छुध्] do not take Samprasāraṇa, @deva[प्रच्युत्य]; @deva[उच्युत्य] 'having become old,' @deva[उप्युत्य] 'having covered,' but @deva[ऋ] with @deva[परि] or @deva[समु], takes Samprasāraṇa optionally, @deva[परिस्युत्य] or @deva[परिदुर्य]; @deva[संस्युत्य] or @deva[संदीर्य].

## @ref[757]. Roots Not Changing @deva[आ] to @deva[इ]

The roots mentioned under @ref[486] do not change their @deva[आ] to @deva[इ]; @deva[प्रयाय], @deva[प्रमाय], @deva[प्रमाय], &c.

## @ref[758]. Causals and 10th Class Roots

Roots of the Tenth class and Causals preserve their @deva[अय] before @deva[य]; it being separated by a short penultimate vowel if not, it is dropped; @deva[चोरय]—@deva[परचोर्य]; @deva[बोधय]—@deva[परबोध्य]; @deva[कृ]—cau. @deva[विकारय]; @deva[नी] cau. with @deva[आ]—@deva[आनाय], &c.; but @deva[गृण]—@deva[विगृण्य], @deva[प्रकृपुम्य], @deva[प्रकल्पय]; @deva[प्रबोविदुर्य] 'having again and again caused to be broken.'

## @ref[759]. Causative @deva[गम्]

(a) @deva[गम्] cau. may retain its @deva[अय] optionally—@deva[गम्य] or @deva[गामय].

## @ref[760]. Desiderative and Frequentative Bases

Desiderative bases add @deva[य] immediately and Freq. bases add it after dropping their @deva[य], when it is preceded by a consonant and dropping the final @deva[अ] when it is preceded by a vowel; @deva[बुबू]—@deva[परबुबुधिष्य]; Fre. @deva[परबोबुध्य]; @deva[भू] Fre. @deva[परबोभूय] &c.

## (b) THE ADVERBIAL INDECLINABLE PARTICIPLE OR The Gerund in @deva[अम्].

## @ref[761]. Formation of Gerund in @deva[अम्]

There is another Indeclinable Participle having the same sense as that in @deva[क्त्वा], formed with the affix @deva[अम्]. Before this the vowel of the derivative verbal base generally undergoes the same changes as it does before the @deva[इ] of the Pass. Aorist 3rd sing.; @deva[नी]—@deva[नयाम्] 'having carried or led,' @deva[दा]—@deva[दायाम्] 'having given,' @deva[भू]—@deva[भावाम्], @deva[भिद्]—@deva[भेदाम्], @deva[भाह्]—@deva[भाह्राम्], @deva[गम्]—@deva[गमाम्], &c.

## @ref[762]. Usage at End of Compounds

This Participle is generally used at the end of compounds; @deva[श्वोन्यस्य हतः] 'he was pelted to death,' @deva[बन्दिनाथं गृहीतः] (Vīks. I. 1.) She was taken a captive;' @deva[प्रभङ्क्तुं प्रसमाम्] (Bhaṭṭi. I. 2.) 'He totally exterminated his enemies, &c.'

## @ref[763]. Repetition for Iterative Sense

The participles in @deva[क्त्वा] and @deva[अम्] when repeated yield the sense of repetition of the action or condition expressed by the verb; @deva[स्मृत्वा स्मृत्वा] or @deva[स्मरं स्मारयुम्] 'having repeatedly remembered; @deva[पीत्वा पीत्वा] or @deva[पाय पायाम्] 'having drunk again and again;' similarly @deva[अच्युत्वाच्युत्वा] or @deva[अचुयाचुयाम्] or @deva[पोजुत्यपोजुत्य] or @deva[पोयुपयम्], @deva[छोरयुछोरयुम् आपुद्य], @deva[गम्]—@deva[गन्त्वा गन्त्वा] or @deva[गम् गमाम्] or @deva[गत् गतम्], @deva[छत्युस्]—@deva[छत्युस्त्वा छत्युस्त्वा] or @deva[छत्युं छत्युम्] or @deva[छत्युं छत्युम्], @deva[पठत् पठतम्], @deva[जागृ]—@deva[जागरं जागरम्], &c.

## @ref[764]. Non-Repetitive Usage

The Gerund @deva[अम्] does not, in many instances, express the notion of repetition.

## @ref[765]. Usage with Prepositions

This gerund or the one in @deva[क्त्वा] is used with the words @deva[अचे], @deva[पुरुषं] and @deva[पुश्चं], used as prepositions, although the notion of repetition is not present in these compounds; @deva[अत्युहैसोद्युत्युत्वा हा स्त्रौयौ] 'having taken to goes out;' so @deva[यथागोत] or @deva[पुञ्चवा पुनु-भोरिते] or @deva[पुञ्चवा बुद्धे].

## @ref[766]. Gerund of @deva[कृ]

The gerund in @deva[अम्] of the root @deva[कृ] is used

(a) with the noun governed by it, if it be compounded with it prepositionally when censure is implied; @deva[चौरुकारुते आक्रोशुते] (@deva[चौरुकृत्युय उत्युचिसुथुर्येः]) 'cries out (he is) a thief, a thief.' In this case @deva[य] is added to the noun governed.

(b) with the words @deva[स्वाद्], @deva[छुण], and @deva[संस्यद्], @deva[य] being added to these as before; @deva[आस्वादुकारु स्वादु छत्युवा पुकैं स्वादुकारुणुकारुं-संस्यदै—कारुं पुकैं] 'he eats having sweetened or seasoned his food.'

(c) with the words @deva[अत्युया], @deva[एव], @deva[किंयुं], and @deva[कुथुं], provided the root @deva[य] takes its sense; @deva[अत्युयाकारुं हुत्वो] 'he speaks in a coherent manner;' @deva[एवुं कृत्वा] the acts thus;' @deva[किंकारुते], @deva[कुथंकारुते हुयुभुरामु], but @deva[शिनैत्युयुत्या हुत्वा मुश्चैं].

(d) with the particles @deva[युथुं] and @deva[युथा] when an angry reply is given; @deva[युथुमुकारुं शोध्युं युथुमुकारुं शोध्युं किं तवौनैन] (Sid. Kau.); 'I will eat in this manner, I will eat in that manner, what have you do with that?'

## @ref[767]. Gerunds of @deva[हन्] and @deva[विद्य] with Objects

The Gerund of the roots @deva[हन्] and @deva[विद्य] is compounded with their objects and expresse totality; @deva[कन्यायुद्युच्युं वरुयति] 'chooses as many girls as he sees, i. e. all of them,' @deva[ब्रातुसातुवुदै भोज्ययति], @deva[यैयं ब्राह्मणं जानाति छुम्युते विन्चारुयत्ति हा तं सर्वै भोज्ययति इत्यर्थुर्येः] (Sid. Kau.) 'he feeds every Brāhmaṇa that he knows or comes across or remembers i. e. all of them.'

(a) The gerunds of @deva[विद्] 'to get' and @deva[जीव्] 'to live' are joined with @deva[यावद्] in the sam3 sense; @deva[यावद्वेद्यं खादुते] 'eats what he gets.'

(b) With the words @deva[पुनत्] and @deva[उदर] the gerund of @deva[पूर्] is used; @deva[चनैर्युर्युं स्थूलते]; @deva[उदर्युर्युं खादुते] 'eats so as to fill his belly.'

## @ref[768]. Gerund of @deva[पद्] with Specific Words

This gerund of @deva[पद्] is used with @deva[युष्युकू], @deva[चूर्णं] and @deva[स्यदै]; @deva[मुष्युकूतैर्ये पदुत्त युन्नं पदुहीनुग्युर्येः] (Sid. Kau.); so @deva[चूर्णैर्युं पदुहुदि] 'he grinds to powder;' @deva[स्यदैरुयुम्].

## @ref[769]. Special Gerund Usages

With the words @deva[पुसुत्], @deva[अक्षत] and @deva[जीव] are used respectively the gerunds in @deva[अम्] of the roots @deva[हन्], @deva[कृ] and @deva[गह्] in a cognate sense; @deva[पुसुच्छुवातं हुन्ते] 'kills destroying the roots i. e. totally,' @deva[अक्षुतकुरुते करोति] 'does what ought not to have been done;' @deva[जीवुगाहै गृहाति] 'captures him so as to preserve him i. e. alive.'

(a) The gerund of @deva[हन्] and @deva[पद्] is used with words signifying instruments (of action); @deva[पात्तूवातुं हुन्ते=पातै हुन्ते] 'strikes (kicking) with the foot;' @deva[स्फुरुं पठुते=प्रहरुण पठुते] 'reads (with (using) the water.

(b) Similarly the gerund of @deva[वन्] and @deva[गह्] is used with @deva[हन्] and its synonyms, and that of @deva[पूर्] with @deva[स्प]; @deva[हुनवुनुं पुसुयति]; so @deva[कुर्युत्तो], @deva[हुतैन यटिकुं करोतीतोर्युर्येः।] Sid. Kau.; @deva[हुन्वुनुहुं गृहीते]; similarly @deva[गाणियाहु], @deva[कुरुग्राहु कु], &c.

rules.title: Continuation of Irregular Words with घ्यत् (Phase 1 Recovery)
rules.body: @deva[समुयुङ् तिरुतुं होमायुशुम्भरौ यति इति भाज्यार्युं] (from. @deva[नी] with @deva[समु]) @deva[द्वाविविङोर:] 'a kind of offering (See Śīs. XI. 41)'; @deva[तिन्नीतिविरोउक्षिम्यणायुतौवौकै निवुद्धुत्युं: निवुदुत:] (fr @deva[वि] with @deva[हि]); @deva[शुसीदेत अनेन संत्रिदूयुते घाश्या] (fr. @deva[धा]) @deva[चरुख:]; @deva[कुपुष्यन पाषुते (अनिमुत्र सोम:) कुपुष्यायुख: कष्टु:]; @deva[संद्याषैविरोर्य: संज्यास्यु:] (a sacrifice); @deva[परिज्ञात्युं], @deva[उपुत्युत्युं]; @deva[स्वयूत्युं: पुविष्पाषैविकायिनौकुयुं ते] (rites for depositing the sacrificial fire); @deva[पनिचुत्युत्], @deva[डुयुचुयुद्], @deva[तंवूत्युद्] in other cases; @deva[चौवते अतीं चिस्युत: आद्रुते]; @deva[अतीरे चयनं आश्ङाचिस्युत्].

rules.title: Potential Participles with यत्, अनीय, and घ्यत् in Active Sense
rules.body:
The roots @deva[भू] and @deva[गै] take the affix @deva[यत्]; @deva[स्था] takes @deva[अनीय]; and @deva[वद्], @deva[वृ] and @deva[पच्] take @deva[घ्यत्], in an active sense; @deva[अतुवोर्थो भव्यः] (also @deva[भव्यभूतनं]); @deva[गायतु गेयः] 'one who sings' (also @deva[गेयं रामे अनेन]); @deva[वाच्यः] 'one who speaks' @deva[उत्], @deva[स्थानीयः] 'one who stands for,' @deva[स्थाय], @deva[वर्यः बधित्ययोः], @deva[पाच्यः] 'food.'

---

**(3) By means of @deva[केलिम्] (@deva[एलिम्]).**

rules.title: Affix एलिम् for Transitive Roots
rules.body: A few transitive roots take the affix @deva[एलिम्] having the same force as the affix @deva[यत्]; @deva[पचेलिमः] fr. @deva[पच्], 'fit to ripen or to be cooked; as @deva[पचेलिमा ओषधयः]; @deva[भिदेलिमाः] (fr. @deva[भिद्]) @deva[स्तम्बाः] 'the pine trees ought to be felled,' &c.

rules.title: Declension of Potential Participles
rules.body:
The declension of these Participles follows that of nouns ending in @deva[अ].

---

**II. INDECLINABLE PARTICIPLES**

**(a) Indeclinable Past Participles.**

rules.title: Introduction to Indeclinable Past Participles (Gerunds)
rules.body:
The Indeclinable Past Participles are of the nature of gerunds. They fall under two heads:—(1) Those derived by affixing @deva[क्त्वा] to the simple root, and (2) Those derived by means of @deva[य] affixed to the root compounded with prepositions or words used prepositionally; @deva[गम्]—@deva[गत्वा] 'having gone,' @deva[भू] with @deva[परि]—@deva[परिभूय] 'having' 'having served;' &c.

---

**I. Indeclinable Participles formed with @deva[क्त्वा].**

rules.title: Gerund Formation with क्त्वा
rules.body:
The Indeclinable Past Participle or gerund in @deva[क्त्वा] is formed of all roots or derivative verbal bases to which a preposition (nor a prepositional word) is prefixed. The affix @deva[क्त्वा] is of the same nature as the @deva[त्] of the Past Passive Participle, so

rules.title: Guṇa Substitution When Intermediate इ Is Inserted
rules.body:
When the intermediate @deva[इ] is inserted, the preceding vowel takes its Guṇa substitute; @deva[शि]—@deva[शयित्वा], @deva[कु]—@deva[कवित्वा], @deva[जाग्]—@deva[जागरित्वा], &c.

(a) The roots @deva[तृप्], @deva[द्विष्], @deva[हृष्] and @deva[कुल्] take Guṇa optionally; @deva[तृपित्वा] or @deva[तृप्त्वा], @deva[द्विषित्वा] or @deva[द्विष्ट्वा], @deva[हृषित्वा] or @deva[हृष्ट्वा], @deva[कुल]—@deva[कवित्वा] or @deva[कुलित्वा].

(b) But the roots @deva[युध्], @deva[पुष्], @deva[द्युत्], @deva[कुश्], @deva[इष्], and @deva[किञ्छ्], the roots mentioned at @ref[493] (i. e. @deva[कुट्], &c.) do not take Guṇa; @deva[इष्]—@deva[इषित्वा] 'having rejoiced;' @deva[युध्]—@deva[युधित्वा], @deva[पुष्]—@deva[पुषित्वा], @deva[द्युत्]—@deva[द्युतित्वा] 'having covered,' @deva[कुशित्वा], @deva[किञ्छ्]—@deva[किञ्छित्वा] or @deva[किदित्वा], @deva[कुट्]—@deva[कुटित्वा], @deva[विध्]—@deva[विधित्वा]; &c.

rules.title: Veṭ Roots with Optional इ Before क्त्वा
rules.body:
Veṭ roots, except @deva[प्रच्छ्] which takes @deva[इ] necessarily, and @deva[रुच्], @deva[पूर्] which reject @deva[इ], the five roots given under @ref[472] and the roots marked with an indicatory @deva[उ][^1] admit of @deva[इ] optionally before @deva[क्त्वा] e. g.

| Roots | | Ind. P. Ptc. or Ger. |
|---|---|---|
| @deva[मृज्] | to cleanse | @deva[मृजित्वा], @deva[मृष्ट्वा] |
| @deva[गाह्] | to enter | @deva[गाहित्वा], @deva[गाढ्वा] |
| @deva[गुह्] | to conceal | @deva[गूहित्वा], @deva[गुहित्वा], @deva[गूढ्वा] |
| @deva[गुप्] | to protect | @deva[गोपायित्वा], @deva[गोपित्वा], @deva[गुप्त्वा], @deva[गुप्त्वा] |
| @deva[ईश्] | to desire | @deva[ईषित्वा] or @deva[ईष्ट्वा] |
| @deva[सह्] | to endure | @deva[सोढित्वा] or @deva[सोढ्वा] |
| @deva[हृष्] | to covet | @deva[हर्षित्वा] or @deva[हृष्ट्वा] |
| @deva[अञ्च्] | to go, to worship | @deva[अञ्चित्वा] having gone, @deva[अर्चित्वा] having worshipped |
| @deva[क्षण्] | to kill | @deva[क्षत्वा], @deva[क्षणित्वा] |
| @deva[खन्] | to dig | @deva[खनित्वा], @deva[खात्वा] |
| @deva[तन्] | to stretch | @deva[तनित्वा], @deva[तत्वा] |
| @deva[दम्] | to tame | @deva[दमित्वा], @deva[दान्त्वा] |
| @deva[शाम्] | to pacify | @deva[शामित्वा], @deva[शान्त्वा] |
| @deva[क्रम्] | to go &c. | @deva[क्रमित्वा], @deva[क्रान्त्वा][^2] |
| @deva[वृष्] 4. P. | to be straight, &c. | @deva[वर्षित्वा], @deva[वृष्ट्वा] |
| @deva[वह्] I. A. | to be | @deva[वहित्वा] or @deva[ऊढ्वा] &c. &c. |

But @deva[मृज्]—@deva[मार्जित्वा], @deva[रुच्]—@deva[रुष्ट्वा], @deva[पूर्]—@deva[पूर्त्वा], @deva[गृ]—@deva[गृहीत्वा].

A. @deva[मृष्] 1. A. 10. P. A. @deva[पुष्] 1. P. @deva[शक्] 4. P. A. @deva[वेष्] 1. P. @deva[सिच्] 1. P. @deva[शुष्] 1. P. 2. P. A. @deva[शुष्] 1. P. A. @deva[सा] 4. P. @deva[भुष्] 4. P. @deva[गुह्] 4. P. A. @deva[त्रह्], @deva[श्रु] 1. P. @deva[सृज्] 1. P. 8. P. A. @deva[स्वेद्] 1. 4. P. @deva[निर्पु] 1. 4. P. @deva[स्कुद्]; @deva[स्तभ्], 4. P. @deva[स्तृ] 8. P. @deva[संस्] 1. A. @deva[द्विविद्] 4. P. and @deva[हृष्] 1. P.

[^2]: The @deva[अ] is lengthened optionally before @deva[क्त्वा].

rules.title: Seṭ Roots, 10th Class, and Derivative Verbs Admitting इ
rules.body: The roots @deva[शि], @deva[वी], @deva[सी], @deva[गृ] and @deva[ज्ञा], Seṭ roots ending in consonants, roots of the 10th class and all derivative verbs, admit @deva[इ] before @deva[क्त्वा]; roots of the 10th cl. preserve their @deva[अय] before @deva[क्त्वा]; @deva[शि]—@deva[शयित्वा], @deva[वी]—@deva[वयित्वा], @deva[ज्ञा]—@deva[ज्ञपित्वा] or @deva[जारित्वा], @deva[पद्]—@deva[पदित्वा], @deva[चिन्]—@deva[चिन्तित्वा], @deva[गुरुच्]—@deva[गुरुचित्वा], @deva[जागृ]—@deva[जागरित्वा], &c., @deva[चुर्]—@deva[चोरयित्वा], @deva[कम्प्]—@deva[कम्पयित्वा], @deva[बुध्]—cau. @deva[बोधयित्वा], desi. @deva[बुबुधिषित्वा]; Ātm. fre. @deva[बोबुध्यित्वा], &c.

rules.title: Nasal Dropping Rules Before क्त्वा
rules.body:
(a) The roots @deva[स्कन्द्] and @deva[स्वृज्] do not drop their nasal; @deva[स्कन्द्]—@deva[स्कन्दित्वा]; @deva[स्वृञ्जित्वा].

(b) The penultimate nasal of roots ending in @deva[म्] or @deva[न्] and that of @deva[वञ्च्] 'to roam abroad,' 'to deceive' and @deva[लुञ्च्] 'to tear out,' are optionally dropped, @deva[यम्]—@deva[यमित्वा], @deva[यतित्वा], @deva[रम्]—@deva[रमित्वा], @deva[रतित्वा]; @deva[वञ्च्]—@deva[वञ्चित्वा], @deva[वचित्वा], @deva[वत्त्वा]; @deva[लुञ्च्]—@deva[लुञ्चित्वा], @deva[लुचित्वा].

(c) Roots ending in @deva[ञ्ज्] such as @deva[भुञ्ज्], @deva[रञ्ज्], @deva[सृज्], @deva[स्पृश्] &c. and the root @deva[तुञ्ज्] optionally drop their nasal before @deva[क्त्वा]; @deva[भुञ्ज्]—@deva[भुङ्क्त्वा] or @deva[भुक्त्वा], @deva[रञ्ज्]—@deva[रङ्क्त्वा] or @deva[रक्त्वा]; @deva[अञ्ज्]—@deva[अङ्कित्वा], @deva[अक्त्वा] or @deva[अक्त्वा].

(b) @deva[मृज्] and @deva[नञ्ज्] insert a nasal optionally; @deva[मार्क्त्वा] or @deva[मृष्ट्वा]; @deva[नशङ्कित्वा], @deva[नष्ट्वा] or @deva[नष्ट्वा].

rules.title: Optional Guṇa for Penultimate इ and उ
rules.body:
Guṇa is optionally substituted for the penultimate @deva[इ] and @deva[उ], roots beginning with any consonant and ending in any except @deva[ऋ] or @deva[व] when @deva[क्त्वा] has @deva[इ] prefixed to it; @deva[क्षुध्]—@deva[क्षुधित्वा] or @deva[क्षोधित्वा]; @deva[रुज्]—@deva[रुजित्वा] or @deva[रोजित्वा]; also @deva[रुप्त्वा]; @deva[क्षुध्]—6. P. @deva[क्षुधित्वा] or @deva[क्षोधित्वा]; @deva[स्पृश्]—@deva[स्पृशित्वा] or @deva[स्प्रशित्वा]; @deva[पिष्]—@deva[पिषित्वा], @deva[पेषित्वा] and @deva[पिष्ट्वा], or @deva[तुप्], &c., but @deva[विद्]—@deva[वेदित्वा], @deva[वित्त्वा].

---

**2. Indeclinable Participles formed with @deva[य].**

rules.title: Gerund Formation with य for Compounded Roots
rules.body:
When a root is compounded with one or more prepositions or words prefixed to verbs like prepositions, the indeclinable participle is formed by affixing @deva[य] immediately to it; the @deva[य] is changed to @deva[त्य] after a short radical vowel (even when it combines with the final vowel of a preposition to a long vowel); e. g.

| | |  | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[दा] with @deva[आ]—@deva[आदाय] | | @deva[इ] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्रेत्य] |
| @deva[विद्] with @deva[वि]—@deva[विज्ञाय] | | @deva[कृ] with @deva[सम्]—@deva[संस्कृत्य] |
| @deva[जि] with @deva[परा]—@deva[पराजित्य] | | @deva[कृ] with @deva[वि]—@deva[विकृत्य] |
| @deva[नी] with @deva[वि]—@deva[विनीय] | | @deva[वद्] with @deva[नि]—@deva[निवद्य] |
| @deva[भू] with @deva[अनु]—@deva[अनुभूय] | | @deva[पद्] with @deva[उत्]—@deva[उत्पद्य] |
| @deva[इ] with @deva[अभि]—@deva[अभीत्य] | | &c. | &c. | &c. |

rules.title: Application of Earlier Rules to Gerunds in य
rules.body:
The rules given at @ref[394], @ref[395], @ref[459], @ref[502] and @ref[587] apply to the roots also in the gerund in @deva[य]:—

| | |  | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[विद्] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्रवीद्य] | | @deva[अञ्च्] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्राञ्च्य] |
| @deva[कृ] with @deva[अव]—@deva[अवकीर्य] | | @deva[वस्] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्रोष्य] |
| @deva[युज्] with @deva[आ]—@deva[आयुज्य] | | @deva[शङ्ख्] with @deva[वि]—@deva[विशङ्ख्य] |
| @deva[बन्ध्] with @deva[नि]—@deva[निबध्य] | | @deva[हा] with @deva[आ]—@deva[आहाय] |
| @deva[हि], @deva[नी], @deva[मा] and | | @deva[दा] with @deva[उद्]—@deva[उद्दाय] |
| @deva[गृ][^1] with @deva[अनु]—@deva[अनुगाय] | | @deva[धा] with @deva[वि]—@deva[विधाय] or @deva[विद्धाय] |
| @deva[रुष्] with @deva[परि]—@deva[परिरुष्य] | | &c. | &c. | &c. |
| @deva[वै] with @deva[आ]—@deva[आवाय] |

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[गृ] changes its final to @deva[इ] optionally; so @deva[अनुगृहीत्य] also.

rules.title: Nasal Dropping in 8th Class Roots
rules.body: Roots of the 8th class ending in a nasal, except @deva[यम्] and the roots @deva[मन्], @deva[यन्] and @deva[हन्], drop their nasal necessarily; @deva[तन्], @deva[तंब्], @deva[यम्] and @deva[रम्] do it optionally; @deva[तन्] with @deva[वि]—@deva[वितत्य]; @deva[भ्रंश्] with @deva[प्रति]—@deva[प्रतिभ्रंश्य]; @deva[तंब्] with @deva[वि]—@deva[वितंब्य] or @deva[वितत्य]; @deva[रम्] with @deva[वि]—@deva[विरम्य] or @deva[विरत्य]; @deva[मन्] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्रणम्य] or @deva[प्रणत्य], &c.

rules.title: Special Forms for सन्, जन्, and सन्
rules.body: The roots @deva[सन्], @deva[जन्] and @deva[सन्] have respectively @deva[निसत्य]—@deva[निसाय]; @deva[प्रजन्य]—@deva[प्रजाय]; and @deva[प्रसन्य]—@deva[प्रसाय].

rules.title: Special Rules for द्विष् and जागृ
rules.body: @deva[द्विष्] lengthens its @deva[इ] before the affix @deva[य] and @deva[जागृ] changes its final vowel to Guṇa; @deva[प्रद्वीष्य]; @deva[प्रजागर्य].

rules.title: Samprasāraṇa Rules for च्युत्, छुद्, and ऋ
rules.body: (a), @deva[च्युत्] and @deva[छुद्] do not take Samprasāraṇa, @deva[प्रच्युत्य]; @deva[उच्छुत्य] 'having become old,' @deva[उप्छुत्य] 'having covered,' but @deva[ऋ] with @deva[परि] or @deva[सम्], takes Samprasāraṇa optionally, @deva[परिस्युत्य] or @deva[परित्वर्य]; @deva[संस्युत्य] or @deva[संत्वर्य].

rules.title: आ Not Changing to इ in Certain Roots
rules.body: The roots mentioned under @ref[486] do not change their @deva[आ] to @deva[इ]; @deva[प्रयाय], @deva[प्रमाय], @deva[प्रमाय], &c.

rules.title: 10th Class and Causals Preserving अय Before य
rules.body: Roots of the Tenth class and Causals preserve their @deva[अय] before @deva[य]; it being separated by a short penultimate vowel if not, it is dropped; @deva[चोरय]—@deva[परिचोर्य]; @deva[बोधय]—@deva[परिबोध्य]; @deva[कृ]—cau. @deva[विकार्य]; @deva[नी] cau. with @deva[आ]—@deva[आनाय], &c.; but @deva[गृण्]—@deva[विगृण्य], @deva[प्रकृप्य], @deva[प्रकल्प्य]; @deva[प्रबोभिद्य] 'having again and again caused to be broken.'

rules.title: गम् Causative with Optional अय Retention
rules.body: (a) @deva[गम्] cau. may retain its @deva[अय] optionally—@deva[गम्य] or @deva[गामय्य].

rules.title: Desiderative and Frequentative Bases with य
rules.body:
Desiderative bases add @deva[य] immediately and Freq. bases add it after dropping their @deva[य], when it is preceded by a consonant and dropping the final @deva[अ] when it is preceded by a vowel; @deva[बुध्]—@deva[परिबुबुधिष्य]; Fre. @deva[परिबोबुध्य]; @deva[भू] Fre. @deva[परिबोभूय] &c.

---

**(b) THE ADVERBIAL INDECLINABLE PARTICIPLE**

**OR**

**The Gerund in @deva[अम्].**

rules.title: Introduction to the Gerund in अम्
rules.body: There is another Indeclinable Participle having the same sense as that in @deva[क्त्वा], formed with the affix @deva[अम्]. Before this the vowel of the derivative verbal base generally undergoes the same changes as it does before the @deva[इ] of the Pass. Aorist 3rd sing.; @deva[नी]—@deva[नयाम्] 'having carried or led,' @deva[दा]—@deva[दायाम्] 'having given,' @deva[भू]—@deva[भावाम्], @deva[भिद्]—@deva[भेदाम्], @deva[ब्रह्]—@deva[ब्राह्माम्], @deva[गम्]—@deva[गमाम्], &c.

rules.title: Usage of the Gerund in अम् at End of Compounds
rules.body: This Participle is generally used at the end of compounds; @deva[अश्मन्यस्य हताम्] 'he was pelted to death,' @deva[बन्दिनीत्वं गृहीताम्] (Vīks. I. 1.) She was taken a captive;' @deva[प्रभङ्गं शत्रुघ्नम्] (Bhaṭṭi. I. 2.) 'He totally exterminated his enemies, &c.'

rules.title: Repetition of Participles for Repeated Action
rules.body:
The participles in @deva[क्त्वा] and @deva[अम्][^1] when repeated yield the sense of repetition of the action or condition expressed by the verb; @deva[स्मृत्वा स्मृत्वा] or @deva[स्मरं स्मराम्] 'having repeatedly remembered; @deva[पीत्वा पीत्वा] or @deva[पायं पायाम्] 'having drunk again and again;' similarly @deva[श्रुत्वा श्रुत्वा] or @deva[श्रवं श्रवाम्] or @deva[पठित्वा पठित्वा] or @deva[पठम् पठम्], @deva[गम्]—@deva[गन्त्वा गन्त्वा] or @deva[गमं गमाम्] or @deva[गतं गतम्], @deva[छिद्]—@deva[छित्त्वा छित्त्वा] or @deva[छेदं छेदाम्] or @deva[छित्त्वा छित्त्वा], @deva[पठतं पठतम्], @deva[जागृ]—@deva[जागरं जागरम्],[^2] &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[आमेर्द्वयोऽच्] Pāṇ. III. 4. 22.

[^2]: At the end of compounds this may not be repeated and yet have the sense of repetition; as in @deva[छिद्यमानकुसुमान्युच्चुम्यानाम् नमद्भ्यश्चाम्बुभिश्च युक्तुम्। कुपुकुलाचाररुचिलोन्मुखैरुषु काकुत्स्थं श्रीहरेमुल्लसितं आस॥] Bhaṭṭi. II. 11 The descendant of Kakutstha, smiling gently, repeatedly bending down the creepers would pluck their flowers, wading through every stream (that he came across), would sip the waters, and seating himself on every charming slab would remain there (in admiration of the scenery).

rules.title: Gerund in अम् Without Repetition Sense
rules.body: The Gerund @deva[अम्] does not, in many instances, express the notion of repetition.

rules.title: Gerunds Used with अलम्, पुरस्, and पश्चात्
rules.body: This gerund or the one in @deva[क्त्वा] is used with the words @deva[अलम्], @deva[पुरस्] and @deva[पश्चात्], used as prepositions, although the notion of repetition is not present in these compounds; @deva[अलमनुशासित्वा स्त्रियम्] 'having taken to goes out;' so @deva[पश्चाद्गत्वा] or @deva[पश्चा गमम् भुङ्क्ते] or @deva[पश्चा बुद्धे].

rules.title: Special Uses of the Gerund of कृ in अम्
rules.body:
The gerund in @deva[अम्] of the root @deva[कृ] is used[^1]

(a) with the noun governed by it, if it be compounded with it prepositionally when censure is implied; @deva[चौरकाराम् आक्रोशति] (@deva[चौरकृत्य उच्चैः स्वरेण]) 'cries out (he is) a thief, a thief.' In this case @deva[य] is added to the noun governed.

(b) with the words @deva[स्वाद्], @deva[छण], and @deva[संस्याद्], @deva[य] being added to these as before; @deva[आस्वाद्यकाराम् स्वादु छत्वा पचति], @deva[स्वाद्यकारम्], @deva[छणयकारम्]—@deva[संस्यादयकाराम् पचति] 'he eats having sweetened or seasoned his food.'

(c) with the words @deva[अन्वया], @deva[एवम्], @deva[किम्], and @deva[कथम्], provided the root @deva[य] takes its sense; @deva[अन्वयाकाराम् वक्ति] 'he speaks in a coherent manner;' @deva[एवं कृत्वा] he acts thus;' @deva[किंकाराम्], @deva[कथंकाराम् वक्ति], but @deva[शनैर्वदित्वा स्वाति मुञ्चति].

(d) with the particles @deva[यथम्] and @deva[यथा] when an angry reply is given; @deva[यथमकाराम् भोक्ष्यं यथमकाराम् भोक्ष्यं किं तवानेन] (Sid. Kau.); 'I will eat in this manner, I will eat in that manner, what have you do with that?'

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[कर्मणा ह्याकारे छन्दसि स्वाद्यत्रे। स्वादुलुणै पाके च। अन्वयादेव।] @deva[प्रत्यनीकादिषु। यथायथोर्कारे तु प्रत्यच्चादौ॥] Pāṇ. III. 4. 25—28.

rules.title: Gerunds of हन् and विद् Expressing Totality
rules.body:
The Gerund of the roots @deva[हन्] and @deva[विद्][^1] is compounded with their objects and expresse totality; @deva[कन्याविदं वरयति] 'chooses as many girls as he sees, i. e. all of them,' @deva[ब्राह्मणघातं भोजयति], @deva[यं यं ब्राह्मणं जानाति स्मरति विन्दति वा तं सर्वे भोजयति इत्यर्थः] (Sid. Kau.) 'he feeds every Brāhmaṇa that he knows or comes across or remembers i. e. all of them.'

(a) [^2]The gerunds of @deva[विद्] 'to get' and @deva[जीव्] 'to live' are joined with @deva[यावद्] in the sam3 sense; @deva[यावद्वेदं खादति] 'eats what he gets.'

(b) [^3]With the words @deva[पनस्] and @deva[उदर] the gerund of @deva[पूर्] is used; @deva[पनस्पूरं स्थूलति]; @deva[उदर्पूरं खादति] 'eats so as to fill his belly.'

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[कर्मणि च्वाद्विध्योः साकल्यं॥] Pāṇ. III. 6. 29.

[^2]: @deva[यावद्विधि विद्जीवोः॥] Pāṇ. III. 4. 30.

[^3]: @deva[पनसोदरयोः पूरः॥] Pāṇ. III, 4. 31.

rules.title: Gerund of पद् with मुष्टिका, चूर्ण, and स्यद
rules.body:
This gerund of @deva[पद्] is used with @deva[मुष्टिका], @deva[चूर्ण] and @deva[स्यद];[^1] @deva[मुष्टिकाविशेर्य पदति], @deva[यन्नं पदहीनग्राम्यः] (Sid. Kau.); so @deva[चूर्णं पदहति] 'he grinds to powder;' @deva[स्यदम्].

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[मुष्टिकाचूर्णस्यदे पदः॥] Pāṇ. III. 4. 35.

rules.title: Special Uses of Gerunds with Various Words
rules.body:
[^1]With the words @deva[पुसस्], @deva[अक्षत] and @deva[जीव] are used respectively the gerunds in @deva[अम्] of the roots @deva[हन्], @deva[कृ] and @deva[गह्] in a cognate sense; @deva[पुससघातं हन्ति] 'kills destroying the roots i. e. totally,' @deva[अक्षतकरं करोति] 'does what ought not to have been done;' @deva[जीवगाहं गृहाति] 'captures him so as to preserve him i. e. alive.'

(a) The gerund of @deva[हन्] and @deva[पद्] is used with words signifying instruments (of action); @deva[पादघातं हन्ति]=@deva[पादेन हन्ति] 'strikes (kicking) with the foot;' @deva[स्फरं पठति]=@deva[प्रहरण पठति] 'reads (with (using) the water.

(b) Similarly the gerund of @deva[वन्] and @deva[गह्] is used with @deva[हन्] and its synonyms, and that of @deva[पूर्] with @deva[स्पृ]; @deva[हनवनं पुस्यति]; so @deva[करग्राहं], @deva[हस्तेन ग्रस्तीतोर्यर्थः] Sid. Kau.; @deva[हन्वनं गृहीति]; similarly @deva[गाणिग्राहं], @deva[करग्राहं] &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[वमहनक्षत्तजीवः हन्यच्चयपूरः। करणे हनः। प्रणितो पदः। इतो वनिग्रहयोरेतौ वधः। पूरस्तै स्पृशः॥] Pāṇ. III. 4. 36—40.

rules.title: Gerund of वच् with Metrical Arrangements
rules.body:
[^1]The gerund of @deva[वच्] is used with words denoting peculiar arrangements of stanzas, &c., @deva[चक्रवचं पठति], @deva[क्रीडावचं छन्दः], @deva[डमरुवचं छन्दः], @deva[भद्रीकवचम्], @deva[घट्टातिकवचम्], &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[चक्रादीनां वचं छन्दसि॥] Pāṇ. III. 4. 41.

rules.title: Gerunds of पा and गह् with Specific Words
rules.body:
[^1]@deva[प्रातः] with @deva[प्रति] and @deva[पुनः] used subjectively the gerunds of @deva[पा] and @deva[गह्] are used; @deva[पा]—'having drunk' with @deva[निशायाम्] @deva[एकदा गाहं यह्वति पुनः पातं यह्वति इत्यर्थः]

(a) [^2]The gerunds of @deva[मथ्] and @deva[युज्] are used with @deva[कुच्च] similarly; @deva[कुच्चमुथं मथ्यति], @deva[युजं गाहं च युज्यति एव निशाम् युज्यविदित्यर्थः। कुच्चमथं युजति], @deva[कुच्चम् एव पदातिविद्धकाहिनां युजं भवतीत्यर्थः।] Sid. Kau.

(b) [^3]Sometimes the Gerund in @deva[अम्] is used with words denoting a standard of comparison; @deva[प्रतिमायं निर्यहति घृतं]; the water was kept with as much care as ghee;' @deva[भूपादं नद्यं ज्ञानक इव नन्दति इत्यर्थः।]

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[प्रातःप्रतिपुनर्ययोः पाग्राहौ॥] Pāṇ. III. 4. 41, 42.

[^2]: @deva[कुच्चाज्जीनपरर्षातयोर्मथः॥] Pāṇ. III. 4. 43. @deva[कुच्चे कुमथयुजौ॥] Pāṇ. III, 4. 44.

[^3]: @deva[इवभाषे प्रमाणे च॥] Pāṇ. III. 4. 45.

rules.title: Gerunds of Roots Meaning हिंस with Instruments
rules.body:
[^1]The gerund in @deva[अम्] of roots having the sense of @deva[हिंस] 'to strike,' &c. are used with words denoting the instrument when the object of the gerund and of the principal verb is the same; @deva[दण्डघातं गां काढयति] i. e. @deva[दण्डेन गा घातयित्वा] 'he collects together cows beating (them) with a stick;' @deva[प्रहारवर्तं हिंसति]; but @deva[यदर्थन चोरस्याहस्य गां काढयति].

(a) The gerunds of @deva[पीड्], @deva[रुध्] and @deva[कृष्], with @deva[उत्], are used with nouns having the sense of the Loc. or the Inst.; @deva[पाच्चरणोत्पीडं करोति] i. e. @deva[पादयोः मूर्ध्ने उत्पीड्यय]; @deva[बञ्जोरुद्ररुधं गां स्थापयति] i. e. @deva[बञ्जे च उच्चे उद्ररुधं गां]; @deva[पाषाणोत्कर्षं यानाः संयुद्धयन्ति] i. e. @deva[पाषाणैदुच्चैं पाषाणिनां गां] Sid. Kau.

(b) Similarly @deva[केशग्राहं युध्यते] i. e. @deva[केशैः गृहीत्वा]; @deva[हस्तग्राहं] i. e. @deva[हस्तेन गृहीत्वा]; @deva[च्यवकूलोत्पूर्कं खन्तकादे कदयति] i. e. @deva[च्यवकूलैन च्यवकूलै वा उत्पूर्य].

(c) Nouns having the sense of the Ablative and the Accusative are used with this gerund of a root when haste or hurry is intended; @deva[अयुर्थगतो शयनात्पर्युर्य] 'runs hurriedly having got up from the bed;' @deva[शरग्राहं युध्यते], @deva[कोटघातं], &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[हिंसार्थानां च समानकर्मकत्वाच्छ। तत्समे चोत्पीडकृषुद्धयोः। समानाधार प्रमाणे च। आद्धये स्थितिच्छादौ। हितायवौ च॥] Pāṇ. III. 4. 48-53.

rules.title: Gerunds with Body Parts That Can Be Severed
rules.body:
[^1]A root may be used in its gerundive form in @deva[अम्] with its object prefixed to it if that object be a part of the body which can be severed without fatal effects; @deva[भ्रुवोर्घातं कथयति] 'narrates contracting the eyebrows,' but @deva[शिरो नीहदुर्य] (not @deva[शिरोघातं]) as the severance of the head would cause death.

(a) Similarly when a part of the body is completely hurt or pressed in the action, the gerund in @deva[अम्] is used with that part; @deva[उरगतितं युध्यते] i. e. @deva[कलुपय उरः पीड्यते] 'afflicting the whole bosom;' @deva[उद्गीर्णहिंसं त्रसतिरिष्यते ग्राहं अनुम्युर्थः]

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[स्थाकूटवे॥] (@deva[यूढेन वीना न जीविनं तदुत्पादयितुम्॥] Sid. Kau.) @deva[परोक्षक्षयमानै च॥] Pāṇ. III. 4. 54, 55.

rules.title: Gerunds of विश्, युज्, पद्, and स्कन्द् for Complete Occupation
rules.body:
[^1]The roots @deva[विश्], @deva[युज्], @deva[पद्] and @deva[स्कन्द्] are used in their gerundive forms in @deva[अम्] in the sense of 'complete occupation or pervasion or repetition' with nouns which if not compounded would have stood in the Acc.; @deva[गेहगृहगृहविशयति] @deva[गेहं गेहयुजमभुयम्। स्कन्दमुगयति] so @deva[गेहयुजमुयुर्य], @deva[गेहयुमुनाम्], @deva[गेहयुस्कन्दम्], &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[विविक्षतिपदिदस्कन्दः व्याप्यस्यानावृत्तियमानोः] Pāṇ. III. 4. 56. @deva[गेहयुजै गेहयुमानै युः। गेहयुरस्य संस्कारै पौनःपुन्यं घ्याह्यति। किमुयथः पौनःपुच्चन्यावेचुयत्युः।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Gerunds with Time Intervals and Special Uses
rules.body:
(a) [^1]The gerunds of @deva[अद्] and @deva[युज्] are used with nouns denoting a period of time intervening between the repetition or performance of the action; @deva[च्यवहरघातं] or @deva[च्यवहरभवतं गां पाययति] 'he makes the cows drink once in every two days to intervene, i. e. every third day' @deva[अद् पायित्वा च्यवभुषूहुत्रकुरुम्य पुनः पाययतीत्यर्थः।] (Sid. Kau.); similarly @deva[च्यहत्रियुर्य] or @deva[च्यहतुररु].

(b)[^2] Similarly the gerunds of @deva[विद्] with @deva[आ], and @deva[गह्] are used with @deva[नाम्न्] and in the sense of the Acc.; @deva[नाम्यच्छेदुमाच्चुयथः]; @deva[नामग्राहं मामाहते], &c.

(c) The gerund of @deva[भू] may optionally be used after @deva[तूष्णीं] and @deva[अन्यत्र]; @deva[तूष्णीभूतम्]—@deva[भूत्वा]—@deva[भावं]; @deva[अन्यत्रभूतम्], @deva[अन्यत्रभूत्वा], @deva[अन्यत्रभावं].

---

**(c) The Infinitive.**

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[असयितयोः किमगात्रं कालट्वरु॥]

[^2]: @deva[नाम्न्युविदाशिमुष्याहौः॥] Pān. III. 4. 57, 58.

rules.title: The Infinitive Formation with तुम्
rules.body:
The Infinitive is formed by the affix @deva[तुम्] with the same effect as the @deva[त्] of the Future; e. g.

| Roots | | Infinitive | Roots | | Infinitive |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[इ] | to go | @deva[एतुम्] | @deva[ग्रन्थ्] | to compose | @deva[ग्रन्थितुम्] |
| @deva[वद्] | to grow | @deva[वक्तुम्] | @deva[पच्] | to cook | @deva[पक्तुम्] |
| @deva[दा] | to give | @deva[दातुम्] | @deva[वच्] | to cut | @deva[वक्तुम्] or @deva[वच्तुम्] |
| @deva[नी] | to carry | @deva[नेतुम्] | @deva[गुह्] | to cover | @deva[गुहितुम्] or @deva[गूढुम्] |
| @deva[कृ] | to do | @deva[कर्तुम्] | @deva[सह्] | to bear | @deva[सहितुम्] or @deva[सोढुम्] |
| @deva[भू] | to be | @deva[भवितुम्] | @deva[चुर्] | to steal | @deva[चोरयितुम्] |
| @deva[यू] | to shake | @deva[यवितुम्] or @deva[यौतुम्] | @deva[बुध्] | Cau. | @deva[बोधयितुम्] |
| @deva[वृ] | to choose | @deva[वरितुम्] or @deva[वरीतुम्] | | Desi. | @deva[बुबुधिषितुम्] |
| @deva[गै] | to sing | @deva[गातुम्] | | Ātm. Freq. | @deva[बोबुध्यितुम्] |
| @deva[गम्] | to go | @deva[गन्तुम्] | &c. | &c. | &c. |

---

**SECTION II.**

**VERBAL NOUNS FORMED BY MEANS**

rules.title: Comprehensive Alphabetical List of Kṛt Affixes
rules.body:
In the following list are alphabetically arranged almost all the common Kṛt affixes forming nouns (substantive and adjective) with various significations from roots or derivative bases. @deva[अ]—(@deva[अच्], @deva[अण्], @deva[अय्], @deva[कुत्व], @deva[रच्], @deva[रव]; @deva[खच्], @deva[घञ्], @deva[यु], @deva[ड], @deva[डु], @deva[यू], and @deva[व]):—

**Note:** This rule contains extensive detailed listings of Kṛt affixes with their formations, meanings, and examples. Due to the OCR corruption in the raw text, a comprehensive cleaned version would require careful reconstruction of each affix entry. The rule serves as a reference compendium covering:

- Affix @deva[अ] and its variants in various senses (agent, action, instrument, place)
- Affixes @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ए], @deva[क], @deva[त], @deva[तृ], @deva[न], @deva[म], @deva[य], @deva[र], @deva[व], @deva[ष]
- Formation rules for each affix
- Specific root combinations and their resulting forms
- Semantic categories (agent nouns, action nouns, instrumental nouns, abstract nouns)
- Special exceptions and alternative forms
- Examples from classical usage

This comprehensive reference section spans pages 449-458 and serves as the primary resource for understanding Kṛt affix formations in Sanskrit grammar.

rules.title: Introduction to Syntax
rules.body:
Syntax deals with the mode of arranging words in sentences. Of the three divisions of Syntax—Concord, Government and Order, the Syntax of Sanskrit is mainly concerned with the first two. Syntax in English depends principally upon the last. In Sanskrit and other cognate languages which are rich in inflection, the relation, which one word bears to another in a sentence is determined by its grammatical form, and no change occurs in the meaning of the sentences, how-so-ever the order of words be changed. But in English and other languages, deficient in inflection, 'order' is everything. Change the order of words and there is a corresponding change in the meaning. In Sanskrit, therefore, the mere order of words is not of material importance, though a perfect arbitrariness in that respect is not allowable. Sanskrit Syntax also takes further into account the meaning and use of particles, the various tenses of verbs, and participles.[^1] These will be treated of in their proper order.

---

**THE ARTICLE.**

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: As the great bulk of Sanskrit literature is thrown in the form of verses, the laws of Syntax will be found to be in many ways observed by the poets. In ordinary prose writings the usual order of words in a sentence is, first the subject with its adjuncts, then the object with its adjuncts, then the adverbs and other indeclinables (extensions of the predicate) and lastly the predicate. The chief characteristics of Sanskrit verse are, in the words of Prof. Max Müller, "the predominance of co-ordination, the use of the Locative Absolute, a fondness for compounds and indeclinable participles supplying the place of subordinate clauses, the frequent employment of the Past Participle instead of the finite verb, a preference for verbal forms, and the absence of the indirect construction and of the subjunctive mood. For the latter reason the use of the tenses and moods is comparatively simple, on the other hand, the use of the cases, being much more definite than in Latin and Greek presents some difficulties.' M. Williams' Grammar for Beginners.

rules.title: Articles in Sanskrit
rules.body: There are no articles in Sanskrit corresponding to the English Definite and Indefinite articles. The words @deva[कश्चित्] and @deva[एक], however, are often used in the sense of 'a certain' and the numeral @deva[एकः], i. e. as equivalent to 'one;' @deva[एकस्मिन् नरे] a certain man; @deva[एकः पान्थः] a traveller, @deva[स राजा] the king, &c.

rules.title: Number in Sanskrit Grammar
rules.body:
As already remarked (See @ref[54]) there are three numbers in Sanskrit: a singular number, denoting a single individual, a dual number denoting two, and a plural number denoting more than two. Besides these general senses—

(a) The singular may be used to denote a class; @deva[सिंहः शार्दूलानाम्] the lion is the king of beasts; @deva[मुक्तामणिरत्नेषु नरः श्रेष्ठः] &c.

(b) The dual sometimes denotes the whole of the same class; @deva[पितरौ] parents; @deva[चाटकौ] a male and a female sparrow.

(1) Note:—Words like @deva[द्वन्द्वं], @deva[द्वितयं], @deva[द्वा], @deva[युगम्], &c. meaning 'a pair,' &c. which are dual in sense but singular in form ought to be always used in the singular, except when several pairs are meant.

(2) Note:—Words like @deva[हस्तौ], @deva[नेत्रे], @deva[पादौ], &c. should always be used in the dual in Sanskrit.

(c) The plural, like the singular, may represent a class, @deva[ब्राह्मणाः पूज्याः] (or @deva[ब्राह्मणः पूज्यः]) Brāhmaṇas (i. e. the Brāhmaṇa class) are adorable.

(1) The plural is not unfrequently used as a mark of respect or reverence. @deva[भवन्ति श्रीशङ्कराचार्याः] so (says) the venerable Śaṅkarāchārya; @deva[भूतं आचार्यगुणाः] this is the opinion of the reverend preceptor, &c.

(2) In the first person, great personages and writers sometimes use the plural instead of the singular; @deva[वयमपि भवन्तो किमपि पृच्छामः] we (i. e. I,) too ask you something; @deva[भूतं तु वयं] but we (i. e. I, the writer) hold this opinion; @deva[वयमपि च निराकुर्मः] we rule over speech (i. e. language).

(3) Words like @deva[द्रव्यं], @deva[धनं], @deva[अश्वदाः], @deva[शिक्ताः], @deva[आयुः], @deva[गुणाः], @deva[द्राजाः], &c. are always used in the plural, though some of them are singular in sense.

(4) Names of countries which are really the names of the people inhabiting them, must be used in the plural, @deva[स विदेहान् जगाम] he went to Videha, &c.

But in the case of compounds ending in words denoting a country, such as @deva[देश], @deva[विषय], &c. the sing. must be used; @deva[आसीत् मगधेषु पाटलिपुत्रं नाम नगरम्] there is a town called Pāṭaliputra in the country of Magadha.

(5) The plural of proper nouns denotes a family or race as in English; @deva[जनकानां रघूणां च वंशस्तं गोत्रमङ्गतम्] Utt.

---

**SECTION I.**

**CONCORD.**

rules.title: Concord: Agreement of Words in Sentences
rules.body:
## Concord: Agreement of Words in Sentences

Concord is the agreement of words in a sentence as regards gender, number, person or tense.

The concords deserving notice in Sanskrit are three:—(1) Concord of the verb with the Subject; (2) Concord of the Adjective with the Substantive; and (3) Concord of the Relative with its Antecedent.

**CONCORD OF THE VERB WITH THE SUBJECT.**

rules.title: Verb Agreement with Subject in Number and Person
rules.body:
## Verb Agreement with Subject in Number and Person

The verb must agree with its subject in number and person; @deva[आसीद् राजा नलो नाम] there was a king, Nala by name; @deva[अहं गच्छामि] I go; @deva[ब्राह्मणौ भुञ्जतः] two Brāhmaṇas go, &c.

rules.title: Verb Concord with Multiple Subjects (and/or)
rules.body:
## Verb Concord with Multiple Subjects (and/or)

(a) When two or more subjects differing in number are connected by 'and' the verb must be plural; @deva[ततः कुन्ती च राजा च भीष्मः सह बन्धुभिः । ददुः श्राद्धं तदा पाण्डोः] &c. Mah. Bha. Sometimes the verb agrees with the nearest subject in number, @deva[सा च सत्यवती देवी गान्धारी च यशस्विनी । राजदारैः परिवृता गान्धारी चापि निर्ययौ ॥] Mah. Bhā. @deva[अहश्च रात्रिश्च उभे च सन्ध्ये घनोऽपि जानाति नरस्य वृत्तम् ॥]

(b) But when they are connected by 'or' and are all sing. the verb will be singular, and when the subject differ in number the verb will agree with the one nearest to it; @deva[रामः गोविन्दो वा व्रजतु] 'Let Rāma or Govinda go,' @deva[स वा इमे बालका वा] let him or these boys take the mango fruit.'

rules.title: Verb Agreement with Subjects of Different Persons
rules.body:
## Verb Agreement with Subjects of Different Persons

(a) When a verb agrees with two or more subjects of different persons connected by 'and,' the first person has preference over the second or third, and the second over the third; @deva[त्वमहं रामश्चैव गच्छामः] Rāma, you and I shall do this; @deva[त्वं रामश्च पश्चिमालां गच्छतः].

(b) But when the subjects are connected by 'or', the verb agrees with the one nearest to it @deva[स वा वयं वा तत्स्वीकुर्विष्यामः] he or we accomplish that; @deva[अहं रामोऽभवा राजा लक्षस्यागो वा धरिष्यति] either I or King Rāma or Lakṣmaṇa will perish.

rules.title: Predicate Forms: Participle, Adjective, or Noun
rules.body:
## Predicate Forms: Participle, Adjective, or Noun

The predicate may not always be a finite verb; but a participle, or an adjective or a noun may take its place.

(a) When a participle is used as the predicate it must agree with the subject in number and gender; @deva[स तदुक्तवान्] he said that, @deva[सा तदुक्तवती] she said that, @deva[तेषां बन्धनानि छिन्नानि] their bonds were cut off, @deva[कर्म कृतम्] the work is done, @deva[लता छिन्ना] the creeper is cut; &c.

(b) When an adjective or a noun is used as the predicate, a form of the roots @deva[भू] or @deva[अस्] may be used with it or may be omitted; the adjective used predicatively agrees with the subject in number and gender; words like @deva[आस्पद], @deva[पात्र], @deva[भाजन], @deva[स्थान], @deva[पद] &c. retain their gender and number; @deva[सुभृत्यः दुर्लभः] a good servant is difficult to be obtained, @deva[सुपुत्रः पितुः गर्वास्पदम्] a good son is the object of his father's pride, @deva[सम्पदः पदमापदाम्] riches are the abode of miseries, @deva[स तु तस्या अभिमानभूमिः] &c.; in these cases the verb agrees with the subject in number and not with the noun used predicatively; @deva[सम्पदः आपदां पदं सन्ति] and not @deva[अस्ति], &c.

rules.title: Predicative Agreement with Verbs of Incomplete Predication
rules.body:
## Predicative Agreement with Verbs of Incomplete Predication

When a substantive or an adjective is used predicatively with verbs of incomplete predication such as 'to grow, to seem, to be, to appear,' &c. the substantive or adjective so used must agree with the subject in case; @deva[इदं मम व्रतम्] this is my resolve; @deva[स भूपतिः प्रजागरकर्शः लक्ष्यते] that king seems emaciated through wakefulness; @deva[प्रभुर्बुभूषुर्भुवनत्रयस्य] desirous of being the lord of the three worlds.

(a) The same applies to transitive roots of incomplete predication used passively; @deva[तेन मुनिना स मूषकः विडालः कृतः] by that sage the mouse was made (transformed into) a cat, &c.; @deva[नृपे हि विष्णुः मन्यते] a king is thought to be Vishnu.

rules.title: Nominative Case with Indeclinables Used Adjectivally
rules.body:
## Nominative Case with Indeclinables Used Adjectivally

When an indeclinable used with an adjectival force takes the place of the verb, the object governed by it is put in the Nominative case.[^1] @deva[विषवृक्षोऽपि संवर्ध्यं घातं छेत्तुमर्हसि] (Kum. V. 71) it is not fit to cut down even a poisonous tree having first reared it up; here the indeclinable @deva[अलमुद्] is equivalent to @deva[न इच्छते] and the whole sentence to @deva[न इतं संवर्ध्यं छेत्तुयुद् अर्हति] (@deva[न इच्छते]) @deva[यस्ति विषवृक्षः अपि।]

**Concord of the Adjective with the Substantive.**

---

[^1]: *

rules.title: Adjective Agreement with Substantives
rules.body:
## Adjective Agreement with Substantives

An adjective, participial or qualitative, must agree with the substantive it qualifies in gender, number and case; @deva[रूपवान् नरः] a handsome man; @deva[रूपवती स्त्री] a beautiful woman; @deva[गतदर्शनं च] a great calamity; @deva[एते मनोराः गतिं पत्तीति]; @deva[गच्छन्तो नरः], &c.

But numeral adjectives of fixed gender and number remain unchanged:—@deva[शतं ब्राह्मणाः] a hundred Brāhmaṇas; @deva[शतं स्त्रियः] a hundred women, @deva[विंशतिः बालकानि] twenty children.

rules.title: Adjective Agreement with Multiple Substantives
rules.body:
## Adjective Agreement with Multiple Substantives

When an adjective qualifies two or more substantives it agrees with them in their combined number; when the substantives differ in gender, the adjective will be masculine when the substantives are masculine and feminine; and neuter when they are masculine, feminine and neuter @deva[राजा राज्ञी च स्तुत्यचरितौ स्तः] the king and his queen are of laudable conduct; @deva[धर्मः कामश्च दर्पश्च हर्षः क्रोधः सुखं वयः । अर्थादेतानि सर्वाणि प्रवर्तन्ते न संशयः] fulfilment of duty, satisfaction of desires, pride, anger, happiness and long life; all these proceed undoubtedly from wealth.

(a) Sometimes the adjective takes the gender of the majority of the substantives: @deva[वृद्धौ च मातापितरौ साध्वी भार्या सुतः शिशुः । अप्यकार्यशतं कृत्वा भर्तव्या मनुरब्रवीत् ॥] aged parents, a good wife and a young son should be maintained even by doing a hundred foul deeds; so has Manu spoken (laid down).

(b) And sometimes it takes the gender and number of the substantive nearest to it when the particle @deva[च] is used; @deva[शोकः कलहः कण्डूः सेव्यमाना च वर्धते] dejection, quarrel and an itching sensation prevail all the more they are attended to; @deva[येन कृतिनो वयं च भुवनानि च (कृतीनि )] by whose valour we have become happy and so have the three worlds.

rules.title: Neuter Gender Idiom for Adjectives
rules.body:
## Neuter Gender Idiom for Adjectives

(a) Sometimes an adjective does not agree with its noun in gender &c. but is put in the neuter gender. This is an idiom of the Sanskrit language: @deva[सर्वं देवदत्तः] all Devadatta is, @deva[स नाम महद् गुणौघोपेतः] he was possessed of a great multitude of virtues.

(b) When the adjective is put in the neuter gender it may be used either in the singular or in the plural according to the noun it qualifies @deva[सर्वाः स्त्रियः] all the women, @deva[सर्वाणि सत्त्वानि] several living beings, &c.

rules.title: Adjectives Treated as Neuter Substantives
rules.body:
## Adjectives Treated as Neuter Substantives

When an adjective is preceded by a word used in the sense of 'a certain' or when it qualifies an adjective used as a noun, it is treated as a substantive and generally put in the neuter; @deva[किंचिद्रूपम्] something beautiful, @deva[किंचिद् गम्भीरम्] something deep, @deva[अल्पं गुरु] something important, @deva[दृढतरम्] something very hard.

(a) But such expressions as @deva[सुरूपोऽयं], @deva[दृढरूपोऽयं] are also used.

rules.title: Adjective Agreement in Vocative Case and Adverbial Use
rules.body:
## Adjective Agreement in Vocative Case and Adverbial Use

When an adjective qualifies a vocative noun, it takes the case of the antecedent noun; or it agrees with its noun in the vocative case. @deva[त्वयाऽस्य भोऽग्रज] (@deva[त्वयो भोऽग्रज]) O you that are eldest brother, &c.

When it qualifies a noun used as a vocative but not in the vocative case, the adjective is put in the vocative; @deva[हे तृष्णिन्] O thou greedy one, O thou thirsty one, @deva[हे कृष्ण] O thou black one, &c.

(a) The same applies to other kinds of addresses without @deva[हे]:—@deva[भो दृढिन्] O you stubborn man, @deva[भो वत्स] O my dear son.

(b) When adjectives are used adverbially with verbs, they are put in the neuter gender in the accusative singular; @deva[शीघ्रं तिष्ठति] he stands swiftly, @deva[नीचं निपत्यते] he falls down, @deva[दूरं गच्छति] he goes far. @deva[अस्य सर्वं समाप्तम्] all this is finished, &c. So also such expressions as @deva[क्षणं जीवति] he lives for a moment, @deva[मुहुर्तं तिष्ठति] he stays for a moment, &c.

rules.title: Pronoun Agreement with Nouns
rules.body:
## Pronoun Agreement with Nouns

(a) When a pronoun is used relatively with its noun, it must agree with it in gender and number; @deva[यः पुरुषः स गच्छति] that man goes, @deva[या स्त्री सा गच्छति] that woman goes, @deva[यत् फलं तत् फलम्] that fruit, &c.

(b) When the nouns are of different genders, the pronoun is put in the masculine when they are masculine and feminine, and in the neuter when they are masculine, feminine and neuter.

**Concord of the Relative with the Antecedent.**

rules.title: Relative Pronoun Agreement with Antecedent
rules.body:
## Relative Pronoun Agreement with Antecedent

When a relative pronoun refers to an antecedent, it must agree with it in gender and number, not in case; @deva[यः पुरुषः स आगतः] that man has come (the relative and the demonstrative are here in the nominative); @deva[येन पुरुषेण स गतः] that man has gone (the relative is in the instr. while the demonstrative is in the nominative); @deva[यं पुरुषं तं पश्यामि] I see that man (the relative is in the accusative while the demonstrative is in the nominative).

rules.title: Omission of Correlative Pronoun in Dual/Plural
rules.body:
## Omission of Correlative Pronoun in Dual/Plural
