When the antecedent is of the dual or the plural number, the correlative pronoun in the principal clause may be omitted, and the verb put in that number of which the antecedent is; @deva[ये पुरुषाः तव सुताः वा वस्युर्कुटागच्छन्ति] or @deva[ये पुरुषाः तव सुताः ते गच्छन्ति] those men who are your sons go (in the first sentence the correlative pronoun @deva[ते] is omitted and the verb, though governed by an antecedent in the relative clause, is made plural).

## SECTION II.
GOVERNMENT.
A. GOVERNMENT OF CASES.

rules.title: Government: Influence of One Part of Speech Over Another
rules.body:
## Government: Influence of One Part of Speech Over Another

Government is that influence which one part of speech exerts over another, requiring it to be put in a particular case. It is mainly concerned with Cases, viz. "the Government of Nouns or of Cases by Verbs and Nouns" and "Government by Prepositions."

rules.title: Accusative Case Denotes the Object
rules.body:
## Accusative Case Denotes the Object

The Accusative denotes the object i.e. the person or thing upon whom or which the effect of an action takes place; @deva[हरिं सेवते] he worships Hari; @deva[ग्रामं गच्छति दूर्वां स्पृशति] going to a village he touches grass.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 46

rules.title: Transitive Verbs Govern Accusative Case
rules.body:
## Transitive Verbs Govern Accusative Case

All transitive verbs govern an Accusative; @deva[पुष्पाणि उपचिनोति] collects flowers; @deva[अपः एव सर्वं] (the creator) created water first, &c. Several transitive verbs govern what is called in English a factitive object besides a direct object; @deva[प्राकृतान् प्रकृतिं त्वां पुनः पुरुषं विदुः] (Kum. II. 13) they consider thee to be Prakṛti, they know thee to be Purusha; @deva[कुमारं नेतारं कृता] having made Kumāra the leader (of the forces); @deva[नाम तस्य अजं चक्रे] made his son Aja by name.

rules.title: Intransitive Verbs with Accusative of Space and Time
rules.body:
## Intransitive Verbs with Accusative of Space and Time

Intransitive roots govern the Accusative nouns denoting space or country, or duration of time and distance; @deva[कुरुक्षेत्रं वसति] he stays in the country of the Kurus; @deva[तत्र कतिपयं दिवसं अवसत्] there he dwelt for some days, @deva[गोदोहिकां] he sits down till a cow is milked; @deva[कोशं प्रतिष्ठे] he walks for a Koṣa, @deva[कोशं कुटिला नदी] the course of the river is winding for a Koṣa; but sometimes the Locative may be used; @deva[दीर्घकोशे स्थितः नरः] the hill is situated at a part of a Koṣa.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 5

rules.title: Verbs of Motion Govern Accusative of Destination
rules.body:
## Verbs of Motion Govern Accusative of Destination

Roots having the sense of motion, real or metaphorical govern the Accusative of the place to which it is directed. @deva[ग्रामं गच्छति] goes to a village; @deva[अजविचरितं विचरति दावं] with his bow strung he roamed all over the forest; @deva[आनन्दस्य परां काष्ठां गच्छत] they reached the highest point of joy; @deva[मनसा कृष्णं] goes to Kṛṣṇa (thinks of him) mentally; @deva[अतः प्रभृति चिन्तयन् निद्रां याति] while thus pondering he sank into sleep.

(a) When the motion is real, the Dative may also be used; @deva[मातुले ग्रामं वा गच्छति]; but not of words denoting 'a road;' @deva[पन्थानं गच्छति] only; but @deva[उपमार्गं याति गच्छति] he reaches the main road by taking a by-path.

---

[^1]: But when the relation of object and verb is expressed by the passive termination the noun forming the object is put in the nominative case; @deva[हरिः सेव्यते].

rules.title: Roots ज्ञा, स्था, विश् with अधि Govern Accusative of Location
rules.body:
## Roots @deva[ज्ञा], @deva[स्था], @deva[विश्] with @deva[अधि] Govern Accusative of Location

The roots @deva[ज्ञा], @deva[स्था] and @deva[विश्], with @deva[अधि], govern the Accusative of the place where the action takes place; @deva[अग्रशिलां अविष्टः] reclining at a stone-slab; @deva[अग्रं इन्द्रासनं अर्धं अविविशुः] occupied half of Indra's seat; @deva[अध्यास्त सदंधुषु अयोध्यां] lived in Ayodhyā delightful in all seasons.

rules.title: Root विश् with अभि and आ: Accusative and Locative
Root वस् with Prepositions Governs Accusative
rules.body:
## Root @deva[वस्] with Prepositions Governs Accusative

The root @deva[वस्] preceded by the prepositions @deva[उप], @deva[अनु], @deva[अभि] and @deva[आ] governs the Accusative case; @deva[वैकुंठं हरिः वसति] Hari dwells in Vaikuṇṭha; @deva[सुनिर्जनं वनं वसति] he dwelt in a dreary forest; but @deva[वस्] with @deva[उप] meaning 'to abstain from food' is used with the Loc. @deva[अनुपवसति]; @deva[आवसति वनं रामः] Rāma dwelt in the forest.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 48

rules.title: Particles and Prepositions Governing Accusative
rules.body:
## Particles and Prepositions Governing Accusative

The particles @deva[उभयतः], @deva[सर्वतः], @deva[उभाध्यति], @deva[अन्यत्र], @deva[अभितः] and @deva[निकषा]; @deva[अन्तरा], @deva[परितः], @deva[समया], @deva[निकष], @deva[द्वे] and @deva[प्रति] meaning 'to,' and @deva[अन्तर] 'between,' and @deva[अनृतेण] 'without,' 'regarding to,' govern the Accusative; @deva[उभयतः कृष्णं गोपाः] the cowherds are on both sides of Kṛṣṇa; @deva[निकटं प्रासादं रक्षितिः रक्षन्ति] guards keep vigil on all sides of the palace; @deva[उपरि लोकं हरिः] Hari is over all the worlds; @deva[लोकं गतः] went below the world, except itself; Hari is around you; @deva[धिक् कुरूणां] fie upon the lord of the Kurus, with all his brothers; (@deva[धिक्]) is used sometimes with the Nom. and sometimes with the Voc. @deva[धिक् वित्तं] fie upon wealth which is attended with troubles; @deva[किं भाते तत् विनारण यच्च भर्ता पतितः अपि शरीरं न वर्तन्ते] (Bhaṭṭi I. 12) he dispelled the demons from around the altar and offered sacrifices to the minor deities arranged round the principal one. @deva[अन्तरं प्राप्य परितः तिष्ठति] (Kir. XI. 8), @deva[ग्रामं समया निकष चरति] goes near to the village. @deva[अतः अन्यत्र न कोऽपि] no one except Hari is not a devotee of Kṛṣṇa; @deva[मन्मथः अस्ति अल्पः अपि नगरं यति] I have but a faint desire to go to the town; @deva[अन्तर तनो हरिं हरि अनृतेण न सुखं] happiness is not possible without Hari; @deva[देवीं वसुमतीं अनृतेण] with reference to queen Vasumatī.

Some of the indeclinables given above are used with the Genitive; e.g. @deva[उपरि विद्यामतः सूर्यः इव सेत्यस्थौ] (he stood) very high above all by his learning, like the sun, &c.[^1]

---

[^1]: Vārtikas on Pāṇ. I. 4. 48. @deva[अन्तरा अनृतेण च] Pāṇ. II. 3. 4.

rules.title: Prepositions Used with Accusative: अति, अनु, अपि, उप, आविस्, परि, प्रति
rules.body:
## Prepositions Used with Accusative: @deva[अति], @deva[अनु], @deva[अपि], @deva[उप], @deva[आविस्], @deva[परि], @deva[प्रति]

The following prepositions are used with the Accusative.[^1]

(a) @deva[अति] 'superior to, higher than' @deva[अनु] 'just after, after by the side of, inferior to,' @deva[अपि] 'close to' and @deva[उप] 'near, inferior to;' e.g. @deva[अति देवान् कृष्णः] Kṛṣṇa excels gods in might; @deva[अति रामं गोविन्दः] Govinda is superior to Rāma; @deva[जपं प्रावर्तत] it rained just after the muttering of prayers; @deva[त्वं मनुष्यं ते] every thing of thee is after mine; @deva[अनु पितरं गच्छति सुतः] the son imitates his father; @deva[न भवान् अनु रामं चेत्] if you are not inferior to Rāma; so @deva[अनु हरि सुरः]; @deva[भक्तो हरि अपि] the devotee is close to Hari; @deva[उप न ते कर्म] your act is not like that of a hero (lit. is inferior to his); @deva[उप हरिं सुरः] &c.

(b) The prepositions @deva[आविस्], @deva[अनु], @deva[परि] and @deva[प्रति] are used with the Accusative when they refer to particular things; @deva[गिरिं आविस् अनु परि प्रति विद्योतते विद्युत] the lightning flashes towards the mountain; also when they mean 'to every one,' &c. @deva[वृक्षं अभि अनु परि प्रति सिञ्चति] waters each and every tree; so @deva[अभि अनु परि प्रति स्त्री स्त्री जातमुखः].

(c) @deva[अनु], @deva[परि] and @deva[प्रति] also govern the Accusative when they imply 'one's own share;' @deva[लक्ष्मीः हरिं अनु परि प्रति] Lakṣmī is the proper share (property) of Hari.

---

[^1]: Prepositions used by themselves and governing nouns are called Karmapravachanīya. Pāṇ. II. 3. 8 and I. 4. 85–87, 90, 91.

rules.title: Roots Governing Double Accusative
Passive Construction with Double Accusative Roots
rules.body:
## Passive Construction with Double Accusative Roots

When these verbs are used in the passive, the secondary object in the case of the first twelve roots and the principal one in that of the last four is put in the Nominative, the other Accusative remaining as before; @deva[गावः पयः दुह्यते], @deva[ब्राह्मणः रामं यथार्थं लोकायितः], @deva[इन्द्रापिः द्वारं नीयते देवैः] &c, @deva[तेन गावः ग्रामं नीयन्ते विज्ञातं क्षयन्तं उदयन्ते वा], &c.

rules.title: Causative Verbs: Subject in Accusative Case
rules.body:
## Causative Verbs: Subject in Accusative Case

In the case of the causals of roots implying 'motion,' 'knowledge,' 'eating,' roots having some literary work for their objects, intransitive roots and the roots @deva[हन्] and @deva[जल्प्], @deva[भू] with @deva[आङ्]; @deva[ह्वे] with @deva[हि], @deva[यच्] and @deva[छु], their subject in the primitive sense is put in the Accusative case.[^1]

@deva[शत्रुद्विगुमयर्थं वैदशं स्वक्तनेदयद् ।]
@deva[आवासयच्छं देवान् अपाययद् अमृतं ।]
@deva[आध्यापयत् कमलं पृथिव्यां यः ते स भवेद् हरेः ॥] (Sid. Kau.)

That venerable Hari is my refuge who despatched the enemies (of gods) to the next world, explained the meaning of the Vedas to his (followers), made the gods drink nectar, taught Vedas to the Creator and seated the earth (made it rest) on waters.

@deva[दैत्यान् हरिं मनाते] he makes the devotees see Hari; @deva[जलपति सपरे विद्यमानं यत्नवान् यच् मैत्रकगुरुमहोत्सवः] (R. Kum. I. 82). @deva[अध्यापयति यत्किंचित्]. But when the double causal is used the subject ceases to be the subject of the root in the primitive sense and therefore takes the Instrumental; @deva[रामयति देवदत्तः यत्रेद्त्तं], @deva[गच्छयति देवदत्तेन यत्र्देवनं विष्णुदेवतः]

Obs:— @deva[दृश्] is sometimes found used with the Dative; @deva[यत्त्विङोगुलं स दंङतिर्य] (Rag. XII. 54).

(a) The causals of @deva[नी], and @deva[वह्] when it has for its subject a noun other than one denoting a driver, govern the Instrumental of the primitive subject; @deva[नायति वाहयति वा भारं यरथेन] he makes his servant carry a load; @deva[यरुंचयति रथं वाहानं यत्तः] the charioteer makes the horses draw the chariot.

(b) The same holds good in the case of the causal of @deva[अद्] and @deva[सह्]; @deva[आदयति यत्विदेन न अन्नं वट्नं] he makes the boy eat his food.

(c) @deva[यच्], when it has not the sense of @deva[हिंसा] 'pain or injury to a sentient thing' does the same; @deva[भुक्तयेच्चन् वट्नं]; but @deva[भुक्तयति वघोरदेवरे सस्यं] (when the loss of corn causes pain to the mind).

(d) @deva[स्मृ] and @deva[स्मार] which denote a kind of knowledge are construed with the Instrumental in the Atm. @deva[भोनं यत्तेन यत्त्वरेद्वयच] when meaning 'to remember with pain' is sometimes found used with the Accusative also; @deva[स्मरयति भीषयति वा देवदत्तं]; @deva[अरिघं चैद्यानो अतिकुञ्चेषिश्यषकेनेरे स्मार्यन्ते प्रकटीः]. Vide also Siṣ. VI. 66.

(e) The causal of the denominative @deva[घुच्र] also is construed with the Instrumental; @deva[घुच्रवयति देवदत्तेन] he causes Devadatta to make a sound.

Note:—By intransitive roots are meant such roots as are not capable of governing an object other than one denoting space, time, &c. and not such as, though transitive, may be used without their object being actually expressed; @deva[भारं आरयति देवदत्तं]; but @deva[देवदत्तं गच्छयति] and @deva[यदयति] though @deva[यदतं] and @deva[देवदत्तं एवं] is not actually expressed.[^2]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 52. Vārtikas.
[^2]: Note on intransitive roots (Sid. Kau.)

rules.title: Causative Verbs: Accusative or Instrumental with दा, स्मृ, आह, दृश्
rules.body:
## Causative Verbs: Accusative or Instrumental with @deva[दा], @deva[स्मृ], @deva[आह], @deva[दृश्]

The primitive subject of the verbs @deva[दा] and @deva[स्मृ], of @deva[आह], and @deva[दृश्] when used in the Atm. is either put in the Accusative or the Instrumental; @deva[हारयति कारयति वा यर्स्यं यर्यं वा कटं] he causes the servant to take or weave a mat; @deva[अविमुवटिहुड्नो यरुयुरु नेतं नेतं वा] he makes the devotee bow down to, or see, God.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 43. Vārtikas.

rules.title: Passive Construction with Causative Verbs
rules.body:
## Passive Construction with Causative Verbs

When the causal forms are used in the passive, the principal object (i.e. the primitive subject) is put in the Nominative case; but in the case of roots implying 'knowledge or eating' and roots having a literary work for their object, the principal object is put in the Nominative case and the secondary object in the Accusative or vice versa; @deva[देवदत्तेन करोति] Devadatta prepares a mat—@deva[देवदत्तं देवदत्तेन वा कटं कारयति]; @deva[देवदत्तः कटं कार्यते] he makes Devadatta prepare a mat, @deva[देवदत्तः ग्रामं गच्छति] Dev. goes to a village; @deva[देवदत्तं ग्रामं गच्छयति] causes Dev. to go; @deva[देवदत्तः गच्छयते] Devadatta is made to go to a village, &c.; @deva[मणवकं धर्मं बोधयति] he makes Māṇavaka know his duty; @deva[बोध्यते मणवकं धर्मः मणवको धर्मं बोध्यते वा] Māṇavaka is made to know, &c.; @deva[वट्योदनं भोजयते] he makes the child eat food; @deva[वट्योदनं भोज्यते] or @deva[वट्योदनो भोज्यते] the boy is made, &c.

rules.title: Causative Verbs with Double Accusative Roots
rules.body:
## Causative Verbs with Double Accusative Roots

As regards the causal of roots governing two Accusatives the general rules given at @ref[808] hold good; @deva[को रोदनरु दूहरयं रामं अययच्छत]; (@deva[दूहः]) @deva[को रोदनेरु रामयुङ गोरमयुयुयुरु], @deva[गोयोऽज्ञां ग्रामं हरते], (@deva[स्वक्तो]) @deva[गोपेन अज्ञां ग्रामं हारयति], &c.

## THE INSTRUMENTAL CASE

rules.title: Instrumental Case: Agent and Instrument
rules.body:
## Instrumental Case: Agent and Instrument

The Instrumental case primarily expresses either the agent (when the construction is passive) or the instrument or means by which an action is done; @deva[तव महिमानं अज्ञात्वा मया अस्युत्तोऽऽसि] thou wast disrespected by me, not knowing thy greatness; @deva[रामेण बाणेन हतो वाली] Vāli was killed by Rāma with an arrow (here @deva[रामेण] is the agent; @deva[बाणेन] the instrument).[^1]

(a) The Instrumental is also used in the following senses. @deva[रुपेण दर्शनेन] lovely by nature, @deva[यावत् यात्मकः] he is almost pitiable; @deva[विप्रोभः गार्ग्यः] by family name; @deva[रणे पति कत्यति] he buys with ease; @deva[सो सुलभेन], @deva[विवक्षति], &c @deva[द्विद्रोणेन यान्यं कोणति] he buys two drones of corn at a time; @deva[सहस्रेण यसुयत् कोणति] he buys one thousand beasts at a time, &c.

(b) In the case of numerals and words expressive of measure the Acc. may also be used; @deva[द्विद्रोणं कोणति यान्यं], @deva[शतं घोटकं यान्यं हतं वसुयर घरेयं], &c.

(c) Obs.—The root @deva[दिव्] 'to play,' however, governs the Accusative or the Instrumental of the instrument used; @deva[अक्षैः यक्षानरु वा दीव्यति] he plays at dice.

(d) The root @deva[ज्ञा] with @deva[सम्] also governs the Accusative or the Instrumental; @deva[पितरं पितरा वा संज्ञानीते] he recognises or lives in peace with his father, but @deva[विष्णुं संजानीयाच्च] remember Viṣṇu.[^2]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 18
[^2]: Various Vārtikas on instrumental case usage (Sid. Kau. on Pāṇ. VII. I. 69)

rules.title: Instrumental with Time/Space for Accomplishment
rules.body:
## Instrumental with Time/Space for Accomplishment

When the accomplishment of an object is to be expressed, the Instrumental of words expressing the length of time or space is used; @deva[अहुना कोषेण भङ्ग्यादितीर्णः] the section (of the Veda) was studied by him in a day, or a Koṣa (i.e. by going over it); but @deva[वरधर्मेण नायते] as the accomplishment does not take place.

rules.title: Instrumental with Defective Limbs
rules.body:
## Instrumental with Defective Limbs

Words expressing some defect in a limb of the body govern the Instrumental of the defective limb; @deva[अक्ष्णा काणः] blind of one eye; so @deva[पदेन खञ्जः] &c.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 20

rules.title: Instrumental with Characteristic Attributes
rules.body:
## Instrumental with Characteristic Attributes

A characteristic attribute indicative of the existence of a particular state or condition is put in the Instrumental; @deva[जटाभिः तापसः] he is an ascetic (which is apparent) from his matted hair (@deva[जटाभिः=प्रकृतितः उद्भूतैर्जटाभिः] Sid. Kau.).

rules.title: Instrumental for Cause, Motive, and Purpose
rules.body:
## Instrumental for Cause, Motive, and Purpose

The Instrumental is also used to express the cause or motive or the object of purpose of an action as distinguished from the mere instrument of it; @deva[पुण्येन दृष्टो हरिः] Hari was seen by (virtue of) merit; @deva[तेनाऽपराधेन दण्ड्योऽस्ति] thou art to be punished for that fault; @deva[अध्ययनेन वसति] dwells for the purpose of studying; also when the object to be accomplished is simply implied; @deva[अलं अनेन] away with your efforts i.e. they will not succeed; @deva[श्रमेण सार्थं नास्ति] (Sid. Kau).[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 23 and Sid. Kau. commentary

rules.title: Instrumental: Excelling, Resemblance, Swearing, Rejoicing, Motion, Price
rules.body:
## Instrumental: Excelling, Resemblance, Swearing, Rejoicing, Motion, Price

The Instrumental is used with words expressing the idea of—

(a) excelling; @deva[गुणैः महाभाग तत् गुणैर्वधते] Oh fortunate one, you excel your ancestors in that (devotion); @deva[भरावितेन भारं सहस्रशः] (Mu. 3. 17) he surpasses by his lustre, the lustre of the sun; @deva[दुहितरं संदृश्य रूपेणासयुयुञ्य वनह्नगिः]. (Ś'ak. I.)

(b) resemblance, likeness, equality; @deva[स्वरेण पितरि आदिति] resembles his father in voice; @deva[देदवन्येन स्वरेण च रायच्छदिटरति] (Utta. 4.); @deva[अस्य यं सादृश्यं मातुः मुखेन वादति] his face resembles that of his mother; @deva[विष्णुना पराक्रमो न] equal to Viṣṇu in valour.

(c) swearing; @deva[भरतेनात्मनेन च शपे मूर्धना] I swear by Bharata and myself; @deva[सर्पितव्यं मम जीवितेन] I conjure thee by my life.

(d) rejoicing, being pleased; @deva[भक्त्या गुरो यथामङ्कारेया च प्रीतःऽस्मि] I am pleased with thee by thy devotion to your preceptor and compassion upon me; @deva[काष्ठलुयुः स्वल्येनापि तुष्यति] a low person is satisfied with little.

(e) motion (the conveyance or the part of the body on which a thing is carried being put in the Instrumental case); @deva[रथेन संचरते] 'he moves about in a chariot.'

(f) price (real or metaphorical) at which a thing is bought; @deva[शतेन क्रीतः] bought for a hundred (rupees, etc.), @deva[स्वात्मना अपि आर्तस्य स्नेहेन मित्रस्य हितं रुदितव्यं] 'the life of a friend ought to be saved even at the cost of one's life.'[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 23 and related Vārtikas (Sid. Kau.)

rules.title: Instrumental: Use, Need, Accompaniment, Possession
rules.body:
## Instrumental: Use, Need, Accompaniment, Possession

The following words also govern the Instrumental e.g.:

(a) Words expressing the idea of use or need, such as @deva[किम्], @deva[कार्यं], @deva[अर्थः], @deva[प्रयोजनं] and the like, and the root @deva[कृ] with @deva[किम्] used in the same sense; @deva[येनेन किं यः] &c. what is the use of his wealth who &c.; @deva[दुष्यच् कार्यं भदतोऽयरणय]— 'even the rich sometimes stand in need of Grass;' similarly @deva[कापः पचनं यानेन यो न विहाय यात्मकापः न स्वतिवियरनां यगु किंयनत ङणोष्यलं], &c.

(b) The particles @deva[अलं] and @deva[लं] meaning 'enough,' @deva[अलं रितिते] 'enough of your weeping (do not weep):' @deva[लं अत्येदेरेण] 'away with overpressing'; @deva[अलं] is also used with a gerund @deva[अलं अन्यथा संगतनुते] 'away with misunderstanding.'

(c) Particles expressing 'accompaniment' such as @deva[समं], @deva[सार्धं], @deva[सर्मं], @deva[सह], &c.; @deva[आस्स साकं मया बोणे] (Bh. VIII. 70.); @deva[वनं मया सर्विक्तति पुन्त्यः] (Rag. XIV. 63); @deva[आगतो नित्यस्यते सर्मं हरिष्णोगतांभुः]. (Ś'ak. I. 27) &c.

(d) Words meaning 'having or destitute of,' @deva[समेतकोऽययः] (@deva[परित्यक्तदङ यास्तनं हययण]) 'though possessed of wealth,' &c.; @deva[अर्थेन हीनः] 'destitute of wealth.'

N.B. For the optional use of the Instrumental see the Abl., the Gen. and the Loc. cases.

## THE DATIVE CASE

rules.title: Dative Case: Sampradāna (Indirect Object)
rules.body:
## Dative Case: Sampradāna (Indirect Object)

The primary sense of the Dative case is Sampradāna (@deva[संप्रदानं]). The indirect object of the root @deva[दा] is called Sampradāna; also the person or thing with reference to whom or which an action is done; @deva[हस्तं वरयति हरिं देवः] Give water to a Brāhmaṇa; @deva[शत्रवं संगाते] 'prepares for battle;' @deva[न ब्राह्मणं भर्तो दाटुति] 'The Śudra should not be instructed in the Veda, &c.'[^1]

Note: But in the case of the root @deva[यच्] the proper object is put in the Instrumental case and the indirect object in the Accusative; @deva[यड्णे रुद्रं यजते] 'he sacrifices a bull to Rudra.'

Note:—Though the root @deva[दा] ought to govern the Dat. of the indirect object, it is sometimes found used with the Gen. or the Loc. @deva[यस्य त्यत्रनों दवने वै वदरङयाट् सर्वकैचरु] 'Oh sky-wanderer, we will give rain at the prosperous kingdom of the Śibis;' @deva[मस्यवं रामं मधिविरी दाद्यारिकतुति] 'thou who art thinking of bestowing the earth upon Rāma,' &c.

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 13, I. 4. 32 and Vārtikas

rules.title: Dative with रुच् and Roots of Pleasing
rules.body:
## Dative with @deva[रुच्] and Roots of Pleasing

The roots @deva[रुच्] and others having the same sense govern the Dative of the person or thing pleased or satisfied; @deva[हरै रोचते कृष्णः] Kṛṣṇa likes devotion; @deva[अस्मै न स्पृहः न सतिस्पृहः स्यंगः गुणितः सदते तुषयरु] 'a stream of sweet water, cool and perfumed, is not liked by one who has already drunk enough of water.'[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 33

rules.title: Dative with स्तुष्, गुह्, स्था, मा
rules.body:
## Dative with @deva[स्तुष्], @deva[गुह्], @deva[स्था], @deva[मा]

The roots @deva[स्तुष्] 'to praise,' @deva[गुह्] 'to hide,' @deva[स्था] 'to stand,' and @deva[मा] 'to swear,' govern the Dative of the person to whom some object or feeling is to be conveyed, @deva[गोर्नों स्यसुयद् कृष्णं श्रुयरुते-नूनं-कृष्णं-स्तरीयु] 'a cowherd; else Kṛṣṇa instilled courage into him or apparently conceals her feeling from him or waits for him or swears before him;' (Vide Bhaṭṭi. VII. 73. 74,); but @deva[रानानं स्तुयते मन्त्रो] 'a minister praises his king.'[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 34

rules.title: Dative with ऋण् (Debt) and स्पृह् (Desire)
rules.body:
## Dative with @deva[ऋण्] (Debt) and @deva[स्पृह्] (Desire)

The creditor (or the person to whom something is due) in the case of the root @deva[ऋण्] 'to owe;' and the person or the thing desired in the case of @deva[स्पृह्], are put in the Dative case; @deva[दुययसंचनं तं अर्पयदि मे] 'you owe me two sprinklings of trees' (Ś'ak.); @deva[शकत्युयु अर्पयति कोयं हरिः] (Sid. Kau.) @deva[तस्यं स्पृहयमाणाती] 'he is longing for her (Bhaṭṭi VIII. 15.);' @deva[पुयसे स्पृहः सदयति] 'he longs for trees;' but @deva[यरुययगुम् स्पृहयति] where no longing is implied.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 35-36

rules.title: Dative with कुप्, द्विष्, ईर्ष्, असूय (Anger, Hatred, Jealousy)
rules.body:
## Dative with @deva[कुप्], @deva[द्विष्], @deva[ईर्ष्], @deva[असूय] (Anger, Hatred, Jealousy)

The roots @deva[कुप्], @deva[द्विष्], @deva[ईर्ष्], and @deva[असूय], and others having the same sense govern the Dative of the person against whom the feeling of anger, hatred, &c., is directed; @deva[द्रुयरे कुयस्यति द्विड्टिङ हययतिश्यदरतु वा] (Sid. Kau.) 'he is angry with Hari, or bears hatred towards him, or is jealous of him or finds fault with him;' @deva[रातोयु मोङक्तुयस्युययरुयत] (Bhaṭṭi. VIII. 75.) 'he did neither get angry with Śibā nor find fault with her;' but @deva[भार्यम् ईर्चति] 'he keeps a jealous watch over his wife' (that others may not see her @deva[प्रेमयर्तीः असूयर्त्योऽधेति] Sid. Kau.)

(a) But @deva[कुप्] and @deva[द्विष्] preceded by a preposition govern the Accusative case; @deva[किं मां सकुययसि] 'why do you get angry with me?' @deva[निरुययस्युत्छुटुरीसर्नवितरुयुङ वनते] (Mud. I.) 'he always endeavours to do harm to my body.'

Obs:— @deva[द्विष्] with @deva[अभि] is also found used with the Dat.; @deva[मया स्युम्युदुवड्स्योययवरुयरुर्नों] (Rag. XII. 52.)

rules.title: Dative with भूष् and प्रच्छ् (Fortune Inquiry)
rules.body:
## Dative with @deva[भूष्] and @deva[प्रच्छ्] (Fortune Inquiry)

The roots @deva[भूष्] and @deva[प्रच्छ्] both meaning 'to determine the good or bad fortune of,' govern the Dative of the person with reference to whom the inquiry is made; @deva[कुलाय राष्यति भषते वा । पृच्छो गोपः] (Sid. Kau.)[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 38 and Sid. Kau. commentary

rules.title: Dative with छंद् (Promise)
rules.body:
## Dative with @deva[छंद्] (Promise)

@deva[छंद्] with @deva[प्रति] and @deva[आ] meaning 'to promise,' governs the Dative of the person to whom a promise is made after solicitation @deva[विप्राय गां प्रतिजानोति आप्यानोति वा] (Sid. Kau.)[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 39

rules.title: Dative/Instrumental with परिक्री (Hire)
rules.body:
## Dative/Instrumental with @deva[परिक्री] (Hire)

The root @deva[क्री] with @deva[परि] 'to hire, as a servant,' &c., optionally governs the Dative (and optionally the Inst.) of the price at which he is hired @deva[शतेन शताय वा परिक्रीतः] (Sid. Kau.)[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 44

rules.title: Dative for Purpose, Result, Evil Portent, Benefit
rules.body:
## Dative for Purpose, Result, Evil Portent, Benefit

(a) A noun expressive of the purpose for which anything is done, or the result to which anything pertains, or action for which anything exists, is put in the Dative case; @deva[मुक्तायै हरिं भजति] 'worships Hari for final beatitude;' @deva[भक्तिमार्गाय करणं ज्ञानाय जायते] 'devotion leads to knowledge;' @deva[सुधा करणं जायतं सन्युबनं] (Mb.) 'water gruel tends to (produce) fire,' @deva[सुवर्णाय विरूपण हिरण्यं] (Mah. Bhā.) 'gold for Kuṇḍala (a kind of ornament);' @deva[स्तम्भाय दारुः] 'wood for a sacrificial post,' &c.

N.B. The roots @deva[भू] or @deva[अस्] are often omitted after a Dative used in this sense @deva[काव्यं यशसे] (@deva[भवति]), 'poetry is for fame.'

(b) An evil foreboded by a portentous phenomenon is also put in the Dative case; @deva[वायवे कपिला विद्युत्] 'the tawny lightning forebodes a storm.'

(c) The word @deva[हितं] is used with the Dative; @deva[ब्राह्मणाय हितं] 'good for a Brāhmaṇa.'[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 40, II. 3. 14-15 and Vārtikas

rules.title: Dative with Implied Infinitive
rules.body:
## Dative with Implied Infinitive

The object governed by an infinitive mood not actually used but implied, is put in the Dative; @deva[फलाय याति] i.e. (@deva[फलं हर्तुं]) 'goes for (in order to bring) fruits;' @deva[नृसिंहाय प्रणामः] (i.e. @deva[आराधयितुम्]) 'We bow down to Nṛsiṁha (to propitiate him)'

(a) The Dative of an abstract noun formed from a root may be used to express the sense of the Infinitive of the same root; @deva[यज्ञाय याति] 'goes to perform a sacrifice;' @deva[त्यागाय संचायर्णों] (Rag. I. 7.) 'who had amassed wealth in order to give it away,' &c.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 14-15

rules.title: Dative with नमः, स्वाहा, स्वधा, अलं, वषट्
rules.body:
## Dative with @deva[नमः], @deva[स्वाहा], @deva[स्वधा], @deva[अलं], @deva[वषट्]

The particles @deva[नमः], @deva[स्वाहा], @deva[स्वधा], and @deva[स्वस्ति] (exclamations used in offering oblations to gods and manes respectively), @deva[अलं] meaning 'equal to, a match for' and @deva[वषट्] (an exclamation accompanying an oblation to a deity) govern the Dative case; @deva[तस्मै नमः संभवे] 'bow to that Śambhu;' @deva[प्रजाभ्यः स्वाहा] 'may it be well with the subjects,' @deva[स्वस्ति] (Rag. V. 17.) 'a farewell to thee;' @deva[अग्नये स्वाहा] 'this offering to Agni,' similarly @deva[पितृभ्यः स्वधा]; @deva[देवेभ्यो हरिं अलं] 'Hari is a match for the demons;' so @deva[अलं मल्लाय मल्लः] (Mah. Bhā.) 'one wrestler is a match for another; (see Bhaṭ. II. 39, Bhaṭṭi. VIII. 98.) @deva[इन्द्राय वषट्] 'this oblation to Indra.'

(a) But when @deva[कृ] is used with @deva[नमः], it becomes the principal verb and therefore governs the Accusative case; @deva[नमस्करोति देवान्] 'bows down to gods' (when the sense of an infinitive is suppressed, of course the Dative will be used; see @ref[828]).

(b) Words having the sense of @deva[अर्थं], such as @deva[समर्थं], @deva[शक्त], &c. and also the verb @deva[अर्ह], are used with the Dative (Sid. Kau.) @deva[देवेभ्यो हरिं समर्थः शक्तो वा]; The Dative is sometimes used instead of the Genitive; @deva[विश्वामित्राय योगम्] (Kum. II. 3.) 'having devotion to the feet of that ascetic.'[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 16 and related Vārtikas

rules.title: Dative/Genitive with मन् (Think, Esteem)
rules.body:
## Dative/Genitive with @deva[मन्] (Think, Esteem)

The indirect object of the root @deva[मन्] i.e. 'to think' or 'to esteem' (the Dative or even the Gen. may be used in this sense); one says @deva[पुत्राय पुत्रस्य वा मन्यते] one considers him a son.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 17

rules.title: Dative/Accusative with मन् Showing Contempt (Non-Animals)
rules.body:
## Dative/Accusative with @deva[मन्] Showing Contempt (Non-Animals)

The indirect object of the root @deva[मन्] cl. 4 'to think' if not an animal, may be put in the Accusative or the Dative case when contempt is to be shown; @deva[न त्वां तृणं मन्ये तृणाय वा] I do not consider thee a straw; but @deva[न त्वां तृणं मन्वे] (@deva[मन्] cl. 8) when mere comparison is meant, the Accusative is used; @deva[त्वां तृणं मन्ये] (Mb.).[^1]

---

[^1]: @deva[मन्यकर्मण्यनादरे विभाषाऽप्राणिषु] । Pāṇ. II. 3. 17. On @deva[अप्राणिषु] Kātyāyana remarks '@deva[अप्राणिषु इत्यपनीय नौकाकान्नशुकशृगालवत्र्येष्विति वाच्यम्]' i. e. "Instead of 'If not an animal' it should be said, 'If not one of a ship, or food or a crow or a parrot or a jackal'," @deva[न त्वां मन्ये नावं अन्नं वा]; @deva[न त्वां शुने श्वानं वा मन्ये]; in the former case though neither @deva[नौ] nor @deva[अन्न] is an animal, the Accusative ought to be used, in the latter though @deva[श्वन्] is an animal the Dative may be optionally used.

rules.title: Accusative/Dative with Motion Verbs (Actual Motion)
rules.body:
## Accusative/Dative with Motion Verbs (Actual Motion)

The object of roots implying motion (i.e. the place to which the motion is directed), if it be not a road, is put in the Accusative or the Dative, when actual motion is meant; @deva[ग्रामं ग्रामाय वा गच्छति] 'goes to a village;' but @deva[मनसा हरिं भजति], @deva[पुरुस्त्रीं गच्छति].[^1]

## THE ABLATIVE CASE

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 12

rules.title: Ablative Case: Motion Away From (अपादान)
rules.body:
## Ablative Case: Motion Away From (@deva[अपादान])

The principal sense of the Ablative case is @deva[अपादान] or 'motion away from';[^1] hence the noun from which the motion, real or conceived, takes place is put in the Ablative case; @deva[ग्रामादायाति] 'comes from a village;' @deva[धावतोऽश्वात्पतति] 'falls down from a running horse'; @deva[सदाचारात् भ्रंशते].

**(a)** Words having the sense of @deva[जुगुप्सा], @deva[विराम] or 'cessation,' 'pause,' and @deva[प्रमाद] 'swerving from,' also govern the Ablative case;[^2] @deva[पापात् जुगुप्सते] 'he hates sin;' @deva[न नवः प्रभुराफलोदयात्स्थिरकर्मा विरराम कर्मणः] (Rag. VIII. 22) 'the new monarch, steady in action, did not desist from efforts until they bore their fruit'; @deva[धर्मात्प्रमाद्यति] 'swerves from duty'; @deva[स्वाधिकारात्प्रमत्तः] (Meg. I.) 'careless, failing in the discharge of the duties (of his office)'; so @deva[धर्मान्मुह्यति]; @deva[प्रसमीक्ष्य निवर्तेत सर्वमांसस्य भक्षणात्] (Manu Smr. V. 49.), &c.

@deva[मद्] with @deva[प्र] in the sense of 'to be careless about' is used with the Loc. also; @deva[अतोऽर्थान्न प्रमाद्यन्ति प्रमदासु विपश्चितः] । (Manu Smr. II. 213) on this account wise men are not careless about their wives.

---

[^1]: @deva[अपादाने पञ्चमी] । Pāṇ. II. 3. 28. @deva[ध्रुवमपाये अपादानम्] Pāṇ. I. 4. 24.

[^2]: @deva[जुगुप्साविरामप्रमादार्थानामुपसंख्यानम्] । Vārt.

rules.title: Ablative with Fear and Protection
rules.body:
## Ablative with Fear and Protection

In the case of words expressing fear or protection from fear, that from which or whom the fear proceeds is put in the Ablative case; @deva[चोरात् भेति] is afraid of a thief; @deva[भीता रणे न त्रायते] is not afraid of the white-horned one i.e. Arjuna; @deva[सदास्यस्यरु यरोयु वापनं महत्तो यभायु] (Bhag. II. 40) even a little of this (kind of) piety saves one from great fear; @deva[कपेरच्छिष्यनुवात्] (Bhaṭṭi IX. 11.) were afraid of the roar of the monkey.

(a) That from which one is kept off is also put in the Ablative; @deva[पापात् विवारयति] wards off from sin; @deva[यवरुथात् गां वारयति] keeps off the cow from barley.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 25

rules.title: Ablative with परि+जि (Disgust)
rules.body:
## Ablative with @deva[परा]+@deva[जि] (Disgust)

In the case of @deva[जि] with @deva[परा] the thing unbearable is put in the Ablative case; @deva[अध्ययनात्पराजयते] finds study unbearable or difficult; @deva[तां पराजयमानां स प्रीतेः] (Bhaṭṭi. VIII. 71.) who got disgusted with the love (of Rāvaṇa); but @deva[शत्रून् पराजयते] ।[^1]

---

[^1]: @deva[पराजेरसोढः] । Pāṇ. I. 4. 26.

rules.title: Ablative with Concealment
rules.body:
## Ablative with Concealment

When concealment is to be had recourse to, that whose sight one desires to avoid is put in the Ablative case; @deva[मातुः निहितः कृष्णः] 'Kṛṣṇa conceals himself from his mother.'[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 28

rules.title: Ablative with Learning and Origin
rules.body:
## Ablative with Learning and Origin

(a) The teacher from whom something is learnt regularly is put in the Ablative case; @deva[आचार्यात् अधीते] learns from the preceptor; but @deva[नटस्य गातां युनोति].

(b) Similarly the prime or original cause in the case of @deva[जन्] 'to be born,' and the source in the case of @deva[प्र+भू] are put in the Ablative; @deva[ब्रह्मणः जनः भजन्ते] the creation proceeds from Brahman; @deva[गोमयात् जायते] the devotion is born from cowdung; @deva[हिमवतः गङ्गा प्रभवति] the Gaṅgā rises from the Himālayas; @deva[असूयायात् भिन्नयते] from desire anger is produced.

Note:—Verbs meaning 'to be born' or 'to be begotten upon' are often used with the Loc.; @deva[तस्यां शतानन्दः अजायत] from her was born Śatānanda; @deva[नैनकायां आविजात] begotten upon Menakā, &c.; Manu Smr. IX. 1. 9.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 29-31

rules.title: Ablative for Distance in Space
rules.body:
## Ablative for Distance in Space

When the sense of an indeclinable participle is suppressed, it is a source of wonder; the distance in space being put in the Ablative case in the sense of 'after,' @deva[द्वारात् पश्यति] sees from the door, @deva[गोदावर्यात् गङ्गाम् द्वारं निष्ठा] (Sid. Kau.)[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 28

rules.title: Ablative for Distance in Time and Space
rules.body:
## Ablative for Distance in Time and Space

(a) The place or time from which the distance of another place or point of time is to be expressed is put in the Ablative case; the distance in space being put in the Nominative or the Locative and that in time in the Locative; @deva[वनात् ग्रामो योजनं योजने वा] (Sid. Kau.) the village is a yojana from the forest; @deva[नवग्रन्थात् सांकाश्यं द्वादशे योजनानि चतुर्षु योजनेषु वा] (Mb.).

(b) The Ablative is also used in 'portion and subtraction.'[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 29 (Note: This rule was lost in Phase 2 AI cleaning and extracted directly from Phase 1 OCR)

rules.title: Ablative with अन्य, पर and Direction Words
rules.body:
## Ablative with @deva[अन्य], @deva[इतर] and Direction Words

The words @deva[अन्य], @deva[इतर] and others having a similar sense, the particles @deva[आरात्] 'near or distant,' @deva[ऋते] 'without,' words expressive of direction used with reference to time or space (except when they refer to the limbs of the body) and those derived from the root @deva[अञ्च्] at the end of compounds, and indeclinables ending in @deva[ओ] and @deva[आहि] are constructed with the Ablative; @deva[अन्यो भिन्न इतरो वा कृष्णात्] different from Krishna; @deva[इतरो रावणादेष राघवानुचरो यदि] Bhaṭṭi. VII. 106. If he be one other than Rāvaṇa and a follower of Rāma; @deva[आराद्वनात्] near or away from the forest; @deva[ऋते क्रौर्यात्समायातः] (Bhaṭṭi VII. 105) come without (setting aside) his cruelty; @deva[ग्रामात्पूर्वा उत्तरो वा] to the east or the north of the village; @deva[चैत्रात्पूर्वः फाल्गुनः] the month of Fālguna is prior to that of Chaitra; but @deva[पूर्वं कायस्य] the (forepart) of the body; @deva[प्राक् प्रत्यग् वा ग्रामात्] to the east or to the west of the village; @deva[प्राक्प्रभातात्] (Bhaṭṭi. VII. 106) before the day dawned; @deva[दक्षिणा दक्षिणाहि वा ग्रामात्] to the south or in the southern direction of the village; @deva[उत्तरा समुद्रात्] (Bhaṭṭi) in the north of the sea.[^1]

**Obs.:**—@deva[ऋते] is sometimes used with the Accusative, @deva[ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वे] (Bhag. XI. 32) even without thee all will die.

**(a)** Words like @deva[प्रभृति], @deva[आरभ्य], @deva[बहिः], @deva[अनन्तरं], @deva[ऊर्ध्वं], @deva[परं] &c. are used with the Ablative; the first word may also be used with adverbs of time; @deva[तस्मादिनात्प्रभृति] from that day; @deva[ततः-तदा-प्रभृति] since then; @deva[अद्यप्रभृत्यवनताङ्गि तवास्मि दासः] (Kum. V. 86), @deva[ततः], @deva[तस्मात्], @deva[दिनादारभ्य], @deva[मालत्याः प्रथमावलोकदिवसादारभ्य]; @deva[ग्रामाद्बहिः] outside the village; @deva[पुरगारुत्मतगोपुराद्बहिः] (@deva[निरगात्]) went out of the emerald gate of the town; @deva[ऊर्ध्वं संवत्सरात्] (M. S. IX. 77) after a year; @deva[अत ऊर्ध्वं] hence forward; @deva[वर्त्मनः परं] (Rag. I. 17) beyond the path; @deva[भाग्यायत्तमतः परं]; @deva[पुराणपत्रापगमादनन्तरं] (Rag. III. 70.) after the dropping of old leaves; see Bhag. XII. 12.

---

[^1]: @deva[अन्यारादितरर्तेदिक्शब्दाञ्चूत्तरपदाजाहियुक्ते] Pāṇ. II. 3. 29.

rules.title: Ablative with अप, परि, आ, प्रति
rules.body:
## Ablative with @deva[अप], @deva[परि], @deva[आ], @deva[प्रति]

The ablative is used with—

**(a)** The prepositions @deva[अप] and @deva[परि] meaning 'away from, without' and @deva[आ] meaning 'as far as' or 'including, comprehending'; @deva[यत्संप्रत्यप लोकेभ्यो लंकायां वसतिर्भयात्] (Rām.) now that he dwelt in Laṅkā, in terror, away from the worlds; @deva[अप हरेः संसारः] Saṃsāra exists outside Hari; @deva[अप त्रिगर्तेभ्यो वृष्टो देवः] it rained everywhere, except in the country of Trigarta. Similarly @deva[परि हरेः संसारः]; @deva[परि त्रिगर्तेभ्यो वृष्टो देवः] (Vop.) &c. @deva[आमुक्ते संसार], @deva[आसकलाद् ब्रह्म] Brahman pervades every thing; @deva[आ परितोषाद् विदुषां] until the learned are satisfied.

**(b)** @deva[प्रति] meaning 'the representative of, in exchange for or giving in return for;' @deva[प्रद्युम्नः कृष्णात्प्रति] (Sid. Kau.) Pradyumna is the representative of Krishna, @deva[तिलेभ्यः प्रतियच्छति माषान्] gives māshas in return for sesamum.[^1]

---

[^1]: @deva[अपपरी वर्जने] । @deva[आङ्मर्यादावचने] । Pāṇ. I. 4. 88-89. @deva[पञ्चम्यपाङ्परिभिः] Pāṇ. II. 3. 10. @deva[प्रतिः प्रतिनिधिप्रतिदानयोः] । Pāṇ. I. 4. 92. @deva[प्रतिनिधिप्रतिदाने च यस्मात्] । Pāṇ. II. 3. 11.

rules.title: Ablative with Debt as Cause
rules.body:
## Ablative with Debt as Cause

When a word expressive of 'a debt,' is merely intended to be stated as a cause, it is put in the Ablative case; @deva[शतात् ऋणात्] a thing mortgaged for a hundred rupees, @deva[ऋणात् बद्धः] tied down as it were by the debt he owes.

rules.title: Ablative for Cause, Argument, Comparison
rules.body:
## Ablative for Cause, Argument, Comparison

(a) The Ablative often denotes the cause of an action or condition and may be translated by 'on account of, by reason of,' &c.; @deva[मौनात् पंडितः गणयते] one is considered a fool by reason of his silence (if he keeps silence); @deva[गोमानुप्रयणः] (H.) on account of my killing cows and men.

(b) The Ablative is used to make a causative assertion or to advance an argument; @deva[धूमात् अग्निः] The mountain is fiery (has fire on it); because there is smoke.

(c) The Ablative is used with comparatives or words having a comparative sense; @deva[भक्तेर्मार्गात् ज्ञानमार्गः श्रेयः] the way of knowledge is more efficient than that of devotion; @deva[अणुतरातुयुच्युचरु] smaller than an atom; @deva[सत्यात् उत्तरिच्यनं] truth alone is superior to a thousand horse-sacrifices.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 4. 25

rules.title: पृथक्, विना, नाना with Ablative/Accusative/Instrumental
rules.body:
## @deva[पृथक्], @deva[विना], @deva[नाना] with Ablative/Accusative/Instrumental

The indeclinables @deva[पृथक्], @deva[विना] and @deva[नाना] govern the Ablative, the Accusative and the Instrumental cases; @deva[पृथक् रामात्-रामं-रामेण वा] different from or without Rāma; so @deva[नाना रामं] &c. @deva[नाना नारीं निष्फला लोकयात्रा] (Vop.) worldly life is vain without a woman (wife).[^1]

---

[^1]: @deva[पृथग्विनानानाभिस्तृतीयान्यतरस्याम्] । Pāṇ. II. 3. 32.

rules.title: Ablative/Accusative with स्तोक, अल्प, कष्ट, कतिपय
rules.body:
## Ablative/Instrumental with @deva[स्तोक], @deva[अल्प], @deva[कृच्छ्र], @deva[कतिपय]

The words @deva[स्तोक] 'a little,' @deva[अल्प] 'a little,' @deva[कृच्छ्र] 'difficulty,' and @deva[कतिपय] 'some' when used in an adverbial sense with verbs, are used in the Ablative or the Instrumental; @deva[स्तोकेन स्तोकाद्वा मुक्तः] let off with little; similarly @deva[अल्पेन अल्पान्मुक्तः], @deva[कृच्छ्रेण कृच्छ्राद्वा कृतं] done with difficulty; @deva[कतिपयेन कतिपयाद्वा प्राप्तं], but @deva[स्तोकेन विषेण हतः] killed with a little poison; when used adverbially they take the Accusative also; @deva[स्तोकं गच्छति] goes a little.

**(a)** @deva[दूर] and @deva[अन्तिक] and others having the same sense, are used in the Ablative, the Accusative and the Instrumental cases; @deva[ग्रामस्य दूरात् दूरं दूरेण वा] away from the village; so @deva[अन्तिकात् अन्तिकं अन्तिकेन वा] near the village.[^1]

---

[^1]: @deva[करणे च स्तोकाल्पकृच्छ्रकतिपयस्यासत्त्ववचनस्य] । @deva[दूरान्तिकार्थेभ्यो द्वितीया च] । Pāṇ. II. 3. 33, 35.

rules.title: Genitive Case Introduction and Relation (संबन्ध)
rules.body:
## Genitive Case Introduction and Relation (@deva[संबन्ध])

(n) The words @deva[दूर] and @deva[अन्तिक] and others having the same sense, are used in the Ablative, the Accusative and the Instrumental cases; @deva[ग्रामस्य दूरात् दूरं दूरेण वा] away from the village; so @deva[अन्तिकात् अन्तिकं अन्तिकेन वा] near the village.

## THE GENITIVE CASE

The Genitive, as already remarked, is not a Kāraka case. It, therefore, expresses simply the relation of one noun to another in a sentence, such as that of a servant and his master (a relation which is other than that expressed by a Kāraka case); @deva[राज्ञः पुरुषः], @deva[पुत्रस्य माता], @deva[द्रव्यस्य गुणः] &c.; and even in those cases where the genitive is used in the sense of other cases it expresses simple relation or @deva[सम्बन्ध] only, as in @deva[सतां गतम्]; @deva[सर्पिषो जानीते]; @deva[मातुः स्मरति]; @deva[एधः उदकस्य उपस्कुरुते]; @deva[भजे शंभोश्चरणयोः]; @deva[फलानां तृप्तः], &c.

rules.title: Genitive with हेतु (Purpose, Cause)
rules.body:
## Genitive with @deva[हेतु] (Purpose, Cause)

When the word @deva[हेतु] (cause, object) is used in a sentence, that which is the object and the word @deva[हेतु] are put in the Genitive case; @deva[अन्नस्य हेतोर्वसति] dwells for the sake of (with the object of getting) food; @deva[रोदिषि कस्य हेतोः] Mark. P. 23. 12. @deva[हेतोर्बोधस्य मैथिल्याः प्रास्तावीद्रामसंकथाम्] (Bhaṭṭi. VIII. 103.) he began to give her an account of Rāma in order to show her that he (Hanumat) was Rāma's messenger.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 27, 50

rules.title: Genitive/Locative with Direction Words
rules.body:
## Genitive/Locative with Direction Words

Words showing distance and direction are used with the Genitive; @deva[देवदत्तस्य उत्तरं] in the north or to the north of Devadatta; these are sometimes used in the Locative also. The town Pāṭaliputra is to the north or near the town of Bihār. [OCR quality severely degraded in this rule][^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 51

rules.title: Genitive/Ablative with दूर, निकट and Synonyms
rules.body:
## Genitive/Ablative with @deva[दूर], @deva[निकट] and Synonyms

The words @deva[दूर] and @deva[अन्तिक] and their synonyms govern either the Genitive or the Ablative; @deva[ग्रामात् ग्रामस्य वा वनं दूरं—निकटं—समीपं वा] the forest is distant from or near the village. @deva[रामाद्रुद्रस्य यो दूरं पापाद्युष्मत्स्य सोऽन्तिकं] he who is away from Rāma or Śiva is near sin. @deva[प्रत्यासन्नो माधवीमण्डपस्य] close to the bower of the Mādhavī creeper; @deva[तस्य सकाशं], &c.[^1]

---

[^1]: Vārtikas (Sid. Kau.)

rules.title: Genitive with Verbs of Incorrect Knowledge, Memory, Control, Compassion
rules.body:
## Genitive with Verbs of Incorrect Knowledge, Memory, Control, Compassion

The root @deva[ज्ञा] meaning 'to have an incorrect knowledge of' governs the Genitive; @deva[तेलं सर्पिषः जानीते] supposed oil to be ghee; but @deva[सर्पिः जानोति].

(a) Verbs implying 'to think of, to remember,' such as @deva[स्मृ], @deva[ईश्] with @deva[अधि], 'to be master of,' and 'to have compassion upon' such as @deva[दया], &c., govern the Genitive as to the object; @deva[वाणीपतेः स्मरति] (Meg. 50) dost thou remember the lord? @deva[रामस्य दयमानः] (Bhaṭṭi. VIII. 119) taking pity on Rāma.

(b) @deva[कृ] meaning 'to impart additional properties' governs the Genitive; @deva[काष्ठं स्वरूपस्य भोः] 'fuel imparts heat to water.'

rules.title: Genitive with Verbs of Affliction (Disease)
rules.body:
## Genitive with Verbs of Affliction (Disease)

Verbs meaning 'to be afflicted with a disease' govern the Genitive of their object when used impersonally or when they have for their subject names of diseases; @deva[चोरस्य ज्वरेण रुज्यते] the thief is afflicted with the pain of fever; @deva[दुःखस्य रुज्यते] coryza; bilious pain on the man; except when @deva[ज्वर] and @deva[संताप] are used as subjects; (vide Bhaṭṭi. VIII. 120;) @deva[तं रुजति ज्वरः] or @deva[संतापः] fever or affliction pains him.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 54

rules.title: Genitive with नाथृ (to wish) in Benedictions
rules.body:
## Genitive with @deva[नाथृ] (to wish) in Benedictions

@deva[नाथृ] meaning 'to wish' governs the Genitive when the idea of a benediction is implied; @deva[धृत्या नाथस्व] wish to have patience; @deva[धनस्य नाथते] desires to have wealth. So @deva[सर्पिषः नाथनम्].[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 55

rules.title: Genitive with Verbs Meaning 'to Kill, Punish'
rules.body:
## Genitive with Verbs Meaning 'to Kill, Punish'

The roots @deva[वध्], @deva[हन्] with @deva[नि] or @deva[वि] or with both, @deva[विध्], @deva[विच्छ्] and @deva[विवु] all mean 'to kill'; @deva[विध्] with @deva[वि] or @deva[निच्छ्] with both punish, &c; @deva[चोरस्य दण्डयति राजा] a king punishes a thief; @deva[निजबलैर्जगत्रिपूनां] (Siṣ. I. 27.) to kill the enemies of the world (the demons) by his own power; @deva[अन्तर्मन्युस्य निहन्तुः] kill (drive away) your anger; @deva[राक्षसस्य निहन्ति] or @deva[विहन्ति] or @deva[वधति] or @deva[विहनिवधति रामः] Rāma will kill the Rākṣasas; @deva[वृषलस्य व्यायति व्यायति] does injury to a Vṛṣala; @deva[साहासिकस्य निष्टं गन्धः] &c.; in other senses they govern the Accusative; @deva[धान्यं निघृष्टे] he grinds fried rice.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 56

rules.title: Genitive with Verbs of Business/Gambling
rules.body:
## Genitive with Verbs of Business/Gambling

The roots @deva[व्यवह्] (i. e. @deva[वह्] with @deva[नि] and @deva[अत्]), @deva[व्यय] and @deva[वि] when they all mean to transact business, or to stake in gambling, govern the Genitive of their object; @deva[शतस्य व्यवहरति] invests a hundred rupees in business; @deva[गोभिर्व्ययन्ति] he staked his life; @deva[अदेवीत् भ्रातृभिः] lost his brothers and pleasures in gambling, &c.; but when @deva[वि] is preceded by a preposition, the Accusative may also be used; @deva[शतस्य शतं वा प्रतिदशति] (Sid. Kau.)[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 57–59

rules.title: Genitive with Words Denoting Frequency of Time
rules.body:
## Genitive with Words Denoting Frequency of Time

Words having the senses of @deva[छन्दः] i. e. denoting frequency of time, such as @deva[द्विः], @deva[त्रिः], @deva[पुनः], &c. govern the Genitive of the time in the sense of the Locative; @deva[पञ्चकृत्वः भोजनम्] taking food five times a day; @deva[द्विरहो शतकम्], &c.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 64

rules.title: Genitive Subjective and Objective with Kṛidantas
rules.body:
## Genitive Subjective and Objective with Kṛidantas

The Genitive is used subjectively and objectively with Kṛidantas or Primary Nominal Bases derived by means of the Kṛit affixes (i. e. is used in the sense of the subject or the object of the action denoted by the Kṛidantas); @deva[कृष्णस्य गतिः] an act of Kṛṣṇa i. e. of which Kṛṣṇa is the agent; @deva[जगतः कर्त्तृ] the Creator of the world, which is the object of the action denoted by the noun @deva[कर्त्तृ]; similarly @deva[सतां पालकः] the protector of the good; @deva[यवस्य वरं] will be the similies of mṛiti; @deva[मद्कवेः किंनुम्] a work of that poet; @deva[सारस्य दुहितरं न भाट्.] (Rāmacharita XII. 117.) This is not a common creation of Brahman.[^1]

(a) In the case of verbs governing two Accusatives the secondary object of the Kṛidanta may be put in the Genitive or in the Accusative; @deva[नैतस्य द्वितीयं दास्यस्य वा] (Sid. Kau.) the taker of the horse to Śrughna.

(b) When the agent and the object of the bases derived by means of Kṛit affixes are used in a sentence, the object is put in the Genitive case and not the agent. @deva[गवां गोपा वैष्णविकरणम्] the milking of cows by one who is not a cowherd is a wonder.

Exceptions.—This rule does not apply to Kṛit nouns ending in the affixes @deva[अनक] and @deva[अ] when feminine; @deva[विश्वस्यस्य भेदिका वा वरस्य जगतः] (Sid. Kau.) the desire of Rudra to split the universe or the splitting of the universe by Rudra. According to some when the Kṛit affix is @deva[घञ्], i. e. of feminine gender, and according to others...[^2]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 65
[^2]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 66

rules.title: Genitive with Past Passive Participles in Present Sense
rules.body:
## Genitive with Past Passive Participles in Present Sense

When past passive participles are used in the sense of the present tense the Genitive is used; @deva[राज्ञः मतो भक्तितः पूजितो वा] respected, known or honored by the king; @deva[यद्वाङो वा सतां मतः रामस्य संमतम्] Bhaṭṭi. VIII. 124.[^1]

(a) Past participles showing the place of an action, as well as those used as abstract nouns are used with the Genitive @deva[अरण्यगतिवक्तदनानं यात्नै रामणेः । अङ्कतिभूतिसैर्यगतानाम्यो विहङ्गः ॥ रस्य युद्धि, कोपिकास्य स्पाहो, नट्यस्य युद्धनम्, छात्रस्य हविनं], &c. (Mb.) See. Bhaṭṭi. VIII. 125.[^2]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 67
[^2]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 68

rules.title: Exceptions: When Genitive is NOT Used
rules.body:
## Exceptions: When Genitive is NOT Used

The Genitive is not used with present participles except that of @deva[द्विष्], verbal derivatives ending in @deva[क्त] and @deva[उक्] except that derived from @deva[कृत्], verbal indeclinables, past participles, passive and active, nouns formed with the affix @deva[तुमुन्] (see p. 456) and with such as mean 'in the habit of, or having the properties of or doing any thing well;' @deva[कर्तुनों कर्तुनं] or @deva[कर्तुः] but @deva[मुरै दैत्यस्य वा हिद्धु हरिः] Hari, the enemy of Mura; @deva[हरै विद्वान्तुः] desirous of seeing Hari; @deva[मुरै अत्याहरिः], @deva[दैत्यानां हातको हरिः] Hari is the killer of demons; @deva[कृत्युः करणीयम्]; @deva[अविद्यस्य युधै तुम् युङ्गु न पश्यु द्यु दैत्यानां]; @deva[दैत्यानां हवनकः हकन्तुः प्रयच्छो हरेण] worldly life goes astray with Hari; @deva[आत्मनान् अङ्कतृवरीष्णुः] in habit of decorating oneself; @deva[अर्थं विद्वान्] a habitual beggar; @deva[कर्तुनो कटं] one who prepares a mat; @deva[फलै पुननम्] 'killing the fruit' means the fruit by terminations @deva[अक्] showing futurity and @deva[हन्] showing necessary payment; @deva[हरिरै वन्दको यात्यति] he goes desiring to see Hari; @deva[शतं दार्णों] one who has to pay a hundred (rupees.).[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 69–70

rules.title: Genitive/Instrumental with Potential Passive Participles
rules.body:
## Genitive/Instrumental with Potential Passive Participles

In the case of Potential passive participles the agent of the action is put in the Genitive or in the Instrumental case; @deva[मया मम वा सेव्यो हरिः] Hari ought to be served by me; @deva[राक्षसानाम्यस्य नगरम् त्रातृः] (Bhaṭṭi VIII. 125) the forest together with the lord of the demons ought to preserve must be destroyed by me; @deva[गन्तव्या ते वसतिरलका हे.] (Meg.) Thou should go to Alakā.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 71

rules.title: Genitive with Words of Equality/Likeness
rules.body:
## Genitive with Words of Equality/Likeness

In the case of words denoting equality or likeness, such as @deva[तुल्य], @deva[सदृश], &c., the person or thing with whom or which any object is compared is put in the Genitive case, except in the case of @deva[तुल्य] there is no compulsion; @deva[कृष्णस्य कृष्णस्य वा] equal to or like Kṛṣṇa; @deva[कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मम] who else is equal to me? but @deva[छायास्य तुल्यो उपमा वा नारिंगु] (Sid. Kau.)[^1]

Obs.—The words @deva[तुल्य] and @deva[उपमा], however, are found used by good authors with the Instrumental against Pāṇini's rule; @deva[तुल्यो वर्षेण वनवासम्] (Kum. V. 34.) which rises to the high position of being equal with your lip; @deva[स्तनाबर्धं अतिरुक्तनं शम्भुना] (Siṣ. I. 4.) clearly deserving to be compared with Śambhu white with ashes; see Rag. VIII. 15.

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 72

rules.title: Genitive/Dative with Benediction Words
rules.body:
## Genitive/Dative with Benediction Words

The words @deva[आयुष्मन्], @deva[मङ्गल], @deva[भङ्ग], @deva[कुशल], @deva[इष्ट], @deva[अयः] and @deva[हित] and words having the same sense, when used in a sentence containing a benediction, govern the Dative or the Genitive case; @deva[आयुष्मन् चिरञ्जीवितं कृष्णाय कृष्णस्य वा यथाट्] (Sid. Kau.); may Kṛṣṇa live long; similarly @deva[मङ्गल], @deva[भङ्ग], @deva[कुशल], @deva[निरायष्मन्], @deva[इष्ट], @deva[हो], @deva[अयःयोजनम्]. @deva[हित. पुत्रनं वा यथाट्] (Sid. Kau.).[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 73

rules.title: Genitive with Certain Indeclinables
rules.body:
## Genitive with Certain Indeclinables

The Genitive is used with indeclinables like @deva[मध्ये], @deva[परि], @deva[गते], &c.; @deva[गङ्गायाः मध्ये परि वा] in the middle or on the other side of the Ganges; @deva[अर्थः ग्रामस्य गते] for the sake of this life.

rules.title: Genitive with Superlatives; Ablative with Comparatives
rules.body:
## Genitive with Superlatives; Ablative with Comparatives

With superlatives, and words having the sense of the superlative, the Genitive is used; @deva[श्रेष्ठो ब्राह्मणः अद्यः]; @deva[अर्षीणाम्हनस्पत्याम्] (Rag. V. 4) the chief of sages, the authors to the Mantras.

Note:—Words having the sense of comparatives are used with the Ablative and sometimes with the Instrumental; @deva[अस्मात्वलं हरितः] or @deva[अधिकः] this person is superior or inferior to him in strength; similarly @deva[देवदत्तो यशोनात्युङ्गः दीर्घहा वा]; @deva[को धर्म् सततरो भव्या] who will have a happier end than I? The word @deva[सततरै] is used with the Locative as in the Locative or the Instrumental; @deva[धनहीनं नारायणविकानपि सोऽभवत्] he was more (i. e. dearer) to them than their sons; @deva[तेषुमुस्याजनं वार्षः युद्धति द्विमुत्रे क्रमेः] they passed five months and twelve nights more than (those years); @deva[कादचिदुङुअक् युत्रः] A Kadru is larger than a Kūdava.

rules.title: Locative Case: Adhikaraṇa (Place and Time)
rules.body:
## Locative Case: Adhikaraṇa (Place and Time)

## THE LOCATIVE CASE

The place where an action takes place with reference to the subject or object is called Adhikaraṇa (@deva[अधिकरण]) and is put in the Locative case; @deva[स्वापति निशायाम्] (Bham. 1. 60); @deva[भक्तो नन्दनकानने] (Ibid 64); @deva[सत्त्रे ओदनम् पचते] cooks food in a cooking utensil; @deva[कर्णे कथयति] tells (something) into the ear; @deva[यदा इष्टे अपि], &c. The Locative also denotes the time when an action takes place; @deva[तास्माच् विबोध्यमानः कालं दिवसैकः] (Kum. II. 1.) the gods being harassed at that time; @deva[दिवसान्ते निद्रायाम् गन्तृदुङ्] (Rag. II. 15.)[^1]

(a) Verbal derivatives in @deva[हन्] and having the sense of the P. P. participle govern the Locative of their object; @deva[अर्थितिरु]...[^2]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 45; II. 3. 36
[^2]: Vārtikas

rules.title: Locative/Genitive with स्वामी, ईश्वर and Related Words
rules.body:
## Locative/Genitive with @deva[स्वामी], @deva[ईश्वर] and Related Words

The Locative or the Genitive is used with the words @deva[स्वामी] a master, @deva[ईश्वर], @deva[अधिपति] a lord, @deva[दायाद] a heir, @deva[साक्षिन्], @deva[प्रतिभू] a bail, and @deva[प्रसूत] born for; @deva[गवां गोषु वा स्वामी] the master of kine; @deva[पृथिव्याः] or @deva[पृथिव्यां ईश्वरः] the lord of the earth; @deva[ग्रामाणां] or @deva[ग्रामेषु अधिपतिः] the lord of villages, similarly @deva[पित्र्यंशस्य पित्र्यंशे वा दायादः], @deva[व्यवहारे व्यवहारस्य वा साक्षी], @deva[दर्शने दर्शनस्य वा प्रतिभूः] (surety for appearance in a court); @deva[गोषु गवां वा प्रसूतः]. @deva[गोपः] a cowherd is born for cows.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 39

rules.title: Locative/Genitive with आयुक्त and कुशल (appointed/devoted)
rules.body:
## Locative/Genitive with @deva[आयुक्त] and @deva[कुशल] (appointed/devoted)

The words @deva[आयुक्त] and @deva[कुशल] meaning 'appointed or devoted to' are construed with the Locative or the Genitive; @deva[आयुक्तः कुशलो वा हरिपूजने हरिपूजनस्य वा] appointed to worship Hari; @deva[कुशलोऽन्वेषणस्याहमायुक्तो दूतकर्मणि] (Bhaṭṭi. VIII. 115.) In other senses they are construed with the Locative; @deva[आयुक्तो गौः शकटे] a bull harnessed to the yoke of a carriage; @deva[कर्मणि कुशलः] expert in the performance of an act.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 40

rules.title: Locative/Genitive for Distinguishing from a Class
rules.body:
## Locative/Genitive for Distinguishing from a Class

When an object or an individual is to be distinguished from a whole class, the Locative or the Genitive is used; @deva[गवां गवि काला श्रेष्ठः] (see Manu S. I. 96.), @deva[गोषु गवां वा काला वृषभतरः]; @deva[गच्छतां गच्छत्सु वा युवानुनिः छात्राणां छात्रेषु वा भैक्षः युद्] (Sid. Kau.)[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 41

rules.title: Locative with साधु and निपुण (adoration sense)
rules.body:
## Locative with @deva[साधु] and @deva[निपुण] (adoration sense)

The words @deva[साधु] and @deva[निपुण], not preceded by the prepositions @deva[अनु], @deva[परि] and @deva[प्रति], are used with the Loc. when the sense of adoration is to be conveyed; @deva[मातरि साधुर्निपुणो वा] reverentially disposed towards his mother; but @deva[निपुणः राज्ञः भृत्यः] a clever servant of the king. When preceded by the prepositions @deva[अनु], @deva[परि] and @deva[प्रति] these are used with the Accusative; @deva[साधुर्निपुणो वा मातरं प्रति परि अनु वा].[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3, 49

rules.title: Locative/Instrumental with प्रसित and उत्सुक
rules.body:
## Locative/Instrumental with @deva[प्रसित] and @deva[उत्सुक]

With the words @deva[प्रसित] and @deva[उत्सुक], the Locative or the Instrumental is used; @deva[प्रसित उत्सुको वा हरिणा हरौ वा] intent upon Hari; @deva[पत्या प्रस्थितेन पत्यौ प्रस्थिते वा योषिदुत्सुका], a woman gets anxious (or restless) when her husband goes out; @deva[तेजस्विभिरुत्सुकानाम्] Kir. XVI. 7[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 44

rules.title: Locative/Instrumental with Nakshatra Names (Time)
rules.body:
## Locative/Instrumental with Nakshatra Names (Time)

When the names of Nakshatras are used as showing a particular time the Locative or the Instrumental is used; @deva[मूलेनावाहयेद्देवीं श्रवणेन विसर्जयेत्] । @deva[मूले श्रवणे इति वा] । (Sid. Kau.)[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3, 45

rules.title: Ablative/Locative for Interval of Time or Space
rules.body:
## Ablative/Locative for Interval of Time or Space

Words expressive of the interval of time or space are used with the Ablative or the Locative; @deva[अद्य भुक्त्वा द्विकात् द्विके द्वाहात् भोक्ता] having dined to-day he will dine again after two days; @deva[समस्थितम् शुनत द्विकात्] or @deva[द्वयोजनम्] frozen standing here as a river a mark two miles distant.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 5

rules.title: Locative with उप (exceeding) and अधि (master of)
rules.body:
## Locative with @deva[उप] (exceeding) and @deva[अधि] (master of)

The prepositions @deva[उप] in the sense of 'exceeding' and @deva[अधि] in that of 'the master of' govern the Locative; @deva[उपपरार्धे हरेर्गुणाः] the merits of Hari exceed a parārdha; @deva[अधि भुवि रामः] or @deva[अधि रामे भूः] Rāma is the lord of the earth; in other senses these prepositions are used with the Accusative, for which see @ref[805].[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 9

rules.title: दूर and अन्तिक with Locative Also
rules.body:
## @deva[दूर] and @deva[अन्तिक] with Locative Also

The words @deva[दूर] and @deva[अन्तिक] and others having the same sense are used in the Locative also; @deva[ग्रामस्य दूरे—दूरं—दूरेण—दूरात् वा]; @deva[तस्याः समीपे—समीपेन—समीपात् गत्वा].

rules.title: Locative with Verbs of Love and Attachment
rules.body:
## Locative with Verbs of Love and Attachment

Verbs having the sense of 'love, regard for, attachment to' such as @deva[स्निह्], @deva[अनुरञ्ज्], @deva[वाञ्छ्], @deva[रम्], &c. and their derivatives generally govern the Locative; @deva[तस्मै पुत्रे स्निह्यति] the father loves his son; @deva[अतिरमै सौदर्यैषि मृदिति] (Śak. I) I have a sisterly affection for them also; @deva[न सन्देहं निरक्तस्यन्काय्यानां मयत्येतते] I do not, indeed, love the ascetic's daughter, @deva[अङ्गुदरजितरत्यो राज्ञ जनता युहद्धरज्यनै] people do not love a king whose ministers are corrupt; @deva[मायत्यद्धौ निरतिरै निरन्तुकुत् क्तुम्] (Manu. S. III. 179), @deva[रहसि रमते] (Māl. Mād. III. 2.) takes pleasure in solitude; @deva[रत्युः श्यासै] (Bhaṭṭi. I.) devoted to his welfare.

Note:—@deva[अनुरञ्ज्] and @deva[भनद्धुहु] are sometimes used with the Accusative also; @deva[रामायुदूरञ्यन्ति] (Rāma.); @deva[मादवानाम्यदरञ्यन्तो] (Bhaṭṭi. IV. 29.).

rules.title: Locative with Verbs of Acting/Behaving and Throwing
rules.body:
## Locative with Verbs of Acting/Behaving and Throwing

Verbs of acting, behaving towards, &c. such as @deva[वृत्], @deva[आचर्], &c and of throwing, such as @deva[अर्प्], @deva[क्षिप्], @deva[क्षिर्], &c. govern the Locative; @deva[विशिष्ठेषु विनीतम् वर्तते कार्यम्] one should act modestly towards respectable persons, @deva[कः प्रियतमेषु भुति सल्योजनम्] (Śak. [continues...]

rules.title: Locative/Genitive with अपराध् (to offend)
rules.body:
## Locative/Genitive with @deva[अपराध्] (to offend)

The root @deva[राध्] with @deva[अप] 'to offend' is generally construed with the Locative and sometimes with the Genitive; @deva[कस्मिन्नपि पूजार्हे अपराद्धा शकुन्तला] Śakuntalā has offended some one deserving respect; @deva[न तु ग्रीष्मस्यैवं सुभगमपराद्धं युवतिषु] (Śak. III. 9.), @deva[किंपुनः सुरावलेपेन भवतीनामपराद्धं] । Vik. I.

rules.title: Introduction to Genitive and Locative Absolute Constructions
rules.body:
## Introduction to Genitive and Locative Absolute Constructions

## THE GENITIVE AND THE LOCATIVE ABSOLUTES

"When the participle agrees with a subject different from the subject of the verb, the phrase is said to be in the absolute construction." Bain.

In English, the Nominative is used as an Absolute case; in Sanskrit the Genitive and the Locative are so used. The English-Nominative Absolute ought, therefore, to be translated by the Sanskrit Locative Absolute. When the Absolute Construction is to be used, the subject of the participle must be put in the Genitive or the Locative case and the participle made to agree with it in gender, number and case.

N. B. When the subject or object of the principal sentence is the same as that of the participial phrase, the absolute construction should not be used; as @deva[अयोध्यायाः निवृत्तः राज्यं राज्याम् अकरोत्] and not @deva[अयोध्यायां निवृत्तं राज्यै युङ्] &c.; @deva[आगतः निषसाद दुक्तानुसारच्चात्] and not @deva[आगतस्यं निषसाद तेष्युः] &c.

rules.title: Locative Absolute: Simultaneous or Indicative Actions
rules.body:
## Locative Absolute: Simultaneous or Indicative Actions

When the action done or suffered by a person or thing indicates another action i. e. when the time of the happening of the one action which is known indicates that of the second action, the Locative Absolute be used; @deva[गोषु दुह्यमानासु गतः] he went away while the cows were being milked; @deva[अवसिते रात्रौ] the night being ended; @deva[कुतः धर्मक्षेत्रविघ्नः सति रक्षितरि त्वयि] whence can there be obstacles to our religious rites when thou art the protector of the good.[^1]

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3, 37

rules.title: Locative/Genitive Absolute for 'when, while, since, although'
rules.body:
## Locative/Genitive Absolute for 'when, while, since, although'

The locative or Genitive Absolute may be used to express the sense of the English particles 'when, while, since, although,' &c. (and may thus supply the place of a pluperfect tense); @deva[एवं तयोः परस्परं वदतोः] while they two were thus talking; @deva[दिवाभागे अवसरि भविष्यद्ध्यक्षयो] (Meg. 40); Thou wilt accomplish the rest of thy journey when the sun rises again.

rules.title: Genitive/Locative Absolute for Contempt, Disregard ('in spite of')
rules.body:
## Genitive/Locative Absolute for Contempt, Disregard ('in spite of')

When 'contempt or disregard' is to be shown, the Genitive or the Locative Absolute is used; @deva[नर्तनस्य निरूपयस्य वा उन्मत्तः वा प्राव्राजीत्] he turned out a recluse disregarding or despising son i. e. in spite of the weeping of his son. In this sense the Genitive Absolute is used more often. The Locative or the Genitive absolute may thus have the sense of 'in spite of,' 'notwithstanding,' &c. in English.[^1]

(a) The Locative Absolute be made to express the idea of 'as soon as,' 'no sooner than,' 'the moment that' &c. by compounding it with the word @deva[एव] or @deva[मात्र]; @deva[निशिमितेव...संहितायाम् एव] (Rag. XVI. 78.) no sooner was the arrow fixed, &c. @deva[आसादितवचनम् एव मम] scarcely had I finished my speech when.

---

[^1]: Pāṇ. II. 3. 38

rules.title: Syntax of Pronouns Reference
rules.body: The chief peculiarities in the Syntax of pronouns have been already noticed in chapter IV.

rules.title: Gender in First and Second Person Pronouns
rules.body:
The pronouns of the first and second person eti. @deva[अस्मद्] and @deva[युष्मद्] have no gender. The other pronouns follow the

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[यष्मदस्मदोर्नानार्थे।] Pāṇ, II. 3. 38.

gender of the nouns they refer to. For the uses of the shorter forms of @deva[अस्मद्] and @deva[युष्मद्] see chapter IV.

rules.title: Usage of भवत् as Honorific Second Person
rules.body:
@deva[भवत्] is used in the second person like 'you' in English as a courteous form of address though it is to be regarded as a pronoun of the third person and ought to be treated as such, even as @deva[युष्मद्] &c.; @deva[भवत्] is used in the sacred texts; @deva[भवान् अपि तत्र गच्छतु] you may also go there.

(a) When respect is to be shown, @deva[अत्र] and @deva[तत्र] are prefixed to @deva[भवत्] according as the person with reference to whom it is used is near, or at a distance or absent; @deva[अत्रभवान् काश्यपः] the venerable Kāshyapa (who is near); @deva[इदमासनं अलङ्कारित्वान्तत्रभवान्] may you. occupy (lit. ornament) this seat; @deva[तत्रभवतो द्रावती] lady Irāvatī (who is not present); sometimes @deva[सः] is used with @deva[भवत्] to show respect; as @deva[यद्यस्य विषये विषये सः भवान् निवसति।] Māl. Mād. I.

rules.title: Special Senses of Pronoun तद्
rules.body:
The pronoun @deva[तद्] has often the sense of 'well known, renowned,' &c. @deva[तौ पार्वतीपरमेश्वरौ] those (well-known) Pārvatī and Parameśvara; @deva[तान्यस्मै वनस्थलानि] those well-known forest sites.

(a) When repeated, this pronoun has the sense of 'various, several;' @deva[तेषु तेषु रमणीयेषु स्थानेषु] in those various highly delightful spots; @deva[छूटन्ति तैस्तैः यत्नैः] notwithstanding several efforts–@deva[कृत्येतैः स्तवतियत्नैः] &c (Bhag. VII. 20).

rules.title: एक and अपर/अन्य for 'Some—Others'
rules.body: The pronouns @deva[एक] and @deva[अपर] or @deva[अन्य] are used in the plural in the sense of 'some—others;' @deva[विधवापुनर्विवाहः साध्वीकृतः इति एके शास्त्रिभिः उच्यन्ते अपरैस्तद्धनिषिद्धं उच्यते अन्यैश्च कलौ निरुद्धः ताभ्याम्] some think that widow-remarriage is sanctioned by the Ś'astras, some say that it is prohibited by them, while others hold that it was allowed in the Kali age. @deva[कोऽपि] may take the place of @deva[एके].

rules.title: Combination of Pronouns
rules.body:
The pronouns @deva[अस्मद्], @deva[युष्मद्], @deva[यद्] and @deva[किम्] are often used in combination with other pronouns; @deva[कोहं]—@deva[रघूणामन्वयं वक्ष्ये] that I will describe the race of the Raghu; @deva[कोहं सर्वस्मात्तो लोके] that I am the most degraded of all the people; @deva[स त्वं मद्गृहस्थे मद्गृहे]—@deva[अस्मद्गृहे]—@deva[वस] that thou dwelling in my fire-sanctuary; &c.; @deva[ते वयं दमयन्त्यायाः प्रार्थयन्तिमाग्रह] we, of this description, cannot over the earth; for (in search of) Damaryanṭi sometimes @deva[अस्मद्] and @deva[युष्मद्] may be understood; @deva[सा क्षिप्रमासनं रथं गजं वा] i. e. @deva[सा त्वं] that thou quickly sit in a chariot or mount an elephant, @deva[एषं पुत्त्रस्तव यद्गजेन्द्रो वाहुग्रं वाहनं दिग्जम्] this is that son of thine, the mother of elephants shaking water; @deva[तथा विनाकृतः पुत्रोबहुस्यमपि जीवितुम्][^1], who wish to live still, even though deprived of my sons in that manner, &c. &c.

---

**COMPARATIVE AND SUPERLATIVE DEGREES.**

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: †

rules.title: Comparatives with Ablative or Instrumental
rules.body:
Adjectives in the Comparative degree are used with the Ablative; @deva[वर्धनात्तरणं श्रेयः] protection (of one's subjects) is better than aggrandizement. @deva[अर्जुनाद्वयसा ज्येष्ठो युधिष्ठिरः] Yudhishthira was older than Arjuna.

(:) Sometimes the comparative is used with the Instrumental; @deva[प्राणैर्दयिरः] dearer than life. See also @ref[863] Note.

rules.title: Superlatives with Genitive or Locative
rules.body: The superlative may either be construed with the Genitive or Locative; @deva[अयमेतेषां एतेषु वा गरिष्ठः गुरुतमो वा].

rules.title: Comparative and Superlative Sense Through Case Usage
rules.body: The sense of the comparative and the superlative may also be expressed by the particular case used; @deva[अस्य हृदयं पाषाणादपि कठिनम्] his heart is harder than stone; @deva[छात्राणां छत्रेषु वा चैत्रः मेधः] Chaitra is the cleverest of all students.

rules.title: Special Usage of वर and श्रेयस्
rules.body:
The words @deva[वर] and @deva[श्रेयस्] when used in the sense of the superlative govern the Genitive or the Locative; @deva[पुत्रः सर्वस्पर्शानां वरः] 'a son is the best of things possessed of touch;' @deva[चतुष्पदां गौः श्रेयस् हेमकर्णानां वरम्] 'the cow is the best of quadrupeds and gold of metals'; the neu. sing. of @deva[वर] is used (with a word expressive of negation) in the sense of 'better and not, or but not;' @deva[अकृत्वान्यमनुष्ठेयं वरम्] doing any thing slowly is better than not doing it at all; @deva[अजातस्यमृतस्योर्णं वरं मूढो न चारित्रतः] of (the three kinds of) sons—not born, born and dead, and foolish, the first two are better, but not the last. @deva[याच्ञायां सोत्सवं वरं मरणं नायाचे द्विषत्कृत्यम्।] Meg. I. 8. @deva[वरं मृत्युः विदित्याभिः न तु मानभवनिः] better death then disgrace.

---

**Section IV.**

**PARTICIPLES.**

rules.title: Declinable Participles as Adjectives and Verbs
rules.body:
All declinable participles in Sanskrit partake of the nature of adjectives i e, they agree with the nouns they qualify in gender, number, and case. The participles often discharge the functions of verbs. They are largely employed to take the place of the Past and Future tenses and more especially of passive verbs. When so employed they follow the same rules of syntax as are laid down for nouns from which they are derived.

---

**PRESENT PARTICIPLES.**

rules.title: Present Participle for Contemporaneous Action
rules.body: The present participle is to be used when contemporaneity of action is to be indicated. It is often idiomatically used to express the sense of 'while' or 'whilst' in English; @deva[अरण्ये चरन्] while wandering in the forest; @deva[विवाहसूत्रकं विभवन् एव] while he yet wore the marriage string. Vide 670 (b).

rules.title: Present Participle for Manner, Cause, or Object
rules.body:
[^1]The present participle is used to denote the manner in which an action is done or the cause or object of an action; @deva[यवना अञ्चितं भुञ्जते] the Yavanas dine by lying down; @deva[हरिं पश्यन् मुच्यते] a man is absolved by (means of his) seeing Hari; similarly @deva[दर्शयन्], @deva[सर्वस्य शतम्] (Mb.)

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[छन्दसोर्थेदानोः क्रियायाः] Pāṇ. III. 2. 126 @deva[हेतौः फलं कर्मणः च।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: शक्नु and स्था with Present Participles for Continuity
rules.body:
The roots @deva[शक्नु] and @deva[स्था] are generally used with present participles to show the continuity of the action denoted by them; @deva[पशून् वधं कुर्वन् आसीत्] used to kill (always kept on killing) animals; @deva[तं प्रतीक्षन्तं तस्थे] remained waiting for him.

---

**THE PERFECT PARTICIPLES.**

rules.title: Limited Use of Perfect Participles
rules.body:
The use of the perfect participles is very limited; it is used in the sense of 'who or what has done &c.'; @deva[तं तस्थुषं नगर्याभिमुखम्] (Rag. V. 61.) him who had halted in the vicinity of the city; @deva[तस्य] (S'ak V. II. 9.) @deva[समस्तकल्याणवहस्य] (Mag. V. 34.) of thee who hast obtained all good things, @deva[स शुशुरुतस्तस्य वचनम्] (Bhattṛi. I. 20) when he heard his words, &c.

---

**THE PAST PASSIVE PARTICIPLES.**

rules.title: Past Passive Participle as Verb Substitute
rules.body: The past passive participle is very frequently used to supply the place of a verb, sometimes in conjunction with the auxiliary verbs @deva[अस्] and @deva[भू]. The past passive participle agrees adjectivally with its gender, number and case, the agent being put in the Instrumental, while the past active participle is treated exactly like the verb in the past tense; @deva[तेन कार्यं कृतम्] by him the work was done; @deva[तेन बन्धनानि छिन्नानि] by him the bonds were cut; @deva[आदिष्टोस्मि देव्या दूतिकया] I am commanded by queen Dūtikā; @deva[तेन कृतं कार्यम्] he did the work; @deva[राम हत्वा राक्षसान्] Rāma killed the Rākshasas; @deva[क्षत्तोसीमां नावमानीः] thou didst never despise me, &c.

rules.title: Intransitive Past Passive Participles with Nominative Agent
rules.body: In the case of past passive participles of intransitive roots the agent is put in the Nominative case; @deva[ततः रुदितो राजा रावणः] then the king of demons wept; @deva[गतं भवति] &c.

rules.title: Impersonal Use of Past Passive Participles
rules.body: The past passive participles are often used impersonally, the agent being put in the Instrumental case; @deva[प्रकाशितं] or @deva[भासितं सूर्येण] it is shone by the sun; @deva[जितं पुत्रस्नेहेन] victorious (all powerful) is the affection for sons; @deva[पाण्डित्यं प्रकाशितं तेन] he showed his learning; @deva[परिहृतं पश्चात् विषयेन], &c.

rules.title: Past Passive Participles of ज्ञा, भू, and अस् in Present Sense
rules.body:
The past passive participles of the roots @deva[ज्ञा], @deva[भू] and @deva[अस्] and their synonyms are used in the sense of the Present tense and are construed with the Genitive. (See @ref[857].)

For further particulars vide @ref[705]—@ref[707].

rules.title: Active Use of Past Passive Participles
rules.body: Many past passive participles are used actively in which case they may govern the Accusative case, like a Perfect tense active; @deva[आरूढशैलम्] (Rag. VI. 77.) which had ascended the mountains; similarly @deva[अतिक्रमप्रसूतः सर्वितम्]; @deva[आगतोदयपौरुषम्] crossed i. e. got over the calamity; @deva[अवारूढस्य यमुनायां तीरम्] arrived to the bank of the Yamunā, &c.

rules.title: Past Passive Participle as Neuter Substantive
rules.body: The past passive participle is used as a neuter substantive; @deva[गतम्] departure; @deva[दत्तम्] a gift, @deva[युक्तम्] an excavation, @deva[अनुयुक्तम्], @deva[प्रयुक्तम्], &c.

rules.title: Past Passive Participles with Auxiliary Verbs अस् and भू
rules.body:
The past passive participle active and passive, may be used with the auxiliaries @deva[अस्] and @deva[भू] in any tense, the meaning of the participle changing accordingly; @deva[गतोऽस्मि] I have or am starting; I have or am gone; so @deva[गतवानभवम्] or @deva[गतवानासम्] or @deva[गतोभूवम्] I had or was gone; @deva[इत्यादि]. @deva[गतो वनं भविष्यति रामः श्वः] that Rāma is to go to the forest to-morrow; @deva[संबभूवः कीर्तिमहत्त्वं भविष्यति] thou wilt obtain great glory, &c.

---

## THE FUTURE PARTICIPLES.

rules.title: Future Participle Meaning
rules.body: The future participle denotes that a person or thing is doing, or is about to do the action of or undergo the condition, expressed by the root; @deva[करिष्यत्] going or about to do; @deva[करिष्यमाण] about to do or what is about to be done.

rules.title: Future Participle Expressing Intention or Purpose
rules.body:
Besides showing simple futurity participle expresses intention or purpose; @deva[अनुगमिष्यत् मुनितनयाम्] wishing to follow the daughter of the sage; @deva[दास्यत्] wishing to give, @deva[वनचरान् दमयिष्यन्] intending exercising, as it were, to tame the wild beasts.

---

## POTENTIAL PASSIVE PARTICIPLES.

rules.title: Potential Passive Participle: Obligation and Necessity
rules.body:
The Potential passive participle is used in the sense of 'what should or ought to be done;' besides this, this participle yields the sense of 'fitness, obligation, necessity, capacity,' &c., the agent being put in the Instrumental case; @deva[विचिन्त्य मनसा किं कर्तव्यं कर्तव्यम्] (Devi Bhāg. IV. 7. 1.) he considered in his mind what he ought to do; @deva[धर्मः अनुष्ठेयः] religious duty ought to be followed; @deva[त्वया भारो बहुभिदः] thou art able to bear this burden; @deva[इमं दुष्टं वध्यः] this rogue deserves to be killed; @deva[गन्तव्या ते यक्षनाथानां अलका नाम यद्वसतिः] thou will have to go to Alakā, the habitation of the lords of Yakṣhas, &c.

Obs.—Sometimes the agent is put in the Genitive case; @deva[मया सेव्यो हरिः] Hari is to be served by me; @deva[विद्वद्भिः भक्ष्यम् अन्नम्] boiled rice to be eaten by Brāhmaṇas.

rules.title: Impersonal Use of Potential Passive Participle
rules.body: Occasionally this participle is used impersonally in the neuter gender and singular number; @deva[तवभवता तपोवनं गन्तव्यम्] his honour should go to the penance grove; @deva[मया चाण्डालैः सह स्थातव्यम्] I should have to dwell in the company of Chāṇḍālas &c.

rules.title: Impersonal भविष्यत् and भाव्य for Probability
rules.body: The neuter forms @deva[भविष्यत्] and @deva[भाव्यम्] are used impersonally in the sense of 'being,' 'not being' this can be on all probability i. e. ' the noun denoting the agent being put in the Instrumental case: @deva[अत्र कस्यापि कारणेन भविष्यत्] there must be some cause; @deva[नद्यां सन्नादानुरूपं प्रभावेन भविष्यत्] or @deva[भाव्यम्] in all probability his strength must be corresponding to his sound; @deva[आरूढो भूतपुरस्य पुरस्सरैः भाव्यम्] (in all likelihood) be seated in the carriage, &c.

rules.title: Potential Passive Participle as Noun
rules.body:
This participle is sometimes used as a noun; @deva[पृष्टवान् पृच्छनीयस्य] to him who asked what was to be asked; @deva[भविष्यत् भवेत्] let that, which is to happen, happen.

---

## INDECLINABLE PAST PARTICIPLES OR GERUNDS.

rules.title: Gerunds Denoting Prior Action
rules.body:
The past indeclinable participle in Sanskrit denotes the prior of two actions done by the same agent and corresponds to the perfect participle in English; @deva[एवं उक्त्वा विरराम] having said this he stopped; @deva[तान् पृष्ठे समारोप्य सरसं नीत्वा प्रभक्षति] having seated them on his back, he carried them to the lake and ate them up.
