As the past indeclinable participles or gerunds serve the purpose of carrying on the action of the verb and act as connecting links between sentences, they account for the sparing use made in Sanskrit composition of relative pronouns, conjunctions and connecting particles. When several powers are used the gerund should be translated by verbal tenses and copulative conjunctions; @deva[अथ संध्याकाले प्राप्ते चन्द्रापीडः पदातिः राजगृहं गत्वा पितुः समक्षम् दण्डमात्रं स्थित्वा इड्यं च विलासवतीं दृष्ट्वा आगत्य प्रमदावतीं प्रणिपत्य विसृष्टः] when the evening time approached, Chandāpīḍa went to the royal palace on foot, remained in the presence of his father for an hour, saw Vilāsavatī, &c.

rules.title: Gerunds Used Prepositionally
rules.body:
A few gerunds are used prepositionally in Sanskrit; @deva[ऋते], @deva[विना] except, @deva[आदाय] with, @deva[उद्दिश्य], @deva[अपिहाय], @deva[अन्तरेण] with reference to, &c.

---

## THE INFINITIVE MOOD.

rules.title: Infinitive Expressing Purpose
rules.body:
The infinitive in Sanskrit generally expresses the purpose or that for which an action is done and thus corresponds to the infinitive of purpose or gerund in English. The infinitive in Sanskrit thus involves the sense of the Dative and may, if desired, be replaced by the Dative of the verbal noun derived from the root; @deva[पानीयं पातुं यमुनातीरम् अवतीर्ण] descended from the bank of Yamunā to drink water; here @deva[पातुम्] may be replaced by @deva[पानाय] (@deva[पानस्य पानम्]); @deva[शाखामृगविनाशायोद्यतः] (Rag. X. 25.) where @deva[विनाशाय] =@deva[विनाशयितुम्].

"The infinitive (formed with @deva[तुम्] tum) in Sanskrit?" remarks Prof. Monier Williams, "cannot be employed with the same latitude as in other languages. Its use is very limited corresponding to that of the Latin supine, as its termination tum indicates."

(a) "Let the student, therefore, distinguish between the infinitive of Sanskrit and that of Latin and Greek. In these latter languages we have the infinitive made the subject of a proposition, or, in other words, standing in the place of a Nominative and an Accusative case often admissible before it. We have it also assuming different forms, to express present, past, or future time, and completeness or incompleteness in the progress of the action. The Sanskrit infinitive, on the other hand, can never be made the subject of a verb, admits of no Accusative before it, and can only express indefiniteness time and incomplete action. Wherever it occurs, it must be considered as the object, and never the subject of some verb expressed or understood. As the object of the verb, it may be regarded as equivalent to a verbal substantive, in which the force of two cases, an Accusative and Dative, is inherent and which differs from other substantives in its power of governing a case. Its use as a substantive, with the force of the Accusative case, corresponds to our use of the Latin infinitive; thus @deva[तव वचनं श्रोतुम् इच्छामि] is I desire to hear thou that, @deva[तत्तव श्रवणम्]; where @deva[श्रोतुम्] and audire are both equivalent to Accusative. Similarly, @deva[रोदितुमारेभे] 'she began to weep,' and @deva[महीं जेतुम् आरेभे], he began to conquer the earth, where @deva[महीजयम् आरेभे], he began the conquest of the earth, would be equally correct.''

(b) "Bopp considers the termination of the infinitive to be the Accusative of the suffix tu (@ref[453], Obs.), and it is certain that in the veda other cases of nouns formed with this suffix in the sense of the infinitive occur; e.g. a Dative in tave, havai, se from han comes hantave 'to kill;' fr, anu-i entease, 'to follow;' fr, man, mantavai, 'to think;' there is also a form in tos generally in the sense of an Ablative; e.g. fr. i, comes stos 'from going;' ir, han, hantos, 'from killing,' 'before killing;' and a form in tsi corresponding to the indeclinable participle in tvā of the classical languages; e.g. fr. han, hatsi 'killing,' fr. bhā bhātsi 'being,' &c &c," Sanskrit Grammar.

rules.title: Infinitive Cannot be Subject or Object
rules.body: The infinitive cannot be used as the subject or object of a verb, abstract nouns supplying its place in this case. Where, therefore, the infinitive occurs in English as the subject or the object in a sentence, the abstract noun derived from the root must be used in Sanskrit; @deva[स्वधर्माचरणं हितवत्] to do one's duty is beneficial and not @deva[स्वधर्ममाचरितुम्].

rules.title: Infinitive with Verbs of Wishing
rules.body:
[^1] The infinitive is used with verbs and verbal nouns meaning 'to wish or desire' provided the agent of it is the same as that of the verb; @deva[को मृगयच्छति हरेः दशनम्] (Mṛid. I.) who wishes to snatch away the jaws of the lion; @deva[मायिनां यदविकतुं श्रद्धां पृथग्जनोच्चित] Bhattṛi. II. 6. But @deva[तेषां तदकर्तुमिच्छामि] I wish him to do this, is wrong.

[^1]: @deva[समानकर्तृकेषु तुमुन्] Pāṇ. III. 3. 158.

rules.title: Infinitive with Verbs of Ability, Knowledge, and Time
rules.body:
[^1] The infinitive is also used with:—

(a) verbs meaning to be able, to make bold, to know, to be wearied, to strive, to begin, to set about, to bear, to be pleased, and to be proficient; @deva[चाण्डालः उत्तुं वचनं न शक्नोति] he is not able to support his neck; @deva[जानासि कोपं निवर्तयितुम्] you know how to restrain anger; @deva[आङ्गदेन समं युद्धं प्रवर्तयितुम्] (Bhattṛi. XV. 77) to strove to fight with Aṅgada; @deva[गन्तुं प्रयतिष्यसि] (Meg. 22) thou wilt try to go; @deva[तर्कं विहर्तुमारभे] (?Meg. 103) begin to speak; @deva[भोज्यमन्नमस्ति दियते वा भोजनाय] (Sid. Kau.) there is food to eat, &c.

(b) [^2] words like @deva[अर्ह्] and others meaning sufficient or able, proficient or skilled in, &c.; @deva[प्रजाः पालयितुं अर्हसि] (Rag. X. 25) thou art able to protect the creation; @deva[कः समर्थो दैवस्य विकृतिं कर्तुम्] who is able to change destiny; @deva[प्रासादानां मनोरमाणां] (Meg. 66) the palaces arc able to stand comparison with thee; @deva[भोज्ये पानीये कुशलः यदर्थे] (Sid. Kau.) skilled in eating.

(c) [^3] words having the sense of 'it is time to do anything?' @deva[कालः समर्थो वेला अवकाशो वा भोजनाय] (Sid. Kau.) it is time to take food.

[^1]: @deva[शक्यादीनामसमानकर्तृकेषु] Pāṇ. III. 4. 65. Vide Apte's Guide @ref[176] and note Rāmakṛiṣhṇa,

[^2]: @deva[अर्हविवक्षायामेकदेशवचने] Pāṇ. III. 4. 66.

[^3]: @deva[कालसमर्थयोरवकाशे तुमुन्] Pāṇ. III. 3. 167.

rules.title: Infinitive Has No Passive Form
rules.body: The infinitive in Sanskrit has no passive form. In turning, therefore, an active construction involving an infinitive into a passive one, the verb should be changed into the passive, the infinitive and the words governed by it remaining unaffected—e. g. @deva[सोऽमुं पुरं गन्तुमिष्टः], @deva[तेन पुरं गन्तुं द्यच्यते]—except where the object of the infinitive and the verb is the same, @deva[स पारं सोढुमिच्छति], @deva[तेन पारं सोढुमिष्यते].

rules.title: अर्ह् with Infinitive for Request or Ability
rules.body: The root @deva[अर्ह्] 'to deserve' when used (in the second person) in combination with the infinitive expresses 'a request, a respectful entreaty,' and is used the same way in English 'I pray, be pleased, &c.;' @deva[अग्निं शाप्तुमर्हसि] (Meg. 55) please put out the fire; @deva[न चेदस्ति न शाप्तुमर्हसि] (Kum V. 40) if you have nothing to conceal from me, please answer me: @deva[विद्यामय वक्तुमर्हसि सौरभेयम्] (Rag. V. 25) you be pleased to tell these days; @deva[किं अनुमन्तव्यम्] one &c. Sometimes it is equivalent to a gentle command: @deva[प्रियाः प्रशाप्तुमर्हसि] (Rag. I. 89) you ought to please her; @deva[न तं चार्थुमर्हसि] you ought not to bewail him. In the third person and under the same circumstances it expresses power or ability and may be translated by 'can;' @deva[शापो हि समर्थो कोऽन्यो सोढुमर्हति फलादपि] Māh. Bhar. IV. 58. 27. @deva[वेदां तत्त्वविशेषेण को निश्चेतुमर्हति] Ibid I. 1. 243.

rules.title: Infinitive Compounds with काम and मनस्
rules.body:
[^1] The infinitive with the final @deva[म्] dropped is joined with the nouns @deva[काम] and @deva[मनस्] to form an adjectival compound meaning 'wishing or having a mind to do any thing;' @deva[प्रत्यासि प्रतिगमिष्यकामं विद्याम् महर्षेः] &c. (Rag. V. 18) the disciple of the great sage was desirous of returning &c.; @deva[अहं जनः प्रष्टुमनाः तुभ्यम्] (Kum. V. 40) this person has a mind to ask you a question.

---

## TENSES AND MOODS.

## THE PRESENT TENSE.

[^1]: @deva[टुकामार्थस्य]

rules.title: Present Tense for Current Action
rules.body:
The Present tense shows that an action is taking place at the present time; @deva[अयमागच्छति तव पुत्रः] here comes (is coming) thy son. [^1] It is the Present progressive, which expresses the continuance of an action which is begun over sometime and is, remarks Prof. Bain, a true or strict Present tense. It is only by means of a special adverb or the context that the sense of the present tense can be limited to that of a present act solely; @deva[अद्य स इह पुरे वसति] now he dwells in this city.

[^1]: "The principal use of the Present Indefinite is to express what is true at all times; 'the sun gives light; twice two is four * * *.' Hence a more suitable name would be the Universal tense. It expresses present time only as representing all time. The permanent arrangements and laws of nature, the peculiarities, habits and properties of living beings and whatever is constant, regular and uniform, have to be represented by the Present Indefinite. * * It is only by a special adverb or by the context that we can confine this tense to mean a present act only." Bain, Higher English Grammar.

rules.title: Special Uses of Present Tense
rules.body:
Besides the general sense given above the Present tense from the context has the following senses:—

(a) [^1] It is sometimes used in the sense of 'immediate futurity,' @deva[कदा गमिष्यामि] when wilt thou go? @deva[एव गच्छामि] Here I go (i. e. shall go); @deva[ऊर्ध्वं क्षणोत्तरस्य म्रिये] I shall die an hour after.

(b) It may also be used to denote an action which is recently completed; @deva[कदा त्वं नगरादागतः]—@deva[इदानीमागच्छामि] when didst thou come from the city? Here I come (have come just now).

(c) In narrations it is used for the Past tense; @deva[गृध्रो ब्रवीति कस्त्वम्] the vulture says, 'who art thou'?

(d) Sometimes it is used to denote a habitual or repeated action; @deva[यदन्नेन जीवति].

[^1]: Pāṇ. III. 3. 131. See p. 525.

rules.title: Present for Past with नु Particle
rules.body:
[^1] When a question is asked and an answer is given to it, the Present is used in the sense of the Past tense when the particle @deva[नु] is used; @deva[कः अकार्षीत् किम्]—@deva[नु करोति सः] where @deva[करोति] is equivalent to @deva[अकरोत्]; when the particles @deva[नु] and @deva[ह] are used the Present may be optionally used; @deva[कोऽकार्षीत् किम्]—@deva[नु करोति] or @deva[चकार]—@deva[ह करोति] or @deva[न्यकार्षीत्].

[^1]: @deva[ननोर्लटः प्रश्ने। ननोर्हिभाषा।] Pāṇ. III. 2. 120, 121.

rules.title: Present for Future with Interrogatives and Conditionals
rules.body:
[^1] With interrogatives the Present is often used in the sense of the Future when thought or desire is implied; @deva[किं करोमि] i. e. (@deva[करिष्यामि]), @deva[क्व गच्छामि] i. e. (@deva[गमिष्यामि]) What shall I do? Whither shall I go? @deva[एतयोः कतरं] or @deva[एतेषां कतमं भोजयसि] (i. e. @deva[भोजयिष्यसि] or @deva[भोजयितासि]) which of these persons will you feed? so @deva[कं नु पृच्छामि दुःखार्तः], &c.; but @deva[कः ग्रामं गमिष्यति]@deva[।]

(a) It is also used in the sense of the Future in conditional sentences as implying a condition and the fulfilment of the desired object; @deva[योऽन्नं ददाति] (@deva[दाता दास्यति वा]) @deva[स स्वर्गं याति] (@deva[याता यास्यति वा]) he, who offers (or will offer) food, goes (or will go) to heaven i. e. if one offers &c.

[^1]: @deva[किंवृत्ते लिप्सायाम्। लिप्स्यमानसिद्धौ च।] Pāṇ. III. 3, 6. 7.

rules.title: Present for Future Perfect with यावत्, तावत्, ह्य, and ध्रुवम्
rules.body:
With the words @deva[यावत्], @deva[तावत्] and others having a similar sense, the Present is sometimes used in the sense of the Future perfect; @deva[यावत्त्वां न पश्यति तावदपयातम्] before he sees you, move away (before he shall have seen you, &c.).

(b) [^1] With the particles @deva[ह्य] and @deva[ध्रुवम्] the Present has the sense of the Future when certainty is indicated; @deva[ध्रुवमेते सारम् अवाप्स्यन्ति] (Rag. X. 25.) it will endeavour to accomplish your object. @deva[ह्य वसुधारो जयति सप्तद्वीपाम्] (S'ak. VII. 33) he will conquer the earth consisting of seven continents. @deva[प्रगृह्यते तव वचनं नमः।] Kir. VIII. 8.

[^1]: @deva[ध्रुवमर्थे विध्यानुमो लृट्] Pāṇ. III. 3. 4. @deva[निश्चये निश्चयनं लोदोट।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Present for Past with स्म Particle
rules.body:
[^1] The particle @deva[स्म] when used with the Present converts it into a Past tense; @deva[प्रतिच्छन्देति विषयेश्वरनां विप्रतारक्यातेन तत्र ब्राह्मणः निषसाद स्म] in a certain village there dwelt a Brāhmaṇa Mitraśarmā by name; @deva[नगरे प्राणिनोधावन्ति स्म] the citizens ran in hundreds. The participle @deva[स्म] may not necessarily be joined with it; @deva[त्वामेव स्म वैद्यो महाराज पश्यामि न विभीषणः नम्रते स्म हितमिच्छन्], &c.

[^1]: @deva[लुट् स्म।] Pāṇ. III. 2, 118.

rules.title: Present for All Tenses with जातु and आत्
rules.body:
When @deva[जातु] or @deva[आत्] is used in a sentence and condemns or censures or implies that the Present may be used in the sense of the three tenses; @deva[आपि जानाति स्मापि जाने भणिकत्वमाप्नोसि] where @deva[स्मापि] and @deva[आप्नोसि] may have also the sense of the Past or the Future tense; @deva[जातु तवभवान् यज्ञपयिष्यति शूद्रम्] (you will even make a S'ūdra perform a sacrifice).

---

## IMPERFECT, PERFECT AND AORIST.

rules.title: Three Past Tenses: Original and Current Usage
rules.body:
In Sanskrit there are three tenses denoting a past action. viz. the Imperfect, the Perfect, and the Aorist. Originally each of these three tenses had a signification of its own and was used in its proper sense in ancient writings. [^1] After Sanskrit ceased to be a spoken language the exact senses of these tenses were lost sight of and writers began to use them promiscuously, so that now any of these may be used to denote past time with certain limitations The original senses of these as well as their other peculiarities are noticed below.

---

## IMPERFECT.

[^1]: For a further explanation of the difference between these three tenses the student is referred to Dr. Bhāṇḍārkar's preface to the 1st Edition of his 2nd book of Sanskrit.

rules.title: Imperfect for Past Action Not Done Today
rules.body:
[^1] The Imperfect according to Pāṇini denotes past action not done to-day i. e. done at some time prior to the current day, @deva[ताभ्यां विभीषणोऽब्रवीत्] (Bhattṛi.) Bibhīshana spoke to them.

[^1]: @deva[अनद्यतने लुङ्] Pāṇ. III. 2. 111.

rules.title: Imperfect Optional with कु and स्माट् Particles
rules.body:
[^1] The Imperfect is optionally used for the Perfect when the particles @deva[कु] and @deva[स्माट्] are used in a sentence, @deva[इति हि अकरोत्] or @deva[चकार राम हि अकरोत्] or @deva[चकार]

(a) [^2] It may also be optionally used in asking questions referring to a very recent time; @deva[अगच्छः किम्] (Qu.) (Ans) @deva[अगच्छम्] or @deva[कथं किम्]? @deva[कथम्] but when the question refers to a very remote time the Perfect alone ought to be used; @deva[शशाङ्कवारे अगम् किम्]? @deva[अगाम्].

[^1]: @deva[महर्षादौ लुङ्लिटावकर्मकात्।] Pāṇ III. 3 142.

[^2]: @deva[इङ्यातो लुट् च। भूतै चादवैदे कुट्युट्।] Pāṇ III, 2. 116, 117.

rules.title: Augment Dropped with म and स्म for Imperative Sense
rules.body:
When the particle @deva[म] in combination with @deva[स्म] is used with the Imperfect in the sense of the Imperative, the augment @deva[अ] is dropped; @deva[म स्म भवः म स्म करोतु], @deva[म स्म विवदितुं प्रार्थयेत].

---

## PERFECT.

rules.title: Perfect for Remote Past Not Witnessed
rules.body:
[^1] The Perfect denotes an action done before the current day and not witnessed by the speaker. It has reference to a very remote time and should, therefore, be used in narrating events of the remote past; @deva[तां ताटकाख्यां निजघान रामः।] Rāma killed her whose name was Tāṭakā. @deva[प्रययावनिन्द्रजित्प्रत्यक्] (Bhaṭṭi. XIV. 16.).

(a) In the 1st person the Perfect shows that the speaker was in a distracted state of mind or was unconscious when the event took place, or that he wants utterly to deny something that he has done, @deva[बहु जगद पुरस्तात्तस्य मत्ताकिलाहम्] (Śiś. XI. 39) being frenzied I prattled much, I am told, before him; @deva[कलिङ्गेष्ववात्सीः किम्]@deva[।] didst thou dwell in the country of the Kalingas? @deva[नाहं कलिङ्गाञ्जगाम] I never went to Kalingas. With these exceptions the Perfect should not be used in the 1st person.

---

## AORIST.

[^1]: @deva[परोक्षे लिट्] Pāṇ. III, 2. 115. @deva[उत्तमपुरुषे चित्तविक्षेपादिना परोक्षम्]@deva[।] (Sid. Kau.); @deva[अत्यन्तापह्नवे लिट् वक्तव्यः।] Vārt.

rules.title: Aorist for Indefinite Past and Today's Actions
rules.body:
[^1] The Aorist simply expresses past action indefinitely i. e. without reference to any particular time (@deva[भूतमात्रे लुङ्]); @deva[अधीष्ट चैकलिङ्गाणां विद्यामतिसुतुम् बन्धून्। यजे यद्वेदैरास्तां पितॄन् पृथग्जनोचितम्] (Bhatt. I. 2.) 'He studied the Vedas, offered sacrifices to the gods, satisfied his departed ancestors, honoured his relatives, subdued the collection of six (i. e. the six passions), took delight in politics and totally annihilated his enemies.' The Aorist, however, properly denotes immediate action or one done during the course of the present day. "It is similar to the English present Perfect," remarks Dr. Bhāṇḍārkar[^2], "which the student will remember defines an action as having happened in a portion of time which is not yet expired; it brings past action in connection with the present time," @deva[अद्यावर्षीत्] it rained to-day.

[^1]: @deva[लुङ्] Pāṇ. III. 2. 110.

[^2]: See note under @ref[925].

rules.title: Aorist for Continuous or Near Actions
rules.body:
[^1] The Aorist ought to be used when the idea of the continuousness or nearness of an action is to be implied; @deva[यावज्जीवमन्नमददात्] (Sid. Kau.) gave food throughout his life; @deva[तेनाश्व पौर्णमास्यां काल्यां अग्निमाधत्तान् आजुहावात् च सोमेन] (Sid. Kāu.) he consecrated the fire on the last Paurṇimā (i.e. full-moon day) and offered Soma, &c.

[^1]: Pāṇ. III. 3. 135. See next Page.

rules.title: Multiple Tenses with पुरा Particle
rules.body:
[^1] With the particle @deva[पुरा] not joined with @deva[स्म], the Aorist, the Imperfect, the Perfect or the Present may be used; @deva[पुरात्राणां पुरा प्रवासिन्यः आसन्] (Sid. Kau.) here formerly dwelt pupils. But when @deva[स्म] is used with @deva[पुरा] the present alone can be used; @deva[पुरासि स्म पुरा] be formerly sacrificed.

[^1]: @deva[पुरे लुङ्लिटौ चादवैदे। पुरादूरात्मैच्छन्दसं परे लुट् च स्मस्यान्वं मा भूत् न तु स्मान्वस्य।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Aorist with मा for Prohibition
rules.body:
The Aorist is used with the prohibitive particle @deva[मा] (@deva[मुङ्]) or @deva[मा स्म], with the temporal augment @deva[अ] cut off, and has then the sense of the Imperative; @deva[हरिं ते चन्द्रादनं मा कार्षीः] Me. Bhā V. 132. 16. have nothing to do with that; similarly @deva[मा रोषं प्रकाशीः] Bhā V Rarely in ancient works the augment is retained @deva[मा निषादप्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः] may you not live, oh Nishāda for many years. When a root is preceded by a preposition, the @deva[अ] is sometimes not dropped; @deva[मा नु प्रवक्ष्यन्मन्युशोकम्] do not submit to sorrow or anger (here the @deva[अ] is not dropped); sometimes it is dropped; as in @deva[मात्मानं स्मावमानीः] do not despise your soul (conscience). Some explain these anomalies by considering the particle to be @deva[मा] and not @deva[मुङ्].

---

## THE TWO FUTURES.

rules.title: Difference Between First and Second Futures
rules.body:
The difference between the Two Futures is the same as that between the Imperfect and the Aorist, the only difference being that the former refers to a future time and the latter to a past one. The First or Periphrastic expresses futurity definitely but not of this day; the Second or Simple Future expresses futurity indefinitely as also that of to-day; it is also employed to denote recent and future contiguous time; as @deva[अद्य वानरेन्द्र त्वं यास्यसि तदयोध्यां भरतपालिताम्] (Bhattṛi XXII,) oh monkey, to-morrow you will go to Ayodhyā governed by Bharata; @deva[आत्मजौ त्वां दृष्ट्वा च इष्यं प्रहर्षिष्यन्ति। श्रोष्यतः सहं मायाश्च होष्यामि प्रापणिष्यतः सह राघवस्य] (Bhattṛi XXII. 14.) they will be delighted on seeing you and will ask you questions about the welfare of us two and Sītā; and Bharata also will be greatly pleased; @deva[एते...उच्छेत्स्यन्ते कपिकेतनेन] (Kir. III. 22) they will be extirpated by the monkey-bannered one (Arjuna); @deva[सत्याद्य पुञ्जशालाः] S'ak. IV.) Śakuntala will go (goes) to-day; @deva[प्रविष्यति जिज्ञासे नु हत्वाप्यन्यं शमम्] (Bhattṛi XVI. 13) if my sons are killed I will die or kill the enemy, &c.

---

## THE FIRST FUTURE OR PERIPHRASTIC FUTURE.

rules.title: When First Future Must Not Be Used
rules.body:
Obs. [^1] When the continuousness of an action or nearness of time (i. e. the non-intervention of the same period between the two points of time referred to) is to be expressed the First Future must not be used. @deva[यावज्जीवमन्नं दास्यति] he will give food throughout his life; and not @deva[दाता]; @deva[य इमामामावास्यामाज्यमागमिष्यति तस्यामग्नीनाधास्यते सोमेन च यक्ष्यते] he will consecrate the fires and offer a Soma sacrifice on the coming Amāvāsyā day; and not @deva[आधाता] and @deva[यष्टा]; also when limit of time or place is expressed and the word @deva[अवर] is used in a sentence; @deva[यः अयमध्वा गन्तव्यः आपाटलिपुत्रात् तस्य यदवरं कौशाम्ब्यास्तत्र सक्तून् पास्यामः] and not @deva[पातास्मः]; @deva[यः अयं संवत्सरः आगामी तस्य यदवरमाग्रहायण्याः तत्र युक्ता अध्येष्यामहे] and not @deva[अध्येतास्महे]; but when the word @deva[रात्र] is used the First Future may be used; @deva[योऽयं मासः आगामी तस्य यः अवरः पञ्चदशरात्रं तत्र अध्येतास्महे] we will study in the earlier fortnight of the coming month. When the period of time meant lies beyond a certain point of time, the First or the Second Future may be used; @deva[योऽयं संवत्सरः आगामी तस्य यत्परमाग्रहायण्यास्तत्राध्येष्यामहे] or @deva[अध्येतास्महे], &c.

---

## THE SECOND OR SIMPLE FUTURE.

[^1]: @deva[अनद्यतने लुट् । न नन्दियोगे । भविष्यति मर्यादावचनेऽवरस्मिन् । कालविभागे चानहोरात्राणाम् । परस्मिन्विभाषा ।] Pāṇ. III. 3. 135-138.

rules.title: Second Future or Present for Immediate Future
rules.body: When the close proximity of a future action is intended, the Second Future or the Present may be used; @deva[कदा गमिष्यसि] when will you go? @deva[एव गच्छामि] or @deva[गमिष्यामि] I shall just go.

rules.title: Multiple Tenses in Conditional with Hope
rules.body:
[^1] When there is the idea of hope implied in a conditional form, the Aorist, the Present or the Simple Future may be used in both the clauses to denote a future time, @deva[दैवादवर्षदेव वर्षति वा वर्षिष्यति वा बपेत् बपति वा बपिष्यति वा।] (Sid. Kau.) If it were to rain it would it would sow corn.

[^1]: @deva[आशासमान्नं वर्तमानं लुट् च।] Pāṇ. III. 3. 132.

rules.title: Simple Future for Courteous Command
rules.body: The Simple Future is sometimes used as a courteous way of command; @deva[प्रातरिष्यास्यतु स तिष्ठसि] (Vik. V.) thus you will go (i e. please then go) to the lake, &c.

rules.title: Simple Future with क्षिप्र for Hope
rules.body:
[^1] The Simple Future is alone used when the idea of hope is conveyed by @deva[क्षिप्र] and words having the sense of @deva[क्षिप्र]; @deva[वृष्टिश्चेत्क्षिप्रं आशु त्वरितं वा वर्षिष्यति शीघ्रं वप्स्यामः] if a shower were to come quickly we would at once sow corn.

[^1]: @deva[क्षिप्रवचने लृट्]@deva[।] Pāṇ. III. 3. 133.

rules.title: Second Future for Imperfect with Verbs of Remembering
rules.body: When the word @deva[नु] is not used with roots meaning 'to remember,' such as @deva[स्मृ], @deva[लुङ्], &c, the Second Future is used in the sense of the Imperfect; @deva[स्मरिष्यति लुङ् गोकुले वस्यावः] Kṛishṇa, do you remember that we dwelt in Gokula?

rules.title: Simple Future for Disbelief or Intolerance
rules.body:
[^1] When disbelief in or intolerance of an action is intended to be expressed, and especially in the form of a question, the Simple Future is used optionally in the sense of the Potential; @deva[न संभावयामि] or @deva[न मर्षये भवान् हरिं निन्देत्] or @deva[निन्दिष्यति] I never believe, or cannot tolerate it, that you would or should speak ill of Hari; @deva[कः] or @deva[कतरः कतमः हरिं निन्देत्] or @deva[निन्दिष्यति] who will speak ill of Hari (I do not believe that any body will, &c.); @deva[कं वृषलं भवान् याजयेत्] or @deva[याजयिष्यति], &c.; when the word @deva[किंकिल] [^2] (a particle, showing great anger) and roots having the sense of 'to be' precede, the Simple Future only should be used; @deva[न संभवामि] or @deva[मर्षये भवान् किंकिल वृषलं याजयिष्यति] I do not believe or like that you should make a Śūdra perform a sacrifice; so @deva[अस्ति भवति विद्यते वा भवान् वृषलं याजयिष्यति].

[^1]: @deva[किंवृत्ते लिङ्लृटौ। अनवक्लृप्त्यमर्षयोरकिंवृत्तेऽपि।] Pāṇ. III. 3.144,145.

[^2]: @deva[किंकिलास्त्यर्थेषु लृट्]@deva[।] Pāṇ. III. 3. 146.

rules.title: Simple Future for Wonder, Doubt, and Certainty
rules.body:
When the idea of wonder is to be expressed and the words @deva[नु], @deva[हि] and @deva[अपि] do not occur in a sentence, the Simple Future should be used; @deva[प्रभुन्दोऽन्दोऽपि हरिं पश्यति हरिं पश्यिष्यति] it is a wonder that a blind man sees Hari.

(a) The Simple Future is also used when the particles @deva[नु] and @deva[आपि] expressing a doubt are used; @deva[नु दण्डः पतिष्यति] will the stick fall? @deva[आपि कपाटं पिदधासिष्यति द्वारम्] will be close the door?

(b) This Future is also used when the particle @deva[अर्ह्] meaning sure or able is used; @deva[अहर्हं हत्वा निश्चयम्] Kṛishṇa is sure sure or able to kill the elephant.

---

## THE MOODS.

## THE IMPERATIVE MOOD

rules.title: Imperative for Command, Entreaty, Blessing, and Advice
rules.body:
[^1] The Imperative Mood does not express merely command, but also entreaty, benediction, courteous enquiry, gentle advice, ability, &c.

(a) In the second person this Mood is used to express command, entreaty, gentle advice and benedictions or blessings; @deva[गच्छ] (@deva[त्वं]) @deva[कुसुमपुरं] go to Kusumapura; @deva[परित्रायध्वं परित्रायध्वं] help! help! @deva[क्षमस्वापराधं] O God! forgive my faults, &c.; @deva[शुश्रूषस्व गुरून् कुरु प्रियसखीवृत्तिं सपत्नीजने] (Śak. IV.) serve your elders and treat your co-wives as if they were your friends; @deva[एधि कार्यकरस्त्वं मे गत्वा प्रवद राघवं] be thou my messenger, go to Rāghava, and say to him; @deva[अनन्यभाजं पतिमाप्नुहीति सा तथ्यमेवाभिहिता हरेण] she was addressed the truth by Hara when he said 'do thou obtain a husband not devoted to any other lady.'

(b) In the third person it is often used to express a blessing and sometimes gentle command; @deva[विघत्तां सिद्धिं नो...प्रकीर्णः पुष्पाणां हरिचरणयोरञ्जलिरयम्] may this handful of flowers scattered on the feet of Hari give us success; @deva[पर्जन्यः कालवर्षी भवतु] may rain pour down in time; @deva[पश्चात्तिष्ठन्तु वीरा शकुनरपतय] (Mud. V. II.).

(c) In the first person it expresses a question, necessity, ability, &c; @deva[किं करवाणि ते] what should I do for you? @deva[अधुनाहं गच्छानि] I must go now; @deva[करवामैतद्वयं देवि प्रियं तव] we will (are able to) do this thing, oh queen, which is agreeable to you; @deva[नहि प्रेष्यवधं घोरं करवाण्यस्तु ते मतिः] (Bhaṭṭi XX. 6.) let your thought be 'I must not commit the horrible murder of an ambassador.'

[^1]: @deva[लोट् च]@deva[।] Pāṇ. III. 3. 162. Vide Pāṇ. III. 3. 161. quoted on the next page.

rules.title: Passive Imperative Third Person for Courtesy
rules.body: The third person singular of the Imperative in the passive voice is often used and sometimes as a courteous form of expression; @deva[आनीयतां राजदाः] the prince should be brought @deva[श्रूयतां संगो पञ्चितैः] may you hear, ye Pandits; @deva[एतत्स्यान्नं स्वाद्यताम्] sake and eat.

rules.title: Imperative After मुहूर्त Time Period
rules.body: When time after a @deva[मुहूर्त] (nearly equal to an hour) is expressed, the Imperative is used; @deva[मुहूर्तोत्तरं यजतु स्म] offer the sacrifice after an hour.

rules.title: Imperative with स्म for Polite Request
rules.body: The Imperative with the particle @deva[स्म] is used when a request is courteously expressed; @deva[बालं पालयतु स्म] please teach the child.

rules.title: Imperative with मा for Present Sense
rules.body: The Imperative has sometimes the force of the present when used in combination with the particle @deva[मा]; @deva[मा भवतु] no, it is not so; @deva[मा च ते निघ्नतः शत्रून्मन्युर्भवतु पार्थिव]@deva[।]

rules.title: Imperative with इच्छामि for Wishes
rules.body: @deva[इच्छामि भवान्भुञ्जीत] or @deva[भुङ्क्ताम्] I wish you should dine. See @ref[958].

rules.title: Repeated Imperative for Frequency
rules.body:
[^1] There is a peculiar use of the Imperative which ought to be noticed. The Imperative second person sigular is repeated when frequency of an act is indicated and the whole used with the root in any tense; @deva[याहि याहि एति गति] (Sid. Kau.) he goes every now and then; @deva[पकाहि पकाहि पाकं पकति] (Sid Kau) he @deva[भिदट्]; @deva[अध्ययनमधीयानै पठेत] be studies steadily. The Imperative second person is also used when several acts are described as done by the same person; @deva[शकुन्च फिर, पानः सुबहारारति] (Sid. Kau.) he takes his meal, now eating fruit, now eating fried rice; similarly @deva[अशकुनं वदै दक्षिणामवहामरते] (Sid. Kau.).

---

## THE POTENTIAL MOOD.

[^1]: @deva[क्रियासमभिहारे लोट् लोटो हिस्वौ वा च तध्वमोः। समुच्चयेऽन्यतरस्याम्। यथाविध्यनुप्रयोगं पूर्वस्मिन्। समुच्चये सामान्यवचनस्य।] Pāṇ III. 4. 1-5. @deva[क्रियासमभिहारे द्वे वाच्ये]@deva[।] Vārt.

rules.title: Potential Mood for विधि, निमन्त्रण, and Other Senses
rules.body:
[^1] The Potential Mood expresses the sense of @deva[विधि] (command,, directing a subordinate, &c.), @deva[निमन्त्रण] (pressing invitation), @deva[आमन्त्रण] (giving permission), @deva[अधीष्ट] (telling one to attend to an honorary office or duty), @deva[संप्रश्न] (courteously asking a person a question), and @deva[प्रार्थना] prayer; @deva[यजेत] one should perform a sacrifice; @deva[त्वं ग्रामं गच्छेः] go to the village; @deva[इह भवान् भुञ्जीत] your honour should take food here; @deva[इहासीत भवान्] you may sit here; @deva[पुत्रमध्यापयेद्भवान्] you may teach my son (as an honorary duty); @deva[किं भो वेदमधीयीय उत तर्कम्] what, oh! shall I learn the Veda or logic? @deva[भो भोजनं लभेय] good Sir, can I get food here? i. e. will you kindly give me food? (All these senses are optionally expressed by the Imperative also).

(a) [^2] In the case of the first two senses viz. @deva[विधि] and @deva[निमन्त्रण] and in that of 'proper time', the potential participle may also be used for the Potential; @deva[भवता यष्टव्यम्], &c.

[^1]: @deva[विधिनिमन्त्रणामन्त्रणाधिकारप्रश्नप्रार्थनेषु लिङ्]@deva[।] Pāṇ. III. 3. 161

[^2]: @deva[प्रैषातिसर्गप्राप्तकालेषु कृत्याश्च]@deva[॥] Pāṇ. III. 3. 163.

rules.title: Potential or Participle After मुहूर्त
rules.body:
[^1] When the words 'after an hour' are used the Potential (also Imperative) or the Potential participle may be used, @deva[मुहूर्तादूर्ध्वं यजेत], @deva[यजताम्] or @deva[यष्टव्यं वा] (Sid. Kau.).

[^1]: @deva[लिङ् चोर्ध्वमौहूर्तिके]@deva[॥] Pāṇ. III. 3. 164.

rules.title: Potential with काल, समय, and होर for Time
rules.body:
[^1] The Potential is used with the words @deva[काल], @deva[समय] and @deva[वेला], when the word @deva[यत्] is used; @deva[कालः समयः वेला वा यद्भुञ्जीत भवान्] it is time now that you should dine.

[^1]: @deva[लिङ् यदि] । Pāṇ. III. 3. 168.

rules.title: Potential or Participle for Fitness and Capability
rules.body:
[^1] When the idea of fitness is to be expressed the Potential or the Potential participle may be used; and sometimes the noun in @deva[तृ] also; @deva[त्वं कन्यां वहेः], @deva[त्वं कन्यायाः वोढा] or @deva[त्वया कन्या वोढव्या] you are fit to marry the girl.

(a) The Potential or the Potential participle may be used when the sense of capability is implied; @deva[भारं त्वं वहेः] or @deva[भारस्त्वया वोढव्यः] thou canst (art able to) carry the load.

[^1]: @deva[अर्हे कृत्यतृचश्च । शकि लिङ् च] । Pāṇ. III. 3. 169, 172.

rules.title: Potential or Future with Interrogatives for Censure and Wonder
rules.body:
[^1] With interrogative words such as @deva[किम्], @deva[कतर], @deva[कतम], &c. the Potential or the Simple Future may be used when censure is implied (see @ref[937]); @deva[कः कतरो वा हरिं निन्देत् निन्दिष्यति वा] ।

(a) When wonder is implied the simple Future is used in preference to the Potential if the word @deva[यदि] be not used; @deva[आश्चर्यमन्धो नाम कृष्णं द्रक्ष्यति] it is a wonder that a blind man should see Hari; but @deva[आश्चर्यं यदि साधीयीत] it is wonder if he study.

[^1]: @deva[किंवृत्ते] (@deva[गर्हायां]) @deva[लिङ्लृटौ] । Pāṇ. III. 3. 144, (@deva[चित्रीकरणे]) @deva[शेषे लृङ्यदौ] । Pāṇ III 3. 151.

rules.title: Potential for Hope Without कवित्
rules.body:
[^1] When hope is expressed without the use of the word @deva[कचित्] the potential is generally used; @deva[कामो मे भुञ्जीत भवान्] it is my desire (I hope) that you will eat; but @deva[कचिज्जीवति] I hope he lives.

[^1]: @deva[कामप्रवेदने कचिति] । Pāṇ. III 3. 153.

rules.title: Potential or Second Future for Expectation Without नु
rules.body:
[^1] When the sense of 'I expect' is implied, the Potential or the 2nd Future may be used provided the word @deva[यत्] is not used; @deva[संभावयामि भुञ्जीत भोक्ष्यते वा भवान्] I expect you will eat; but @deva[संभावयामि यद्भुक्षीयास्त्वम्] (Sid. Kau).

[^1]: @deva[विभाषा धातौ संभावनवचनेऽयदि] । Pāṇ. III. 3. 155.

rules.title: Potential or Simple Future in Conditionals
rules.body:
[^1] When in a conditional sentence one thing is expressed as depending upon another as effect upon a cause, the Potential or the Simple Future may be used; @deva[कृष्णं नमेच्चेत्सुखं यायात्] if he will bow to Kṛishṇa he will attain happiness; so @deva[कृष्णं नंस्यति चेत्सुखं यास्यति].

[^1]: @deva[हेतुहेतुमतोर्लिङ्] । Pāṇ. III. 3. 156.

rules.title: Potential or Imperative with Verbs of Wishing
rules.body:
[^1] When words having the sense of 'to wish,' such as @deva[इष्], @deva[वृ], &c. are used, the Potential or Imperative is used; @deva[इच्छामि भवान्भुञ्जीत] or @deva[भुङ्क्ताम्] I wish you should dine; @deva[इच्छामि सोमं पिबेत्पिबतु वा भवान्] (Sid. Kau.) I wish Your Honour will drink Soma.

(a) But when the agents of both the actions are the same, the Potential alone is used in the sense of the Infinitive; @deva[भुञ्जीयेतीच्छति] (Sid. Kau.) i. e. @deva[भोक्तुमिच्छति] wishes that he will eat (wishes to eat).

[^1]: @deva[इच्छार्थेषु लिङ्लोटौ । लिङ् च] । Pāṇ III. 3. 157. 159.

rules.title: Impersonal Potential for Precepts
rules.body:
Sometimes the Potential is used without a subject when it is used in the sense of 'a precept or advice'; @deva[आपदर्थं धनं रक्षेद्दारान् रक्षेद्धनैरपि । आत्मानं सततं रक्षेद्दारैरपि धनैरपि] ॥ (a man) should save money for adversity, he should save his wife at the cost of his wealth and himself even at the expense of his wife and wealth; @deva[यथारोचेत विप्रेभ्यस्तत्तद्द्यादमत्सरः] (one) should serve Brāhmaṇas with all that they like, without being jealous.

---

## THE BENEDICTIVE MOOD.

rules.title: Benedictive for Blessings and Wishes
rules.body:
The Benedictive Mood is used to confer a blessing or to express the speaker's wish; @deva[चिरं जीव्याद् भवान्] may you live long! @deva[वर्षिपीड्रा स्वजातेषु वध्यास्त्वं रिपुसंहतिः । भूयास्त्वं गुणिनां मान्यस्तेषां स्थेया व्यवस्थितौ] ॥ (Bhaṭṭi. XIX. 26); @deva[कृतार्थः भूयासम्] may I be successful!

---

## THE CONDITIONAL.

rules.title: Conditional for Unfulfilled Conditions
rules.body:
[^1] The Conditional is used in those conditional sentences in which the Potential may be used when the nonperformance of the action is implied or in which the falsity of the antecedent is involved as a matter of fact. It expresses both future and past time. It must be used in both the antecedent and the consequent clauses; @deva[यद्यवर्षिष्यद् अवर्षिष्यन्नन्नस्य बाहुल्यमभविष्यत्] if ever if there would be plentiful rain there would be an abundance of corn; @deva[यदि तदपिनिर्भत्स्यदलाभ्यच्यतत्पुष्पाणां तव रतिरभविष्यदहो किमस्यनु] hadst thou obtained (which thou hast not) the sweet fragrance of her breath, wouldst thou have had any liking for this lotus?

[^1]: @deva[लिङर्थेविधौ लृङ् क्रियातिपत्तौ।] Pāṇ. III. 3 139 @deva[इच्छार्थेऽचिन्त्यति लिट्युलिङर्थेच्छन्यं तन् प्रात्यनुमितस्य लृङ् स्यात् क्रियामोक्षेतिधार्यो गमिष्यत्यारः] : Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Conditional Optional for Past Actions
rules.body:
Obs. [^1] When a past action is to be indicated the Conditional may be optionally used in the sense of the Potential; @deva[कथं नाम तत्रभवान्धर्ममत्यक्ष्यत्] or @deva[त्यजेः] how could you give up your religion?

(a) Also where the Potential is used in conjunction with the particles @deva[उत], @deva[अपि], @deva[जातु] &c; @deva[अपि तत्र रिपुः सीतां नार्थयिष्यत दुर्मतिः । क्रूरं जात्ववदिष्यच्च जात्वस्तोष्यच्छ्रियं स्वकाम्] ॥ @deva[संकल्पं नाकरिष्यच्च तत्रेयं शुद्धमानसा । (तृषा) सत्यामर्षमवाप्स्यस्त्वं राम सीतानिबन्धनम्] ॥ (Bhaṭṭi. XXI. 3. 4.)

(b) When wonder is to be expressed the Conditional is optionally used where the Potential is used in combination with the particles @deva[यच्च], @deva[यत्र] or @deva[यदि] when the action does not take place; @deva[आश्चर्यं यत्र यत्र स्त्री कृच्छ्रेऽवर्त्स्यन्मते तव । वासादस्यां विनटायां किं किमालप्स्यथाः फलम्] ॥ (Bhaṭṭi XXI. 8).

[^1]: @deva[भूते च] Pāṇ. III. 3 140

rules.title: Neuter Singulars as Adverbs
rules.body:
## SECTION V.

## Indeclinables.

## ADVERBS.

The neu. singulars of the Nominative and other cases of several nouns are used as adverbs; @deva[चिरम्] or @deva[चिरेण] or @deva[चिराय स्मस्य] having contemplated for a long time; @deva[दुःखम्] or @deva[दुःखेन विद्यापि] he is in distress; so @deva[दूरम्] or @deva[दूरेन] &c.

(a) The word @deva[विध] is used adverbially in combination with several words such as @deva[बहु], @deva[नाना], &c.; @deva[बहुविध], @deva[नानाविध] in various ways. The word @deva[पूर्वम्] is also used adverbially as the latter member of a compound when some action is to be expressed as having happened before something; said something by way of consolation; @deva[ध्यात्वापूर्वम्] thoughtfully, (i. e. thought preceding a certain action); @deva[अबुध्यपूर्वं मृगत्वदारेण हता च भो] O venerable Sir, I killed this cow unwittingly; @deva[शरणेन अध्यायनम्] &c.

rules.title: Reference to Previous Discussion of Prepositions
rules.body:
## PREPOSITIONS.

The use of Prepositions has already been explained at @ref[365]–@ref[371]. The Prepositions governing cases are already noticed under the various cases.

rules.title: General Note on Conjunctions
rules.body:
## CONJUNCTIONS.

The use of Conjunctions has not many syntactical Peculiarities and needs no special notice here. They are used in their proper senses in sentences.

rules.title: Special Uses of च Conjunction
rules.body:
The most important of these conjunctions and the one very frequently used is @deva[च]. It can never stand first in a sentence; nor can it be used like 'and' in English. It is used with such of the words or assertions it connects or is placed after the last of the words or assertions it joins together; @deva[रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्च] or @deva[रामः लक्ष्मणश्च]; @deva[कामश्च जृम्भितगुणो नवयौवनं च] love with its excellences expanded, and fresh youth; @deva[कुलेन कान्त्या वयसा नवेन गुणैश्च तैस्तैर्विनयप्रधानैः] ।

(a) Sometimes this particle has a disjunctive force; @deva[शान्तमिदमाश्रमपदं स्फुरति च बाहुः]—the hermitage is tranquil yet my arm throbs.

(b) Rarely this particle is used in the sense of 'if'; @deva[जीवितुं चेच्छसि मूढ हेतुं मे गदतः शृणु] oh fool, if you wish to live, &c.

(c) Sometimes it is used as an expletive; @deva[भीमः पार्थस्तथैव च] ।

(d) Sometimes it is used to connect a subordinate fact with a main one; @deva[भिक्षामट गां चानय] wander for alms and bring a cow; @deva[कुट्टिनी च शासिता गोपी च नि सारिता कन्दर्पकेतुश्च पुरस्कृतः] the procuress was chastised, the cowherdess was expelled and Kandarpaketu was honoured.

(e) When the particle is repeated it has sometimes the sense of 'on the one hand,' 'on the other hand,' 'and yet,' @deva[क्व च हरिणकानां जीवितं चातिलोलं क्व च निशितनिपाता वज्रसाराः शरास्ते] where, on the one hand, is the extremely frail life of fawns, and where, on the other, are thy arrows hard like adamant and falling sharply; @deva[न सुलभा सकलेन्दुमुखी च सा किमपि चेदमनङ्गविचेष्टितम्] । on the one hand the full moon-faced lady is not easy to obtain and yet there is this unaccountable sport of love.

(f) Sometimes the repetition of @deva[च] shows the simultaneous or undelayed occurrence of two events; @deva[ते च प्रापुरुदन्वन्तं बुबुधे चादिपूरुषः] they reached the ocean and at the same time the primeval Being also awoke.

rules.title: तथा as Substitute for च
rules.body: @deva[तथा] 'likewise' often supplies the place of @deva[च]; @deva[रामः लक्ष्मणश्च] Rāma and Lakshmana; @deva[अङ्गस्त्रविष्टा च प्रत्युत्पन्नमतिरेव] both Aṅgastravishtā and Pratyutpannamatī; @deva[तथा हि] means 'for instance, to be more plain;' @deva[तथा च] 'likewise;' both are often used introducing quotations.

rules.title: तु, हि, and वा Excluded from First Position
rules.body: @deva[तु] but, @deva[हि] for, because, and @deva[वा] are also excluded from the first place in a sentence. @deva[आत्मीयः पुत्रः स्त्री प्रीयां सुख्यो तु इन्नूनां किल] the son is one's own son, the wife one's friend, but the daughter a source of anxiety; @deva[अध्यनुयुदुन जनुजनुपायोनुपायो वा प्रयोति संशरितायुदु वशत्युत्युनै। कार्यो हुयुमीनां संकुनीतीं द्विजैनै युवन्युकारेणैनुयुयुं ते।] (V. 10.); @deva[अशकनि वा शरस्यनै वा घृरु] choose either the missiles or your person.

rules.title: यदि and चेत् with Potential and Conditional
rules.body:
## The Particles @deva[अथ] and @deva[इति].

The @deva[यदि] and @deva[चेत्] 'if' are usually used with the Potential or the Conditional; as @deva[यदि सोऽत्र संलहितो गौर्वं तर्हिनां ननु सहायम् कुर्यात्मसि] if he were here he would assist me; @deva[यदि दैवदत्तोऽत्र विवरुरनभविष्यदकर्यदेच्] had Devadatta been here, he would have undoubtedly done this; but they are also construed with the Present Indicative; @deva[यदि देवदत्त प्राहर्षि प्रयारानम्] if he lives till to-morrow; @deva[याजयिष्यामि]; @deva[यदि परा देवार्थायुनै युयोकायुरुनौनि] if Your Majesty has any thing to do with me, &c; @deva[क्षोत्यसि मुन जीवितेन यदि बाष्पं न कश्चरोयु] I conjure you by my life if you will not tell this in words. @deva[चेत्] is rarely used at the beginning of a sentence, &c.; @deva[चेत्सुत्युयुदुनुन्युन्यु प्रारं नयुविरधासत्] (S'ak. VII. 4) if the thousand-rayed one (sun) did not place him at the yoke of his car, @deva[आदि रौदैराकुरोतोयु] (have recourse to) @deva[नो चेत्] &c Dha. V. I. 44.

rules.title: Six Uses of अथ Particle
rules.body:
[^1] @deva[अथ] is used in the following senses:—(1) as a sign of auspiciousness [^2]; @deva[अथातो ब्रह्मजिज्ञासा] now begins the inquiry about Brahma; cf. the Bhāṣya on this sūtra; (2) marks the beginning or commencement of a work; @deva[अथेदमारभ्यते प्रथमं तन्त्रम्] now is begun the Ist Tantra; so @deva[अथ योगानुशासनम्], &c; (3) 'then,' 'after that,' &c; @deva[अथ प्रजानामधिप] &c. (Rag. II. 1.) After that (i. e. passing of the night) the lord of the earth, &c. (4) asks a question; @deva[अथ भगवान् लोकानुग्रहाय कुशली काश्यपः] is the venerable Kaśyapa all right that he may oblige the world? @deva[अथ शक्नोषि भोक्तुम्] are you able to eat? (5) 'and, including'; @deva[भीमः अथ अर्जुनः] Bhīma and also Arjuna; (6) 'if;' @deva[अथ मरणमवश्यमेव जन्तोः] if death is sure to befall a creature, &c.

[^1]: @deva[मङ्गलानन्तरारम्भप्रश्नकार्त्स्न्येष्वथो अथ] । Amara

[^2]: Properly speaking this is not the sense of @deva[अथ]. The mere utterance or hearing of this word if considered as auspicious as the word is supposed to have emanated from the throat of Brahmā

rules.title: Six Uses of इति Particle
rules.body:
As @deva[अथ] marks the beginning, so @deva[इति] marks the close of a composition. This particle is used in the following senses; (1) to quote the exact words spoken by some one, thus taking the place of the quotation marks and being used generally after the words quoted; [^1] @deva[देव काचिच्चण्डालकन्यका शुकमादाय देवं विज्ञापयति...देवपादमूलमागताहमिच्छामि देवदर्शनसुखमनुभवितुमिति] । O lord a certain *Chandala* girl requests Your Majesty (saying)...... "I who have come to your majesty's feet wish to enjoy the happiness of the sight of Your Majesty;" @deva[ब्राह्मणाः ऊचुः कृतकृत्याः स्म इति] the Brāhmaṇas said "we have accomplished our objects;" (2) cause (rendered in English because, since &c.); @deva[वैदेशिकोऽस्मीति पृच्छामि] I ask you because I am a foreigner; @deva[पुराणमित्येव न साधु सर्वं] every thing is not good simply because it is old; (3) purpose or motive; @deva[मा भूदाश्रमपीडेति परिमेयपुरःसरः] they two took a limited number of servants with them that there should be no disturbance, &c.; (4) so, thus; as follows; @deva[रामाभिधानो हरिरित्युवाच]. (5) in the capacity of, as regards; @deva[पितेति स पूज्यः गुरुरिति निन्द्यः] as a father he ought to be respected, as a teacher ought to be censured; (6) to state an opinion; @deva[इति आश्मरथ्यः] this is the opinion of Āśmarathya. It is often used by commentators in the sense of 'according to the rule'; @deva[इति शक्यार्थे लिङ्] &c. &c.

---

## INTERJECTIONS.

[^1]: In Sanskrit there is no indirect construction, so that in translating indirect constructions the actual words of the speaker followed by @deva[इति] must be used.

rules.title: Illustration of Interjections from Bhaṭṭi Kāvya
Prose and Verse in Sanskrit Poetry
rules.body:
## Prose and Verse in Sanskrit Poetry

This appendix treats of **Prosody**.[^2]

Poetical composition in Sanskrit may be in the form of @deva[गद्य] 'prose', or @deva[पद्य] 'verse' or metrical composition.[^1]

[^1]: @deva[काव्यं गद्यं च पद्यं च तद्द्विधैव व्यवस्थितम्] Daṇḍin Kāv. Pr. I.

[^2]: The earliest writer on Prosody is Piṅgalācārya. His work is known as "The Piṅgalachhandaḥ-śāstra." It is written in Sūtras and is divided into eight books. The Agni Purāṇa also deals with the subject very fully. The present chapter, however, is chiefly based on the Vṛttaratnākara and Chandomañjarī.

rules.title: Definition and Basis of Sanskrit Prosody
rules.body:
## Definition and Basis of Sanskrit Prosody

Prosody treats of the laws of versification or metrical composition. Sanskrit verse is regulated by quantity, not by accent.

rules.title: Structure of a Stanza: Pāda, Syllable, and Mātrā
rules.body:
## Structure of a Stanza: Pāda, Syllable, and Mātrā

A @deva[पद्य] or stanza consists of four lines each called a pāda or quarter. A pāda is regulated either by the number of syllables (@deva[अक्षर]) or by the number of syllabic instants (@deva[मात्रा]).

### (a) Definition of Syllable

A syllable is as much of a word as can be uttered distinctly by one effort of the voice, i.e. a single vowel with or without one or more consonants.

### (b) Definition of Mātrā

A mātrā (@deva[मात्रा]) is the measure of time required to pronounce a short vowel.

rules.title: Light and Heavy Syllables
rules.body:
## Light and Heavy Syllables

A syllable is @deva[लघु] 'light,' or @deva[गुरु] 'heavy' according as its vowel is short or long.

### (a) Short and Long Vowels

The vowels @deva[अ], @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ] and @deva[लृ] are short; and the vowels @deva[आ], @deva[ई], @deva[ऊ], @deva[ॠ], @deva[ए], @deva[ऐ], @deva[ओ], and @deva[औ] are long.[^1]

When a short vowel is followed by an anusvāra or Visarga or by a conjunct consonant, it is converted into what is called 'a prosodially long vowel;' as @deva[अंश], @deva[अच्छ], &c.

[^1]: @deva[सानुस्वारश्च दीर्घश्च विसर्गी च गुरुर्भवेत् ।]

rules.title: Treatment of Final Syllable in a Pāda
rules.body:
## Treatment of Final Syllable in a Pāda

The last syllable of a pāda is either heavy or light according as the exigence of the metre requires it, whatever be its natural length;[^1] as in @deva[वक्षःस्थली रक्षतु वो जगन्ति], &c. (Vik. I.); @deva[तस्याः खुरन्यासपवित्रपांसुम्] (Rag. II. 2.)

[^1]: Vide Vṛttaratnākara I. 9. @deva[वर्णः संयोगपूर्वश्च तथा पादान्तगोऽपि वा ॥] Chhandomañjarī.

rules.title: Eight Gaṇas (Syllabic Feet)
rules.body:
## Eight Gaṇas (Syllabic Feet)

In the case of metres regulated by syllables each line is divided into groups of three syllables each, called gaṇas or syllabic feet, named as @deva[म], @deva[न], @deva[भ], @deva[य], @deva[ज], @deva[र], @deva[स], and @deva[त]. The names and the Schemes of these are given in the following stanza.[^1]

### Mnemonic Verse

@deva[मस्त्रिगुरुस्त्रिलघुश्च नकारो भादिगुरुः पुनरादिलघुर्यः ।]
@deva[जो गुरुमध्यगतो रलमध्यः सोऽन्त्यगुरुः कथितोऽन्त्यलघुस्तः ॥]

That is: @deva[म] has all its syllables long; @deva[न] has all its syllables short; @deva[भ] has its first syllable long, @deva[य] has its first syllable short; @deva[ज] has its middle syllable long; @deva[र] has its middle syllable short; @deva[स] has its last syllable long and @deva[त] has its last syllable short.[^2]

### Symbolic Notation

The symbol ∪ stands for a short or light syllable; the symbol — denotes a long vowel or a heavy syllable. Symbolically represented these Gaṇas will stand as under:

| Gaṇa | Pattern | | Gaṇa | Pattern |
|------|---------|---|------|---------|
| @deva[म] | — — — | | @deva[ज] | ∪ — ∪ |
| @deva[न] | ∪ ∪ ∪ | | @deva[र] | — ∪ — |
| @deva[भ] | — ∪ ∪ | | @deva[स] | ∪ ∪ — |
| @deva[य] | ∪ — — | | @deva[त] | — — ∪ |

Similarly the letter @deva[ल] (la) is used to denote a short syllable and @deva[ग] (ga) a long one at the close of a line.

[^1]: Vide Vṛttaratnākara I. 9. @deva[वर्णः संयोगपूर्वश्च तथा पादान्तगोऽपि वा ॥] Chhandomañjarī.

[^2]: The following verse is easier to remember than one given above; @deva[आदिमध्यावसानेषु यरता यान्ति लाघवम् । भजसा गौरवं यान्ति मनौ तु गुरुलाघवम् ॥]

rules.title: Five Mātrā Gaṇas
rules.body:
## Five Mātrā Gaṇas

In the case of metres regulated by syllabic instants each line is divided into groups of four mātrās called the Mātrā Gaṇas; one @deva[मात्रा] or instant is allotted to a short vowel and two to a long one. The Mātrā gaṇas are five in number. These may be symbolically represented thus:[^1]

| Mātrā Gaṇa | Pattern |
|------------|---------|
| @deva[म] | — — |
| @deva[स] | ∪ ∪ — |
| @deva[ज] | ∪ — ∪ |
| @deva[भ] | — ∪ ∪ |
| @deva[न] | ∪ ∪ ∪ ∪ |

[^1]: Chandomañjarī

rules.title: Vṛtta and Jāti: Two Types of Metrical Stanzas
rules.body:
## Vṛtta and Jāti: Two Types of Metrical Stanzas

A pāda or stanza may be either a @deva[वृत्त] or a @deva[जाति].

### (a) Vṛtta

A Vṛtta is a stanza the metre of which is regulated by the number and position of syllables in each pāda or quarter.

### (b) Jāti

A Jāti is a stanza the metre of which is regulated by the number of syllabic instants in each Pāda or quarter.

rules.title: Three Types of Vṛtta
rules.body:
## Three Types of Vṛtta

A Vṛtta again is of three kinds:[^1]

1. **@deva[समवृत्त]** (samavṛtta) or that in which all the quarters are similar
2. **@deva[अर्धसमवृत्त]** (ardhasamavṛtta) or that in which the alternate quarters are similar
3. **@deva[विषम]** (viṣama) or that in which the quarters are all dissimilar

[^1]: @deva[समर्धसमं वृत्तं विषमं च तथा परम् ॥] The full note continues with the definitions of the three classes from the Chandaḥśāstra.

rules.title: Twenty-Six Classes of Samavṛttas
rules.body:
## Twenty-Six Classes of Samavṛttas

There are 26 classes of Samavṛttas or regular metres generally accepted. This classification rests on the number of syllables in each quarter which may vary from one to twenty-six. Each of these classes comprises a variety of metres all differing from one another according to the combination of the various gaṇas.

rules.title: Yati (Caesura)
rules.body:
## Yati (Caesura)

Yati (@deva[यति]) is the Sanskrit name for the caesura or pause which may be made in reciting a quarter or verse.

rules.title: Scope of Metres Covered
rules.body:
## Scope of Metres Covered

Only the metres in common use with their schemes in Gaṇas will be given here; all unimportant metres, as well as Vedic and Prākṛta metres will be ignored.

---

*Section I (@deva[समवृत्तानि], metres with 8 syllables to a pāda onward) begins in [§ 13](013.md).*

rules.title: Comprehensive Catalogue of Samavṛttas
rules.body:
## Comprehensive Catalogue of Samavṛttas

This section presents a comprehensive catalogue of Samavṛtta metres organized by the number of syllables per pāda (quarter). Each metre is given with its definition, gaṇa scheme, and illustrative examples from Sanskrit literature.

---

## Metres with 8 Syllables per Pāda

### (1) @deva[अनुष्टुभ्] or @deva[श्लोक]

This is the commonest of all Sanskrit metres; it forms the chief metre of the great epics and many of the Purāṇas.[^1]

There are many varieties of this metre; but that in which there are eight syllables in a Pāda the fifth being short and no deviation from these rules occur in the Mahābhārata and Rāmāyaṇa.

### (2) @deva[गजगति] (4+4)

**Definition:** @deva[नभलगा गजगति]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[भ], @deva[ल], @deva[ग] = ∪∪∪ | —∪∪ | ∪

### (3) @deva[प्रमाणिका] (4+4)

**Definition:** @deva[प्रमाणिका जरो लगो]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[ज], @deva[र], @deva[ल], @deva[ग] = ∪—∪ | —∪— | ∪

### (4) @deva[माणवक] (4+4)

**Definition:** @deva[भातलगा माणवकम्]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[भ], @deva[त], @deva[ल], @deva[ग] = —∪∪ | ——∪ | ∪

### (5) @deva[विद्युन्माला] (4+4)

**Definition:** @deva[मो मो गो गो विद्युन्माला]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[म], @deva[म], @deva[ग], @deva[ग] = ——— | ——— | —

### (6) @deva[समानिका] (4+4)

**Definition:** @deva[रलो रजो समानिका हु]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[र], @deva[ज], @deva[ल], @deva[ग] = —∪— | ∪—∪

---

## Metres with 9 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[बृहती]

### (1) @deva[भुजगशिशुभृता] (7+2)

**Definition:** @deva[भुजगशिशुभृता नौ नः]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[न], @deva[म] = ∪∪∪ | ∪∪∪ | ———

### (2) @deva[भुजंगसंगता] (3+6)

**Definition:** @deva[सजरैभुजंगसंगता]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[र] = ∪∪— | ∪—∪ | —∪—

### (3) @deva[मणिमध्य] (5+4)

**Definition:** @deva[रयास्मणिमध्यं चेद्रमसाः]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[भ], @deva[म], @deva[स] = —∪∪ | ——— | ∪∪—

---

## Metres with 10 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[पङ्क्तिः]

### (1) @deva[त्वरितगति] (5+5)

**Definition:** @deva[त्वरितगतिर् नजनगौः]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[ज], @deva[न], @deva[ग] = ∪∪∪ | ∪—∪ | ∪∪∪ | —

### (2) @deva[मत्ता] (4+6)

**Definition:** @deva[त्रैया मत्ता सभसमसुष्ठ]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[म], @deva[भ], @deva[स], @deva[ग] = ——— | —∪∪ | ∪∪— | —

### (3) @deva[रुक्मवती] (5+5)

Also called @deva[चम्पकमाला]

**Definition:** @deva[रुक्मवती सा यत्र भमसगाः]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[भ], @deva[म], @deva[स], @deva[ग] = —∪∪ | ——— | ∪∪— | —

---

## Metres with 11 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[त्रिष्टुभ्]

### (1) @deva[इन्द्रवज्रा] (5+6)

**Definition:** @deva[स्यादिन्द्रवज्रा यदि तौ जगौ गः]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[त], @deva[त], @deva[ज], @deva[ग], @deva[ग] = ——∪ | ——∪ | ∪—∪ | — —

### (2) @deva[उपेन्द्रवज्रा] (5+6)

**Definition:** @deva[उपेन्द्रवज्रा जतजातद्वौ गौ]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[ज], @deva[त], @deva[ज], @deva[ग], @deva[ग] = ∪—∪ | ——∪ | ∪—∪ | — —

### (3) @deva[उपजाति]

**Definition:** A mixture of Indravajrā and Upendravajrā gives a metre called Upajāti. It is said to have fourteen varieties.

**Gaṇa Scheme:** Mixed pattern of @deva[इन्द्रवज्रा] and @deva[उपेन्द्रवज्रा]

When other two metres are mixed in one stanza, they are still called Upajāti.

### (4) @deva[द्रोधकन्द] (6+5)

**Definition:** @deva[द्रोधकनिच्छुति भवितगाद्वौ]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[म], @deva[ग], @deva[ग] = —∪∪ | —∪∪ | ——— | — —

### (5) @deva[श्रमरविलंसितन्द] (3+6)

**Definition:** @deva[स्योगं श्रळो य स्याङ्गमरविलंसितन्द]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[भ], @deva[न], @deva[ल], @deva[ग] = ∪∪∪ | —∪∪ | ∪∪∪ | ∪— | —

### (6) @deva[रयोद्धृता] (3+8 or 4+7)

**Definition:** @deva[राच्चराविद्यं रयोद्धृता लगौ]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[र], @deva[न], @deva[र], @deva[ल], @deva[ग] = —∪— | ∪∪∪ | —∪— | ∪— | —

### (7) @deva[शालिनी] (4+7)

**Definition:** @deva[शालिन्युक्ता स्तौ तर्गौ गोत्रिघैल्युके]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[म], @deva[त], @deva[त], @deva[ग], @deva[ग] = ——— | ——∪ | ——∪ | — —

### (8) @deva[स्वागता] (3+8)

**Definition:** @deva[स्वागता रनभगैर्दुरुणा च]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[र], @deva[न], @deva[भ], @deva[ग], @deva[ग] = —∪— | ∪∪∪ | —∪∪ | — —

---

## Metres with 12 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[जगती]

### (1) @deva[वंशस्थविल] (5+7)

Also called @deva[वंशस्थ] and @deva[वंशस्तानित]

**Definition:** @deva[वदन्ति वंशस्थविलं जतौ जरौ]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[ज], @deva[त], @deva[ज], @deva[र] = ∪—∪ | ——∪ | ∪—∪ | —∪—

### (2) @deva[इन्द्रवंशा]

**Definition:** @deva[तचैन्द्रवंशा प्रथमाक्षरे यरौ]

(Same as Vaṁśasthavilla except that its first syllable is long)

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[त], @deva[त], @deva[ज], @deva[र] = ——∪ | ——∪ | ∪—∪ | —∪—

### (3) @deva[चन्द्रवदना] (4+8)

**Definition:** @deva[चन्द्रवदनं निगदन्ति रनभसै]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[र], @deva[न], @deva[भ], @deva[स] = —∪— | ∪∪∪ | —∪∪ | ∪∪—

### (4) @deva[जलधरमाला] (4+8)

**Definition:** @deva[मौ भस्नौ चैज्जलधरमालाइस्यन्यौ]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[म], @deva[म], @deva[स], @deva[स] = ——— | ——— | ∪∪— | ∪∪—

### (5) @deva[जलोद्धतगति] (6+6)

**Definition:** @deva[जसौ जसयुतौ जलोद्धतगति]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[ज], @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[स] = ∪—∪ | ∪∪— | ∪—∪ | ∪∪—

### (6) @deva[तामरस] (5+7)

**Definition:** @deva[हृहु वद तामरसे ननजा य]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[न], @deva[ज], @deva[य] = ∪∪∪ | ∪∪∪ | ∪—∪ | ∪——

### (7) @deva[तोटक] (4+4+4)

**Definition:** @deva[वरु तोटकमन्चिधसकारशुतम्]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[स] = ∪∪— | ∪∪— | ∪∪— | ∪∪—

### (8) @deva[द्रुतविलम्बित] (4+8 or 4+4+4)

**Definition:** @deva[द्रुतविलम्बितमाह नभौ भरौ]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[र] = ∪∪∪ | —∪∪ | —∪∪ | —∪—

### (9) @deva[मन्द्राकिनी] or @deva[मधा] (7+5)

**Definition:** @deva[ननरर घटिता नु मन्द्राकिनी]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[न], @deva[र], @deva[र] = ∪∪∪ | ∪∪∪ | —∪— | —∪—

### (10) @deva[प्रमिताक्षरा] (5+7)

**Definition:** @deva[प्रमिताक्षरा सजससै कथिता]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[स], @deva[स] = ∪∪— | ∪—∪ | ∪∪— | ∪∪—

### (11) @deva[भुजंगप्रयात] (6+6)

**Definition:** @deva[भुजङ्गप्रयातं चतुर्भिर्यकारै]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[य], @deva[य], @deva[य], @deva[य] = ∪—— | ∪—— | ∪—— | ∪——

### (12) @deva[मणिमाला] (6+6)

**Definition:** @deva[त्यौ त्यौ मणिमाला छिन्नायुद्वुङ्गुकै]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[त], @deva[य], @deva[त], @deva[य] = ——∪ | ∪—— | ——∪ | ∪——

### (13) @deva[मालती] (5+7)

### (14) @deva[वैश्वदेवी] (5+7)

### (15) @deva[स्त्रविणी] (6+6)

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[र], @deva[र], @deva[र], @deva[र] = —∪— | —∪— | —∪— | —∪—

---

## Metres with 13 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[अतिजगती]

### (1) @deva[कुटहंस] (5+8)

Also called @deva[सिंहनाद] and @deva[कुटजा]

**Definition:** @deva[सजसा सगौ च कथित कल्ठहंस]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[ग]

### (2) @deva[क्षमा] (various)

### (3) @deva[महर्षिणी] (3+10)

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[ज], @deva[भ], @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[ग]

---

## Metres with 14 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[शक्वरी]

### (1) @deva[अपराजिता] (7+7)

**Definition:** @deva[ननरसलधुगै स्वैररपराजिता]

### (4) @deva[मध्यक्षामा] (4+10)

## Metres with 15 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[अतिशक्वरी] (@deva[पञ्चदशाक्षरा])

### (1) @deva[तूणक] (4+4+4+3 or 7+8)

### (3) @deva[लीलाखेल]

**Definition:** @deva[एकन्युनो विद्युन्मालापादो चैल्लौलाखेल]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[म], @deva[म], @deva[म], @deva[म], @deva[म]

### (4) @deva[शशिकला] (7+8)

**Definition:** @deva[उरुनिधनमधुलधुरिहं शिशिकला]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[न], @deva[न], @deva[न], @deva[स]

The same is called @deva[लग्नु] when the caesura is at the 6th syllable, and @deva[यणिग्युणिदकर] when it is at the 8th and 7th syllables.

---

## Metres with 16 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[अत्यष्टि] (@deva[षोडशाक्षरा])

### (1) @deva[चित्र] (8+8 or 4+4+4+4)

**Definition:** @deva[त्रिच्चसंड्गमौरितं समानिकापदद्यं दु]

Two Pādas of Samānikā make one Pāda of Chitra.

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[र], @deva[ज], @deva[र], @deva[ज], @deva[र], @deva[ग]

### (2) @deva[पञ्चचामर] (8+8 or 4+4+4+4)

**Definition:** @deva[प्रमाणिकापदद्युर्यं वदन्ति पञ्चचामरम्]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[ज], @deva[र], @deva[ज], @deva[र], @deva[ज], @deva[ग]

### (3) @deva[वाणिनी]

**Definition:** @deva[नुजभञ्चरेयद्वा भवति वाणिनी गशुकै]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[ज], @deva[भ], @deva[ज], @deva[र], @deva[ग]

---

## Metres with 17 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[अत्यष्टि]

### (1) @deva[नन्दृटक] (8+9)

**Definition:** @deva[यादै भवतौ नजौ भञ्जला ङ्गुरु नंदृटकम्]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[ज], @deva[भ], @deva[ज], @deva[ज], @deva[ल], @deva[ग]

### (2) @deva[मन्द्राक्रान्ता] (4+7+6)

**Definition:** @deva[मन्द्राक्रान्ताद्युविरसनगेमो भनौ तौ गशुरु]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[म], @deva[भ], @deva[न], @deva[त], @deva[त], @deva[ग], @deva[ग]

### (3) @deva[पृथ्वी] (8+9)

**Definition:** @deva[जसौ जसयला घडुप्रहयातिक्र पृथ्वी युरु]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[ज], @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[स], @deva[य], @deva[ल], @deva[ग]

### (4) @deva[वंशपत्रपतित] (6+6+5)

**Definition:** @deva[दिड्युत्रुनि वंशपत्रपतितं भरवभनलगौ]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[भ], @deva[र], @deva[न], @deva[भ], @deva[न], @deva[ल], @deva[ग]

### (5) @deva[शिखरिणी] (6+11)

**Definition:** @deva[रसैरुद्वैविच्छुरुसा यम्नसभूला ग शिखरिणीं]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[य], @deva[म], @deva[न], @deva[स], @deva[भ], @deva[ल], @deva[ग]

### (6) @deva[हरिणी] (6+4+7)

**Definition:** @deva[नसभरसला ग रुड्द्वैहैयैहरिणीं मता]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[स], @deva[भ], @deva[र], @deva[स], @deva[ल], @deva[ग]

---

## Metres with 18 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[धृति]

### (1) @deva[चित्रलेखा] (4+4+4+6)

**Definition:** @deva[मन्द्राक्रान्ता नपरलधुयुता कौर्तिता चित्रलैखा]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[म], @deva[भ], @deva[न], @deva[य], @deva[य], @deva[य]

### (2) @deva[नन्दन] (11+7)

**Definition:** @deva[नजभजेरसु रेफस्ताहितैर्ध शिविहैर्यनैन्दनम्]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[ज], @deva[भ], @deva[ज], @deva[र], @deva[र]

### (3) @deva[नाराच] (8+5+5)

**Definition:** @deva[इहु ननरच्चतुश्कसूष्टं तु नाराच्चमाच्युशुते]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[न], @deva[र], @deva[र], @deva[र], @deva[र]

---

## Metres with 19 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[अतिधृति]

### (1) @deva[मेघविस्कुज्जिता] (6+6+7)

**Definition:** @deva[रसहर्चैध्मोन्सौ रर्युल्युर्युतौ मैघाविस्कुज्जिता रु]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[य], @deva[म], @deva[न], @deva[स], @deva[र], @deva[र], @deva[ग]

### (2) @deva[शार्दूलविक्रीडित] (12+7)

**Definition:** @deva[दयाथैधोगैदं म सजौ सततगा शार्दूलविकुरीडितम्]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[म], @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[स], @deva[त], @deva[त], @deva[ग]

This is one of the most popular metres in classical Sanskrit poetry.

### (3) @deva[स्वमधुरा] (7+6+6)

**Definition:** @deva[भो भो मौ नौ ङ्गुरुश्रैवर हयनमुदुरसैरुक्ता स्वमधुरा]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[म], @deva[र], @deva[भ], @deva[न], @deva[म], @deva[न], @deva[ग]

---

## Metres with 20 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[कृति]

### (1) @deva[गीतिका] (5+7+8)

**Definition:** @deva[सजजा भरौ सढुलगा यदा कथिता तदा खलु गैतिका]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[ज], @deva[भ], @deva[र], @deva[भ], @deva[ल], @deva[ग]

### (2) @deva[स्वमुवदना] (7+7+6)

**Definition:** @deva[ड्त्रैया सदाभघरुश्भैभैरभनयुता रुष्ठौ ग स्वमुवदना]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[म], @deva[र], @deva[भ], @deva[न], @deva[य], @deva[भ], @deva[ल], @deva[ग]

---

## Metres with 21 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[प्रकृति]

### (1) @deva[सरसी] (10+11)

Also called @deva[पद्युकावल्ली] and @deva[धृतवाही]

**Definition:** @deva[नजभजा जरौ यदि तद्वुा गदिता सरसी कथित]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[ज], @deva[भ], @deva[ज], @deva[ज], @deva[ज], @deva[र]

### (2) @deva[स्रग्धरा] (7+7+7)

**Definition:** @deva[प्रभैयोर्गां ड्रैयेण त्रिधुनियतिधुता स्रगधरा कौर्धै]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[म], @deva[र], @deva[भ], @deva[न], @deva[य], @deva[य], @deva[ग]

This is one of the most ornate and dignified metres in Sanskrit.

---

## Metres with 22 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[आकृति]

### (1) @deva[मन्दिरा]

**Definition:** @deva[सप्रभकारश्युतक्युरुगैदितैयष्ठुद्वारन्तरा मन्दिरा]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[ग]

### (2) @deva[हंसौ] (8+14)

**Definition:** @deva[मौ गौ नाश्रैस्वारौ गौ गौ वछुसुष्ठुवनयतिरिते रु]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[म], @deva[म], @deva[त], @deva[न], @deva[न], @deva[स], @deva[न], @deva[ग]

---

## Metres with 23 Syllables per Pāda

### @deva[त्रिकृति]

### (1) @deva[अद्विततनया]

Also called @deva[अम्बुललित]

**Definition:** @deva[नजभजभा जगौं लधुयुरु इुधैरुरु गदितैयमद्वुिततनया]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[ज], @deva[भ], @deva[ज], @deva[भ], @deva[ज], @deva[भ], @deva[ल], @deva[ग]

---

## Metres with 24-26 Syllables per Pāda

Metres with 24, 25, 26 syllables in a pāda are only three; but they are very rare.

---

## @deva[दण्डक] (Daṇḍaka)

Metres with 27 syllables or more in each pāda are denoted by the general name Daṇḍaka. Many varieties of this are mentioned (as the number of syllables in each pāda may sometimes reach 999), such as @deva[चण्डवृत्तप्रयात], @deva[प्रचितक], @deva[मत्तकोकिल], @deva[कर], @deva[सिंहविक्रान्त], @deva[कहुसमस्तनक], @deva[अनभङ्गोद्वर], @deva[सङ्ग्राम] &c.

Mālavikāgnimitra I.36 is an instance of the species last named, having 54 syllables in each pāda.

---

## SECTION II

## @deva[अर्धसमवृत्तानि] (Ardhasamavṛttāni)

Metres with their alternate quarters similar.

### (1) @deva[उपचित्र]

**Definition:** @deva[विषमे यदि सौ सल्युगा द्वुटे भौ युनि भाहुरुकाङ्गुपचित्रम्]

**Gaṇa Scheme:**
- Odd quarter: @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[ल], @deva[ग]
- Even quarter: @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[ग], @deva[ग]

### (2) @deva[अपरवक्त्र]

Sometimes called @deva[वैतालीय]

**Definition:** @deva[अयुनि ननरला युरु समे तद्युपरवकत्रमिदं नजो गम्]

**Gaṇa Scheme:**
- Odd quarter: @deva[न], @deva[न], @deva[र], @deva[ल], @deva[ग]
- Even quarter: @deva[न], @deva[ज], @deva[ज], @deva[र]

### (3) @deva[पुष्पिताग्रा]

Also called @deva[ओपच्छन्द्रुसिक]

**Definition:** @deva[अयुनि नूरगैरुक्तो यक्रारो युनि च नजो जरम्]

**Gaṇa Scheme:**
- Odd quarter: @deva[न], @deva[न], @deva[र], @deva[य]
- Even quarter: @deva[न], @deva[ज], @deva[ज], @deva[र], @deva[ग]

### (4) @deva[मालभारिणी]

**Definition:** @deva[विषमे सतजै नगै नर्गं नाविभभैस्मेणं तु माल्युभारिणी]

**Gaṇa Scheme:**
- Odd quarter: @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[ग], @deva[ग]
- Even quarter: @deva[स], @deva[भ], @deva[र], @deva[य]

### (5) @deva[वियोगिनी]

Also called @deva[वैतालीय] or @deva[हंसुरी]

**Definition:** @deva[विषमे ससजा यरु समे सभरा लौऽथ युरुर्वियोगिनी]

**Gaṇa Scheme:**
- Odd quarter: @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[ग]
- Even quarter: @deva[स], @deva[भ], @deva[र], @deva[ल], @deva[ग]

### (6) @deva[वेगवती]

**Definition:** @deva[सयुगास्सयुरु विषमे चैद्वु भाविद्वु वैगवती युनि मासौ]

**Gaṇa Scheme:**
- Odd quarter: @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[ग]
- Even quarter: @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[ग], @deva[ग]

### (7) @deva[हरिणप्लुता]

**Definition:** @deva[सयुगास्सल्युयु विषमे यरुयुनि नभौ भरुकौ हरिणप्लुता]

**Gaṇa Scheme:**
- Odd quarter: @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[ल], @deva[ग]
- Even quarter: @deva[न], @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[र]

---

## SECTION III

## @deva[विषमवृत्तानि] (Viṣamavṛttāni)

Unequal Metres

The most common metre of this class is called @deva[उद्गता].

### @deva[उद्गता]

**Definition:** @deva[प्रथमे सजौ यदि सलौ च नसजगुरुकाण्यनंतरम् । यद्यथ भनजलगाः स्युरथो सजसा जगौ च भवतीयमुद्गता]

**Gaṇa Scheme:**
- First quarter: @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[स], @deva[ल]
- Second quarter: @deva[न], @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[ग]
- Third quarter: @deva[भ], @deva[न], @deva[ज], @deva[ल], @deva[ग]
- Fourth quarter: @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[ग]

Another variety of Udgatā is mentioned where the first quarter has @deva[भ], @deva[न], @deva[भ], @deva[ग] instead of @deva[भ], @deva[न], @deva[ज], @deva[ल], @deva[ग].

Other kinds of metres in which every quarter differs in the number of syllables, are included under the same name '@deva[गाथा]' (Gāthā). The same name is applicable to a strophe consisting of any number of quarters other than four.

[^1]: @deva[समसर्वसमं तथा अर्धसमवृत्तं विषमं च तथा त्रिधा]

rules.title: Ardhasamavṛttāni and Viṣamavṛttāni: Metres with Alternate or Unequal Quarters
rules.body:
## Section II — @deva[अर्धसमवृत्तानि]

*Metres with their alternate quarters similar.*

In these metres the odd quarters (first and third) agree with one another, and the even quarters (second and fourth) agree with one another, but the two pairs differ.

### (1) @deva[उपचित्रम्]

**Definition:** @deva[विषमे यदि सौ सलगा दले भौ युजि भाद्गुरुकावुपचित्रम्]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[ल], @deva[ग] (odd quarter); @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[ग], @deva[ग] (even quarter).

**Example:**

@deva[सुरवैरिविपुस्तनुतां मुदं हेमनिभांशुकचंदनलिप्तम् ।]
@deva[गगनं चपलामिलितं यथा शारदनीरधरैरुपचित्रम् ॥]

### (2) @deva[अपरवक्त्रम्]

*(sometimes called @deva[वैतालीयम्])*

**Definition:** @deva[अयुजि ननरला गुरुः समे तदपरवक्त्रमिदं नजौ जरौ][^1]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[न], @deva[र], @deva[ल], @deva[ग] (odd quarter); @deva[न], @deva[ज], @deva[ज], @deva[र] (even quarter).

**Example:**

@deva[स्फुटसुममधुवेणुगीतिभिस्तमपरवक्त्रमवेत्य माधवम् ।]
@deva[मृगयुवतिगणैः समं स्थिता व्रजवनिता धृतचित्तविभ्रमा ॥]

### (3) @deva[पुष्पिताग्रा]

*(also called @deva[औपच्छंदसिक])*

**Definition:** @deva[अयुजि नयुगरेफतो यकारो युजि च नजौ जरगाश्च पुष्पिताग्रा][^1]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[न], @deva[न], @deva[र], @deva[य] (odd quarter); @deva[न], @deva[ज], @deva[ज], @deva[र], @deva[ग] (even quarter).

**Example:**

@deva[अथ मदनवधूरुपप्लवान्तं व्यसनकृशा परिपालयांबभूव ।]
@deva[शशिन इव दिवातनस्य लेखा किरणपरिक्षययूसरा प्रदोषम् ॥]

### (4) @deva[मालभारिणी]

**Definition:** @deva[विषमे ससजे गुरू नगे नौ नाविषमभरैस्तु मालभारिणी][^1]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[ग], @deva[ग] (odd quarter); @deva[स], @deva[भ], @deva[र], @deva[य] (even quarter).

**Example:**

@deva[मुहुरङ्गुलिसंत्रुताधरोष्ठं प्रतिषेधाक्षरविक्लवाभिरामम् ।]
@deva[मुखमंसविवर्ति पक्ष्मलाक्ष्याः कथमन्युन्नमितं न चुम्बितं मे ॥]

### (5) @deva[वियोगिनी]

*(also called @deva[वैतालीय] or @deva[सुंदरी])*

**Definition:** @deva[विषमे ससजा गुरुः समे सभरा लोऽथ गुरुर्वियोगिनी][^1]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[ज], @deva[ग] (odd quarter); @deva[स], @deva[भ], @deva[र], @deva[ल], @deva[ग] (even quarter).

**Example:**

@deva[सहसा विदधीत न क्रियामविवेकः परमापदां पदम् ।]
@deva[वृणुते हि विमृश्यकारिणं गुणलुब्धाः स्वयमेव संपदः ॥]

### (6) @deva[वेगवती]

**Definition:** @deva[सयुगात्सगुरू विषमे चेद् भाविह वेगवती युजि][^1]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[ग] (odd quarter); @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[ग], @deva[ग] (even quarter).

**Example:**

@deva[स्मरवेगवती व्रजरामा केशववंशरवैरतिमुग्धा ।]
@deva[रभसान्नगुरून् गणयंती केलिनिकुंजगृहाय जगाम ॥]

### (7) @deva[हरिणप्लुता]

**Definition:** @deva[सयुगात्सलघु विषमे गुरुर्युजि नभौ भरकौ हरिणप्लुता][^1]

**Gaṇa Scheme:** @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[स], @deva[ल], @deva[ग] (odd quarter); @deva[न], @deva[भ], @deva[भ], @deva[र] (even quarter).

**Example:**

@deva[स्फुटफेनचया हरिणप्लुता वलिमन्नोन्नततटा तरणेः सुता ।]
@deva[कलहंसकुलारवशालिनी विहरतो हरति स्म हरेर्मनः ॥]

[^1]: The right-hand margin of the source scan is cropped for pages 557–558; the closing syllables of the definition lines are not visible in the image and have been restored from the standard definitions of these metres, which agree with the gaṇa schemes printed alongside.

*Section III (@deva[विषमवृत्तानि], the Udgatā metre) continues in [§ 13](013.md), which carries the close of page 558.*

rules.title: Jāti: Metres Regulated by Syllabic Instants
rules.body:
## Jāti: Metres Regulated by Syllabic Instants

The most common variety of metres regulated by syllabic instants is @deva[आर्या]. It is of nine kinds:[^1]

@deva[पथा वियुला चपला मुखचपला जयमयचपला च ।]
@deva[गीत्युपगीत्युद्वुरीतय आर्योभीतिद्यु नवश्रयाः॥]

Of these the last four are generally used and described here.

---

## @deva[आर्या] (Āryā)

### Definition

@deva[यस्याः पादे प्रथमे द्वादशा मात्रास्तथा तृतीयेऽपि ।]
@deva[अष्टादश द्वितीये चतुर्थैकै पञ्चदुश सार्धं ॥]

The first and third quarters have each 12 mātrās or syllabic instants, the second 18 and the fourth 15.

### Structure

| Quarter | Mātrās |
|---------|--------|
| 1st | 12 |
| 2nd | 18 |
| 3rd | 12 |
| 4th | 15 |

### Example

From Hitopadeśa, Suhṛdbheda 96.

---

## @deva[गीति] (Gīti)

### Definition

@deva[आर्योप्रथमाद्विवर्षं यस्याः परांधोमारिता गीतिः]

i.e. the third and fourth quarters of this metre are similar to the first and second quarters of an Āryā.

### Structure

| Quarter | Mātrās | Pattern |
|---------|--------|---------|
| 1st | 12 | (same as Āryā 1st) |
| 2nd | 18 | (same as Āryā 2nd) |
| 3rd | 12 | (same as Āryā 1st) |
| 4th | 18 | (same as Āryā 2nd) |

---

## @deva[उपगीति] (Upagīti)

### Definition

@deva[आर्योपराधैनुत्युयै दुल्युद्युश्रै प्राहुरुपगीतिम्]

i.e. the first and third quarters of this metre are those of an Āryā while the second and fourth quarters have 18 mātrās each.

### Structure

| Quarter | Mātrās |
|---------|--------|
| 1st | 12 |
| 2nd | 18 |
| 3rd | 12 |
| 4th | 18 |

---

## @deva[उद्गीति] (Udgīti)

### Definition

@deva[आर्यैशुकुलद्वितैयै विरैरिते पुनर्युोहृोत्ति]

i.e. the first and third quarters of this metre have 12 syllabic instants respectively; the second and fourth have 16 and 18 syllabic instants respectively.

### Structure

| Quarter | Mātrās |
|---------|--------|
| 1st | 12 |
| 2nd | 16 |
| 3rd | 12 |
| 4th | 18 |

---

## @deva[आर्यागीति] (Āryāgīti)

### Definition

@deva[आर्यां प्राग्दुलभन्तैऽवैकप्रुरुस्तोदमराधैभागोगीतिः]

i.e. the first and third quarters of this metre have 12, the second and the fourth quarters must contain 20 syllabic instants respectively.

### Structure

| Quarter | Mātrās |
|---------|--------|
| 1st | 12 |
| 2nd | 20 |
| 3rd | 12 |
| 4th | 20 |

## @deva[वैतालीय] (Vaitālīya)

### Definition

@deva[यदिष्युदैऽद्धुौ मदै कल्युास्ताद्युयं मदै म्युनिर्न्तरं ।]
@deva[नं समात्रं परांब्रिता कल्युौ चैतालीयन्दै रलं युरुः ॥]

### Structure and Rules

The first and third quarters of this metre should contain fourteen syllabic instants and the second and fourth sixteen each; of these:

1. The last eight mātrās should consist of a @deva[र]-gaṇa (—∪—) followed by a short and a long syllable (∪—)
2. The syllabic instants in the even quarters should not be at all composed of short syllables or long syllables
3. The even syllabic instant in each quarter (i.e. the 2nd, 4th and 8th) should not be formed conjointly with the next (i.e. 3rd, 5th and 9th)

| Quarter | Mātrās | Final Pattern |
|---------|--------|---------------|
| 1st | 14 | @deva[र] + @deva[ल] + @deva[ग] (—∪— ∪—) |
| 2nd | 16 | @deva[र] + @deva[ल] + @deva[ग] (—∪— ∪—) |
| 3rd | 14 | @deva[र] + @deva[ल] + @deva[ग] (—∪— ∪—) |
| 4th | 16 | @deva[र] + @deva[ल] + @deva[ग] (—∪— ∪—) |

## @deva[आर्योपच्छन्दसिक] (Āryopacchandasika)

### Definition

@deva[पर्यैन्तैयौ तथैव शेषमोपच्छैन्दुसिकं सुधाभिरुरुकम्]

This is the same as Vaitālīya except that at the end of each quarter there must be a @deva[र] Gaṇa, followed by a @deva[ग] Gaṇa instead of @deva[ल] and @deva[ग] i.e. it is the same as Vaitālīya with a long syllable added at the end of each quarter.

### Structure

| Quarter | Mātrās | Final Pattern |
|---------|--------|---------------|
| 1st | 15 | @deva[र] + @deva[ग] (—∪— —) |
| 2nd | 17 | @deva[र] + @deva[ग] (—∪— —) |
| 3rd | 15 | @deva[र] + @deva[ग] (—∪— —) |
| 4th | 17 | @deva[र] + @deva[ग] (—∪— —) |

[^1]: The nine kinds of Āryā are: Pathyā, Vipulā, Capalā, Mukhacapalā, Jayamayacapalā, Gīti, Upagīti, Udgīti, and Āryāgīti.
